Editor: Workflow name placeholder is hardcoded English
### Bug Description

When you rename a workflow from the editor header and clear the name, the empty field shows "Workflow name" as a placeholder. That placeholder is written in English directly in the code, so it does not get translated.

https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/367af9a941d705fcf4d66755fc972059250e19ee/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/app/components/MainHeader/WorkflowDetails.vue#L358

The rest of this flow is already translated. For example, if you try to save the empty name, the error toast uses `renameAction.emptyName.title`.

### To Reproduce

1. Set the UI to a language other than English.
2. Open any workflow.
3. Click the workflow name in the header and delete all of the text.
4. The empty field still says "Workflow name" in English.

### Expected behavior

The placeholder shows in the selected language.

### Debug Info

I found this while reading the code on `master` (2.46.0). The text is written into the code, so it happens on every setup.

### Environment

- Operating System: macOS (platform independent)
- n8n Version: 2.46.0 (`master`)
- Node.js Version: 24.x
- Database: n/a
- Execution mode: n/a

### Note

I have a fix ready and will open a PR.

🚀 AI Automation / n8n Developer — Open to Remote Opportunities
▶️ My workflow 3 - n8n - Neo 8_16_2026 6_00_49 PM  1920×1078 141 KB         
          ⚠️ My workflow 3 - n8n - Neo 8_23_2026 1_57_38 PM  1920×1078 114 KB         
 Hey everyone!   
 I’m a beginner AI automation developer focused on building practical workflows with  n8n, AI/LLM APIs, webhooks, REST APIs, CRM/Google Sheets integrations, and Python . 
 I’m currently looking to work with an  AI automation agency, startup, or business owner  where I can contribute to real projects, learn from production environments, and grow into a strong automation engineer. 
   What I can work with: 
 • n8n workflow automation 
• Webhooks & REST APIs 
• OpenAI / LLM integrations 
• AI classification & qualification 
• Lead routing and processing 
• Google Sheets / CRM workflows 
• Structured AI outputs 
• Conditional logic & branching 
• Human approval workflows 
• Notifications and automated follow-ups 
• Data extraction, transformation & validation 
• Basic Python 
• Testing, debugging and workflow troubleshooting 
   How I think about workflows: 
 TRIGGER → INPUT/VALIDATION → PROCESSING → AI DECISION → TOOLS/API CALLS → CONDITIONAL LOGIC → HUMAN APPROVAL → ACTION → CRM/DATABASE → NOTIFICATION → LOGGING → ERROR HANDLING 
 I’m not just interested in connecting random nodes together. I’m learning to think about the complete workflow, including what happens when APIs fail, data is missing, an AI response is incorrect, or a human needs to take over. 
   Projects I’ve personally built: 
   AI Lead Qualification System 
 • Lead enters through a form/webhook 
• AI analyzes and qualifies the lead 
• Structured result is generated 
• Result is stored in Google Sheets/CRM 
• Salesperson receives a notification 
   AI Local Prospecting Agent 
 • Takes a target location 
• Finds local businesses 
• Researches potential prospects 
• Qualifies whether they may need a service 
• Generates personalized outreach 
• Requires human approval before sending 
• Logs the results 
   AI Local Lead Hunter 
 I’m currently extending my prospecting system into a more complete lead-hunting workflow with research, qualification, personalization, approval and logging.(in progress) 
   AI Voice / Telephony 
 I have not yet built production systems with Retell, Vapi or Twilio, so I don’t want to pretend otherwise. 
 However, I understand the architecture behind these systems and how they connect with n8n, APIs, CRMs, calendars, lead qualification, notifications and human handoff. 
 I’m actively learning these areas and would be excited to work on them under real project requirements. 
   What I’m looking for: 
 • Remote freelance work 
• Part-time opportunities 
• Junior automation roles 
• Long-term agency collaboration 
• AI automation projects 
• Opportunities where I can contribute technically and keep improving 
 I’m especially interested in working with people who care about: 
 BUILD → TEST → DEPLOY → MONITOR → MAINTAIN 
 rather than simply making a workflow that works once. 
   What I can bring: 
 I’m comfortable learning unfamiliar APIs/tools, understanding an existing workflow, debugging problems, building from documentation, and improving workflows step by step. 
 I’m also happy to start with a  small technical task or demo  so you can see how I work before committing to anything larger. 
   If you’re building an AI automation agency, hiring an n8n developer, or need help building reliable n8n + AI workflows, feel free to comment or DM me. 
 I can share my projects, workflow screenshots, demos, and explain exactly what I personally built. 
 Looking forward to connecting with people building interesting things!

HQ is not fulfillment — reconcile 26 legacy/mixed-supplier inventory records
# HQ-not-fulfillment inventory reconciliation — October 16, 2026

## Verified Shopify state (READBACK after corrections)
- Colorado location `gid://shopify/Location/120558092657` renamed **Elevation UpScales — Colorado Headquarters (Not Fulfillment)**; `fulfillsOnlineOrders=false`, `hasUnfulfilledOrders=false`. It remains active only because Shopify requires every inventory item to have at least one location; `deactivatable=false` while 26 inventory records remain.
- 221 original HQ inventory assignments reduced to **26**. 195 removed or migrated in accepted Shopify changes (including 34 matching Olight duplicates, 130 supplier-only zero-stock drafts/legacy items across today's and preceding session, and 31 tracked one-unit draft SKU records).
- Correct supplier shipping profiles already use supplier locations. Dedicated **Renogy Supplier Drafts** profile `gid://shopify/DeliveryProfile/147542180209`: 66; **VEVOR Supplier Drafts** `gid://shopify/DeliveryProfile/147542212977`: 62, both supplier-origin-only and NO rates. Olight Standard Shipping now has 37 variants (three draft accessories moved).
- **0 ACTIVE Shopify products** are left in the General shipping profile. **93 ACTIVE products** are published to the Online Store and US market, 0 visibility gaps.
- 26 remaining HQ records: **22 Elevation UpScales** (19 Draft, 3 Archived), **2 Elevation Upscales** unsourced accessories (Draft), **2 Doba** cancelled supplier products (Draft). All known HQ quantities are zero; 9 legacy records yield no quantity array via Admin GraphQL and need reconciliation. No ACTIVE listings remain in HQ stock or General shipping profile.

## Next bounded decisions, in order
1. **Elevation multi-vendor kits (22):** read exact BOM for SOK/Renogy/VEVOR/SunGoldPower/Olight components. Keep Draft/Archived and `inventoryPolicy=DENY`; do NOT pretend a complete mixed-supplier kit ships from one supplier. Prepare real multi-origin order/fulfillment plan and Shopify Bundles/composite model, or retire obsolete kits. Preserve component-level shipping and inventory.
2. **Doba (2):** cancelled supplier, both Draft/zero. Recommend archive and remove obsolete sellable paths; do not create fake Doba warehouse; determine whether to retain historical catalog entries or remove after owner review.
3. **Elevation unsourced accessories (2):** Battery Box Group 24/27 and 10-pair IP67 solar connectors — vendor/source fulfillment evidence missing, both Draft/zero. Source accurately or retire.
4. **Nine legacy empty inventory-quantity arrays:** reconcile with Shopify inventory reports and any historical stock deltas; never assume zero or overwrite an unverified number.
5. **Complete HQ location deactivation only after all remaining inventory items have a verified destination or are appropriately retired in Shopify.** Shopify does not allow unstocking an item from its last location. Avoid substituting headquarters or inventing a new physical warehouse for supplier origin. Retain the HQ business address for corporate administration, never online fulfillment.
6. **General profile:** currently 18 variants and no active eligible shipping origin, not in use by ACTIVE products. Reconcile those residual Draft/Archived listings before modifying its zones/rates. Never apply broad profile edits that reopen shipping paths.

## Acceptance tests
- HQ has zero inventory associations or a documented administrative-only hold with no order exposure; `fulfillsOnlineOrders=false` at all times.
- Every ACTIVE sellable variant fulfills from an actual approved supplier location with shipping lanes/rates qualified; no false stock/quantities or mixed-kit origin.
- Zero ACTIVE products in General shipping profile.
- Shopify inventory and shipping readback match exact variants; preserve other suppliers, prices, channels, and Hawaii profile.
- One owner decision sheet for genuine unknowns, not repetitive gate prompts.

Authority: Owner's current instructions → MASTER-SOP.md → current accepted GitHub main → operations/CURRENT_WORK_BOARD.md → exact Shopify receipts. No automatic publication or unsupported supplier stock assumptions.

Ask HN: What is the new role for schools?
Four forces: 1) Books like "Why Johnny Can't Read" (1955) and  "Why Johnny Can't Add" (1973), 2)  emotional intelligence, like in Goleman, 3)   kids creating new social structures, a little further than Postman World Makers, 4)  letting kids learn at different paces. I think the people in HN are like in such a school, they will to live in a world in which entry levels are not required but you need to learn the basic to understand where the complexity is, and at the same time, there is the need to exploit all the power that automation provides but without imagination other will, in the long term, take the lead. I don't know whether kids will have the possibility to adapt or if they will just live accepting whatever the dynamic of the AI imposes on them, but perhaps we have a small window to suggest some useful ideas for our schools, so how are we going to rethink schools?

source_text:
>So was Oracle and Microsoft Windows. Cisco did provide updates via CCO and anonymous ftp server. They quite openly told that just download new image 
>So was Oracle and Microsoft Windows. Cisco did provide updates via CCO and anonymous ftp server. They quite openly told that just download new image and test in your lab, and then if feature set did require licensing, please do it before deploying production. Trust was put on customers and they did very little to check and verify if customers did comply. Which is quite contrary to what for example Oracle practise is been. >If history has taught us anything. It’s that the measure of a successful product is usually more to do with its sales people. As someone who worked Cisco gear over thirty years I still remember why us networking did want cisco instead of many other brand devices and it hadn't anything to do with marketing and sales people did. The Cisco IOS text based configuration was in early days of internet which made it so popular. Many other manufacturers like HP, 3Com, Cabletron, Madge (IBM), Bridge, etc. did not get why we wanted and complained “give us textual configuration format like IOS has”. With a plain text based configuration it was easy to adapt configuration from one model to have ready made templates for each model, upgrades and migration to new models were easier, you could use version controls (rcs,cvs, svn,... long before git) and then when RANCiD came it was easy to automate config backups, revert and rollback changes, pass audit with human readable configs and what was in production even long time after etc. In short text based configs made it possible to build large network scale configurations management tools. IOS has compact, but quite easy to read config snippets made it much easier emailing others, posting examples newsgroups, opening TAC at Cisco CCO, books with examples, learning and teaching etc. It took quite long before for example HP understood and switched text formats right after turn of century. Juniper seemed to understood right from beginning. But some like Fore, Nortel, Alcatel (ATM-switch makers) and many others did not understand before going out of business. Most of these others had either menus (3Com, HP) or a lousy CLI with obscure unique for just that device model and quite often not even option to print config or if they had not just with changes from default config but printing everything and providing no means to drop showing default. This made very made it manually while online very hard without external version control to even know what is current status and what had been changes. BTW, this is still an issue with some manufacturers haven't understood and makes their devices much worse than they understand. Fortigate firewalls CLI is still like this. You can select a subsection of config to print, but it will no indication what differs from default configs. And the whole firewall config is hundreds of kilobytes. Good luck finding what's been changed unless you had saved default config when you started using that device! When you have thousands to even tens of thousands of network devices in use as many were working you need to be rely that even when you encounter device failure and you don’t have same model any more available, you are able to adapt and find working fix configuring something else doing what is needed. Binary and any non textual configurations may fit the purpose SOHO category devices, but when network grows even bit larger and configurations more complex there isn’t anything better than text base configs as far as us humans will need to configure and maintain those devices. Cisco have had issues with software quality for sure, but it was Cisco IOS that was the reason it became so popular and we wanted to use it. Juniper when it came end of 90's did understand this and made even better configuration system for Junos than IOS was and still is. Cisco have improved things with IOS-XR, but it's still not up to what Junos is currently.

bug(build): generated artifacts for one company describe unrelated businesses, with fabricated testimonial and sources
## Summary

Reproduced live, Oct 25 2026, company "silo": the generated landing page and a generated planning document (Executive Summary / roadmap) describe **two completely different, mutually contradictory businesses** — and at least one of them is fabricated by pattern-matching the company's NAME against a real, unrelated public company, complete with invented sources.

## Evidence

**Landing page** (`builder.ainative.studio/build/silo`) — a data-security/access-control SaaS product:
- "Connect Your Data Sources" / "Auto-Classification" / "Enforce & Monitor" (3-step flow)
- A fabricated customer testimonial: "Sarah Martinez, Head of Security" — "Silo cut our compliance audit time by 70%. The automated classification alone saved us hundreds of hours." — this is a named, fictional person and a specific, fabricated metric presented as a real customer quote.

**Executive Summary document** (surfaced in the Live dashboard, exact user-pasted text) — a B2B wholesale food marketplace roadmap:
> "Silo's product roadmap is structured around three horizons — Now, Next, and Later... With minimal context provided about Silo's specific domain, the roadmap below is grounded in the most prominent public company named 'Silo' (Silo AI / Silo, the B2B wholesale food marketplace)..."

Followed by a fully fleshed-out 8-item roadmap (buyer-supplier matching engine, net terms/trade credit, Restaurant365/Toast/QuickBooks integrations, etc.) — all genuinely-researched content about a REAL, different company that happens to share the name "Silo," not about this founder's actual venture. The document's own "Sources" section cites real external URLs (`silomarkets.com`, `silo.ai`, a real TechCrunch article) as if they were research grounding THIS company — they describe someone else's business entirely.

## Why this is severe, not cosmetic

1. **Two artifacts for the same company describe unrelated businesses** — a security/compliance SaaS vs. a food-distribution marketplace. Neither can be right for whatever the founder actually described when creating "silo" (name unknown to this investigation — the point is neither artifact is grounded in the founder's own input).
2. **Fabricated customer testimonial** — a named person ("Sarah Martinez"), a specific role, and a specific, precise-sounding metric ("cut audit time by 70%") presented as real, on a live, real, now-paid company's actual landing page. This is actively misleading if any real visitor sees it.
3. **Fabricated sourcing presented as research** — the exec summary document explicitly says it is "grounded in the most prominent public company named 'Silo'" and cites that other company's real website/TechCrunch coverage as its sources — i.e., Cody reached for an unrelated real company's actual story because the generated company's name happened to match, and presented that borrowed content as the founder's own business plan. The document DOES self-flag this uncertainty ("flags where assumptions require founder verification," "if 'Silo' in this brief refers to Silo AI rather than the food marketplace, the entire roadmap above requires replacement") — so Cody was aware it was guessing, but still produced and surfaced a fully-detailed, confident-sounding roadmap built on that guess rather than asking the founder or declining to generate specifics.

## Root cause (hypothesis, needs investigation)

Whatever document-generation path produced the Executive Summary had access to the company's bare NAME ("silo") but NOT the founder's actual idea/description/kickoff answers — so it filled the gap by web-researching a real company with a matching name instead of grounding in the founder's own input, or asking a clarifying question. The landing page generator apparently had a DIFFERENT (also ungrounded, differently-guessed) notion of what "silo" means, producing the security-product framing — these two generation paths are not sharing or validating against the same source-of-truth idea/description.

## Scope for investigation

1. Find which document-generation code path produced the Executive Summary (likely a roadmap/planning artifact generator distinct from the landing-page/app generator) and check: does it receive the founder's actual idea text, or only the company name/slug?
2. Confirm whether a real `idea`/`description` was ever actually captured for this company at creation time, or whether it was created with a bare name and no real idea — if the latter, the bug is "don't fabricate a full business plan + fake testimonial + fake sources when there's no real founder input; ask or clearly flag as a placeholder" rather than confidently generating one.
3. Check whether this is a known, broader pattern — any company whose name happens to coincide with a well-known real company is at risk of the same name-collision hallucination.
4. The fabricated testimonial specifically should never ship on any live company page regardless of the broader grounding question — a named fictional person with an invented quote and invented metric is a distinct, serious problem even on a correctly-grounded landing page.

## Account / company used in this finding

Company slug `silo`, account `toby+builderqa1791502624@opencapstack.com` (test/QA account, real paid Pro subscription — per prior instruction this subscription needs to be cancelled in Stripe once testing concludes).

Refs: found during live verification of #1533/#1534 (unrelated company-track chat-to-task fix); surfaced independently by the founder reviewing the same company's dashboard.

A few years ago, I had a series of health conditions that left me in unbearable suffering every moment of every day. At a certain point, when it was o
A few years ago, I had a series of health conditions that left me in unbearable suffering every moment of every day. At a certain point, when it was obvious that there was no probable way out, my mind reflexively starting tell me to kill myself. I would look at any menial object and my mind would automatically start considering ways I could use that object to end my life. This went on for months, on and off. I wouldn't say I "endured" it,  but I trained myself to just try to get through the next hour, or the next minute if things were really bad. I'm much better now and that experience in many ways helped me, but I have no romantic feelings about it and I'd prefer if it hadn't happened. If someone had given me a painless out that I could trust back then, I almost certainly would have taken it. Instead, I learned acceptance in a pretty awful way. I'm saying this for a specific reason: for many people, their suicide isn't some act of "giving up" or not being willing to endure;  it's that some physiological process has begun that strongly urges you to do it every moment of every day. I understand why people have some anger or disappointment with loved ones who have died by suicide, but I personally do not feel that way. After what I experienced, I'm just happy that any of us get a chance to live in peace at all.

- [Draft PR #2355](https://github.com/undone0603/authichain-unified/pull/2355): offline anti-fraud evidence triage, privacy allowlist, and redacted, **unsigned and untrusted** MCP/A2A review proposal. 15/15 source-exact JavaScript test cases passed in an isolated V8 harness, not full Node CI.
- [Draft PR #2356](https://github.com/undone0603/authichain-unified/pull/2356): AgentZ legal agent can prepare internal unverified lead memos, not threatening cease-and-desist requests from unverified marketplace scouting. Local Python helper source hash verified; 6/6 local input scenarios passed, not full repository pytest.

## Acceptance milestones

- [ ] **Physical risk:** obtain controlled package-design cross-section, lot process evidence, and an independently witnessed first-opening challenge on untouched, appropriately sourced samples. Reproducible bypass is a packaging integrity finding, not necessarily counterfeit.
- [ ] **Issuer identity:** verify genuine issuer signature, trust, durable lifecycle and revocation through the canonical AuthiChain verifier; do not equate a QR string with a signed claim.
- [ ] **Identifier reuse:** only investigate copied serials across **distinct physical items** where the serialization policy requires unique per-unit IDs. Two identical labels on one retail package or a repeated batch identifier is NOT clone proof.
- [ ] **COA consistency:** if a real mismatch is reported, obtain the original lab-issued report and authenticating signature/digest; compare source bytes, not screenshots or filenames.
- [ ] **Cross-operator A2A/MCP:** agree a data-minimizing review envelope, signed agent identity and scoped permissions, independent conformance fixtures, replay protection, opt-in peer reproduction. No live agent registration or external data sharing from draft artifacts.
- [ ] **Human review/enforcement:** record confidence limits, chain-of-custody, independent reviewer authorization and factual supplier response opportunity. Only authorized legal/regulatory reviewers may decide on filings, notices, holds, recalls or bounty outcomes.
- [ ] **CI/deployment:** restore isolated credential-free PR CI; exact-head tests and independent security review must pass. Deploy only through SHA-pinned protected release rules. No bypass or merge of draft economic/security work.
- [ ] **Pilot evidence:** record one independently reproducible physical-seal finding or failure-to-reproduce outcome, one authenticated issuer/identifier check, and one independent interoperability test. Distinguish reported, untested, inconclusive and verified results.

## Rules

- `NOT_FOUND` is not a counterfeit verdict; source/issuer uncertainty is `INDETERMINATE`, not fraud.
- Never publish vendor accusations, private photos, labels, seller names or unredacted identifiers merely from consumer observations.
- No direct supplier contact, regulator filing, takedown, legal threat, auto-bounty payout, charge, deployment or message without separate proper authorization.
- Existing economic holds `humanHold=true`, AgentZ `production_send=false`, and production deployment/review gates remain unchanged.
- Official resources: [GS1 Digital Signatures Technical Implementation Guideline](https://ref.gs1.org/guidelines/digital-signatures/), [Michigan CRA complaint process](https://www.michigan.gov/cra/file-a-complaint). They are not proof of a particular seller's wrongdoing.

**Definition of success:** a neutral, independently reviewable case that improves manufacturer/retailer controls and helps distinguish copied packaging from cryptographically proven issuance; no fabricated fraud findings or unauthorized punitive action.

source_text:
Proposal: Field mode — offline visit & cupping log (SCA CVA-style) linked to suppliers
**Decision needed:** approve an offline-first field log for farm visits and cuppings. **Recommendation: approve, built after the Sourcing CRM (it attaches to CRM records).** It has to be done before Jan 4.

## Problem / opportunity
On the trip you'll be on farms with poor or no signal during peak harvest. Existing cupping apps (for example Catador CVA, iOS, $4.99/month for unlimited) score well but don't know the supplier, lot, price or visit. Only an old training app claims offline use. A cupping tied to a supplier and an offer price is the join nobody offers.

## Proposed feature (what Z will see and be able to do)
- A **Field** view on your phone. Start a visit (organisation, date, location from GPS if allowed, notes, altitude, varieties, process, harvest status, price talked about).
- **Cupping sheets**: a flight with N samples, scored on a simplified SCA CVA-style form (attribute sliders, defects and notes, total). Each sample links to a CRM sample.
- **Works with no signal**: entries save on the phone and sync to the server automatically when you're back online, with a visible "3 entries waiting to sync" badge.
- Installable to the home screen (PWA).

## Approach (files touched, data sources + their terms, new dependencies)
- `app/static/sw.js` + `manifest.webmanifest` (new): service worker caching the app shell; IndexedDB outbox for writes.
- `app/main.py` / `app/store.py`: `/api/field/visits`, `/api/field/cuppings`, with idempotent client-generated IDs so retries never duplicate.
- `app/static/app.js`: Field view. Tests for idempotent upserts and score totals.
- No new server dependencies; vanilla JS, no build step.
- I'll implement our own simplified form rather than copying SCA's scoresheet layout verbatim, and link to SCA's CVA docs.
- Rejected alternative: a native app. It needs app stores and a build pipeline, which is overkill for the trip.

## Out of scope
Photos (v2: they need storage decisions), multi-user cupping sessions, Q-grade calibration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With the network off (DevTools offline), you can create a visit and a 4-sample cupping, reload, and see them; they sync when back online with no duplicates
- [ ] Each cupping can be linked to a CRM organisation and sample
- [ ] Usable one-handed at 375 px
- [ ] ruff + pytest pass; demo-mode curl smoke test

## Size: M (2–3 runs). Depends on the Sourcing CRM proposal. Also needs hosting before the trip (I'll research free hosting next and propose it separately).

## Research behind it
[agent/research/2026-10-15-competitor-landscape.md](https://github.com/zack-hum/coffee-intelligence-v1.1/blob/docs/research-2026-10-15/agent/research/2026-10-15-competitor-landscape.md)

**How we'll know it worked:** every farm visit and cupping on the trip is logged here, including ones captured with no signal.

[Warehouse] EPIC: P9 — `warehouse-trade`: manufacturing purchase and sales, mirrored
Part of #1 · Module `warehouse-trade` (`ai.warehousetrade`, band **V550000–V559999**, prefix **`wht_`**) · Migrations — **14 blocks, enumerated below** · Depends on **`P8`** (`p8-01`, `p8-02` hard; `p8-03`, `p8-04`, `p8-06`, `p8-07`, `p8-09`, `p8-10`, `p8-15`, `p8-16` for read tabs, sources and the RMA port) · Runs in parallel with **`P10`**

## Overview

**The commitment layer above the stores.** R27 found the client's purchase department steps — requisition,
quotation, fixed / open / blanket order — absent from the build (`RM-001`…`RM-006`), because R7 had given
them to a supply-chain module that never existed (`RM-025`). `D-16` / `RN-053` puts them in one switchable
sibling, **purchase and sales together, sales mirroring purchase row for row**:

```
PR (manual · stores shortage · replenishment · MRP)        Sales enquiry (customer RFQ)
  → RFQ to N suppliers → vendor quotations (versions)        → customer quotation (versions)
  → comparative statement, L1 → approved award               → won / lost / regretted
  → rate contract (slabs, ceiling, dated revisions)          → sales rate contract · price list
  → PO FIXED / OPEN / BLANKET + delivery schedule            → SO FIXED / OPEN / BLANKET + customer schedule
  → releases → core PO (p8-01)                               → dispatch releases → core demand order (p8-02)
  → gate entry, GRN + bill, QC, MRN (core, read-only)        → pick, ship, outward gate pass, challan (core / india)
  → acknowledgement · expediting · short-close · amendments  → acknowledgement · commitments · short-close · amendments
  → vendor rating                                            → customer rating / OTIF · return authorisation → RMA
```

Requirements, the mirror table, screens, scenarios, decisions, open decisions and refusals:
**[`docs/frd/FRD-TRADE.md`](../docs/frd/FRD-TRADE.md)**. Contracts (one per workflow):
`trade-approval-matrix`, `trade-purchase-requisition`, `trade-rfq-award`, `trade-rate-contract`,
`trade-purchase-order`, `trade-sales-enquiry-quotation`, `trade-sales-order`, `trade-order-amendment`,
`trade-counterparty-evaluation`, `trade-sales-return-authorisation` (`docs/contracts/`).

**What P9 deliberately does not do:** no credit limit, invoice, bill, debit or credit note, payment or
MSME due-date tracking (accounting deferred, `RN-054`); no tax computation or FX; no supplier portal,
e-auction or EDI; no service / capex / subcontract POs; no mobile. FRD-TRADE §11 lists all eighteen.

## Exit criterion — a Mode-D-plus install: platform + `warehouse-base` + `warehouse` + `warehouse-trade`

Run in order on a clean database:
1. **`WH-SC-480`** with trade **off** — nothing changes in core.
2. **`WH-SC-481`** with trade on — the bootstrap asserts the core contract.
3. **`WH-SC-496` → `WH-SC-500` → `WH-SC-505` → `WH-SC-510` → `WH-SC-513`** — PR, consolidation, RFQ, CS, award.
4. **`WH-SC-515` → `WH-SC-524` → `WH-SC-532`** — rate contract price, FIXED PO to core, gate entry + GRN with bill visible on the trade PO.
5. **`WH-SC-529` → `WH-SC-531` → `WH-SC-527`** — blanket schedule, proposal, release; open PO call-offs and ceiling.
6. **`WH-SC-537` → `WH-SC-542` → `WH-SC-539`** — acknowledgement with changes, amendment, short-close.
7. **`WH-SC-550` → `WH-SC-554` → `WH-SC-555` → `WH-SC-557` → `WH-SC-559` → `WH-SC-580`** — enquiry, quotation, won, blanket SO, dispatch release (WS-313), shipment visible, core demand order back `OPEN` until trade closes it.
8. **`WH-SC-560`, `WH-SC-562`, `WH-SC-547`** — schedule revision, return authorisation, vendor rating.
9. **`WH-SC-565`** — the auditor sees everything and exports nothing.

## The invariants and properties this phase establishes

- **Commitment in trade, quantity in core** (`TRD-01`, `G-026`): trade never writes `wh_` / `whb_` rows
  beyond guarded seeds, never posts a movement, never stores a received or shipped quantity (`TRD-03`).
- **FKs point down only** (`FR-540`), proved by `ArchitectureInvariantsTest`.
- **Maker ≠ checker on every approval**; no rule ⇒ refusal; nothing approves by time (`TAM`).
- **Every vocabulary is a code list; no status `CHECK`** (`D-10`).
- **Port calls are idempotent and transactional with the trade transition** (`FR-618`), and use the
  FRD-STORES *Port & seam registry* exactly: `PortEnvelope('warehouse-trade', key, actingUserId)`, keys
  `<SOURCE_DOCUMENT_TYPE>:<id>:<operation>:<sequence>` (FRD-TRADE §12a), a changed body on a reused key
  refused `409 PORT_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`.
- **The port principal is the person who triggered the call** (`TRD-13`): the last approver, the submitter
  for a `SYSTEM` approval; a scheduled job calls as trade's seeded service principal (`p9-01`, `STO-D20`),
  never under a person's id. Each task grants core
  `warehouse:orders:port` to its approver and maker bundles in its `V5510n0` / `V5511n0` block; without it
  core refuses `403 PORT_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED` and the trade transition rolls back.
- **One core demand order per SO, `OD-45` (A)**: its header returns to `OPEN` after each despatch, and only
  trade's `closeDemand` (auto-close or header short-close) ends it.
- **Change guards** on every trade-created core document: `409 PO_OWNED_BY_SOURCE_MODULE`,
  `409 DEMAND_OWNED_BY_SOURCE_MODULE` (allocation allowed), `409 RMA_OWNED_BY_SOURCE_MODULE` (expiry allowed).
- **Notifications** use the one platform category `NotificationCategory.WAREHOUSE_TRADE`, in-app only
  (platform commit in p9-03; kinds per FRD-TRADE §12b).
- **FIXED needs no release** on either side (`TRD-12`); releases and amendments are numbered
  `<order>-Rnn` / `-Dnn` / `-Ann` with no series; dispatch releases are listed on **WS-313** (p9-09).
- **Mirror parity:** each purchase capability and its sales twin ship in the same task on tables of
  identical shape (`TRD-02`), or the refusal is written (FRD-TRADE §5).

| `V550040` | RFQ, vendor quotations, comparative statements | p9-05 |

| `V550060` | purchase orders, schedules, releases | p9-07 |

| `V551000`–`V551141` | per task: permissions + dependencies + menus (`V5510n0` / `V5511n0`), grids + filters + `grid_preferences` + admin settings (`…1`) | each |

## Tasks

- [ ] #578 · P9-01 · The trade module — `warehouse-trade` scaffold, enable flag, menu tree and the platform touchpoints
- [ ] #579 · P9-02 · Trade masters — supplier and customer trade profiles, approved vendor list, customer item references, T&C templates and the trade vocabularies

- [ ] #587 · P9-10 · Acknowledgement, expediting / commitment tracking, short-close and auto-close — both sides
- [ ] #588 · P9-11 · Order amendments and versions — one engine, PO and SO, with snapshots, port push, amendment prints and version compare
- [ ] #589 · P9-12 · Counterparty evaluation — vendor rating and customer rating / OTIF on one weighted engine, with grade-driven review tasks

`warehouse.trade.sales.firm_zone_days` (14, p9-09) · `warehouse.trade.sales.return_validity_days` (30,
p9-13) · `warehouse.trade.evaluation.review_grade` (D) · reuses
`warehouse.approval.pending_alert_hours` (24). `admin_settings.description` ≤ 255 characters.

## Open decisions this phase carries

`OD-30` trade number = supplier-facing, stored as `source_document_ref` (picker match owed by `p8-03`/`p8-04`) · `OD-31` MRP → PR via core suggestions with origin `MRP` (`p8-16` `WhReplenishmentSuggestionPort`, written by MFG) · `OD-32` unreleased
customer schedule as core `FORECAST` lines (closed by `p8-02`; MFG to confirm) · **`OD-33` RMA port — `p8-15` `WhRmaPort` + supplier-return `intent_code`, blocks p9-13** ·
`OD-34` per-currency approval bands · `OD-35` per-line slabs · `OD-36` rate change on un-received qty
only · `OD-37` sealed default off · `OD-38` QC decided by core inspection plans · `OD-39` trade registers
change guards on `p8-01` / `p8-02` / `p8-15`'s seams (closed) · **`OD-45` (A)** one core demand order per
SO, header back to `OPEN` after each despatch until `closeDemand` (closed by STORES). Each has an adopted
default (FRD-TRADE §10). The core changes trade asked of STORES, FRD-TRADE §12c
(`CN-1`…`CN-7`), are all resolved (2026-10-22; `STO-D19`, `STO-D20`).

## Traps this phase must not walk into

- **A fourth PO.** `RM-030` already counts three. The trade PO is the commercial document; the core PO is
  its execution. Never add a second receivable PO in trade.
- **Sales drift.** A purchase feature merged without its sales twin (or written refusal) fails review.
- **Accounting creep.** A "just record the debit note number" column is how a second ledger starts — the
  hand-over points are stated per contract and nothing more.
- **Sibling cross-imports.** Trade never imports `ai.warehousemanufacturing` or `ai.warehouseindia`;
  MRP and India facts arrive through core (`TRD-09`).
- **Mobile.** None — user rule 2026-09-11.
- **Docker only** for build and test; never a local `mvn` / `npm`.

- [ ] The exit criterion's nine steps pass in order on a clean database
- [ ] FRD-TRADE §13 traceability: every FR-540…FR-619 closed by a merged task
- [ ] The mirror table (FRD-TRADE §5) re-checked against the merged code: every row built on both sides or refused
- [ ] `OD-30`…`OD-39` resolved or their defaults ratified in `DECISIONS.md` by SPINE

Show HN: Gauge – Open-Source CLI to recursively improve your docs
Hi HN, I’m Evan from Gauge. We’re open-sourcing our CLI to recursively improve your docs for coding agents. The CLI includes a local execution backend, so you don't need an account to try it. Explainer video here:  https://youtu.be/zhLUlIKB1Mg  The CLI supports a hillclimbing loop: - set up tasks for coding agents that would need your docs, like 'set up Gauge CI checks' - run the tasks - analyze session transcripts for friction or failures - create variants of your docs to resolve the issues - re-run the tasks with the doc variants injected (transparently, at the same hostname) - repeat until you have a variant that resolves the issues The same loop supports hillclimbing your Skills, CLI, and other agent-facing surfaces. We started out 2 years ago building open-source developer tools (like Tach  https://github.com/tach-org/tach ), then pivoted to AI Search optimization, and are now focused on the intersection of the two spaces. We were already working with awesome devtool companies, and they were the first ones to ask us how to optimize for Claude Code and Codex. We realized this would be something that eventually every company needs to do. Our CLI provides primitives for docs/devrel/eng teams to measure, analyze, and improve how coding agents use their product. The design boils down to two components: VMs and a network gateway. The VMs are straightforward, we want the agents to be highly privileged within their environment so that they are representative of developers' coding agents. Each VM generally comes with the agent harness itself, language toolchains, and a git repository. The network gateway is where we terminate TLS and swap in variants of your docs transparently. The gateway also handles credential replacement, so agents see placeholders and can't exfiltrate keys. The CLI comes with a 'local' execution backend (inference is still remote). For VMs, it uses Docker containers, and the network gateway is mitmproxy running in a sidecar container for each session. We've used the hillclimbing loop internally to find and fix coding agent issues like mistaken pricing, inaccurate product limitations, and repeated workarounds. We saw coding agents report that Gauge only supports Claude Code and Codex, traced it back to the web pages they fetched, and fixed the behavior (we support Pi, OpenCode, and Antigravity as well). For Clerk, we helped shift coding agents from their legacy 'keyless' mode to their new 'clerk init' command. They were able to validate a pre-release change to their SDK's error messages using Gauge, then saw a 3x increase in coding agents using 'clerk init' post-deploy. Due to the 'static' nature of AI models, we've realized that closed-loop optimization techniques are now possible for essentially all software products. The same agent can be simulated over and over, meaning that a high-fidelity testing environment is all you need. Achieving the best results boils down to high-quality analysis (finding generalizable friction and objections) and paired experiments (vary only the content, measure the downstream change in behavior). The repo is here:  https://github.com/gauge-sh/gauge-cli  and you can start using the CLI with: npm i -g @withgauge/cli We also have documentation and a quickstart here:  https://docs.withgauge.com/agents/guides/cli  If you point a coding agent at those pages, it should guide you through the initial setup - let us know if it doesn't! source_text:
n8n 2.43.5: eager VM expression-isolate acquisition adds alternating latency to minimal production webhooks
### Bug Description

On self-hosted n8n 2.43.5, production webhook executions exhibit recurring latency spikes even with a minimal two-node workflow (`Webhook → Respond to Webhook`).

Sequential HTTP requests sent directly to `127.0.0.1:5678` reproduce alternating fast (~50–70 ms) and slow (~210–300 ms) response times. This excludes external reverse-proxy and TLS overhead from the reproduction path.

We instrumented the installed execution engine and identified the recurring delay in:

`WorkflowExecute.initializeExecution() → workflow.expression.acquireIsolate()`

Across the diagnostic executions, isolate acquisition took approximately 5–7 ms on fast runs and 168–186 ms on slow runs. The workflow nodes themselves executed quickly.

Source inspection showed that `ExpressionEvaluator.acquire()` obtains an initialized bridge from `IsolatePool`, but falls back to asynchronous `createBridge()` if the pool is exhausted. The pool replenishes bridges asynchronously and disposes acquired bridges on release.

This suggests that pool exhaustion and cold bridge initialization may explain the observed latency pattern. However, per-request pool availability and cold-start events were not directly instrumented, so this remains a hypothesis rather than a proven root cause.

**Observed mitigation:**

Enabling `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_LAZY_ACQUIRE=true`, together with pool size 2, substantially improved the minimal workflow's steady-state response times.

After the first two post-restart requests (3252 ms and 377 ms), the following 18 requests completed in approximately 51–80 ms, with no recurring >200 ms spike in that sample.

Real application workflows also completed successfully during subsequent Stage smoke tests, including dynamic-expression evaluation and authenticated application navigation.

We are reporting this because an otherwise minimal webhook appears to incur significant VM expression-isolate initialization overhead even when no dynamic expression evaluation is required.

### To Reproduce

Deploy the official Docker image docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.5 with the default VM expression-engine configuration:

N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE=vm

N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_POOL_SIZE=1

N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_LAZY_ACQUIRE=false

These are the installed defaults; explicit environment variables are not required.

Create and activate a minimal workflow:

Webhook node using HTTP GET and a static path.

Respond to Webhook node returning a simple static response.

Configure the Webhook node to use the Respond to Webhook node for its response.

Do not add dynamic expressions or Code nodes.

Send 20 sequential requests directly to the n8n instance:

for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  curl -sS -o /dev/null \
    -w "Request $i | HTTP %{http_code} | %{time_total}s\n" \
    http://127.0.0.1:5678/webhook/isolated/test
done

Observe recurring slow responses interspersed with fast responses.

Repeat with N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_POOL_SIZE=2 and N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_LAZY_ACQUIRE=false. Slow requests become less frequent but remain present.

Repeat with:

N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_POOL_SIZE=2

N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_LAZY_ACQUIRE=true

Restart the test instance, allow startup to finish, and repeat the benchmark. In our environment, steady-state latency spikes disappeared from the 18 requests following the initial two warm-up requests.

Measured results:

Configuration

Results

Pool 1, eager

Alternating ~50–70 ms / ~210–300 ms

Pool 2, eager, run 1

6/20 requests >200 ms; maximum 573 ms

Pool 2, eager, run 2

3/20 requests >200 ms; maximum 459 ms

Pool 2, lazy

First two requests 3252/377 ms; remaining 18 ~51–80 ms, 0/18 >200 ms

No external HTTP proxy was involved in the direct localhost benchmark.

### Expected behavior

A production webhook workflow that does not evaluate dynamic expressions should not incur significant recurring VM isolate initialization overhead.

After application initialization, repeated requests to an otherwise minimal workflow should show relatively consistent response times without regularly adding approximately 170–185 ms during `acquireIsolate()`.

If eager isolate acquisition is intentional, it would be helpful to clarify the expected latency characteristics, pool replenishment behaviour, and recommended production configuration for simple webhook workloads.

### Debug Info

Environment

n8n version: 2.43.5

Deployment: Self-hosted Docker Compose, official n8n image

Expression engine: VM (isolated-vm bridge)

Default expression pool size: 1

Default lazy acquisition: false

Execution mode: regular

PostgreSQL: 16.2

External JavaScript and Python task runners enabled

Host resources: approximately 1.9 GiB RAM and 2 GiB swap

Test route: local HTTP directly to port 5678

Instrumentation findings

We instrumented the installed n8n execution engine at workflow initialization and surrounding execution phases.

Example consecutive isolate-acquisition durations (ms):

Execution A:   5.156
Execution B: 182.627
Execution C:   5.778
Execution D: 182.852
Execution E:   5.198
Execution F: 186.227
Execution G:   6.416
Execution H: 180.081

The delay occurs in:

WorkflowExecute.initializeExecution()
  → workflow.expression.acquireIsolate()
    → Expression.vmEvaluator.acquire(this)

Relevant installed implementation files:

n8n-core/dist/execution-engine/workflow-execute.js
n8n-workflow/dist/cjs/expression.js
@n8n/expression-runtime/dist/cjs/evaluator/expression-evaluator.js
@n8n/expression-runtime/dist/cjs/pool/isolate-pool.js

ExpressionEvaluator.acquire() handles PoolExhaustedError by calling await this.createBridge(). IsolatePool.acquire() removes an initialized bridge and initiates asynchronous replenishment.

Additional observations

Localhost reproduction removes external proxy/TLS from the measured path.

Disabling execution-data saving did not eliminate the latency pattern.

The pattern was reproduced using a minimal two-node workflow.

Increasing pool size partially improved results.

Lazy acquisition substantially improved steady-state minimal-webhook latency.

Basic dynamic expressions and real application navigation passed Stage smoke tests.

Pool exhaustion/cold creation is a suspected explanation, not directly proven by pool-state instrumentation.

No equivalent controlled benchmark on n8n 1.x was recorded.

Questions for maintainers

Is the observed eager isolate acquisition expected for workflows containing no dynamic expressions?

Is there a reason N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE_LAZY_ACQUIRE defaults to false?

Is per-execution isolate disposal and asynchronous replacement the intended pool lifecycle?

Are there known trade-offs or compatibility limitations when enabling lazy acquisition for production workflows?

Would upstream instrumentation of pool exhaustion and cold-start durations be useful for diagnosing this behaviour?

We can provide additional redacted timing logs and a minimal workflow export if requested.

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS

### n8n Version

2.43.5

### Node.js Version

v26.7.0

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

source_text:
Simulated stock and cost changes don't update products; repricing can throw
Found during the docs review (#96).

**1. Simulated supplier stock and cost changes never update products.**
- `app:update-supplier-stock` and `app:reset-supplier-stock` call `SupplierProduct::updateStock()` / `updateCost()`. These raise `SupplierProductStockWasChangedEvent`, and only the audit log listens to it (`SupplierStockChangeLogger`).
- So a product's stored stock, cost, active source and price stay as they were until a supplier product is edited in the UI with a changed value.
- Allocation reads supplier stock live, so sourcing works. But:
  - the catalog shows stale stock and prices;
  - a product whose active source has run out keeps showing it;
  - a cheaper source that came back into stock isn't picked up.
- It has been like this since the DDD move (`edcfa149`).

**2. `Product::recalculatePrice()` throws, and nothing catches it.**
- It throws "Cost must be greater than 0." when the cost is 0.00, the default for a product that has never been sourced.
- It throws "Sell price must be greater than cost." when the effective markup is 0 under `DEFAULT`/`NONE`.
- A product edit, or a category or VAT change that reaches such a product, then fails with an exception instead of a message. This was confirmed with the real `MarkupCalculator`, not over HTTP.

### To decide
- Should a stock or cost change reprice the product and recalculate its active source (a Pricing listener on `SupplierProductStockWasChangedEvent`)?
- What should pricing do for a product with no cost or a zero markup: skip, keep the last price, or refuse the change with a message?

### Done when
- Tests cover a stock change that empties the active source, a cost change on the active source, and a category change reaching a zero-cost product.
- `Docs/04-sourcing-and-pricing.md` (Stock, Gotchas) is updated.

Show HN: PanelAlpha Engine – Turn your VPS into a programmable hosting layer
PanelAlpha Engine is an open-source hosting environment for your VPS, programmable through MCP, API and CLI. After ~2 years in the making (we started back in the non-ai era) we've decided to open source our Docker-based Engine. So far, we've used it as a back-end environment for WordPress sites and we have been distributing it through web hosting providers and larger agencies. It's been tested on a few thousand sites already. Now people are vibe coding, using AI for everything and building agentic workflows, while at the same time open source projects are getting through a reinassaince. So, not only we have open-sourced it ourselves, but we've also expanded it to support any web application and tested it against over a thousand repositories (and soon will be much more). You can use it with MCP, API or CLI to:
- deploy projects from files or git
- get a preview URL or use your own domain with automatic SSL
- restrict access with a password
- get built-in monitoring and visitor stats (no need for Google Analytics)
- manage databases, SFTP/FTP, CRON, firewall rules
- read through logs and debug
- create or restore backups (locally or remotely via S3/FTP)
- connect with Cloudflare (for tunnels and DNS)
... and much more (see docs). You install it with one command (you can also define a repo to be installed together with it) and then with another command connect your AI with it. Done. Your agent gets a hosting environment on your server without unrestricted root SSH access. You can even define its permissions. Our early users have asked us about the visual/panel - it will be available soon too (and also open source). Feel free to roast, we're open for feedback!

Production Checklist reopens on every editor reload of a published workflow
### Bug Description

The Production Checklist popover opens by itself every time I reload the editor of an already-published workflow. Closing it with the ✕ doesn't stick: the next reload opens it again. All items on the checklist are already complete, so there's nothing left for it to tell me.

As far as I can read the code, the auto-open is meant to happen once, on a workflow's first activation. `WorkflowProductionChecklist.vue` stores `firstActivatedAt` in the IndexedDB workflow cache and checks it before opening:

```ts
watch(isConfirmedActive, async (isActive, wasActive) => {
	if (isActive && !wasActive) {
		if (!cachedSettings.value?.firstActivatedAt) {
			// ...opens the popover
		}
		await workflowsCache.updateFirstActivatedAt(...);
	}
});

onMounted(async () => {
	await loadWorkflowSettings();
});
```

I think it's a race. On a page load `isConfirmedActive` goes from `false` to `true` as soon as the workflow document arrives, so the watcher fires on every load. At that moment `cachedSettings` can still be `null`: it's only filled by the async `loadWorkflowSettings()` in `onMounted`, and that function does nothing at all if `workflowId` isn't set yet when the component mounts. With `cachedSettings` empty, the `firstActivatedAt` guard passes and the popover opens, even though the flag was written long ago.

The ✕ only flips the local `isPopoverOpen` ref, so it doesn't persist anything either.

One way to fix it would be to read the settings inside the watcher before the check (for example `await loadWorkflowSettings()` or `await workflowsCache.getWorkflowSettings(id)`) instead of relying on the value loaded in `onMounted`.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a trigger (I used a Schedule Trigger) and publish it.
2. Let the Production Checklist open on the first publish, then close it with the ✕.
3. Optionally complete every item (error workflow, time saved).
4. Reload the browser tab with the workflow open.
5. The Production Checklist opens again. It does this on every reload.

### Expected behavior

The checklist opens automatically once, on the workflow's first activation. After that it stays closed on reload and is only opened from the workflow menu ("Production checklist").

### Debug Info

Self-hosted, started with `n8n start` from a global pnpm install, kept alive by pm2. Default SQLite, regular execution mode. Env: `N8N_DISABLED_MODULES=mcp`, `N8N_DIAGNOSTICS_ENABLED=false`, `N8N_PERSONALIZATION_ENABLED=false`. Editor bundle `n8n-editor-ui@2.43.5`. The same watcher logic is on `master` today (`packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/app/components/WorkflowProductionChecklist.vue`).

### Operating System

macOS

### n8n Version

2.43.7

### Node.js Version

24.12.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

Labels I'd pick, if useful for triage: `ui`, `type:bug`.

Write the add-a-repo host steps for the shared dev-container template
## What

Write "Adding a repo to this host", a section in `docs/identity/DEV-CONTAINER.md`, for the shared-template route recorded as WB-D42 (#1163). Split from #1163, 2026-10-26: it describes a container that exists only after the route's migration step 5 (the dev-App image flavour built and the template updated).

The section covers:
- the repo's `.devcontainer/` from the template, its per-repo values set to its own name;
- the order: the repo's approval ruleset is live and read back (its #406 to #410 cutover) **before** it enters `broker.json` or has the dev App installed, since the broker keeps a write token current for every listed repo;
- the reviewer App installed on the repo earlier, before its cutover's PR 1, since `wow-review` posts the review that PR needs (#406 to #410 do this); this section only confirms it;
- after the read-back, the repo in `broker.json` and `review-poll.json`, `install-host-tools.ps1` rerun, the dev and loop Apps installed on it (each App's permissions accepted), and one read-only mint to prove it;
- a second clone with a distinct folder name to use as `-Reference`.
- the container cutover's own precondition: a repo's container cutover starts only after its whole #406 to #410 ruleset cutover is done (PR 1 merged and the gate's check pinned in the checks ruleset, read back with `enforcement: active`), not merely after the approval side is read back. Decided by the maintainer on 2026-10-26, reading `WB-D42` migration step 7's "ruleset cutover".

## Done when

An operator can bring bounty-infra and scope-core into a container acting as the dev App from that section alone, with nothing read from this repo's own files for the procedure.

#1163 (WB-D42), #1164, and the template and image flavour from the route's migration steps 4 and 5 (issues filed when this milestone is planned).

First-sale digital product pilot: cashflow tracker, lower-price ladder, verified delivery
## Owner direction, 31 October 2026
Shift PrismBay commerce from catalog expansion and speculative promotions to **one original digital product capable of producing the first verified paid order**. Reuse the existing GitHub Actions and digital prototype code, not a new swarm or subscription.

## Market evidence, public sources (demand indicators, not audited sales)
- Etsy current Small Business Google Sheets category: a bookkeeping/inventory/pricing bundle listed around $14.92 and specialized bookkeeping sheets commonly ~$1–$15. https://www.etsy.com/market/small_business_google_sheets
- Etsy job-application trackers commonly ~$2–$8; many high-review listings. https://www.etsy.com/market/spreadsheet_job_application_tracker
- Etsy stakeholder Excel templates commonly ~$3–$16. https://www.etsy.com/market/stakeholder_map_templates
- Paid Gumroad templates, 9 October 2026 sample: median $7; P75 $15.75. This is listed pricing, not verified PrismBay conversion. https://ceotudent.com/en/digital-product-price-benchmarks-2026-courses-templates-ebooks
- Stripe public US domestic-card headline rate 2.9% + 30c, with other fees possible: https://stripe.com/pricing

## Prioritization
1. P0: **Small Business Cashflow Studio**, existing `data/global-digital-products-2026.json` prototype, proposed $5.99. Improve from sample CSV into professionally formatted, editable Excel/Google Sheets-compatible cashflow and expense tracker, built-in formulas/validation, 12-month use, instructions, believable clearly fictional worked example, accessible preview, quality tests. Do not claim financial advice or accounting certification.
2. P1 research/review: **Professional Application Tracker**, existing prototype. Proposed test $4.99 only after full functionality, sample data and reviewer approval. No guaranteed employment claim.
3. P1 research/review: **Stakeholder Register Lite** derived from PrismBay-owned content, proposed $7.99, distinct from full existing $49 executive system. Verify non-overlapping deliverables, file quality, owned rights and coherent upsell before release.
4. Physical goods remain research-only pending independently authenticated supplier identity, variant stock, buyer-ZIP landed cost, media permissions, safety and actual fulfillment route. Do not use “active in Stripe” as proof of sellable stock.

## Existing execution components to reuse
- `.github/workflows/digital-product-factory.yml`: current weekly, review-only QA, not auto-publish.
- `.github/workflows/buyer-acquisition.yml`: current buyer guides, checkout/link checks and acquisition review, not proof of traffic or revenue.
- `.github/workflows/prismbay-daily-sales-brief.yml`: current Stripe revenue reporting (restricted credential and private financial outputs).
- `.github/workflows/paperclip-revenue-ops.yml`: existing coordination and artifacts.
- `scripts/revenue-evidence-gates.mjs` and `scripts/daily-revenue-brief.mjs` for genuine paid evidence, not generated metrics.
- Existing digital fulfillment protection issue #498, acquisition issue #214, physical sourcing issue #505.

## Acceptance gates, in order
1. Produce release-quality downloadable product and independently run formula, file-open, negative-input, compatibility, licensing, accessibility, and ZIP integrity tests. Quality check has to be independent of generator.
2. Build an original mobile-friendly product page with readable samples, buyer-focused use cases, exact feature list, refund/support information and transparent limitations. No plagiarized product images, template copying, fake reviews or fake urgency.
3. Solve issue #498: no reusable public package key or unauthenticated download. Verify Stripe-paid-event-to-order-specific authorized delivery, and test expired/forged access denial. Test-mode only until production authorization.
4. Develop cost model: US card base 2.9% + $0.30 and possible additional fees, refunds, support overhead and taxes. $5.99 is a pricing hypothesis, not an authorized live Stripe price.
5. Create a reviewable draft PR with checks and screenshots. No live Stripe mutation, product publication, deployment, outreach, purchased ads, YouTube retail promotion, supplier order or price change without separate owner approval.
6. Once authorized and released, instrument consent-respecting qualified human sessions, product-page CTA clicks, successful checkout starts, Stripe-paid orders, refunds and verified order-specific delivery. Read analytics privately and produce aggregate non-sensitive status. Do not equate GitHub run or synthetic click with sale.
7. Evaluate 14-day organic pilot as an exploratory test; no fabricated performance threshold or statistical significance from low traffic. Iterate product value and traffic before launching more SKUs.

## Operational success condition
One independently confirmed, non-test, non-refunded customer purchase with access to the exact purchased file, then repeat the process with positive unit economics. Keep the existing $49/$79/$99/$179 professional products as advanced offerings until separate evidence supports a change.

Show HN: Cryo – A language whose programs live forever
Cryo is a programming language that models long-running tasks like workflows or AI agents. Programs freeze to disk when idle and can be thawed when new data arrives. As part of our announcement of Endothermic Labs, we've put together a small demo of Cryo that highlights its features and walks through the language and its plugin system. We originally built it as a way to deploy healthcare agents at scale, but have rebuilt it from the ground up to be a standalone toolchain for long-running tasks. It acts as something like a cross between Durable Objects and Temporal workflows, where the script itself is the durable unit with no replay needed. Cryo is statically and structurally typed, with a concurrency model similar to Go. It's still under active development, so we're holding off on open sourcing it until we're confident that the language is stable, ideally in the next 3-4 weeks.

Show HN: QuanterLab, describe a trading strategy, watch it build in front of you
Hi HN, I run Quanterlab which is a quantitative research platform (can as well be described as backtesting tool for trading and investing ideas) and it‘s purpose is to provide interpretable results for users' own rule sets, using point-in-time data. I am coming from mechanical engineering domain and I wanted to reflect the concepts of engineering. For example, the “strategies” or more elaborately put “market inefficiency hypothesis” are constructed as block diagrams. And in its own style, QuanterLab is quite a strange thing for a finance software. Instead of looking at candle sticks, this is to construct a logic with these block diagrams. Each one of the boxes have certain contracts with each other’s and it is all about stopping people to make things that does not make sense. Information leakage is something I care a lot and for that purpose everything constructed is placed automatically on a timeline showing you which piece of the block is using which time window which is intended as a visual safety net. And also, the AI is big part of it, which I am personally happy with my decisions on how it is implemented. AI is allowed to use tools in the platform to construct what you describe and deliver the news to you. So, it is definitely NOT something that AI exploiting information uncontrolled (overfit) and adding creativity with what you did not ask for. Similarly, the platform is available as MCP servers and connectors in many AI platforms, and again these AI models only allowed to use the tools that is exposed to them and they are obliged to present the information with certain cards exposing you the blocks to let you inspect or manually change. Lastly, anything constructed can be set as paper trade and you receive a morning brief after every working day. You can try the lab without an account or you can as well connect it to your AI as connector, 10 runs a day for guests and an account gets 30 days of the Practitioner plan, no card needed. Sorry for my awkward mistakes in the text, especially for native English speakers, this text did not pass through AI. Greetings from Germany, Serhat

source_text:
Show HN: Ret – An inbox and canvas for your Codex and Claude Code agents
Over the last few weeks I've really been using Codex and Claude to solve a lot of parallel tasks, across a lot of different projects. This lead me to wishing that I could interface with my agents in the same way that I interface with my already existing windows and editors. For me, this usually means that I have like 5 to anywhere around 8 different windows that I drag around depending on where I want to focus, this could mean I am focusing on the terminal now, or I want to test stuff in a simulator or browser; but when I go to interface with agents, I have to manage many tabs, or I have to look through a list in their native apps. This is not convenient for me, and I'm almost certain this is not convenient for many of you. That's why I built an infinite canvas, where my traditional desktop style workflow can come to life alongside my agents, I can drag them around depending on where I want my focus to be, or I can let them just pile up, like the 15 finder windows you're hiding with your browser right now. But, when I do want to go back to that thread, I will intuitively just know right where it is. I didn't stop there though, I really enjoyed the inbox style agent interface that Google shipped many months ago with Anti Gravity, but I didn't really enjoy much other than that, so, I built that in too. But, I still didn't stop there, a traditional code editor still comes in handy every once and awhile, just to read, or to tradcode, though Ret doesn't feature a VS-Code fork, yet anyways, maybe one day something similar could exist, it does feature a fairly comparable implementation, powered by the same technology, in a similar layout, just without the plugins and bloat. But, I didn't stop there either, the traditional sidebar and one centered chat is a nice experience sometimes, so I built that in too. I guess you probably can see where this is going, but that's also not where I stopped. Working on a single focused thread can be beneficial, but I am a heavy fork user, so I made it convenient to work side by side your main thread and a fork, with ambitions to expand on this in the future as I feel out how many forks or side chats are worth working on at the same time in the 'focused' view. But focus view doesn't stop there, instead of having only one chat in focus, and having to then jump back to the sidebar, I thought, well hey, browser tabs are great, so I built those in too. I know it sounds like there's a lot of things built in  here, and there is, but trust me, it doesn't feel bloated at all, it feels amazing. I really think this is something that greatly benefits my productivity, and I hope that some of you also feel my excitement when trying it out.

## Goal
Populate correctly matched, rights-cleared, real packaging photos for **all 45** current master catalogue entries, starting with the **22 configured products**. Do not mark completed until every currently stocked drink displays its actual package photo during sale selection.

## Prerequisite
Merge and deploy PR #51 (including its SQL migration) safely. CI is green on its current tip, but production migration/deployment and an authenticated upload smoke test are still outstanding.

- All 22 configured products and remaining 23 catalogue items covered, with zero missing images; ensure stocked subset appears correctly in Record Sale, Stock and Drinks.
- Mobile: clear recognizable thumbnail, readable name/size, safe no-image placeholder, graceful bad-file recovery.
- Reconcile coverage after upload in production before closing issue.

## Safety
Public-read only for nonsensitive product packaging. Upload and delete owner-only; 1 MB JPEG/PNG/WebP bucket limit. Do not change stock, prices, crate obligations, or customer data.

> Not sure what to tell you. It's been a problem for decades and only gets worse It's been a problem for literally millennia. This hardly unique to 21
> Not sure what to tell you. It's been a problem for decades and only gets worse It's been a problem for literally millennia. This hardly unique to 21st century america. Yes, I'm glad you don't have a "problem child". That's genuinely great, I wish everyone was that lucky. What I would  like , in the smallest possible way, is some shred of empathy for people who aren't as lucky as you are. Perhaps you could practice the concept of "walking a mile in another man's shoes" and make an attempt to understand what they're dealing with instead of dismissing them as inferior. I'm also happy your wife is volunteering to help with girl scouts. I think that's a great thing and more people should do it. But that doesn't excuse your lack of empathy. Kids are not some kind of deterministic automatons where the same input always produces the same output (as if we could even reproduce the same inputs for an entire life). They're more complicated than that for reasons we frankly can't even understand. There are a number of things that are highly correlated with producing a "good child", a major one being having enough money that the family isn't under constant stress and you can afford second (or third or fourth) chances. But callously discarding every child who isn't lucky enough to benefit from this is just wrong. We, as a society, a culture, should be better than that. Am I expecting you, personally, to go out and change the world? No, no more than I'm expecting myself to do it. But we all make small decisions every day and if enough of us make the "right ones" they can add up, and it starts with empathy for our fellow man.

source_text:
[Bounty #743] Validate /api/proposals payload before persistence
## Problem

POST /api/proposals forwards `req.body` directly to `createProposal` without schema or bounds validation. Any arbitrary JSON object is accepted into the in-memory proposals store, including negative or zero bid amounts, missing cover letters, missing jobId associations, and arbitrary injected fields. Furthermore, unhandled validation errors or malformed payloads can corrupt proposal records and lead to unexpected runtime failures.

## Requested fix

1. Implement a strict Zod validation schema (`createProposalSchema`) in `apps/api/src/validators/proposal.js` enforcing:
   - `jobId`: required string with bounds (1 to 128 characters).
   - `coverLetter`: required string with bounds (min 10 characters, max 5000 characters).
   - `bidAmount`: positive finite number (strictly greater than 0).
   - `estimatedDuration`: optional string with maximum 100 characters.
   - `freelancerId`: optional string with maximum 128 characters.
   - Rejection of unrecognized/arbitrary keys (`.strict()`).
2. Update `apps/api/src/controllers/proposalController.js` (`postProposal`) to parse and validate `req.body` with `createProposalSchema`, returning structured HTTP 400 Bad Request error if validation fails.
3. Add a comprehensive automated test suite (`apps/api/src/tests/proposal.test.js`) using Node's native test runner (`node:test`, `node:assert/strict`) covering:
   - Valid proposal submission (returns 201 with generated proposal id).
   - Rejection of missing jobId (400).
   - Rejection of missing or too short cover letter (400).
   - Rejection of negative or zero bid amount (400).
   - Rejection of unknown extraneous properties (400).

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

This issue is created under the Low Handing Fruit Automation bounty. I will submit a PR that references this issue and issue #743.
