source_text:
Discovery: open contributor database and opt-in PR blocking rule
## Requested outcome

Create a Tripwire-owned open database of listed contributor accounts, with manual curation, and an opt-in workflow rule that blocks a pull request when its author has an active entry. This issue tracks discovery and a reviewable implementation proposal; it does not enable the database or enforcement today.

## References

- [Fossier](https://github.com/PThorpe92/fossier): trust tiers, registry integration, maintainer decisions and decision history.
- [UnsafeLabs/Bounty-Hunters](https://github.com/UnsafeLabs/Bounty-Hunters).
- [Clankers leaderboard](https://clankers-leaderboard.pages.dev/).

Study source, licenses and demonstrated behavior before borrowing mechanics. Treat the database and Tripwire rule as separate capabilities.

## Discovery deliverables

- [ ] Compare evidence collection, account identity, public distribution, corrections and automation interfaces in the references; distinguish demonstrated behavior from claims.
- [ ] Define identity as forge plus immutable account ID, with handles as display metadata; cover rename/deletion without inferred cross-forge identity.
- [ ] Specify manual add/remove, review states, evidence/provenance, reasons, timestamps, expiry/reversal and appeal/correction. Define listing criteria; leaderboard appearance or AI usage alone must not silently become the policy.
- [ ] Propose public format/API or versioned snapshot, license, update/caching model, integrity and unavailable-source behavior. Decide whether outsiders may report and who publishes active entries.
- [ ] Design a versioned, opt-in rule through existing rules/workflows/actions. Distinguish active match, no match and unavailable evidence; record matched entry and database version in each run. Keep lookup I/O in the worker and core evaluation pure.
- [ ] Decide whether block means merge-blocking check, configured close action, or both; preserve explicit workflow configuration, exemptions and overrides. An outage must not become a fabricated account match.
- [ ] Produce the smallest scoped implementation plan, schemas, regression/rollout criteria and open decisions. No new packages/apps/dependencies or production activation during discovery.

## Done when

A cited discovery note and scoped proposal explain the data lifecycle, public distribution and match-to-enforcement path, with explicit admission/removal policy and recovery behavior. No real accounts are imported or listed during discovery.

Background discovery is underway. GitCafe protection remains a separate active implementation priority.

## Initial discovery findings — 2026-10-28

- **Bounty-Hunters is a PR-opener tracker, not a reviewed misconduct feed.** Its [tracking workflow](https://github.com/UnsafeLabs/Bounty-Hunters/blob/a82477dc7d98a1812fb0c59c0b4f09e8d562a1e8/.github/workflows/track-clankers.yml) automatically adds/increments every PR author's username. There is no bot or misconduct adjudication in that path. Its [sync workflow](https://github.com/UnsafeLabs/Bounty-Hunters/blob/a82477dc7d98a1812fb0c59c0b4f09e8d562a1e8/.github/workflows/sync-clankers.yml) combines aggregate counts by username without incident-level provenance. Borrow inspectable, machine-readable publication; do not automatically import those people into an enforcement list.
- **Fossier demonstrates useful registry consumption and withdrawal mechanics.** Its [registry client](https://github.com/PThorpe92/fossier/blob/d2ef6eacab5f50cb799703da21e50c860f2fc739/src/fossier/registry_client.py) checks/reports by username and supports withdrawing a repository's report. Server moderation, independence of reports, appeals, retention and data licensing remain unverified. [Configuration](https://github.com/PThorpe92/fossier/blob/d2ef6eacab5f50cb799703da21e50c860f2fc739/src/fossier/config.py) makes registry checking/reporting opt-in. Do not copy mutable-handle identity or infer that a report count establishes a verified incident.
- **Smallest proposed implementation:** one owner-curated, explicitly licensed, versioned snapshot and one optional versioned pure rule. Worker fetches/validates; core matches the normalized PR author's forge-qualified immutable account ID. Reuse existing workflows, run evidence, exemptions, human review and forge actions. No new service, federation, public reporting flow, auto-import, classifier or global activation is implied.
- **Three separate outcomes:** active eligible match fails the requirement; complete fresh snapshot with no match passes; missing/stale/invalid/incomplete source skips with a bounded reason. Persist snapshot/case revision in evaluated evidence. Existing degraded-floor policy may hold a skipped evaluation for human review; unavailable is neither a match nor a clean result.
- **Block differs from Close:** merge-blocking checks/reviews leave the PR open; closing requires explicit workflow configuration. Neither prevents a user from opening another PR. Effective merge enforcement requires the repository's branch protections.
- **Open decisions:** listing criteria and terminology; manual admission authority; evidence visibility and license; correction/appeal/reversal/expiry; snapshot publication home and freshness; precedence with local exemptions; reevaluation after removal. No real accounts were imported, reports submitted or enforcement enabled during discovery.

Source inspection is not a live registry or accuracy evaluation. The public leaderboard was inspected without authentication; prompt datasets and private/user environment information were not collected.

source_text: Intermittent `fetch failed` errors in Google Gemini Chat Model with AI Agent, while OpenAI-compatible Gemini endpoint works ### Bug Description The Google Gemini Chat Model node intermittently fails when connected to an AI Agent, returning the following error after approximately 3 minutes: ``` [GoogleGenerativeAI Error]: Error fetching from https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3.1-flash-lite:generateContent: fetch failed Unknown error ``` The issue occurs repeatedly throughout the day. During affected periods, every workflow using an AI Agent connected to Google Gemini Chat Model fails, including newly created test workflows. Interestingly, other methods of accessing the same Gemini API continue working normally during these failures: - **Google Gemini "Message a Model" node:** Works correctly. - **Direct HTTP requests from inside the n8n Docker container:** Work correctly, although sometimes with slightly higher latency. - **AI Agent + OpenAI Chat Model configured with Google's OpenAI-compatible Gemini endpoint:** Works correctly, even while the same AI Agent fails using Google Gemini Chat Model. - **AI Agent with OpenRouter using other models:** Works correctly. The most significant finding is that switching only the model node from Google Gemini Chat Model to OpenAI Chat Model, configured to use Google's Gemini API directly, immediately restores functionality without changing the AI Agent itself. The problem persists after updating n8n to the latest available version. This strongly suggests an issue specific to the Google Gemini Chat Model integration, its underlying SDK, or its HTTP connection handling, rather than a general Gemini API outage or network connectivity problem. Related issue: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/issues/21801 The following screenshot was taken before updating n8n, confirming that the issue occurs across different n8n versions and is not specific to the latest release. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a new workflow in a self-hosted n8n instance running in Docker. 2. Add a Manual Trigger and an AI Agent node. 3. Connect a Google Gemini Chat Model node to the AI Agent. 4. Configure the model as `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` (it happens with other models as well) using a valid Google Gemini API key. 5. Execute the workflow several times throughout the day. 6. During an affected period, the AI Agent fails after approximately 180 seconds with `GoogleGenerativeAI Error: fetch failed`. 7. Create another test workflow using Google Gemini's native "Message a Model" node. Observe that requests succeed. 8. Test the Gemini API directly from inside the n8n Docker container using Node.js `fetch()`. Observe that requests succeed. 9. Replace the Google Gemini Chat Model connected to the same AI Agent with an OpenAI Chat Model configured as follows: - Base URL: `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/` - API Key: The same Google Gemini API key - Model: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` 10. Execute the AI Agent again during the same affected period. The request succeeds. **Note:** The issue is intermittent and cannot be reproduced consistently on demand. However, once an affected period begins, all tested workflows using Google Gemini Chat Model with AI Agent fail, while the alternative integrations continue working. ### Expected behavior The Google Gemini Chat Model should successfully process requests through the AI Agent without intermittent connection failures, especially when the same Gemini API is accessible and functioning normally through other n8n nodes and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. If a temporary network or API error occurs, the integration should handle it appropriately and provide a meaningful underlying error instead of hanging for approximately 180 seconds before returning a generic `fetch failed` message. The Google Gemini Chat Model should provide connection reliability comparable to the OpenAI Chat Model configured to access the same Gemini API. ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.43.8 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 26.7.0 - nodeEnv: production - database: postgres - executionMode: regular - concurrency: -1 - license: enterprise (production) - consumerId: c61a07ff-fd9d-4365-85de-6bbfad9dd7db ## storage - success: all - error: all - progress: false - manual: true - binaryMode: memory ## pruning - enabled: true - maxAge: 100 hours - maxCount: 10000 executions ## client - userAgent: mozilla/5.0 (windows nt 10.0; win64; x64) applewebkit/537.36 (khtml, like gecko) chrome/155.0.0.0 safari/537.36 - isTouchDevice: false ## cluster - instanceCount: 1 - versions: 2.43.8 - instances: - instanceKey: 5ec4f651-6a85-4eb3-99f1-efe2d1eba1ee, hostId: main-7af0076e47ec, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.43.8 - checks: - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: - Generated at: 2026-10-20T19:36:17.313Z ### Operating System Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS ### n8n Version 2.43.8 ### Node.js Version 26.7.0 ### Database PostgreSQL ### Execution mode main (default) ### Hosting n8n cloud

## Paradigm shift

source_text:
TWO-WHEELER-ENG-001: co-design bicycle, e-bike, motorcycle and microfactory benchmarks
## Mission

Create an evidence-bounded, two-wheeler engineering benchmark that jointly evaluates bicycle/e-bike/motorcycle design and the production/service systems that make those vehicles affordable and maintainable.

This is a specialization of existing owners, not a competing vehicle solver or factory scheduler.

## Paradigm shift

Optimize for **verified mobility delivered over the vehicle's service life**, not one headline specification such as mass, top speed, range or initial price. Co-design the product, production cell, service tasks, parts network and end-of-life path. Preserve a Pareto frontier rather than hiding incompatible goals in one weighted score.

## Reuse existing owners

- Transport architecture: #6244
- Road/off-road tire/contact, braking, handling and qualification semantics: #6247
- Vehicle/logistics hardware manufacturing qualification: #5985
- Low-consequence physical qualification ladder: #6254
- Factory scheduler and manufacturing-value work: #7677 / PR #7678; #7608
- Repairability-first personal/family transport research: PR #7751
- Symtropy mobility simulation/whole-life optimization: PR #1762 and issues #1601, #1773, #1780
- Mycelix vehicle dossier and maintenance-event evidence: PR #5131 / issue #5132

Do not duplicate road dynamics, physics, battery/electric-machine models, material science, scheduling, lifecycle optimization, service history or authority semantics. Add two-wheeler-specific profiles only where existing contracts demonstrably lack them.

## Work packages

1. **Start with a conventional utility/commuter bicycle** as the low-energy anchor; define the user/duty-cycle envelope, freeze comparable baselines and document exclusions. A cargo-bike profile must not silently inherit a general bicycle standard's applicability.
2. Add a cargo/utility bicycle profile, then an electrically assisted bicycle profile with its electrical safety and jurisdiction-specific classification kept separate from mechanical qualification.
3. Only after the contract is stable, add a bounded commuter/utility motorcycle profile with motorcycle-specific braking, vehicle dynamics, E/E functional-safety, type-approval and physical test gates.
4. Co-design product and manufacturing cell: fabrication route, fixture access, tolerances, inspection, assembly, first-pass yield, material utilization, worker/tool capability, serviceability and parts resilience.
5. Compare volumes of 1, 10, 25, 100 and 1,000 units; keep quoted prices, catalog prices, modeled costs and observed production costs distinct.
6. Emit reproducible, digest-bound scenarios and adversarial controls that make missing evidence, changed configuration, incompatible units, invalid model scope, unavailable tools/parts and safety-gate regressions fail closed.

## Proposed scorecard (research targets, not achieved results or standards)

- **Evidence integrity:** zero false accepts across the frozen negative-control suite; all output claims identify configuration, model revision, input digest, evidence class, uncertainty and applicability.
- **Product trade space:** report a Pareto frontier for mass, durability, useful payload, energy/fuel, comfort/fit, repair time, downtime, lifecycle cost and environmental burden. Safety/legal constraints are hard gates.
- **Model validation:** report errors by observable and operating envelope against held-out physical data; target <=10% error only for specifically defined observables after adequate independent data exist. No aggregate accuracy claim.
- **Repairability:** freeze at least 10 common tasks; measure diagnosis, hands-on work, verification, rework, tools, parts lead time and vehicle downtime separately; target >=25% reduction in median and P90 task time against a matched baseline, subject to safety-equivalent procedures.
- **Microfactory economics:** report yield-adjusted cost per conforming unit and sensitivity to labor, scrap, rework, supplier delay, equipment amortization and volume. A candidate target is >=30% lower assembly touch labor at 25+ units with no reduction in acceptance quality; validate with observed runs before claiming savings.
- **Lifecycle and locality:** compare whole-life cost per 1,000 completed km and service continuity under parts/fuel/electricity/cash-flow shocks. Keep local sourcing percentage separate from actual renewable productive closure.
- **Robustness:** test wet/low-friction surface, payload and CG shifts, fatigue and brake thermal degradation, worn/changed tire generations, calibration/configuration changes, missing or contradictory telemetry, and supplier/tool outages.

Tune numerical targets after baseline measurements are frozen. Report failed cases, uncertainty and missing data; never convert unmeasured values to zero.

## Evidence and safety boundaries

- Synthetic schema/optimizer pass != validated dynamics.
- Simulation pass != component durability or physical vehicle qualification.
- One prototype test != fleet reliability or manufacturing capability.
- Local assembly != local productive closure.
- Procedure authored != repair performed and independently checked.
- A benchmark result != roadworthiness, type approval or permission to operate.

Applicable references include ISO 4210-2/-6 for in-scope bicycle types, ISO 8710 for motorcycle brake test methods, ISO 26262-12 for motorcycle E/E functional-safety development (a new DIS is under enquiry as of 2026-10-18), UL 2849 for e-bike electrical systems where applicable, and ISO 14040 for lifecycle-assessment framework. Applicability and current local rules must be rechecked for the exact vehicle class and target market.

## Acceptance criteria

- Publish an owner map and non-duplication audit.
- Freeze at least one bicycle baseline protocol and explicit scenario manifest.
- Define scenario/result schemas with synthetic, simulated, workshop-measured, field-observed and regulatory evidence classes kept distinct.
- Include positive controls and seeded negative controls for configuration, unit, evidence, safety gate and economic-accounting errors.
- Define a staged qualification ladder from static checks through simulation, component/bench work, controlled track testing and independent legal/physical approval.
- Document benchmark commands/replay procedure or, if implementation is a later slice, explicitly label the current artefact documentation-only.
- State exact limitations and do not claim unexecuted build/test/CI results.

## Current scope ceiling

Planning and benchmark contracts only. No vehicle design is declared safe, optimized, affordable, manufacturable, roadworthy or certified by this issue.

source_text:
Map: cut sheets and filled fields for every team-added part
> Copied from [brauneric/SWE_Library#52](https://github.com/brauneric/SWE_Library/issues/52) · original author `brauneric` · opened 2026-10-21

## Destination

Every **team-added part** in the SWE library (12,775 as of the 2026-10-21 shared export; the 3 sample parts the team edited included, the other 420 sample parts excluded) has a decided path, in run order, to: a **cut sheet** in `\mfp-hud-sw\data\Datasheets\_CutsheetDetails` linked as its SWE datasheet (catalog link moved to userData10), and its fields filled to the verified-part standard (`audit/Checks.cs`). The order is a runbook of change sets that can be proven one at a time on TSUMMERS-LAP-21 (dry run → local write → audit diff), then handed to Eric for the shared server.

## Notes

- Domain: SWE shared library. Vocabulary in `GLOSSARY.md` (catalog, cut sheet, team-added part, verified datasheet). Standard and triage come from the closed map [SWE library audit and verified-part standard](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/1); its rules hold here unless a ticket amends them.
- Machine rules and EwAPI know-how: `docs/handoff-TSUMMERS-LAP-21.md` and `docs/agents/swe-api.md`. Planning map: tickets decide, they don't run change sets (task tickets only where a decision waits on the work).
- **Pipeline per part:** catalog in the MFP All Staff Library → catalog and product family filed in the knowledge base (`knowledge-capture/knowledge/library/<maker>/`) → cut sheet made by the knowledge-capture `cutsheet` engine → link in SWE → fill fields from the cut sheet.
- **MFP-made parts** (MB/MA/DA/E/EP/C/RES/…): the "catalog" is the released drawing in Control Docs (read only), per rule #10 of the audit map. The All Staff Library is for supplier catalogs.
- **Catalogs not in the Library** go on the catalogs-to-get list. A candidate found on `\Mfp-hud-sw\Data\Datasheets` is only a suggestion: a person confirms it before it's filed. Nothing is copied into the Library automatically.
- **Writes:** SWE database writes only on the laptop's local Collaborative Server; the shared server stays on hold, and nothing is read or checked against it in this effort (Eric, 2026-10-21). New cut sheet files may be added to `_CutsheetDetails` from any machine, never overwriting or deleting. The Library and Control Docs are read only.
- **Order (decided while charting):** pre-link cleanup from the audit map first (manufacturer aliases → re-source supplier parts filed under MFP → class tree → retire/move duplicates), so no cut sheet is made for a part about to go; then link the 417 existing cut sheets → make and link the 404 the engine can make now → fix the 110 that don't parse → build Parker/Sun families (3,744) → new engines manufacturer by manufacturer, largest first.
- **Part of a larger destination (2026-11-04 meeting):** this map's runbook is stages 1–2 (datasheet, user fields) of the four-stage clean library charted in [Map: four-stage clean library on TSUMMERS-LAP-21](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/67). A part finishing this runbook is not yet a clean-library part; symbol and 3D stages, the hold/clean split and the stage tracker belong to #67.
- **Catalogs on demand (Eric, 2026-11-04):** a catalog in the Library `_Inbox` is harvested only when a part in the change set being worked needs a cut sheet and has no filed catalog; nothing is harvested ahead of need. Details: [How is a catalog harvested only when a part being worked needs it?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/78).
- **Approval (Eric, 2026-11-04):** agents run and check each change set; Eric approves what is accepted as good (see #67).
- Skills: `grilling` + `domain-modeling` for grilling tickets; `research` for research tickets.

## Decisions so far

- [Which MFP-made parts have a released drawing in Control Docs?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/55): 1,721 MFP-manufacturer parts; 1,497 carry an MFP number, of which 812 have an exact-variant release, 284 a bare-number or sibling release, 398 none (349 no folder, 49 empty); 1,064 have a PDF in the newest release; 224 un-numbered, 161 of them supplier parts filed under MFP (re-source).
- [Where do SWE's user-data label files live?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/59): in XML files on the shared working folder, not the database; one file labels every manufacturer part, each class names its own component file; EwAPI can't change label text, so re-labelling is a share write the laptop can't test alone.
- [Which team-added parts have no catalog in the All Staff Library?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/53): of 11,035 supplier parts (408 makers, 3,381 series), 2,985 have a series the Library/KB names, 4,501 sit with a Library maker but an unnamed series (Daman, Magnaloy, LDI, DMIC… lack KB codes), and 3,549 from 389 makers need a catalog got (1,438 of them with a Datasheets candidate); table in `out/catalogs-to-get/`.
- [Which candidate catalogs are confirmed for the Library?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/54): confirmation tabled by Eric; instead a per-maker list of catalogs to gather or check (`docs/catalogs-to-gather.csv`: 389 makers / 3,549 parts to get, 18 makers / 4,501 parts to check Library coverage), Datasheets PDFs kept as unconfirmed hints.
- [How does the laptop's local server get a current copy of the shared library?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/56): the copy Jake already made is the one we edit (separate from shared, current to 2026-10-19 17:10, method not recorded); no fresh copy now.
- [Does a library part's update() persist on the local server?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/57): yes: `setX` + `update()` survives a session restart and `""` clears a field; every write restamps `modifiedBy`/`modified` (no setter back), so the audit diff must expect it; the check against the shared server was dropped, as this work is localhost only.
- [How are retired parts retired?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/58): only duplicates and invalid P/Ns are retired, kept not deleted: moved to root class `99_RETIRED` with a fixed `RETIRED: …; USE …; WAS …` note in userData6; discouraged parts stay live with a `DISCOURAGED: USE …` note; misfiles just move class; alias-only duplicates retire during the alias step; a person confirms a review CSV first.
- [What does a cut sheet for an MFP-made part look like?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/60): the released drawing PDF copied whole (outline then schematic for assemblies) with one blue source note; named `<SWE reference>.pdf`, release pinned in the note and metadata; no-PDF releases held for Engineering; made by an `mfp` mode in the knowledge-capture cut sheet tool, exact-variant matches only.
- [Where does an MFP part with no exact release get its cut sheet?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/61): only from a release whose drawing itself names the exact variant (title block, finish set, or stated variant rule; tiering re-run with a title-block read); everything else, including no/empty folders, E/RES/EP child parts and other-finish-only MB blocks, is held on one list for Engineering (`docs/mfp-drawings-to-release.csv`) with cross-prefix and Engineering Files paths as hints only; the 224 un-numbered parts moved to their own ticket.
- [How do the user-data label files get changed on the share?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/62): as the last runbook step; the manufacturer-part file shows only slots 0–6 today (torque on 891 parts is invisible), so it is rewritten to slots 0–10 in order, all visible and editable, with labels from the audit's slot breakdown (slot 10 `CATALOG LINK`); tested first by repointing the laptop's own `UserDataDescription` path at a local copy, then copied over the share's file with a dated backup.
- [How is the writer that links cut sheets and fills fields shaped?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/63): one generic C# writer in `writer/` applying §6.2 change-set CSVs (fixed field list, `class` by path, one all-or-nothing `update()` per part, `--undo` from the write log); it also creates the bare `99_RETIRED` class via an `add-class` row (first run proves `newEwClass`); the audit diff ignores the stamp but requires stamped parts = write-log parts.
- [Where do MFP-filed parts with no MFP number get their cut sheet?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/64): supplier parts filed under MFP are re-sourced via a confirmed review CSV and join the supplier pipeline (before the duplicate step); catalog manifolds (VPOM, FPOM, …) were later ruled out of scope; LEGACY drawings count as releases; RapidMod PMAs and other unnumbered MFP designs, and custom-fab job parts, go on the Engineering hold list; `DUMMY`/`MOTOR` retire; the two typo references are corrected.
- [Which SWE parts does the Manifold Solutions catalog cover, and from which pages?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/65): 8 MFP-filed parts decode exactly (VPOM 049Y/4289/4544, FPOM 1165, HEB 1521, RCM 2815, TSM 1064, PTU 1892), each from one ordering page + one dimension page; TLSM-6036 (3) is outside the catalog; SQDIN/LFG accessories stay with re-sourcing; the KB says MFP uses MA numbers, not these codes, and the bodies were re-released after 2016, so those parts were ruled out of scope (see Out of scope).
- [How is a catalog harvested only when a part being worked needs it?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/78): per change set, its parts are matched to the Library `_Inbox` (catalog-finder manifest; maker + series found in the PDF text) and Eric approves one harvest plan; a matching catalog is harvested even when an older one is filed, and series built from an older print are re-checked and their cut sheets remade (old sheets copied to `_CutsheetDetails\_superseded\<date>\` first: an approved exception to the no-overwrite rule); missing engine families are built automatically; all 436 Sun inbox datasheets are harvested into the KB's Sun collection, families built for every SWE-used Sun series, and the Sun engine reads Library copies first; matching is a read-only `audit/catalog_match.py`.

## Not yet specified

- Gathering, confirming and filing the missing catalogs into the knowledge base: tabled 2026-10-21; Eric does it later (by hand or with another agent) from `docs/catalogs-to-gather.csv`. Includes who Fluidyne/CRS really are (reseller vs maker) and the engine-order tie-break.
- For each new engine: which catalog sections and code tables it needs; graduates manufacturer by manufacturer as their catalogs are confirmed.
- Commodity parts sold under a supplier number (Digi-Key): whether the supplier's product page is the catalog and how it's archived.
- Whether and how the laptop's library copy is refreshed from the shared server while the runbook is worked (Unarchive with the working folder moved off `\mfp-hud-sw`, or a SQL restore by a DBA), and how often.
- The long tail of catalogs to get: 275 makers with under 5 parts each (450 parts), and whether each earns a filed catalog or a lighter path.
- How a proven change set reaches the shared server: the same writer with an override only Eric passes, SWE's own import, or another route; open while the shared server is on hold (from [How is the writer that links cut sheets and fills fields shaped?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/63)).
- **Run order vs usage (2026-11-04 meeting):** the meeting wants hands-on work ordered by product family and use on released jobs (hydraulic valves, motors, pumps; Parker and Sun valves first), excluding master parts. Decide whether that re-orders this runbook after the pre-link cleanup or only the hands-on track in #67; the usage source and window are [Which released-job data shows how often a part is used, and over what window?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/72).
- **High-confidence automation only (2026-11-04 meeting):** catalog-backed updates are automated and anything unresolved goes on a review list. Check that each change set writes only what its cut sheet decodes exactly, and that its leftovers land on one list per change set.

## Out of scope

- The 420 SWE sample parts the team never edited.
- Verifying parts: a named person confirms datasheet, symbol and values after this map's runbook runs; an agent never marks a part verified.
- Retired parts (`99_RETIRED`): kept only as records, so no cut sheet or field fill; see [How are retired parts retired?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/58).
- Component label files (`HP_Z_…` and the other per-class files, incl. the class pointing at a missing file): they label components in projects, not library parts; see [How do the user-data label files get changed on the share?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/62).
- Deliberate placeholders `MB-PLACEHOLDER` and `RESERVOIR-CSM`: kept as-is, no cut sheet or field fill; see [Where do MFP-filed parts with no MFP number get their cut sheet?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/64).
- Catalog manifolds (the 8 *Manifold Solutions* parts, VPOM 049Y, TLSM-6036): they take their cut sheet from their MA release, but renumbering them and finding their source is left out of this map (Eric); see [Do the catalog manifolds take their cut sheet from the catalog or from their MA release?](https://github.com/ebraunMFP/SWE_Library_Update/issues/66).
- McMaster-Carr parts (402 team-added parts filed under any McMaster spelling, 2026-10-15 audit): only the manufacturer alias step applies, merging `MCMASTER`, `McMASTER-CARR` and `McMASTER` into `MCMASTER-CARR` and retiring the 2 alias-only duplicates it creates (4830K173, 46635K66). Otherwise no re-sourcing, class move, cut sheet or field fill (Eric, 2026-11-03).

P0: Complete and prove the TRACER supply-to-sale-to-tracking pipeline
## Objective
Finish the TRACER supply-to-sale-to-fulfillment pipeline with evidence-backed end-to-end verification. A passing build or configured status alone is not completion.

## Workstreams and acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Bright Data MCP collection** — merge and deploy the end-to-end ingest fix; run the authenticated production smoke and verify provider=`brightdata_mcp`, accepted candidates (1–30), and at least one persisted observation. Do not count fallback providers as MCP success.
  - Related PR: #806 (currently open; mergeability/conflict must be resolved).
- [ ] **Child variants persisted** — run the deployed collection and verify child variant rows are actually present in `marketplace_bestseller_variants`, with explicit parent-child evidence and dimensions; record attempted/fetched/persisted/error counts. A zero-row table means this is not done.
  - Related PR: #806.
- [ ] **Supplier matching and landed economics** — verify exact supplier product + child variant/SKU, fresh stock, source currency, cost, confirmed Japan shipping, orderability, tracking capability and positive contribution profit. Marketplace demand evidence must never be treated as supplier proof. Amazon/Rakuten are not supplier sources; Yahoo Shopping is demand research only.
  - Related PR: #808 (currently open; Vercel check pending).
- [ ] **TRACER ↔ BASE ↔ Shopify reconciliation** — take complete paginated snapshots and reconcile stable product/listing IDs, product/variant IDs, SKU, price/currency, stock, published/hidden state and sync acknowledgements. Report matched/unmatched/conflicting/incomplete counts; never infer a match from title/image/price. Resolve BASE stable `TRC-<listing UUID>` recovery and Shopify pagination completeness.
  - Related PRs: #756 and #742 (both currently Draft/non-mergeable; resolve base conflicts before review).
- [ ] **Order → supplier purchase → tracking lifecycle** — first prove a sandbox/no-charge supplier order with fresh evidence and idempotency; then verify supplier acknowledgement/order ID, status transitions and tracking number persist back to TRACER and channel fulfillment. Confirm required Shopify fulfillment scopes. Do not enable paid live auto-ordering before this passes.
  - Related work: #723 sandbox quota window; existing order/procurement safety PRs.
- [ ] **Sales/profit feedback loop** — persist per-product sales, returns/refunds, landed cost, shipping, fees and contribution profit; rank by actual net profit and demand, suppress stale/out-of-stock/negative-margin products, and run a bounded repeatable evaluation report.

## Execution order
1. Resolve conflicts and get CI/Preview green on #806, then deploy and run its production MCP smoke.
2. Verify child-variant rows exist in production; fix persistence/schema issues if they do not.
3. Refresh CJ supplier evidence and persist child SKU/freight only after successful live reads (#808).
4. Run read-only, complete three-site reconciliation and fix exact-ID mappings.
5. Run the guarded sandbox lifecycle proof; verify tracking and channel fulfilment.
6. Start the sales/profit feedback loop only from reconciled, trustworthy order/cost data.

## Safety and reporting
- Do not relax identity, stock, shipping, currency, image, Japanese-copy or positive-profit gates merely to raise listing counts.
- Do not bulk-publish, bulk-unpublish/delete, make a paid supplier purchase, or claim auto-ordering works without the relevant explicit approval and observed evidence.
- Report deployed commit, workflow/run links, counts, and failures for each step. Keep code/CI status separate from production/provider readiness.

## Power & Datacenter Infrastructure (6)

🔴 **[10-19 22:00 Beijing] CNBC: The Race To Power AI Is Reshaping America's Electric Grid**  
AI data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and putting renewed pressure on America's power grid to modernize its equipment and develop greener, more efficient sources of power. Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon are all spending millions of dollars on local infrastructure upgrades and companies like SpaceX are even building off-grid power plants to power their data centers.  
  
Google's planned 780-megawatt data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, could offer a model for powering the AI boom. In a proposed agreement with Xcel Energy, Google will support 1,900 megawatts of new wind, solar and battery capacity, while minimum payments and exit fees are intended to protect local ratepayers if demand falls short. The video examines whether such projects can make the grid cleaner without shifting costs to existing customers, why some energy experts argue that smaller data centers could make better use of existing infrastructure, and how utilities' financial incentives can complicate efforts to build less.  
_Video · YouTube · Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, SpaceX, Xcel Energy · [Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wh1zlJXKy1M)_

source_text:
Aggregate silently overwrites values when nested fields have the same final name
### What happened?

When I aggregate `customer.name` and `supplier.name` without renaming the output fields, both become `name`. The second field overwrites the first field's values, and the workflow finishes successfully without a warning.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pass these two items into an Aggregate node:

```json
[
  {"customer": {"name": "Alice"}, "supplier": {"name": "Acme"}},
  {"customer": {"name": "Bob"}, "supplier": {"name": "Beta"}}
]
```

2. Select **Individual Fields** and add `customer.name` and `supplier.name`.
3. Leave **Rename Field** off for both fields and keep dot notation enabled.
4. Execute the workflow.

The output is:

```json
[{"name": ["Acme", "Beta"]}]
```

The customer names are lost.

### Expected behavior

The node should report the duplicate output name instead of silently overwriting values. It already raises an error if I explicitly rename both fields to `names`: `The 'names' output field is used more than once`.

Renaming the fields to `customer_names` and `supplier_names` works and preserves both lists.

### Verification

I reproduced this with the official n8n 2.45.0 Docker image, using an Aggregate node with typeVersion 1. I imported and executed the workflow through the n8n CLI. The collision case and the unique-name control both completed successfully. I also ran a separate control with explicitly duplicated names, which raised the expected error.

The current source appears to check uniqueness using the full input path, then shorten nested paths to their final segment when creating the output. This lets `customer.name` and `supplier.name` pass the check before both become `name`:

https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/fb08a75c5072c072486d9868af3d9ea78b896445/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Transform/Aggregate/Aggregate.node.ts

I'd like to work on a fix and add a regression test. Would the team be happy for me to take this on?

Show HN: Rouler – Steer Windows traffic per app or IP across multiple interfaces
Hi HN, Rouler is "rules for your routes". It allows you to steer network traffic across multiple network interfaces on Windows. For example: - Run Tailscale, Mullvad and OpenVPN official clients simultaneously. - Use Rouler to send Slack via the OpenVPN connection, Chrome + an IP range via Tailscale and a torrent client via Mullvad. Rouler is VPN agnostic, so you can "split-tunnel" with anything that sets up a windows network interface. I'm an independent developer from Australia and have been working on Rouler for a bit over a year. It's been a challenging project to say the least, but I'm really happy with how it's turning out. I have spent a great deal of time building and throwing things away, starting over, belting the initial poc into something that I find intuitive... hopefully others do too! I've done all the testing, fixing and improving I can, so now it's open for public beta. I'd love to hear your feedback... and there are some specific points I'm interested in hearing about listed on the Rouler website. Please reply with any questions you might have. Thanks for reading! Brendan p.s. Rouler is "built in Rust" TM ;-) --- On AI (skip if you're sick of hearing about it): Since AI is the hot topic and people are naturally cautious about it, I'll add some quick notes about it, specifically about the driver development as that's the key thing to get right. The driver is hand written and every detail has been poured over many times over. I spent somewhere around 6-9 months manually building and testing just the driver, staring at Dbgview logs, wireshark logs, windows route tables, restarting VM's back to their snapshot and manually copying things across to start again. That's not always the most efficient way of doing things, but it's the way it had to be done. If I had tried to vibe code it Rouler simply wouldn't exist. I did try to lean on AI at times, but it constantly sent me in the wrong direction, told me things weren't possible, tried to take shortcuts and implement poor performing trade-offs. It also loved to hallucinate the windows api. Keep in mind this was around the Opus 4.1 - 4.6 days. Outside of the driver, in user mode land, AI has crept more and more into my workflow. I've had a lot of success utilising the latest models in the app in particular, and I purposefully separated the UI and core logic so I'm able to quickly iterate on the UI. I've also found AI very useful for scripting and refactoring. It has built some great scripts that would've taken me days or weeks to build and fine tune.

GMP Certification in Indonesia
GMP Certification in Indonesia – Good Manufacturing Practices
GMP Certification in Indonesia helps manufacturers establish controlled, hygienic, and consistent production practices that support product quality and safety. GMP, or Good Manufacturing Practices, provides principles for controlling manufacturing activities so products are produced and handled according to defined quality requirements.
GMP is particularly relevant to industries such as pharmaceuticals, food and beverages, cosmetics, medical devices, dietary supplements, and other sectors where manufacturing conditions can directly affect product safety and quality. Organizations can use GMP principles to strengthen production controls, documentation, hygiene, quality assurance, and traceability.
For professional guidance, explore[ GMP Certification in Indonesia](https://certvalue.com/gmp-certification-in-indonesia/).
What Is GMP Certification in Indonesia?
GMP Certification in Indonesia generally refers to an assessment, certification, inspection, or compliance process against applicable Good Manufacturing Practice requirements. The exact requirements depend on the product category, industry, applicable regulations, and relevant regulatory or certification scheme.
GMP focuses on controlling manufacturing risks throughout the product lifecycle. It can cover raw materials, personnel, facilities, equipment, production processes, quality control, sanitation, packaging, storage, documentation, and distribution.
Indonesian manufacturers may need to consider requirements established by relevant authorities, including the Indonesian Food and Drug Authority (BPOM), together with sector-specific regulations and customer requirements. Organizations should determine which GMP requirements and regulatory approvals apply to their specific products.
Why Is GMP Important for Indonesian Businesses?
Indonesia's manufacturing sector supplies products to both domestic and international markets. Maintaining consistent production conditions is essential for organizations whose products can affect consumer health, safety, or product performance.
GMP provides a systematic approach to identifying and controlling manufacturing risks. It encourages organizations to maintain suitable facilities, control raw materials, train employees, monitor processes, maintain equipment, and keep accurate production records.
Effective GMP practices can also support preparation for regulatory inspections, customer audits, supplier evaluations, and applicable market requirements. However, GMP certification or assessment does not automatically replace product registrations, licenses, approvals, or other legally required authorizations.
Benefits of GMP Certification in Indonesia
1. Consistent Product Quality
GMP controls help organizations standardize manufacturing activities and reduce variations that could affect product quality.
2. Improved Product Safety
Hygiene controls, sanitation procedures, equipment maintenance, and process monitoring can help reduce contamination and manufacturing-related risks.
3. Better Regulatory Preparedness
A structured GMP system can help organizations organize manufacturing activities around applicable regulatory and industry requirements.
4. Stronger Documentation and Traceability
Accurate production records, batch information, inspection results, and corrective action records help organizations track manufacturing activities and investigate quality issues.
5. Increased Customer Confidence
Documented manufacturing controls can provide customers, distributors, and business partners with greater confidence in an organization's production practices.
6. Reduced Operational Risks
Employee training, preventive maintenance, process controls, and defined procedures can reduce production errors, contamination risks, and inconsistent outputs.
Key Elements of GMP in Indonesia
An effective GMP framework commonly addresses:
Personnel: Appropriate training, hygiene, responsibilities, and competency.
Facilities: Suitable premises designed and maintained to support hygienic operations.
Equipment: Properly selected, cleaned, maintained, and controlled equipment.
Raw Materials: Controlled sourcing, inspection, identification, storage, and handling.
Production: Approved procedures and controlled manufacturing processes.
Quality Control: Appropriate inspection, testing, and product evaluation.
Documentation: Accurate procedures, production records, inspection records, and corrective actions.
Storage and Distribution: Controlled conditions that help preserve product quality.
GMP Certification Process in Indonesia
The process varies according to the industry, product, applicable regulations, and assessment arrangement.
Step 1: Initial Review
The organization identifies its products, manufacturing activities, applicable GMP requirements, and regulatory obligations.
Step 2: Gap Assessment
Facilities, processes, documentation, hygiene practices, equipment, and quality controls are reviewed to identify gaps.
Step 3: GMP System Development
Required procedures for production, sanitation, quality control, maintenance, training, documentation, and other activities are established or improved.
Step 4: Implementation and Training
Employees implement approved procedures and maintain appropriate records throughout manufacturing operations.
Step 5: Internal Evaluation
Internal audits, inspections, or management reviews may be conducted to identify weaknesses and corrective actions.
Step 6: Assessment and Corrective Action
The applicable inspection, assessment, certification, or regulatory process is completed and identified issues are addressed.
Step 7: Final Documentation
Certification, inspection records, regulatory documentation, or other evidence is issued according to the applicable scheme.
Why Choose CertValue for GMP Support in Indonesia?
CertValue provides consulting and certification-related support for organizations seeking to improve their manufacturing and compliance practices. Indonesian businesses can obtain guidance on GMP requirements, documentation, procedures, implementation, internal reviews, and assessment preparation.
The appropriate assessment depends on the product category, industry, applicable regulations, and selected certification or regulatory arrangement. Organizations should confirm whether they require certification, regulatory approval, inspection, registration, or another form of conformity documentation.
For more information, visit[ GMP Certification in Indonesia](https://certvalue.com/gmp-certification-in-indonesia/).
Conclusion
GMP Certification in Indonesia helps organizations establish controlled manufacturing practices focused on product quality, safety, consistency, hygiene, and traceability. By implementing appropriate procedures and maintaining effective production controls, businesses can strengthen their manufacturing operations and improve readiness for applicable regulatory and customer requirements.
Organizations seeking GMP implementation and certification-related support can contact CertValue for guidance on applicable requirements and available services.

Consume rather than fork the [existing installed-supplier receiving work #4](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/capability-pricing-service/issues/4), [Coesite original compute/Bazaar Work](https://github.com/coesite-operations/capability-market-services-section/issues/5), [Group paid-Work sourcing](https://github.com/561-group/561-group-opportunity-services-section/issues/35), and [Gathering the Mist receiving](https://github.com/561-group/561-group-opportunity-services-section/issues/3).

### Specific defect and requirement
Present `compareComputeWorkOffers` correctly refuses omitted costs, unsupported commercial rights, underbilled GPU seconds, unverified same-task reliability and uncertain pricing. But it cannot represent **full positive economic shadow/resource cost with $0 marginal new cash** when the requester already controls fixed-paid compute entitlements. Provider sticker price, historical fixed commitments, cash outlay, opportunity cost, GPU headroom, and customer income are distinct facts.

- **NC-01** Source-own an *optional* principal-held-capacity comparison branch within the existing exact-rational quote method (not a new market or scheduler). Preserve existing external paid-provider behavior.
- **NC-02** Require a bounded original Work principal, per-kind cash disposition for all 12 resource-cost categories, source-bound exact consumption quantity, evidence of rightful original account/entitlement and sufficient uncommitted usable capacity to cover retry-adjusted demand. Treat data as attributed source assertions, not independently verified reservations.
- **NC-03** Apply a same-denomination exact *new cash ceiling* independent of total economic quote. A ceiling of zero must refuse any positive additional cash, unclassified cost, expired/wrong-principal entitlement, exhausted headroom, forbidden relationship, unknown rights, incompatible workload or uncertain source.
- **NC-04** Return comparable price-per-accepted-result and modeled incremental cash-per-accepted-result as **separate** quantities; never equate a cash-free internal allocation with free compute, margin, sales, settled payouts, or external buyer acceptance.
- **NC-05** Prove the distinction on executable native tests: (a) a source-asserted eligible previously funded capacity option within a zero-new-cash cap, (b) a nominally cheaper billable provider refused, (c) wrong principal/expired or insufficient quota refused, (d) retry-adjusted quota and cash, (e) unchanged original procurement behavior.

**Receiving:** source/Node tests alone are not live capacity or income. Follow [the original CFO financial-stewardship procedure](https://github.com/561-group/561-group-services-section) and Coesite installed Work before calling it operational. A real positive outcome needs original source/custody/rights and current provider usage measurement, accepted external Work, distinct buyer charge/settlement and seller attribution, with zero **additional** cash expenditure established from the authoritative bill/ledger. No external provider order, account enrollment, billable API request or scheduled task is authorized by this issue.

I wouldn't interpret the chart as indicative of the gains in the quality of AI writing; it's more that it's a fairly new phenomenon and there is a dra
I wouldn't interpret the chart as indicative of the gains in the quality of AI writing; it's more that it's a fairly new phenomenon and there is a dramatic increase in people who try to smuggle AI stories into contests (be it for personal gratification or to "show" human writers), and an increase in the scrutiny that submissions receive. Fundamentally, I know that HN has plenty of people who will react with "ha-ha, human authors should pack their bags", just like what we keep telling mathematicians, because we see the discipline as just another market that can be conquered by automation or another benchmark to track. But literature, similarly to most other forms of higher-brow entertainment, isn't just about reducing unit-cost or hacking engagement metrics. For the same reason why a genuine van Gogh painting is worth a lot more than a nearly-perfect replica, people who care about the craft usually care about it telling genuine human stories and celebrating the author as much as the result. Now, the mass consumer may not care; if you have an infinite Harry Potter sequel machine, many will partake. But then, I guess the question is, if you build the sequel machine, are you leaving the world better off or not? Do you want to be interacting exclusively with machines down the line? And if there's no inherent value to humanity, why should the machines be compelled to interact with you?

title: hasKey() throws on objects created with Object.create(null)
source_text:
hasKey() throws on objects created with Object.create(null)
## 现象

`hasKey()` in `packages/workflow/src/utils.ts` calls `value.hasOwnProperty(key)` directly:

```ts
export function hasKey<T extends PropertyKey>(value: unknown, key: T): value is Record<T, unknown> {
	return value !== null && typeof value === 'object' && value.hasOwnProperty(key);
}
```

When `value` is an object without a prototype (created via `Object.create(null)`), `hasOwnProperty` is not inherited, so the function throws `TypeError: value.hasOwnProperty is not a function` instead of returning a boolean.

## 最小复现

```ts
import { hasKey } from 'n8n-workflow';

const record = Object.create(null);
record.key = 'value';

hasKey(record, 'key');     // throws TypeError: value.hasOwnProperty is not a function
hasKey(record, 'missing'); // throws instead of returning false
```

Prototype-less records are produced inside the repo itself (e.g. `nullProtoRecord()` in `packages/workflow/src/connections-diff.ts`) and are a common way to hold key-controlled data.

## 期望

`hasKey` should use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(value, key)` and return `true`/`false` for prototype-less objects, consistent with its behaviour for ordinary objects, arrays and primitives.

## 影响

Any code path that feeds a prototype-less record into `hasKey` (for example error/metadata parsing built on `hasKey`) crashes with a `TypeError` instead of performing a simple key lookup. This turns an ordinary key check into an execution failure whenever the input object has no prototype.

Show HN: Beeline Multiplayer Agent Harness
Shipped Beeline today. 
It's a team chat for humans and agents - a kind of multiplayer harness. You can bring your codex, Claude code, opencode subscriptions and also works with pi and goose. We built beeline itself with early versions of beeline, and use it to build our other projects - it's boosted productivity quite a bit for us. - Open source and not a business. We use beeline internally, and just thought it would be a really cool thing to exist in the world. There are still lots of bugs
- Sweepstakes things like computer use, lots of third party connector integrations are there. What's cool is that beeline agents can automate _auth_ through trustysquire.ai - they can sign up to most services and APIs without you having to do it for them. 
- A new primitive called workflows, that are skills for teams of agents. 
- multi way call with your entire team, humans and agents. I like it quite a bit. Looking forward to feedback!

source_text:
Ask HN: Windows Signing for FOSS Projects
Hey, all. I'm wondering how people handle signing packages for Windows when your project is open-source and there is no budget for an expensive code-signing certificate. I thought I had found a solution with SignPath's (https://signpath.org/) free certs for open source, but I ran into two snags with them. - I can't use custom runners in my github workflow. I was using a larger runner (still github hosted, I just picked a larger size) to run my tests faster, and SignPath failed the job because it didn't recognize the runner name. So I would have to go back to a standard runner with a name they recognize, which runs my tests about 3x slower. - I have to approve each package signing, which means that a release process that was fully automated now has a step I have to manually approve. I raised both of these issues with SignPath over a week ago, and I have yet to get a response, or to even have my signing certificate issued. So I'm about to give up on them. Windows is only about 10% of my user base, so right now I'm leaning towards just continuing to not sign my Windows releases. But before I throw in the towel, I wanted to ask if anyone here knows of a better way to handle this. Oh, and shameless plug for my project, a kubernetes management app: https://github.com/luxury-yacht/app/

Show HN: An offline desktop companion to help maintain a healthy blink rhythm
Profession like software engineer, mechanical / graphics designer takes a lot of strain on your eyes, observing minute details for hours and hours on screen can significantly reduce the blink rate which you might not even notice until it gets irreversibly painful, leaving you with dry eyes. I am already a victim of it, working 20 years as a research engineer in computer vision, zooming into pixel level details to hand craft algorithms. Help Needed: Building an AI-Powered Personalized Fitness Plan Automation with n8n + Google Forms + WhatsApp
Hi everyone, 
 I’m currently working on an  AI-powered fitness automation using n8n , and I would appreciate some guidance from the community on how to design the workflow properly. 
 The basic idea is to create an automated system where a user first fills out a  Google Form  with their personal fitness requirements. The form would collect information such as: 
 
 
 Name 
 
 
 Age 
 
 
 Current weight 
 
 
 Target weight 
 
 
 Fitness goal 
 
 
 General fitness 
 
 
 Weight loss 
 
 
 Weight gain 
 
 
 Muscle building 
 
 
 Other goals 
 
 
 
 
 Current fitness level 
 
 
 Type of workout they prefer 
 
 
 Gym 
 
 
 Home workout 
 
 
 Outdoor workout 
 
 
 
 
 Available workout time 
 
 
 Dietary preferences 
 
 
 Food preferences/restrictions 
 
 
 Number of meals they prefer 
 
 
 Any relevant limitations or conditions they want the system to consider 
 
 
   Proposed n8n Workflow 
 I’m thinking of building something like: 
  Google Form → Google Sheets → n8n → AI → Personalized Fitness Plan → WhatsApp  
 After the user submits the form, n8n would collect and process the information and send it to an AI model. 
 The AI would then generate a  personalized daily fitness plan , including: 
    Workout Plan  
 
 
 Exercises for the day 
 
 
 Sets and repetitions 
 
 
 Workout duration 
 
 
 Rest periods 
 
 
 Gym/home workout variations 
 
 
    Daily Meal Plan  
 
 
 Breakfast 
 
 
 Lunch 
 
 
 Snacks 
 
 
 Dinner 
 
 
 Suggested food options 
 
 
 Approximate calorie and protein targets 
 
 
    Daily Targets  
 
 
 Estimated calorie target 
 
 
 Protein target 
 
 
 Water intake 
 
 
 Daily activity/step goal 
 
 
 Workout duration 
 
 
    Personalized Schedule  
The system should ideally generate a plan based on the user’s goal and preferences and provide a different daily plan as the user progresses. 
   WhatsApp Automation 
 Once the plan is generated, I want n8n to automatically send it to the user through  WhatsApp . 
 For example: 
 
  Good Morning, Rahul!    
   Goal: Weight Loss 
  Today’s Target: ~2,000 kcal 
  Water: 2.5–3 L 
    Today’s Workout  
• Squats – 3 × 12 
• Push-ups – 3 × 10 
• Walking – 30 min 
    Breakfast  
• Eggs + oats + fruit 
    Lunch  
• Rice/roti + vegetables + protein source 
    Dinner  
• … 
 Have a great workout!   
 
 I would also like to eventually add  daily reminders , progress tracking, and possibly allow users to update their weight or progress through WhatsApp. 
   What I Need Help With 
 I would especially appreciate suggestions on: 
 
 
  How should I structure the n8n workflow?  
 
 
 Which nodes would be best for processing the Google Form/Google Sheets data? 
 
 
 What is the best way to structure the  AI prompt  so that the generated plans are consistent and personalized? 
 
 
 How should I maintain a user’s information and progress over multiple days? 
 
 
 What is the best approach for sending the generated plan through  WhatsApp ? 
 
 
 How can I create a system where the AI generates a new plan each day rather than repeating the same plan? 
 
 
 What would be the best database/storage option for user profiles and progress? 
 
 
 Are there any important things I should consider regarding  fitness, nutrition, calorie calculations, and user safety ? 
 
 
 I’m fairly new to building larger n8n workflows, so I would really appreciate  a recommended architecture or example workflow  that I can use as a starting point. 
 Thanks in advance!   
I’d love to hear suggestions from anyone who has built similar  AI + n8n + WhatsApp automation systems .

source_text:
Apex P0 — November 4 larger-supply intake and catalog reconciliation
## Goal / target
**Target: Wednesday, November 4, 2026** — prepare to evaluate the *potential* expanded supplier catalog; do not treat it as confirmed inventory.

## Acceptance checklist
- [ ] Obtain an authorized supplier-provided list through an appropriate private channel (not public GitHub): supplier identifier, item/variant identifiers, descriptions, package quantities, pricing basis, media rights, documented availability date, current stock evidence, and applicable product eligibility documents.
- [ ] Compare supplier-provided identifiers against the existing **63 saved product records** and 63 staged import candidates; classify **existing / modified / new / unclear** without creating duplicates.
- [ ] Validate unique product/variant identity and prevent accidental overwriting of manually edited descriptions/images/prices.
- [ ] Separate **potential supply / supplier-reported availability / received-and-verified stock**. Do not alter real on-hand or reserved inventory from rumors or a quote.
- [ ] Collect evidence of lawful sourcing, product eligibility, shipping restrictions, and supplier authorization **privately** before deciding any public visibility.
- [ ] Produce a review-only before/after diff with counts: new, existing, conflicts, missing fields, blocked items, approved items. Require supplier review before any database write.
- [ ] Verify repeat upload is idempotent and does not introduce duplicate SKUs or supplier ownership errors.
- [ ] Keep global release and checkout disabled; no actual sales, shipping or payments in this issue.

## Current verified checkpoint (Nov 3)
63 saved products, 50 active, 13 uncategorized, no publicly published products, 0 on-hand inventory, 0 verified sales. Availability expansion is **unconfirmed**.

## Dependency
Existing supplier bulk CSV, image reuse, selective save and duplicate-safe source candidate workflows. Scope only catalog intake/validation, not publishing or purchasing.

## Definition of done
Validated private intake diff + reproducible duplicate-handling tests, with supplier decision recorded. PR small and reviewable; CI pass.

| LM2596 可調降壓、帶數位顯示 | 2202111533 (E1-3) | 80 | DC-DC buck module | [exact listing](https://www.taiwaniot.com.tw/product/20w-dc-dc%E5%8F%AF%E8%AA%BF%E9%99%8D%E5%A3%93%E6%A8%A1%E7%B5%84-%E5%B8%B6%E9%9B%BB%E5%A3%93%E8%A1%A8%E9%A1%AF%E7%A4%BA/) |

## 2. 腳位／Ports 候選（逐件，僅明確標示之規格才可成為工程真值）

### A. 紅板 8 路 5 V 繼電器，8493632

- **可證實的賣方規格**：DC 5 V，8 個機械繼電器，COM / NO / NC 類型，高低電平由跳線設定，最大接點標稱 AC 250 V/10 A 或 DC 30 V/10 A；外形 141.5 × 50 × 18.5 mm；固定孔 4 個、孔徑 3.1 mm。數值為供應商聲明，不等於已驗證額定條件。
- **Ports 候選**：
  - 控制與電源端子：DC+, DC-, IN1–IN8（控制編號為八路推定；官方頁寫 `IN`，尚未證明每個實際印刷端子順序／總數）。
  - 繼電器輸出：`K1 ... K8` 每組 `COMx, NOx, NCx`（8×3=24 個可能負載接點，需逐一對應絲印；`NC` 此處是 Normally Closed 功能名稱，**PinStatus 不得設為 Not Connected**）。
  - 高／低觸發選擇跳線：賣方有描述，但實際接點數與對應通道未確定，不能填 Complete。
- **需解決**：模組製造商/板號、實體控制端子數、繼電器接點順序、觸發跳線組數、電流條件；不可誤用另一個 SKU `1807111656` 的 JD-VCC 接法。
- 圖片來源（**僅外部連結，尚未保存檔案**）：![TaiwanIOT 8493632 product](https://www.taiwaniot.com.tw/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/8way2.jpg)

### B. Nano V3.0 CH340，1806251545

- **可證實賣方資訊**：副廠 CH340、ATmega328P、5 V 邏輯，18 × 45 mm、D0–D13、A0–A7、6 PWM 引腳 D3/D5/D6/D9/D10/D11；USB 供電。**注意這不是 Arduino 官方製造的 A000005**。
- **30-pin 物理排針參考清單**（來自 [Arduino 官方 classic Nano pinout](https://www.arduino.cc/en/uploads/Main/ArduinoNanoManual23.pdf)，**僅為 compatible-board candidate，不證明此 CH340 clone exact physical numbering**）：
  - 1 D1/TX; 2 D0/RX; 3 RESET; 4 GND; 5 D2; 6 D3~; 7 D4; 8 D5~; 9 D6~; 10 D7; 11 D8; 12 D9~; 13 D10~; 14 D11~; 15 D12.
  - 16 D13; 17 3V3; 18 AREF; 19 A7; 20 A6; 21 A5/SCL; 22 A4/SDA; 23 A3; 24 A2; 25 A1; 26 A0; 27 5V; 28 RESET; 29 GND; 30 VIN.
- **Port candidates**：2×15 independent header contacts (Pins mode)；Mini USB whole-mated connector (Connector mode；需實板核對 USB connector pin count/variant，不能把 USB contacts 當成已驗證 clone pins)。
- **需解決**：此副廠板 pinout exact variant、USB connector type（商品照片所見與圖紙須核對）、5 V / VIN 電源處理、CH340 clone board 的 pin sourcing。
- 圖片來源（僅外部連結）：![TaiwanIOT 1806251545 product](https://www.taiwaniot.com.tw/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/nano-340.jpg)

### C. MAX485 TTL/RS485，652467635

- **可證實的賣方資訊**：MAX485 半雙工 UART↔RS485 模組、5.08mm 2P 接線端子、供應商產品規格稱 5 V 供電、板尺寸有 46×12 mm 與 44×14 mm 兩個互相衝突的說法。
- **腳位候選**：`VCC`(power), `GND`(return), `RO`(UART receive output), `/RE`(receiver enable, active low), `DE`(driver enable), `DI`(UART transmit input), `A` / `B` (RS485 pair)；6-pin MCU header + 2-pin RS485 screw terminal **尚待實板絲印/模組圖確認**。
- **資料衝突**：供應商頁敘述中一次寫「供電 3.3 V，相容 5 V 邏輯」、另處寫「工作電壓 5 V」。不得把 3.3 V 當成經確認的模組正常供電。
- **需解決**：實際 PCB 端子名稱、同一張板的全部實體接點、是否有預載 120Ω 終端、尺寸、5V 供電範圍。
- 圖片來源（僅外部連結）：![TaiwanIOT 652467635 product](https://www.taiwaniot.com.tw/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/rs-485-module-ttl-to-rs-485-5v-600x600.jpg)

### D. PWM→0–10 V，1805251612

- **可證實的賣方規格**：供電 **DC 12–30 V**；PWM 輸入頻率 **1–3 kHz**，5V 檔接受 4.5–10 V 峰值、24V 檔接受 12–24 V 峰值；AO 0–10 V，供應商標稱誤差 5%。
- **賣方列出的 6 個介面標記／功能**：`VCC` 12–30 V、`GND_supply`、`PWM`、`GND_pwm`、`VOUT` 0–10 V、`GND_out`。若實板絲印是 `DIN+` / `DIN-` / `12–30V` / `GND` / `AO`，則需建立**逐接點映射並核對，不可直接臆測三個 GND 物理上等電位**。
- **Ports 候選**：電源2、PWM訊號2、AO訊號2（各 `TopologyEndpointMode=Pins`）；輸入電平 jumper 接點數待確認。
- **需解決**：實板端子順序、jumper 三實體接點、正反接與 PWM 電壓、AO 負載條件、外形尺寸。
- 圖片來源（僅外部連結）：![TaiwanIOT 1805251612 product](https://www.taiwaniot.com.tw/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/pwm.jpg)

### E. LM2596 降壓顯示板，2202111533

- **可證實的賣方資訊**：此 SKU **帶三位電壓顯示器**（不是無顯示的普通 LM2596）；4.0–40 V 輸入、1.25–37 V 可調輸出（輸入需高於輸出至少約 1.5 V）、標示 3 A、建議 ≤2 A、20 W、外形 66 × 36 × 12 mm。
- **可辨識的候選端子**：`IN+`, `IN-`, `OUT+`, `OUT-`，兩組 2P 螺絲端子、端點模式 Pins；輸入與輸出功率/地連接需依實板文件核對。
- **供應商頁描述衝突**：頁頭提 4–40 V，內文另有「0–40 V」但後文明載 4–40 V；不得寫成已核實 0 V 下能運作。網頁歷史抓取價格也有 $80/$100 差異，使用者採購記錄 $80 單獨保留。
- **需解決**：板子原廠/板號、接線端子絲印與位置、最大輸出條件／散熱規格、孔位。
- 圖片來源（僅外部連結）：![TaiwanIOT 2202111533 product](https://www.taiwaniot.com.tw/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/LM2596LCD-600x528.jpg)

## 3. 權威門檻與後續動作

1. **IDENTITY**：請核實 5 款 PCB 真正 Manufacturer + Model / 板號，或取得供應商明確核准以 `TaiwanIOT + SKU` 作為供應商代料號的正式身份。不將 IC 製造商假定為整板製造商。
2. **EVIDENCE**：取得逐款原廠/供應商核准的正反面實照、端子功能／編號／跳針說明及文件。上述嵌入圖片只是源站 hotlink，不是 `Documents/.../product.jpg` 本地歸檔；不能填 ImagePath。
3. **PORTS/PINS**：完整核對每一個實體端子，包括 relay 觸發選擇 jumpers、Nano USB、PWM 輸入選擇 jumpers。未核實的實體接點不能設 Complete；pin number、physical side 不可由照片猜。
4. **VALIDATE**：身分確定後先重新 ArchiveLookup，產生每一型號的 schema changeset，跑 Validator；`TopologyStatus=Review`, `LayoutStatus=NeedsData/Review` 直到門檻滿足。
5. **WRITE/SYNC**：唯有 validator PASS 及寫入 capability 可用時，才應更新正式 Google Sheet，Readback，重新輸出 `Component_Intelligence_Database.xlsx`，驗證雙表一致。此 issue **不構成已更新中央資料庫**。

**追蹤結論：** 五個賣方 SKU、商品規格、可辨識腳位候選與照片原始來源已整理；五件正式 archive 都尚未完成。不得宣稱 Ready/COMPLETE。

# TYME-HALL-LAUNCH-001 — Independent Reviewer and Release Steward Qualification

**Priority:** P0 · **State:** OPEN / UNASSIGNED / NO ACCESS GRANTED · **Release target:** October 30, 2026 (conditional)  
**Governing command:** [Notion launch command](https://app.notion.com/p/3f5c51d54b758197a92ff59d2c203045) · [Launch dependency ledger #15](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-control-center/issues/15)  
**Authority posture:** human-governed. No issue, model or agent may grant GitHub merge/release privileges, production publication, payment, secrets, contributor identity, or Canon promotion.

## Why this gate is P0

Current [Hall ruleset #24880323](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/rules/24880323) is active and requires **one approving review**, last-push approval, stale approval dismissal, resolved conversations, and no bypass. Independent GitHub review is currently missing for:
- [Hall PR #19](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/pull/19) — Office freshness and premerge checks (draft).
- [Hall PR #20](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/pull/20) — controlled production release (draft; 38 offline test cases passed, not a live deploy).
- [Control Center PR #18](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-control-center/pull/18) — release packet/assurance evidence (draft).

**Production safety constraint:** Authenticated Cloudflare Pages `codex-interface` still has Git-triggered automatic **production** deploys enabled on `main`, while all preview deployments remain enabled. The production-only auto-build freeze must be **separately authorized and verified OFF BEFORE merging either Hall PR**; a code-only merge could otherwise publish without a separate founder release GO. Live Cloudflare settings, main, ruleset, secrets and GitHub environments are unchanged by this issue.

## Separated human responsibilities (do not collapse)

| Role | Mandate | Authority NOT conferred |
|---|---|---|
| A — independent code reviewer | Review exact PR head, changed files, denials, test evidence, supply chain, route preservation, licensing/privacy and rollback; return an independently attributable review | Not authorized to publish, modify Cloudflare, change GitHub rulesets, grant credentials, spend funds, approve Canon or sign founder GO |
| B — production release operator | When qualified and designated, manually start a release workflow against a specific independently reviewed `main` SHA | Cannot independently approve their own environment execution or expand release scope |
| C — founder / delegated separate human release approver | Record a distinct, explicit G6 GO and approve the protected deployment environment for an exact source SHA after all release gates pass | No hidden model/agent delegation; does not waive independent technical review |

Role B and role C **must be different human actors** when environment self-review prevention applies. Technical independence requires reviewer A not to be the author of the reviewed change. A public participant completing a cold-read/a11y test under [Hall issue #18](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/issues/18) is not thereby qualified to approve security-sensitive source code or obtain write access.

## Qualification protocol — evidence before access

- [ ] **Q1 — public-only screening:** Verify candidate controls the claimed GitHub identity. Request an uncoached review of these public artifacts, without credentials, private links, tokens or remote machine access. Record disclosure of affiliations/conflicts and scope availability.
- [ ] **Q2 — exercise technical judgment:** Require concrete file/line findings for at least one release-blocking case (e.g. production autobuild before merge; environment declaration without required reviewer; wrong/moved SHA; false route equivalence; supply-chain version pinning; bypass; credentials exposure) and a safe reproducible verification approach. Distinguish observed defects from speculation.
- [ ] **Q3 — understand governance:** Candidate must explicitly acknowledge GitHub review != founder G6, green CI != live Cloudflare deployment, test receipts != institutionally durable positive Phase 2, and new participants receive no implied identity/governance rights.
- [ ] **Q4 — identify least privilege:** Confirm GitHub's minimum permissions for an eligible required PR review under current repository rules and plan, separately from a mere commenter. Obtain explicit founder authorization **before** adding collaborator access. No Admin, Cloudflare, repo secrets, bypass actors, environment approver, or unattended automation credentials in initial reviewer assignment.
- [ ] **Q5 — source/head-specific review:** Obtain review of PR #19 and PR #20 against current head SHAs, explicit unresolved findings and one approving review only after defects have been addressed. Existing ruleset must never be bypassed. Review Control Center PR #18 independently if qualification extends to governance packet review.
- [ ] **Q6 — release operator vs founder:** Designate named human release operator and a separate founder-controlled environment reviewer; manually inspect actual `tymehall-production` required-reviewer settings, protected-main branch restriction, no-bypass/self-review posture, and protected environment-only secrets. **Do not rely on the YAML environment field alone**.
- [ ] **Q7 — staging/denial evidence:** Verify manual release source SHA equality, controlled asset route diff, missing-credential denial, unapproved environment denial, branch-race denial, isolated staging run, rollback and independent production readback. No live mutation before separate explicit authorization.
- [ ] **Q8 — documented acceptance:** Record actual reviewer GitHub login, scope of review, timestamp, exact PR commit SHAs, linked test evidence, outstanding findings, permissible permissions, independent founder authority, and GO/HOLD decision. If no qualified reviewer, retain intentional freeze.

## Public invitation posture

**Do not offer a paid bounty yet.** The related mobile cold-read contribution candidate is [UNFUNDED](https://github.com/sovereign-codex/Codex-interface-/issues/18). If recruiting volunteers, begin with a bounded public documentation/code-review exercise using only published material. No promised compensation, privilege, institutional authority or project endorsement. Screen attempts to redirect toward wallets, off-platform payment, unverifiable automated test claims or demands for credentials. Keep original issue #18's spam lock intact.

source_text:
Has anyone built a reliable multichannel inventory system that actually keeps up during flash sales?
Running into a wall that I suspect a lot of sellers here have hit. 
 We’re selling across Shopify and two marketplaces. Everything runs fine during normal trading. The moment we run any kind of promotional event flash sale, limited drop, festive season push inventory starts drifting across channels. 
 A sale happens on one platform and by the time the other channels update, we’ve already taken orders we can’t fulfil. It’s not a huge volume problem - it’s a timing problem. The sync just isn’t fast enough when orders are coming in quickly from multiple places simultaneously. 
 We’ve tried a few apps from the App Store but most of them seem to operate on a scheduled sync every 10, 15 or 30 minutes. Which is fine at low volume but completely breaks down the moment anything sells quickly. 
 What I think we actually need is something event-driven, where a sale on any channel immediately triggers an update everywhere else, rather than waiting for the next scheduled job to run. 
 Has anyone solved this properly? Specifically looking for: 
 -> Real-time sync across Shopify and external marketplaces → Somthing that handles concurrent orders without overselling → Ideally a single dashboard for orders across all channels too 
 Would genuinely love to know what’s working for people here whether that’s an App Store solution, a custom setup or something else entirely.

Show HN: Open-source early-reading reader with phonics help
My kid is 6 y/o and she is learning to read. She's moved through the basic phonics with Teach Your Monster to Read but was struggling with how repetitive it was. I wanted to give her some stories to read, but she still needed help sounding words out - and I wanted her to have the experience of sitting and reading by herself. So I built this book reader app to allow her to click on the words, sound out the phonemes, and read by herself. My 12 year old son wrote the first story, there's a cliffhanger at the end and he's working on the next section. We're going to release more chapters and more stories in the near future. And there's one other thing - The reader has an MCP connection, so you can connect your Claude or ChatGPT or Grok, give them a PDF of a book you like (or even a set of scans done quickly with a phone camera) and have them import your favorite books into the app (private to your account, for your own kid, if you own the book of course). The reader is free to use on its website and open source if you want to tinker and create your own version. The included stories are under Creative Commons.
