Bounty Board launch: hosted preview, playtests, score policy and submission gates
## Goal
Ship **the expanded post-js13k game**, not the frozen 13 KB competition ZIP, to Bounty Board Arcade with evidence from a real hosted preview and first-time players. PR #60 made CI test the exact upload archive; PR #62 added bounded competitive scoring; PR #63 added real keyboard/mouse browser acceptance. These all passed the exact merged `main` SHA `bbf76fd` on October 19, 2026. Neither automation nor a successful upload is proof of real host behavior.


## Completed technical release work
- [x] [PR #60](https://github.com/sidhulyalkar/unicorn-stampede/pull/60): exact ZIP integrity and main push Arcade qualification.
- [x] [PR #62](https://github.com/sidhulyalkar/unicorn-stampede/pull/62): finite separate ranked score and anti-farming invariants (0–99,500), unchanged campaign scoring.
- [x] [PR #63](https://github.com/sidhulyalkar/unicorn-stampede/pull/63): real Chrome/Firefox title, WASD, Q, mouse-Whip, Space, pause/resume qualification against extracted ZIP.
- [x] All three merged-main CI workflows green on `bbf76fd`; exact ZIP, screen captures and machine-readable QA included in the Arcade artifact.

## P0 release blockers
- [x] Verify fresh `main` Arcade, showcase and satisfaction workflows on the same SHA after PRs #60, #62 and #63. All three passed on `bbf76fd`.
- [ ] Download `unicorn-stampede-arcade-preview` from the newest green **Arcade showcase qualification** main run, including ZIP, manifest, 16:9 cover and screenshots. Confirm SHA-256 and ZIP root `index.html`.
- [ ] Create a free Bounty studio account and upload the **ZIP** (not the frozen js13k artifact) in private/test mode; select *Leaderboards* and set a reviewed score ceiling.
- [ ] **Signed-in host preview:** title load, true gameplayStart/Stop on start/pause/resume/tab switch, integer score updates, exactly one gameOver, cloud mastery saved and restored after refresh and signing out/in.
- [ ] **Guest host preview:** fully playable without localStorage, no cloud-save success claim, no SDK-related softlock or console errors.
- [ ] **Competition isolation:** Prismborough/Medium starts at zero with reproducible shared town; other modes/worlds are free-play and do not produce positive ranked scores; test score cap failures.
- [ ] **Complete a natural physical run:** v1.22 Chromium/Firefox verified actual title selection, WASD paint, Q switch, mouse Whip, Space Dash and P pause/resume from the packaged ZIP. Still require a complete **natural** ranked conquest and natural three-capture defeat/restart, without directly setting landmark HP/paint.
- [ ] **Validate ranked scoring in live play and host:** v1.21 replaced unbounded raw campaign points with finite milestone points (theoretical maximum **99,500**). CI proves raw-score manipulation and erase/repaint loops cannot increase the board directly. Sample completed-run distributions, confirm the Bounty score ceiling is **at least 99,500**, verify score rejection feedback, and audit unexpected strategies. Client scoring remains alterable by determined users, so avoid paid stakes until authoritative verification exists.
- [ ] Desktop QA in Chromium, Firefox and Safari where possible: music/SFX unlock, keyboard focus inside iframe, Escape/P/Q/Space, fullscreen, narrow viewport and page visibility changes.
- [ ] At least **five uncoached first-time testers**, 30-second attempt then playthrough: ≥80% can say the goal; median first successful Whip+Dash building smash ≤45 s; ≥80% understand TEAM count; no softlocks; capture/rescue comprehension and replay interest recorded. Fix actual observed points of confusion before extra mechanics.

## Listing and outreach
- [ ] 16:9 cover, ≥100-word description, controls, screenshots and a 20–40-second gameplay clip showing a herd handoff, multicorn demolition and the consequences of capture.
- [ ] Upload via https://www.bountyboard.gg/arcade/submit and verify private preview before requesting publication/review. Publication requires Bounty approval.
- [ ] Reply to Grant in existing Stretchicorn thread: confirm Stretchicorn submission interest, share https://js13kgames.com/games/unicorn-stampede and explain that the expanded four-world Bounty-ready build is being prepared. Share the actual Arcade play link only once approved/available.

## Shipping boundary
- Frozen: `release/js13k-2026-submitted` and Wavedash PR #56.
- Canonical showcase: `main`.
- Official instructions: docs/BOUNTYBOARD_SUBMISSION.md and docs/BOUNTYBOARD_ARCADE_PLAN.md.
- Integrations are optional; standalone game must always start if SDK fails.

Help interpreting Orders-CSV export fields
Hi everyone, 
 Not sure if this is the right forum for that but I hope that you can help me out. 
 I’m exporting order data from our shop system and I’m struggling to understand the logic behind three discount-related fields: 
 
 
  Discount amount  
 
 
  Refunded Amount  
 
 
  Lineitem discount  
 
 
 I can’t figure out what each field is supposed to represent, or under which conditions the system fills one vs the other. The main problem is: From my understanding  these values must not be double-counted , but in some of our orders, sometimes one sometimes all three fields, are populated even though (from the business case) there was only a single discount/refund event. 
 Example 1 has only 1 refund of 65.00, but: 
 Order:  EU4429  
Subtotal: 93.82 
Shipping: 27.38 
Discount code: (empty) 
Discount amount: 65.00 
Refunded Amount: 65.00 
Lineitem discount: 65.00 
 This looks like “Discount amount” sometimes behaves like the full refund field. Also, if there are multiple items in the order,like: 
 Example 2, has two items ordered and just one lineitem discount, but somehow the discountet amount is working for the whole order, 
 
 
 
 
 Name:EU4403 Discounted amount: 30.00 
 
 
 
 
 Name:EU4403 Discounted amount: 0 Lineitem Discount: 30.00 
 
 
 
  I’m not seeing a consistent rule. 
 
 
 What does each of these fields typically include (voucher discount, automatic discount, item-level discount, cart-level discount, refunds, partial refunds, etc.)? Because some of these fields seems to include information from the other fields. Or have we simply broken something in our backend? 
 
 
 Are any of them just different “views” of the same value (e.g., order-level vs line-level), meaning only one should be used for reporting? 
 
 
 What’s the correct approach to avoid double counting when building revenue/refund reporting from these exports? 
 
 
 Thanks a lot for your help in advance.

Show HN: Retex, a Faster LaTeX Engine
retex is a clean-room, CC0, reimplementation of LuaLaTeX in rust. It can either be used as a faster (x2-3) drop-in replacement for LuaLaTex (--compat mode) , or as a more modern TeX engine, with much nicer error messages, support for SVG, ODP/ODT output, native PDF/X1 and PDF/X4 for printing, auto-download of missing packages (like eg Miktex), python bindings, etc. User manual with examples:  https://retex-ef747d.gitlab.io/retex-manual.pdf  retex has been entirely generated by a Large Language Model (LLM). India is recognised for its jewellery manufacturing expertise and wide range of jewellery designs. Working with an experienced exporter can help international buyers explore different styles suited to their markets, customers and occasions.

When choosing a diamond jewellery exporter in India, buyers should consider design variety, product quality, craftsmanship, communication and the ability to support international orders.

Zoniraz offers diamond jewellery across a range of categories, including:

This variety makes Zoniraz a relevant choice for buyers exploring an Indian jewellery supplier with multiple product categories.

Zoniraz: Jewellery Manufacturing and Export Expertise

Choosing the right jewellery partner involves more than finding attractive designs. Buyers also look for craftsmanship, consistency, product variety and clear communication throughout the sourcing process.

With around 50 years of experience in the jewellery business, Zoniraz brings industry knowledge and manufacturing expertise to its jewellery operations. The brand focuses on quality, detailed craftsmanship and designs that cater to different preferences and occasions.

As an Indian diamond jewellery manufacturer and exporter, Zoniraz aims to connect its jewellery expertise with the needs of international buyers seeking designs from India.

International Diamond Jewellery Shipping

International buyers need clear information about order handling, shipping arrangements and delivery expectations when sourcing jewellery across borders.

Zoniraz's export services are intended to support overseas jewellery enquiries and international orders. Buyers can contact the team to discuss product availability, design requirements, order quantities and applicable international shipping arrangements.

Before placing an order, international customers should confirm shipping destinations, delivery timelines, payment terms, applicable customs duties and any import requirements relevant to their country.

Zoniraz combines jewellery industry experience with a variety of diamond and gemstone designs to serve different customer preferences. Its focus on craftsmanship and product variety makes it a brand to explore when sourcing jewellery from India.

Module 7 — Supply Chain Risk: source coverage, golden lessons and no-rework release gates
## Purpose
Build **Module 7 — Supply Chain Risk** as the next fully release-audited module, using the **v6.0.1 synchronized Modules 1–6 baseline**, without repeating the earlier rework.

## Source scope / completeness
- Primary detailed source: the 2026 CSCP v5.4 risk module (155 PDF pages).
- Presentation: 20 slides, divided into Section A (risk management and supply-chain risks) and Section B (risk analysis and response).
- Flashcards: 22 defined terms across the two sections.
- The currently uploaded question bank does **not** contain a complete Module 7 set. **Write original questions; never reuse the bank verbatim.**
- Manual section ranges: A, pp. 8–62; B, pp. 63–140; appendix exhibits pp. 141–155 available for checking the original illustrations.

## Planned architecture (coverage-gate proposal; may change only after full source mapping)
- **Section A:** 12 substantive lessons + review. Risk/threat/opportunity; SCRM process, maturity, roles; known and unknown risk; appetite/tolerance/thresholds; strategy and risk plan; COSO ERM/GRC; ISO 31000, ISO 31010 and Guide 73; identification; risk registers; tangible, financial, intellectual-property, reputation and litigation loss categories.
- **Section B:** 19 substantive lessons + review. Internal/external risk types; qualitative matrix, urgency and evidence quality; distributions; EMV and cost incidence; sensitivity/Monte Carlo; accept/avoid/transfer/mitigate; preventive versus contingent response; strategic, supply, demand, process, environmental, hazard, financial, malfeasance and litigation response; BCMS, ISO 22301, ISO 28000, recovery and cross-partner continuity.
- **Integrated fictional capstone:** *Stonebridge Industrial Components — Disruption Resilience Decision Pack*; worked expected-loss mitigation choices, decision-changing sensitivity, hard gates, cross-functional implementation and recoverability.
- Proposed 10 purpose-built fictional CSV datasets and 31 topic-specific SVG models; exact counts freeze only after the coverage review.

## Explicit alignment — avoid re-teaching
- **M1:** risk consequences of forecast volatility, demand shaping, S&OP.
- **M2:** resilient network design, cyber architecture, supply-chain performance and financial metrics.
- **M3:** sourcing, sole/single/multisourcing, contractual risk allocation, product/IP issues.
- **M4:** MPS/MRP, inventory, capacity, quality and operational controls.
- **M5:** shipping routes, trade exposure, cargo loss, reverse-flow dependencies.
- **M6:** CRM/SRM, supplier qualification, concentration, strategic relationships and crisis communications.

Link to the authoritative earlier lessons; Module 7 adds formal exposure, priorities, responses, and continuity—not cloned explanations.

## Release-blocking checkpoints
- [ ] **G0 baseline freeze:** use v6.0.1, inspect live `QUALITY.md`, released module conventions and validator.
- [ ] **G1 full source-to-lesson matrix:** every meaningful section objective, exhibit, slide and flashcard term mapped, with no manual headings left orphaned.
- [ ] **G2 golden lessons:** A01 and quantitative B05/B06 at ≥500 original topic-specific words each, final lesson headings, relevant SVGs, operational flows, original Q/A and distractor rationale, genuinely worked calculation, both-width raster diagram QA.

- [ ] **G4 Section B:** all lessons + original review (≥10 Q), independent cost/EMV calculation recheck, scenario/decision gates.

- [ ] **G7 draft PR → approval → merge → CI/release:** keep the work off `main` until all release conditions pass; no premature tag/release.

## Lessons learned / special checks
1. Avoid repeating generic SVG layouts; topic-specific compositions must be inspected at standard/narrow widths for clipping and legibility.
2. Prevent answer-position bias across topic, section review and capstone questions; all four options plausible, all distractors explained.
3. Mandatory dataset links must be enforced (including the analogous Module 6 A09 link regression).
4. **Cost incidence and probability must be correct:** a *certain* mitigation outlay is not multiplied by event probability; probability-weight only event-contingent losses/costs and label all assumptions. Source examples that define conditional net-outcome cost require explicit treatment.
5. Hard ethical/safety/legal/security/continuity gates precede numerical ranking.
6. Check external standard versions and the difference between historical curriculum language and currently applicable standards/laws. Do not reuse broken/superseded external links.
7. No APICS PDFs, slides, flashcards, question bank, copyrighted diagrams, private client data, or internal source metadata in the public release.
8. Verify the release SHA equals `main`; do not confuse a passing CI check with a manual quality audit.

**Current state:** source review and blueprint completed. No incomplete public Module 7 folder or release has been published. Next operational action: finish G1 coverage evidence and develop G2 golden lessons before bulk authoring.

raw_evidence_quote:
Play a complete Tony turn from a prepared Gathering position
## Problem Statement

The next decision is whether that broader playing loop is useful and manageable through the existing Rust/tabletop path.

source_text:
Play a complete Tony turn from a prepared Gathering position
## Problem Statement

The application currently administers one scripted skill test. Joel cannot yet choose a sequence of investigator actions and have the application account for restrictions, enemy responses and end-of-turn consequences. The next decision is whether that broader playing loop is useful and manageable through the existing Rust/tabletop path.

## Solution

Offer a clearly named Tony-turn experiment alongside the existing experiment. A **prepared position** is an explicitly arranged game state from which a bounded play task begins; it does not imply that campaign setup or the preceding turns have been played through. Begin at the prepared position below, offer every legal choice reachable there, and finish after Tony's turn and mandatory end-of-turn effects. Preserve manual camera control, readable explanations, save/reopen and step-driven replay. The player chooses tactics; the application administers the rules.

## User Stories

1. As Joel, I want to see the prepared position and its boundary, so that I know what I am playing.
2. As Joel, I want to see Tony's ordinary actions and restricted additional action, so that I can plan a legal sequence.
3. As Joel, I want to fight or evade the Ghoul, so that I can choose how to manage its threat.
4. As Joel, I want to investigate, draw or gain resources while engaged, so that I can weigh their benefits against an attack of opportunity.
5. As Joel, I want to remove Internal Injury using its two-action ability, so that I can choose between immediate action cost and end-of-turn damage.
6. As Joel, I want to commit eligible cards or decline commitment, so that I control my investment in each test.
7. As Joel, I want actual random Standard chaos draws and readable symbol consequences, so that outcomes remain uncertain and understandable.
8. As Joel, I want to engage an eligible exhausted enemy or fight it directly, so that legal alternatives remain available.
9. As Joel, I want the bounty payout and remaining actions to update correctly, so that I do not have to track them manually.
10. As Joel, I want to end my turn voluntarily with remaining actions, so that the application does not force a strategy.
11. As Joel, I want illegal or stale choices refused without changing play, so that a mistaken input cannot corrupt the turn.
12. As Joel, I want to undo choices only before crossing new hidden information, so that I can correct an input without rerolling or concealing an outcome.
13. As Joel, I want to save at a pending choice and reopen offline, so that an interruption preserves costs, choices and randomness.
14. As Joel, I want a failed save to leave the live turn unchanged, so that retrying cannot duplicate an effect or change the next draw.
15. As Joel, I want to understand why damage, horror, clues and resources changed, so that I can follow the rules without administering them.
16. As Joel, I want Next/Previous replay moments and camera override, so that I can inspect and narrate the turn.
17. As Joel, I want readable substitutes when artwork is unavailable, so that presentation assets do not block play.
18. As Joel, I want existing Jacqueline saves and recordings preserved with an explicit compatible reopening path, so that the new experiment does not destroy prior work.
19. As Joel, I want a new attempt to preserve the previous record, so that restarting cannot silently replace it.
20. As an agent playtester, I want the same player observations and legal choices as the tabletop, so that automation tests the actual rules authority.

## Implementation Decisions

### Prepared position

This is a deliberately constructed position consistent with the cited local rules. It does not prove that scenario setup or a preceding campaign history reaches it.

| Element | Prepared value |
| --- | --- |
| Campaign context | Original Gathering, Standard, three investigators, Act 1 Trapped and agenda 1; no agenda threshold or pending scenario trigger. |
| Turn boundary | Investigation phase, Tony is the active investigator after turn-begin; no pending test, spawn or reaction. Stop after his end-of-turn effects and turn marker, before selecting the next investigator or advancing a phase. |
| Location and clues | Only the Study is in play, revealed; six clues on it, none held by investigators; no connecting destination is available. |
| Tony | Printed attributes, nine health/five sanity, zero damage/horror, five resources, three ordinary actions and his unused restricted additional action. No weapon or other optional asset. |
| Tony's hand | One On the Hunt, original level-zero version. |
| Tony's threat area | Internal Injury, already resolved into play. |
| Bounties | Bounty Contracts in play with five; one bounty on the Ghoul. |
| Enemy | One ready, undamaged Ghoul Minion, engaged with Tony. |
| Other investigators | Patrice and Jacqueline are at the Study with empty hands and no available response or relevant asset ability. Jacqueline's reaction is already used this round; her two Arcane Research permanents and two starting horror remain inert but preserved. Neither companion takes a turn inside this task. |
| Tony's draw pile | Preserve the pinned 35-copy slot multiset: Contracts, Injury and the hand card are outside the draw pile, leaving 32 cards. Its fixed hidden prefix is Guts, Guts, On the Hunt; the remaining 29 cards retain their identities and quantities in a stable private order. They are unreachable during this task. |
| Chaos bag | Original Standard composition: +1; two 0; three −1; two −2; −3; −4; two skull; cultist; tablet; auto-fail; elder sign. No curses or blessings. |

Fixed incidental values and private ordering are reversible fixture choices, not new campaign rules. Other unresolved campaign preparation, including the companions' basic-weakness selections, is not simulated or claimed complete. No missing input may become a silently invented live ability.

### Legal behavior and closure

- Offer basic Fight, Evade, Investigate, Draw, Resource, Engage when eligible, Internal Injury's ability and voluntary End turn. End turn is available at a legal action boundary, never to skip a pending test or mandatory consequence; saving and closing can interrupt a pending choice without advancing it. Refuse invalid targets, unaffordable costs, inappropriate commitments and stale revisions without mutation.
- The first Fight or Engage qualifying for Tony's restricted action automatically consumes it. The player does not choose ordinary-action payment instead. The extra action cannot pay for Injury, Evade, Investigate, Draw or Resource. Zero ordinary actions does not end the turn while a legal bonus action remains.
- Internal Injury costs two ordinary actions. A ready engaged Ghoul makes one attack of opportunity for that activation, not one per action spent. Removing it prevents its end-of-turn damage. Leaving it causes one direct damage when Tony ends his turn, including an early end.
- Basic Fight uses combat five against fight two and deals one damage on success. Evade uses agility two against evade two; success exhausts and disengages the Ghoul. Investigate uses intellect three against Study shroud two; success discovers one clue. Ordinary tests preserve optional commitments and their discard at test completion.
- An exhausted Ghoul can be engaged and remains exhausted. Tony can fight it without engaging first. He cannot engage an enemy already engaged with him. Bounty Contracts' payout after Tony defeats the Ghoul is mandatory.
- On the Hunt can contribute its combat/intellect icon to applicable tests; its fast event requires a mythos-phase encounter draw and is not playable here. Multiple eligible copies may be committed. Guts' willpower icons match no reachable test, so it cannot be committed and its draw effect is unreachable. No reachable card grants further actions, card draws, searches or reshuffles.
- There are at most three ordinary Draw actions, so the three-card prefix closes the reachable hand inventory. There are at most three successful investigations, insufficient for the six-clue act threshold. Movement, act advancement and deeper deck behavior are unavailable because of those rules and state, not arbitrary disabled choices.
- Every Standard face is supported: numeric modifiers use their printed values; skull is minus the number of Ghouls at the location, including exhausted Ghouls; cultist is −1 and deals one horror on failure; tablet is −2 and deals one damage if a Ghoul is at the location; auto-fail fails the test; Tony's elder sign is +2 and adds one bounty to Contracts, not resources or the enemy. Return physical tokens at the correct test-end boundary. Six starting bounties is not a maximum.
- From this exact undamaged/unhorrified position, defeat is unreachable. Maximum damage is eight: a tablet bonus Fight, three tablet investigations each preceded by an opportunity attack, and Injury at turn end. Maximum horror is three: each ordinary action can cause opportunity horror or a failed cultist Evade, but cultist Fight/Investigate succeeds at the base values. These bounds must remain valid for the supplied state; do not give Tony immunity or suppress harmful choices.
- Another investigator could use Injury's action ability on their own turn at this location. Companions cannot spend actions during Tony's turn. Do not generalize this case into an owner-only rule or a blanket prohibition on other investigators' reactions.

### Player path, continuity and presentation

The rules authority remains observation plus revision-bound player choice, shared by native UI and driver. A local turn implementation is sufficient. Ordinary internal decomposition, algorithms, record-kind separation and fixture representation remain delegated; no generalized action engine, card interpreter or migration framework is selected.

Use session-owned randomness with unbiased selection respecting physical token multiplicities. Privileged deterministic draws support checks but are not player operations. Player observations omit future deck order and random state. Save candidate state before installing it or displaying its consequences. Failure leaves the live state and future random sequence unchanged. Retry and reopening must not reroll, repeat costs or repeat opportunity attacks.

Autosave committed decisions and permit manual saves at pending choices. Reopen the exact continuation, including held tokens, commitments, action availability, enemy state and random state. Interrupted animation has no rules authority. Replay consumes recorded observations/events rather than executing current rules or drawing randomness.

Honor the play contract's undo boundary: reverse a deterministic committed choice only when no intervening card/token revelation would be crossed. Restore the whole affected state, persist a new revision and retain an intelligible undo history. A reveal is a barrier when committed, before its animation completes. Never truncate an exported recording or reinterpret replay Back as undo.

Preserve existing Jacqueline records and an explicit tested compatible reopening path, using the retained experiment mode or a pinned compatible build. New turn records must identify their own supported input/source/application identity. Corrupt, mismatched or unsupported records fail visibly with originals intact. No automatic migration promise. New attempts preserve earlier records; saving in replay cannot overwrite live state.

Present actions, remaining action types, hand, enemy condition, bounties, clues, health/sanity and meaningful consequences in the native tabletop. Explain in ordinary game language; do not expose fixture machinery as gameplay controls. Preserve manual camera control and step-driven replay with manual override of automatic camera following. Reuse the prepared asset collection contract for exact selected new art and readable substitutes. Runtime never reads the source archive. New assets require selection, preparation and verification before dependence; image/font bytes stay outside Git.

## Testing Decisions

Use the existing highest behavioral seam: player observations and submitted legal choices through the same authority as the UI. Existing decision tests and actual driver-process save/reopen tests are the prior art. Check external available choices and consequences against the independent expectations below, rather than private type layout or output generated by the implementation under test.

| Witness | Independent expectation |
| --- | --- |
| Two successful Fights, then remove Injury | Bonus action, one ordinary action, then two ordinary actions. Ghoul defeated, one bounty paid as a resource, no opportunity damage/horror and no Injury damage. |
| Remove Injury first, then two successful Fights | Two ordinary actions and one opportunity attack (one damage/one horror), then bonus and last ordinary action. Same defeat/payout. |
| Resource three times while engaged | Gain three resources and take three damage/three horror. Bonus Fight remains. Voluntary End then adds one Injury damage; no enemy-phase attack occurs. |
| Evade, then Engage or Fight | Successful Evade exhausts/disengages. Engage can spend the bonus without readying; Fight does not require re-engaging. Both preserve the exhausted state until relevant removal. |
| Investigate with numeric −2 | Base three fails against two; one On the Hunt commitment makes four minus two succeed. Both provoke an opportunity attack first if ready/engaged. |
| Commitment and costs | Refuse Guts, On the Hunt's event timing, own-engaged Engage and Injury funded by one ordinary plus one restricted action. Permit appropriate On the Hunt subsets and decline. |
| Draw inventory | Three draws expose exactly Guts, Guts, On the Hunt. A fourth ordinary Draw is refused. Future cards never appear in player observations. |
| Every chaos face | Exercise numerical modifiers, auto-fail and each source-derived symbol effect against the applicable tests, including exhausted versus defeated Ghoul and changing Contracts bounty count. Use fixed independent token injections; statistical sampling alone is not a rules oracle. |
| Turn ending | Early end is legal; apply Injury once if present; stop at the declared turn boundary without running companions or enemy phase. |
| Undo | Reverse deterministic consequences before a reveal; refuse crossing a committed draw or token reveal, including during animation and after reopening; preserve visible history and exported records. |
| Failed-save retry | Inject persistence failure before installation, then retry: same pending state and next draw as uninterrupted play; no duplicated action cost, attack or commitment. |
| Fresh-process continuation | Save during a pending skill test, exit, reopen in a separate process and finish. Match committed choices/outcomes and unrevealed continuation against an uninterrupted control. |
| Recorded replay | Navigate actual stored moments forward/back, then return to unchanged live state. No new randomness, reconstructed outcome or live save from the past. |
| Legacy and refusal | Reopen a baseline Jacqueline save/record through the declared compatible path. Corrupt/incompatible records retain their bytes and receive a clear refusal. |

Run the repository check command for implementation. Inspect the affected native paths with isolated saves/settings using existing checked capture/input tools, including actual art and substitutes. Headless text assertions, screenshots, source fidelity and human experience retain their separate limits. Do not consume the owner allowance on avoidable infrastructure retries.

The two owner sessions inspect materially different choices: a threat-removal turn and a turn that evades or accepts opportunity costs while pursuing another benefit, with interruption and narrated replay included. Automation supplies technical evidence; only Joel judges clarity, pacing, control burden and whether the task is worth playing. Their combined ceiling is 40 minutes including retries. These runs establish only this experiment, not sustained return-use or general engine fitness.

## Out of Scope

Full scenario setup or progression; subsequent turns/phases; whole-deck random play; unresolved weaknesses/upgrades; extra weapons, Quick Thinking or other additional-action chains; Olive/Dark Prophecy; companion turns; general content support; runtime LLM rules interpretation; reusable engine/DSL/framework; automatic record migration; new native diagnostic tools; unrelated refactors; video encoding/upload; paid services. Impossible branches in this exact position are justified above, not disabled legal behavior.

This issue publishes the selected bounded spec with `ready-for-agent`; it does not start implementation. No commit, push, PR, merge or release is authorized by this spec publication. The finished implementation returns as one exact reviewed patch with source, technical and native evidence plus Joel's separate acceptance.

## Further Notes

### Selection, baseline and authority

Joel explicitly selected this direction and scope during the grill-with-docs interview, then invoked to-spec to publish this spec. The prepared testing approach was carried forward with that handoff: one shared player-observation/choice seam, fresh-process continuity and separate native/human inspection. No new framework or technical approval gate is introduced.

Implementation baseline: `fc37a4fefc9e2de86a12a142a3464747095fc0f7`. The source preparation artifact used for this synthesis has SHA-256 `f1fb5f264e91c3a96823a5cdea8f28ea4468ee8fcbce4220bec3ca2e06cbc74a`; the prepared glossary has SHA-256 `3b9f5c57549958962fc06aa22ee801b7c64c3594a74556c10bafc3d273b5c2c1`. Both remain local uncommitted inputs at publication. This issue includes the complete contract and evidence bindings, so readiness does not depend on a missing GitHub document link.

The [accepted assessment](https://github.com/joeloverbeck/arkham-unfolded/issues/1) and [accepted Jacqueline experiment](https://github.com/joeloverbeck/arkham-unfolded/issues/2#issuecomment-6449874991) are prior evidence, not open blockers or parents with unfinished work. Recent maintenance #13, #14 and #20 is closed. No open issue or PR duplicated this task at publication.

Joel accepted the recommendation to prepare one spec for a complete Tony turn from a prepared Gathering position. He then accepted the proposed unarmed Tony/Ghoul/Internal Injury position, fixed hidden deck order, genuinely random Standard chaos draws, and a prospective implementation ceiling of **24 aggregate active engineering hours**, including source preflight, implementation, verification and reviews, plus **two owner sessions of at most 20 minutes each**, including retries. The incumbent is the accepted Jacqueline skill-test experiment plus manual administration for everything outside it. A local implementation of this one prepared turn is the least-complex credible intervention. The broader alternative, a playable Gathering segment, combines more unresolved content and scenario obligations. The narrower alternative, scripted chaos outcomes, would expose less ordinary tactical uncertainty. Neither alternative is selected.

One implementation item returns for disposition at its cap. It does not create authority for further maintenance, additional experiments or a general engine. Prior maintenance selections and their allocation history remain intact; only the particular human-inspected effect can establish its own result.

### Source baseline and independent derivation

title: Compression Node: Decompress evaluates dynamic binary field expression using item index 0 for all items
raw_evidence_quote:
Compression Node: Decompress evaluates dynamic binary field expression using item index 0 for all items ### Bug Description

Bug Description

The Compression node's Decompress operation appears to evaluate dynamic expressions in the "Input Binary Field(s)" parameter only against the first input item.

When processing multiple items containing different binary property names, the node may decompress an unintended file instead of the file selected by the expression.

The execution completes successfully without reporting an error
source_text:
Compression Node: Decompress evaluates dynamic binary field expression using item index 0 for all items ### Bug Description

Bug Description

The Compression node's Decompress operation appears to evaluate dynamic expressions in the "Input Binary Field(s)" parameter only against the first input item.

When processing multiple items containing different binary property names, the node may decompress an unintended file instead of the file selected by the expression.

The execution completes successfully without reporting an error.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Create multiple input items containing gzip-compressed binary files.

  2. Ensure the same target filename is stored under different binary property names in each item.

  3. Add a Compression node with the operation set to Decompress.

  4. Set "Input Binary Field(s)" to the following expression:

{{ Object.keys($binary).find(
  key => $binary[key].fileName === 'target.json.gz'
) }}

  1. Execute the node with all items in a single execution.

Example Input (Synthetic Data)

The following example uses generic filenames and illustrates the observed behavior.

Item | data0 | data1 | data2 -- | -- | -- | -- 1 | other-a.json.gz | target.json.gz | other-b.json.gz 2 | target.json.gz | other-b.json.gz | other-a.json.gz 3 | other-a.json.gz | other-b.json.gz | target.json.gz 4 | other-b.json.gz | target.json.gz | other-a.json.gz

Expected Behavior

The expression should be evaluated independently for each input item.

Expected binary property selection:

Item 1: data1
Item 2: data0
Item 3: data2
Item 4: data1

Expected decompressed output:

Item 1: target.json
Item 2: target.json
Item 3: target.json
Item 4: target.json

Actual Behavior

The node appears to reuse the binary property selected for the first item (data1) across all items.

For the synthetic example above, this would result in:

Item 1: target.json
Item 2: other-b.json
Item 3: other-b.json
Item 4: target.json

This matches the failure pattern observed during execution: files located under the binary property selected for the first item are decompressed, even when they do not match the requested filename.

No error is raised if the incorrectly selected binary property exists.

Suspected Root Cause

Source code inspection suggests that the Decompress operation uses a hardcoded item index when evaluating the binary property parameter.

File:

packages/nodes-base/nodes/Compression/Compression.node.ts

Relevant implementation:

for (let i = 0; i < length; i++) {
  try {
    if (operation === 'decompress') {
      const binaryPropertyNames = this.getNodeParameter(
        'binaryPropertyName', 0
      )
        .split(',')
        .map((key) => key.trim());

The getNodeParameter() call explicitly uses index 0, despite executing inside a loop over the input items.

Later, binary data is accessed using the current item index:

const binaryData = this.helpers.assertBinaryData(
  i, binaryPropertyName
);

This appears to cause the following behavior:

  1. The parameter expression is evaluated using the first input item.

  2. The resulting binary property name is reused for subsequent items.

  3. Binary data is retrieved from the current item using that property name.

  4. If the property exists but contains another file, that file is decompressed instead.

Source Code Reference

https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/master/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Compression/Compression.node.ts

The hardcoded index was identified during source inspection of n8n 2.33.5, n8n 2.45.4, and the master branch.

This does not imply that every intermediate release was independently verified.

Suggested Fix

The Decompress operation should evaluate dynamic binary property expressions against the corresponding input item.

A possible correction would be:

const binaryPropertyNames = this.getNodeParameter(
  'binaryPropertyName', i
)
  .split(',')
  .map((key) => key.trim());

However, the Compress operation already uses version-dependent item index handling:

let binaryPropertyNameIndex = 0;

if (nodeVersion > 1) {
  binaryPropertyNameIndex = i;
}

A similar approach may be appropriate for Decompress to preserve compatibility with older node versions.

The exact implementation should be evaluated by the maintainers.

Suggested Regression Test

A regression test could use synthetic binary items containing different compressed files.

The test should verify that:

  • Dynamic binary field expressions are evaluated for each individual item.

  • The correct compressed file is selected regardless of binary property ordering.

  • No unintended file is decompressed.

  • Existing workflows and older node versions remain compatible.

Workaround

Normalize the target binary property before passing items to the Compression node.

For example, a Code node can select the desired file by filename and assign it to a fixed binary property:

return $input.all().map((item, index) => {
  const entry = Object.entries(item.binary ?? {}).find(
    ([key, file]) => file.fileName === 'target.json.gz'
  );

  if (!entry) {
    throw new Error(
      `Target file not found in item ${index + 1}`
    );
  }

  return {
    json: item.json,
    binary: {
      data: entry[1]
    },
    pairedItem: { item: index }
  };
});

The Compression node can then use the fixed binary field data.

AI Assistance Disclosure

AI assistance was used to investigate the issue, identify the suspected root cause, and propose a potential fix.

Specifically, ChatGPT (OpenAI) assisted with:

  • Analyzing the observed execution behavior.

  • Identifying the relationship between binary property names and incorrectly decompressed files.

  • Reviewing the relevant n8n source code.

  • Identifying the hardcoded item index as the suspected cause.

  • Suggesting a possible code correction and regression test.

  • Drafting and anonymizing this issue report.

The reported failure pattern originates from actual n8n execution observations.

The reproduction example in this report is synthetic and has not been independently executed as an automated test.

The proposed fix has not been implemented or validated in a running n8n instance.

The maintainers should independently verify the diagnosis and evaluate compatibility requirements before applying a change.

### To Reproduce 1. Create multiple input items, each containing several gzip-compressed binary files. 2. Ensure that the same target file (`target.json.gz`) is stored under different binary property names (`data0`, `data1`, `data2`, etc.) across items. 3. Add a Compression node and select the **Decompress** operation. 4. Set **Input Binary Field(s)** to: ```javascript {{ Object.keys($binary).find(key => $binary[key].fileName === 'target.json.gz') }} ``` 5. Execute the node with multiple items simultaneously. **Actual result:** The node appears to evaluate the expression only against the first item and reuses the resulting binary property name for all subsequent items. This causes incorrect files to be decompressed when the binary property names differ. ### Expected behavior The Compression node should evaluate the **Input Binary Field(s)** expression independently for each input item. Each item should have its own matching binary property selected, regardless of the property's name or position. In this example, every output item should contain the decompressed `target.json` file, and no unrelated files should be decompressed. ### Debug Info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.33.5 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 24.18.0 - nodeEnv: development - database: postgres - executionMode: regular - concurrency: -1 ## storage - binaryMode: filesystem ### Operating System unknown ### n8n Version 2.33.5 ### Node.js Version 24.18.0 ### Database PostgreSQL ### Execution mode main (default) ### Hosting n8n cloud

CERTIFICATION L5 — E2E Chromium complet des marchés KM/CM/CG/DJ et P1–P7
## Mission
Faire évoluer la baseline lecture seule de la PR #2901 en une véritable certification métier staging des marchés, avec navigateur Chromium, données canoniques, vraies transitions P1–P7 et preuve de chaque acteur/rôle/scénario. L'objectif est une matrice complètement couverte et verte avant GO, sans faux PASS.

## Matrix complète
- Marchés : KM / CM / CG / DJ, y compris marché sans activité, non prêt, suspendu, et tests d'isolation.
- Rôles : admin, market_operator, finance, sourcing, agent_hub, agent_relais, agent_transitaire ; rôles non autorisés testés négativement.
- Viewports : 1440 et 390.
- P1 : Sourcing → décision → Raffinerie → Catalogue → prix local LOCAL_ACTIVE → exposition ENABLED → boutique.
- P2 : commande, paiement, liens Order 360, progression, remise.
- P3 : achat, PO, fournisseur, paiement, réception physique.
- P4 : Hub mutualisé, colis, expédition pays, douane, relais et remise.
- P5 : Stripe sandbox signé/cash, garde, dépôt, rapprochement, settlement.
- P6 : CDR estimé vs constaté, marge finalisée, revue humaine de prix et absence d'automodification.
- P7 : PROVISIONING → readiness → ACTIVE / SUSPENDED / CLOSED terminal ; délégation, capacités effectives, livrabilité prouvée.
- Négatifs obligatoires : scope interdit, prix non actif, exposition désactivée, marché non prêt, route non prouvée, devise non supportée, idempotence, données non attribuables, inconnue ≠ zéro.

## Exécution et preuve
1. D'abord lancer la batterie **lecture seule** Chromium L5 de #2901 sur le véritable staging ; vérifier SHA /health/version.
2. Étendre aux véritables scénarios mutationnels **uniquement sur staging isolé autorisé**, avec fixtures identifiées par run_id, guards de cible et nettoyage sélectif sans toucher les données catalogues/prix/de production.
3. Pour chaque cellule applicable : identifiants de provenance, attendu indépendant, état SQL propriétaire, API, capture et trace Chromium, clic, résultat, retour contextuel, cas négatif, statut PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_PROVEN.
4. Mettre les artefacts, causes racines et tickets de correction en regard de chaque anomalie. Faire des PR ciblées et rejouer la même matrice.
5. Aucune certification globale verte tant qu'une cellule obligatoire reste BLOCKED, NOT_PROVEN ou FAIL. Pas d'auto-merge des corrections sans preuve.

## DoD
- Couverture des menus N1/N2/N3 et de tous les liens contextuels par rôle et viewport, aucune destination orpheline.
- Vérification de vérité API / source canonique / UI sur tous les KPI sensibles.
- Matrice scénarios × rôle × marché × viewport exhaustive ; exclusions explicitement justifiées et acceptées, pas de skip vert.
- Tous les E2E nécessaires exécutés sur la version staging réellement servie, tous verts ; preuves des cas négatifs et du cleanup.
- GO/NO GO fonctionnel et technique signé, résultat reproductible sur le même SHA.

Références : #2901, docs/doctrine/KOMERCE_CARTOGRAPHIE_PROCESSUS_P1_P7.md, docs/recette/RCT1_GOLDEN_P1_P7_CONVERGENCE_20261021.md.

## Contrat executable P1 — une chaîne fournisseur → produit vendable

Ce parcours est un **seul scénario corrélé**, et non cinq PASS séparés. L'initiateur utilise un article fournisseur authentique, un run d'import dédié et un identifiant de produit suivi jusqu'à la boutique. RCT1-P1..P5 seuls ne prouvent pas cette filiation. Aucun scénario ne peut attribuer une provenance à un produit préexistant sans preuve de lien.

### Chemin nominal unique, prouvé de bout en bout
1. **Source** : source/provider autorisé, configuration fournisseur et run`_ref` existants, récupération de l'observation réelle ou fixture V2 normalisée sur base jetable ; conserver `supplier_product_id`, source V2, horodatage, quantité de lignes entrantes.
2. **Sourcing** : chaque input classé, décision `TEST/PRIORITY` (équivalent métier KEEP) ou `WATCH/AVOID/LOSS` ou `EXCLUDED`, raisons et événements append-only ; comptabilité `UNACCOUNTED=0`, `OVERFLOW=0`. Un WATCH n'est jamais compté comme prêt Raffinerie.
3. **Remise à la Raffinerie / Catalogue** : `sourcing_candidate_id` relié au produit `product_ref`, `imported_to_catalog` équivaut uniquement à candidat : `lifecycle_status='candidate'`, `is_active=false`, `is_available=false`, exposition pays nulle.
4. **Raffinerie** : contrat fournisseur V2, enrichissement français, catégorie+sous-catégorie boutique actives, données douanières, media réel, variantes/SKU, Supplier Order Identity complète, revue et preuves source. Les refus restent visibles et traçables, pas de fallback métier silencieux.
5. **Certification catalogue** : `catalog-certification` et `product-publication-guard` PASS avant toute première publication, approbation humaine via le service owner et audit de décision. Une fiche techniquement complète mais sans revue obligatoire doit être bloquée.
6. **Publication globale** : le *même* `product_ref` devient publié dans le catalogue global. Cela **n'autorise aucune exposition marché implicite**.
7. **Prix et marché** : pour KM/CM/CG/DJ selon readiness réelle, autorité pays décide un prix `LOCAL_ACTIVE` dans la devise serveur, puis acteur autorisé choisit l'exposition `ENABLED`; prix et exposition sont des décisions séparées. Pas de devise, de FX ou de coût inventé.
8. **Boutique** : le même SKU commercialisable devient visible dans le marché éligible, avec prix/devise locaux, fiche détaillée et stock/livrabilité conformes ; reste absent ou non achetable pour les autres marchés non autorisés. L'étape suivante est un checkout réel sandbox en P2, pas une preuve automatique de paiement.

### Scénarios négatifs non négociables
- `WATCH`, rejet, quarantaine, doublon : raison et comptage, **aucune publication**.
- Source V2 absente, catégorie invalide, traduction FR incomplète, SKU/SOI incomplet ou média non validé : garde publication refusée, sans création d'un produit vendable.
- Produit candidat et/ou simplement publié globalement : jamais visible en boutique par défaut.
- Prix pays absent/non actif, pays suspendu/non ready, exposition DISABLED, acteur non habilité : aucun achat.
- Défaillance de FX : candidat fournisseur conservé dans un état différé explicite, sans rejet abusif ni tarif inventé.
- Réexécution idempotente : aucune création de doublon produit/SKU ou publication supplémentaire.
- Un seul identifiant source relié à deux produits non justifiés, ou un input disparu : FAIL.

### Preuves obligatoires, même provenance
`certification_run_id → import_run_ref → source_ref/provider → supplier_product_id → sourcing_candidate_id → product_ref → variant/SKU/SOI → publication_decision_id → market_id → local_price_decision → exposure → storefront_url`.

Pour chaque frontière, garder **avant / action via owner / après**, version déployée, rôle autorisé, API + SQL, capture/trace Chromium 1440 et 390, raison de refus et prochaine action. Les opérations mutationnelles requièrent une **base staging de recette isolée et gardée** ; le READ ONLY #2901 ne peut pas effectuer P1 mutationnel. Pas de publication automatique en production, pas de RESET global, pas de détournement des prix ou du stock.

### Gate P1
**P1 = PASS** seulement si l'objet traçable termine le parcours source → boutique pour au moins un marché prêt et si les refus et l'absence de visibilité dans les autres marchés sont prouvés. Les étapes partielles, les datasets historiques juxtaposés, les mocks Playwright et les fixtures sans ancêtre réel restent `NOT_PROVEN`. Si aucun marché n'est prêt, traiter la cause de readiness comme un blocage explicite ; ne pas activer artificiellement le marché pour obtenir le vert.

Sources de vérité : `docs/doctrine/DOCTRINE_CERTIFICATION_CATALOGUE_SOURCING.md`, `services/sourcing-certification.js`, `services/catalog-certification.js`, `services/catalog-approval.js`, `services/market-local-price-activation-service.js`, `services/catalog-market-exposure-service.js`.

source_text:
HABITAT-VERTICAL-001: co-design factory, product, and end-to-end supply chain for repairable household goods
## Mission

Extend [SLEEP-PRODUCT-001 #8039](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/8039) from an excellent product concept to an evidence-bearing **factory-to-product vertical**: upstream materials and suppliers, conversion, components, assembly, quality, utilities, workforce, facility design, distribution, repair/refurbishment and material recovery.

The intended paradigm shift is product–process–factory–supply-chain co-design. Do not optimize a mattress topper, furniture article or garment in isolation and only afterward discover that its materials, tools, factory layout, labor model, energy/water needs, transport, repair path or economics make it infeasible.

This issue is an integration / benchmark profile. It is **not** a new generic MRP/ERP, scheduling engine, process semantics, factory ontology, material registry, inventory ledger, digital twin, commissioning engine, or execution-authority system.

## Existing owners to compose (avoid duplication)

- Symthaea **MFG-PROC-000 #5686** and its children: process identity, process capability, recipe, process plan, pre/postconditions, manufacturability and process qualification.
- Symthaea **MFG-LIFE-000 #5705**: lifecycle/circularity projection.
- Symthaea **BUILT-ENV-001 #6032**, **BUILT-CX-001 #6037**, **BUILT-BIM-001 #6036**, **BUILT-SITE-001 #6034**, **BUILT-ROB-PILOT-001 #6040**: site/facility/workcell realization, commissioning, model exchange and low-risk demonstrator.
- Symthaea **FACTORY-OPS-001 #7677**: reuse the existing capability-constrained deterministic scheduling direction; do not create a second operations-research scheduler.
- Symthaea **ENG-DESIGN-001 #6005**, **ENG-DESIGN-003 #6091**, **ENG-MAT/materials**, structural, thermal/thermofluids, equipment, energy, water, metrology, reliability and safety owners as applicable.
- Mycelix **MFG-EVID-001 #3084** and **MFG-PROC-001 #3085**: design revisions/BOM-to-unit evidence, supplier/resource offers, routings/work orders, production and lot genealogy.
- Mycelix **LOG-COMMONS-001 #4900** and existing Supply Chain / Manufacturing functions: federated logistics and participant-owned operational/provenance facts.
- Mycelix carries operational events and multi-party provenance; Symthaea owns engineering meaning, analysis and scoped qualification. No cross-project claim may silently promote an offer, plan, signature, simulation or event into physical capability or product qualification.

## Initial vertical: human-habitat goods

First use the modular mattress topper from #8039, with two follow-on product profiles:
1. a flat-pack desk or storage unit;
2. one repairable everyday garment / workwear item.

Keep the first physical pilot to a low-risk, small-scale textile/converting-and-assembly cell. Furniture and garment cases may initially be synthetic process/fixture cases until their dedicated material and product-function evidence exists. The common vertical contract should accommodate all three without pretending that mattress comfort, furniture strength and garment fit are interchangeable.

## End-to-end value chain to represent

Use exact identified stages and evidence-bearing transitions; do not let existence of an upstream material claim establish downstream product capability.

```
demand / user requirements / product variants
-> product architecture + design revision + test requirements
-> bill of materials + process plan + manufacturing capability demands
-> upstream raw/secondary feedstocks and supplier claims
-> material processing / grade qualification
-> fabric / cover / layer / panel / fastener / component production
-> inbound logistics, lot receipt, inspection and quarantine/acceptance
-> workcell routing, labor/tools/equipment and production plan
-> transformation, assembly and intermediate inspection/hold/rework
-> final article identity + acceptance/quality evidence
-> packaging, storage, outbound transport and delivery
-> use, maintenance, replacement parts and repair
-> return triage, refurbishment/remanufacture/reuse
-> material recovery with actual route/grade evidence or disposal
-> observed demand/defect/repair/recovery feedback into redesign
```

Every transformation must retain input identities, material state/grade, quantity and unit semantics, process profile/revision, facility/equipment/workcell identity, responsible execution evidence, inspection observations, outputs/yield/scrap/byproducts, and uncertainty where relevant. A process plan is not an executed process; a completed operation is not an accepted article; recyclability is not recovered feedstock.

## Factory design scope

Create an evidence-bound reference-design profile for an SME-scale, modular microfactory/workshop. Do not start with an expensive, fully autonomous "lights-out" factory. Compare manual, assisted, and appropriately automated layouts where all have the same stated demand, quality, staffing, and safety requirements.

The factory model should include:

- Site and facility: site/geotechnical applicability references; spatial layout; receiving, quarantine, storage, workcells, inspection, finished goods, repair/returns and waste/recovery zones; access, egress and expansion constraints.
- Utilities: electrical demand and quality, thermal conditioning, ventilation/dust extraction where needed, lighting, water and wastewater if process-relevant, data/communications, compressed air if justified, backup/common-mode dependency assumptions.
- Equipment/workcell: exact equipment and tool identities, capability envelope, process/material applicability, maintenance/calibration status, cycle/setup time distributions or bounded ranges, changeover and inspection needs.
- Material flow: travel distance/time, handling damage, WIP buffers, storage conditions, lot segregation, ergonomic handling, packaging and reverse flows.
- Workforce: required skills, training pathways, accessible workstations, workload and ergonomic constraints; no optimization that treats injury exposure, worker dignity or legal labor obligations as a compensable cost.
- Environment and safety: domain-appropriate guarding, fire/egress, dust/noise/chemical exposure, occupational safety and building-code review; these must be supplied by qualified owners/professionals, not guessed from a digital layout.
- Facility lifecycle: commissioning, observation, maintenance, calibration, repair, change impact and recommissioning. Installed, powered or successfully started is not the same as commissioned under requirements.
- Local capability and sourcing: separate local labor/value-added, locally available commodity inputs, imported specialty materials/parts, single points of failure and recovery options; do not equate "assembled locally" with full local supply-chain closure.

A site/factory simulation may compare candidate layouts and utility profiles, but does not grant permit, construction, safety, commissioning, or equipment execution authority.

## Proposed benchmark framework

All numbers below are **proposed target directions**, not current results or universal industry thresholds. Freeze metric definitions, data boundaries and baselines before interpreting outcomes.

### 1. Traceability and qualification integrity
- 100% of selected critical inputs in the pilot must link from received supplier lot through process/inspection events to the finished article or explicitly recorded scrap/rework.
- Every output must bind exact product revision, BOM, process-plan revision, material lots, workcell profile and disposition.
- 100% of deliberately unknown, stale, unqualified or mismatched critical prerequisites must be blocked from a qualified-pass state.
- Target recall/containment query: identify all affected units from a seeded input-lot fault in under 5 minutes on the bounded pilot corpus; report corpus size and hardware/runtime.
- Track supplier substitution, source license/specification, freshness and approval as independent fields.

### 2. Production flow and economic performance
- Establish baselines for end-to-end lead time, touch time, queue time, setup/changeover, WIP, first-pass yield, rework, scrap, delivered cost and on-time-in-full delivery.
- Benchmark deterministic scheduling against a simple documented baseline for the same orders, skills, resource capacities and calendars. Feasibility must be exact; optimization quality can be measured separately.
- Target a 20% reduction in delivered cost versus a named functional reference for the selected product where feasible. Include materials, yield loss, labor, consumables, depreciation/capacity allocation, QA, maintenance/spares, energy, water where applicable, packaging, freight, returns, tax/duty and replacement burden. Publish assumptions and sensitivity.
- Proposed pilot improvement gate after a valid measured baseline: reduce order lead time or WIP by 15–20% without worsening safety, quality, worker loading or service level. If the synthetic model alone shows improvement, label it a simulation result and validate it physically later.

### 3. Resource use and environmental performance
- Report metered or explicitly modeled energy per accepted functional unit; distinguish idle/base load, process energy and facility utilities.
- Report process-water withdrawal/consumption and wastewater only where applicable; do not invent a water benefit for a dry process.
- Track input mass, accepted output, scrap, rework, packaging, byproducts and recovered material mass with an explicit balance and measurement uncertainty.
- Compare lifecycle impact only with a declared ISO 14040/14044-compatible goal/scope, functional unit, boundary, allocation choices, data quality and sensitivity. Never infer environmental superiority from a recycled-content percentage alone.
- Target at least 15% lower energy per accepted unit from a frozen baseline as an exploration goal, not a release requirement until metering and quality equivalence are shown.

### 4. Facility and resilience
- Compare layouts on material travel, throughput, ergonomic exposure, egress/access, inspection separation, utility demand, changeover flexibility and space for repair/recovery flows.
- Run supply/operations stress cases: a critical supplier lot rejection, alternate supplier with different lead time/grade, machine outage, power interruption, water interruption if relevant, workforce-skill absence, transport disruption, and demand mix change.
- Quantify lost output, backlog, recovery time, service impact and cost for each disruption. Do not use a vague "resilience score" without declared scenarios.
- Show that a modular cell can add/remove a workcell or change product mix without corrupting lineage, qualification or resource-capability claims.
- Commissioning and operational qualification remain separate gates; a planned factory layout is not a commissioned factory.

### 5. Maintenance, workforce and circularity
- Track planned/unplanned downtime, maintenance time, calibration expiry, spare-part lead time, time-to-diagnose and repair, training time and skills coverage.
- Target replacement of the common wear component within the product-specific benchmark, with documented tools/parts and trained-operator conditions.
- Quantify jobs/skill hours and ergonomic risk indicators without reducing human flourishing to simple throughput per worker.
- Report return triage, repair/refurbishment yield, product/component reuse, material recovery and disposal separately. Count recovery only when a real route accepts that material grade and condition.
- Include a training and operator-feedback loop; workers must be able to stop, challenge or annotate a plan without retaliation encoded into the software.

## Machine-readable benchmark corpus and hostile controls

The first synthetic corpus should include at least:

1. Valid single supplier → receiving inspection → fabric/cover preparation → sewing/assembly → inspection → accepted article.
2. Exact upstream input lot exists but actual delivered grade is unverified.
3. Substitute supplier has the same marketing name but a different grade/process envelope.
4. A material transformation is marked completed with no required observation; downstream qualification is blocked.
5. A rejected lot contaminates multiple WIP/final units; containment enumerates exactly affected descendants and does not falsely recall unrelated units.
6. Machine/tool says it can perform the process but its qualification, calibration or availability is stale.
7. Scheduler plan omits a required skill, resource or inspection hold point.
8. Queue/setup/cycle data missing but an optimizer reports a precise completion date.
9. Price excludes scrap/yield loss, labor, utilities, freight or returns.
10. Low-carbon/recycled input has unknown provenance, grade or upstream burden; environmental claim stays unresolved.
11. Nominally recyclable multi-material construction has no regionally available recovery route.
12. Factory layout appears feasible while ventilation, emergency egress, guarding or accessibility evidence is absent.
13. Power interruption affects both primary production and inspection/calibration; model must surface the common mode.
14. Product revision changes a seam/layer/fastener/process and stale qualification cannot carry forward.
15. Supplier or carrier cannot share sensitive commercial details; preserve minimum provenance commitments and access control without fabricating data.
16. Repair returns arrive but no capacity/spare part exists; "repairable by design" does not become "repair completed".
17. Mycelix inventory or signed delivery event conflicts with a physical receiving measurement; preserve both source events and an unresolved discrepancy.
18. A complete synthetic path is reported correctly as synthetic-only, never actual production capability.

## Interoperability and external research anchors

Use standards as external mappings and test-method references; do not make an external standard the sole internal identity or assume the pilot is certified.

- [ISA-95 / IEC 62264](https://www.isa.org/standards-and-publications/isa-standards/isa-95-standard): enterprise/logistics to manufacturing operations/control interfaces and vocabulary. Current ISA page includes ANSI/ISA-95.00.01-2025.
- [ISO 22400-1](https://www.iso.org/cms/%20render/live/en/sites/isoorg/contents/data/standard/05/68/56847.html) / [ISO 22400-2](https://www.iso.org/standard/54497.html): manufacturing-operations KPI concepts and formulas; ISO/DIS 22400-2 is under development, so pin the edition actually used.
- [NIST Digital Thread for Manufacturing](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/digital-thread-manufacturing): product definition, manufacturing, inspection and measured result linkage.
- [GS1 Global Traceability Standard](https://www.gs1.org/standards/gs1-global-traceability-standard/current-standard): traceability goals, object IDs, batch/lot versus instance-level identity.
- [ISO 50001](https://www.iso.org/standard/69426.html): energy management framework.
- [ISO 14040](https://www.iso.org/standard/37456.html): lifecycle assessment principles and framework.
- [EU ESPR Regulation (EU) 2024/1781](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/eng) and [European Commission DPP working plan/FAQ](https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/single-market/digital-product-passport/explore-our-faqs_en): model/batch/item-level product data, open interoperable data and product-group-specific implementation. The Commission's 2 July 2026 plan puts textiles in the 2027 workstream, furniture in 2028, and mattresses in 2029; these are planned rule-adoption windows, not proof that every product already requires a DPP.

For an initial South African/regionally adaptable pilot, keep site-, electricity-, water-, labor-, freight-, standards- and supplier-specific assumptions explicit and replaceable. Do not hard-code a US/EU factory model as universal. Before physical implementation, a locally qualified engineering team must review actual zoning, building/fire/occupational-safety requirements, electrical compliance, environmental permits and applicable product standards.

## Execution sequence and acceptance criteria

1. Freeze the exact consumer product candidate, comparable baseline, BOM/material identities, supplier geography, lot rules, production demand, shift/calendar, skill/resource capabilities, test/inspection gates and unit/currency basis.
2. Publish one small synthetic supply-chain + factory manifest that links supplier-lot events to a workcell/process DAG, inspections, product disposition, cost/resource metrics and end-of-life path.
3. Define deterministic calculations and an independent, stdlib-only Rust qualifier using the existing manufacturing contracts/operations-research owners if their exact public API is qualified and usable. Do not implement a second scheduler or manufacturing state machine.
4. Freeze expected outputs and negative-control receipts before running candidate comparisons.
5. Report exactly which contract/corpus tests were run, on which source heads, plus pass/fail and skipped explicitly. A queued/skipped runner is never a pass.
6. Only after synthetic qualification should a low-risk physical pilot be staged: incoming-lot tagging, textile cutting/sewing or cover assembly, low-energy handling, calibrated dimensional/weight checks, and manual operator sign-off. Do not introduce autonomous high-risk equipment or hazardous processing.
7. Plan the factory layout and utility studies through BUILT-ENV/BUILT-CX/BUILT-ROB-PILOT and qualified engineers; no floorplan simulation acts as permission to construct or operate.
8. Publish a reusable follow-on mapping for repairable furniture and clothing, with product-specific tests and safety/legal owners.

## Claim ceiling

Opening this work establishes an architecture and benchmark plan only. It does not establish physical supply, qualified suppliers, product quality, factory readiness, local self-sufficiency, cost competitiveness, environmental superiority, compliance, worker safety, or production capability. Synthetic and modeled outputs remain distinct from measured and independently replicated facts.

source_text:
Show HN: shadowclone, skills learned from your coding agent corrections
shadowclone reads the coding-agent sessions already on your disk, finds where you corrected the agent and turns those corrections into skills your agents load next time. It supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and Antigravity. Every capture source is off by default and has its own consent setting. Why I'm building it? I use multiple harnesses and agents, I extensively use Claud Code and Codex, but I also use Cursor and Antigravity every now and then. I didn't want to have to teach every harness or model the things I taught the other ones between my last session and the current one. I also cannot have my personal rules and preferences in all the repositories I work on because my collaborators may have varying levels of trust with AI and their own preferences. shadowclone helps me build and improve trust with my agents so I can give them more autonomy while running multiple sessions in parallel. --- Who is this for? If you only use Claude or Codex or any one of these, you may not need the shadowclone CLI and the harness and agent you use might already be sufficient. But, if you are like me and work across harnesses and agents, shadowclone will help you avoid repeating your preferences each time. --- Built-in skills and skill builds shadowclone is also great for someone who is just now adopting AI into their coding workflows because it ships with several skills that they can use to customize their agent's behavior. They can equip all the skills, or just some of them, they'll see the "personality" their agent gets from equipping those skills from the `shadowclone wizard`. --- Setup is extremely easy, just ask your Claude Code, or Codex, or another agent - "Set up shadowclone:  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/mai... " --- Privacy shadowclone is free and open source, it uses the MIT license. It doesn't have a subscription, or a server. It just uses your existing agent subscription i.e. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Antigravity, or even your local model via Pi. You can explicitly disable sources, it also redacts any and all sensitive information it uses for learning. --- PR reviews and Cloud bots It can review PRs with the `shadowclone review` command, it ships a guided review skill that will perform a deep review of your code (or someone else's) and produce an HTML document you can annotate, add comments to and submit so your agent can stage a draft review on the PR you are reviewing. --- Evals I performed several evals, I won't describe them here, all of them are available in the repository -  https://github.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/tree/main/evals  --- Comparison to other tools? You can also see how it compares to other tools here -  https://github.com/theonly1me/shadowclone/tree/main#how-shad...

That left-wing politics is part of what makes Het Schip so cool: a "workers' palace", commissioned by a socialist housing association. They believed t
That left-wing politics is part of what makes Het Schip so cool: a "workers' palace", commissioned by a socialist housing association. They believed that working people deserved beautiful homes, with elaborate brickwork and thoughtful design -- not just somewhere cheap to sleep. I love taking visiting friends around Spaarndammerbuurt and into the museum.  https://www.hetschip.nl/en/visitors/locations-opening-hours/...  The museum is amazing, and the gift shop has treasures like this set of historical posters.  https://www.hetschip.nl/webshop/souvenirs/set-historische-po...  The top one, Wilhelmina Drupsteen's "De Vrouw 1813-1913", advertised an exhibition organized by the women's movement, including the campaign for voting rights. Dutch women wouldn't get the vote until 1919. The front poster, Albert Hahn's "Stemt Rood!" ("Vote Red!"), shows a worker raising a pickaxe while pinning down an octopus representing capitalism and its evils. His boot is planted on a tentacle. The lettering names capitalism, anarchy, famine, the suffering of war, and food profiteering. Still painfully relevant issues today. Makes me picture the tentacles of Trump and his owners, Putin and Netanyahu, getting thoroughly stomped and pickaxed by progressives winning democratic elections, and how Iran resoundingly won Trump's war by causing regime change in the United States.  https://x.com/AmoneyResists/status/2118357108643234240  The gift shop doesn't carry the cardboard hats anymore, but I once got one modeled on Het Schip's phallic brick tower, like the Pope's mitre, only too tall to wear indoors.  https://wittebouw.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Amsterdam_He...  They're repairing the wrought-iron "tree of life" on top of the tower, which was accidentally struck during maintenance:  https://www.facebook.com/MuseumHetSchip/posts/pfbid0HQDNrwXU...  >In early 2026, the exterior woodwork of Het Schip (the homes and museum) was painted. While scaffolding components were being hoisted into the courtyard, the tower's finial was struck, leaving it tilted. It took a while, but at the end of October the finial was finally removed for repair. The top is temporarily covered with plastic. >Het Schip was designed by architect Michel de Klerk. The book "Een kunstwerk van baksteen" ("A Work of Art in Brick", 2018) describes the tower: "The tower can be seen as a characteristic Amsterdam School form. It enhanced the building's sculptural qualities and plays an important role in its overall appearance." Housing Department director Arie Keppler was rather surprised by the tower's presence: "There had occasionally been passing remarks about the lack of a tower in this part of the city. Imagine the astonishment when he unrolled his plan!" Then we go to Grand Hotel Amrath in the former Scheepvaarthuis: Amsterdam School extravagance built for shipping companies rather than workers. They've let us explore the lobby, and you can rent the lavish historic meeting rooms. Look at the stained glass and woodwork, and don't miss the paternoster lift.  https://www.amrathamsterdam.com/en/information/history/the-s...  Cafe Batavia 1920 makes a great stop for a drink and lunch in another Amsterdam School building, if it's not overrun with obnoxious British football fans.  https://manchesterhistory.net/architecture/1920/batavia.html  And then Tuschinski, an extravagant mixture of Amsterdam School, Art Deco, and Jugendstil.  https://celluloidjunkie.com/2017/10/19/cinema-of-the-month-p...  There's also De Dageraad, the housing complex designed by Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer around P. L. Takstraat and Burgemeester Tellegenstraat. More beautiful homes for workers, commissioned by a socialist housing association.  https://items.amsterdamse-school.nl/details/objects/54  The best thing to do is to just ride a bike randomly around town all over the place, looking at the architecture and parks and canals. Here are a few of my recent rambling rides, including wandering around Spaarndammerbuurt and Het Schip, and flood filling every road in De Pijp:  https://ebike-safari.com/?lat=52.3905&lon=4.8737&zoom=16&rid...

What I'm seeing here is that Binance has the IT culture of a SV start-up when it should have the IT culture of a bank. Sounds to me like a thug with a
What I'm seeing here is that Binance has the IT culture of a SV start-up when it should have the IT culture of a bank. Sounds to me like a thug with a $10 wrench could've been just as effective. > Lots of people have their work tools setup on their work computer, but not on their personal computer...you don't want your interview performance to suffer because you're using an unfamiliar tool or service... I struggle to come up of even the most absurd interview scenario where the tool makes the difference especially in our field where if a FOSS tool is not standard, then there's a sufficiently powerful free tier (eg., Sublime, IntelliJ). Heck most remote interviews, they take you out of your tools completely and ask you to code on some shared browser-based editor. > That's a very uncommon mindset and worldview. I'm calling HN SV start-up bias. Outside of the startup software eng'g industry, a lot of people exercise very good separation between work tools and personal tools. I know a lawyer, _who's the head of his own law firm,_ bring his personal laptop to the office just so he could purchase tickets during office hours. I think this is also down to a few factors: - SWEs are typically issued high-end machines in contrast to other professions whose standard issue is still 4GB (or 8GB, if you're lucky) RAM. For those professions buying a better personal laptop is a low bar to clear. - SWEs are more efficient when they have admin access to their own machines. Though it begs the question that maybe some inefficiency would've been an acceptable tradeoff to $6.3B. - SWE is one of the professions on the poster for the "Get paid good while working from Bali" lifestyle, wherein BYOD is implied, especially if you are freelancing.
