source_text:
F5 Directory and marketplace: vendor, venue and professional listings, search, enquiries, quotes and reviews
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01). Planning only, no implementation until Jonathan asks. Template: [Feature set spec template and list](<https://linear.app/resnovas/document/feature-set-spec-template-and-list-26b9f78cf17a>). Defaults in section 15 are the recommended options and stand unless Jonathan picks otherwise on the decision card.

## 1. Goal

An organiser finds, compares and engages vendors, venues and freelance professionals inside the same app they plan the event in, and a vendor wins work from a listing they manage in the same app they run their business in.

## 2. Users and jobs

| User | Jobs |
| -- | -- |
| Organiser (planner, producer) | Search by category, location, date, capacity and budget; shortlist; send one enquiry (RFP) to several suppliers; compare quotes side by side; accept one and have it land on the F1 Event; review afterwards |
| Vendor or venue (a business with its own Eventiva tenant) | Publish and maintain a listing (venue rooms, services, packages, media, service area); answer enquiries; send and revise quotes; respond to reviews; see listing performance |
| Professional (freelancer: rigger, LD, sound engineer, stage manager) | Publish a personal profile with skills, qualifications, day rates and availability; receive enquiries and booking offers |
| Attendee or public visitor | Browse the public directory anonymously (read only) |
| Finance | Sees accepted quotes become purchase commitments for F11 |
| Platform moderator (Eventiva staff role) | Verify businesses, handle reports, remove unlawful content, manage the category taxonomy |
| Agent (first-party or external, acting for one of the above) | Everything that person can do, through the same actions, with approvals on anything that contacts another business |

## 3. Market check

Checked 2026-11-01 from public product pages; names stay out of customer-facing copy.

| Tool | What it does | Where Eventiva matches or differs |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Cvent Supplier Network | Venue sourcing for meeting planners: venue profiles with meeting space and room data, one RFP sent to many venues, proposal comparison, venues pay for advertising placement; free for planners | Match: multi-recipient RFP and side-by-side quote comparison, structured space data. Differ: covers vendors and freelancers, not just venues and hotels; the accepted quote lands directly on the event plan, budget and schedule in the same app instead of a separate tool |
| Tagvenue and Peerspace | Consumer and SMB venue marketplaces: rich listings, instant or request booking, platform payments, booking fees or commission, reviews only after a booking | Match: rich listings, verified reviews tied to a completed engagement. Differ: no platform payments or commission in v1 (decision D5-2); bookings run through Eventiva's own quote, F9 and F11 flows |
| The Knot / WeddingWire | Vendor storefronts, lead messaging, paid visibility tiers, reviews with vendor replies | Match: storefront, messaging thread per lead, vendor replies to reviews. Differ: vendors are full Eventiva tenants, so their listing is fed by their real inventory (F6), rosters (F2) and availability (Resnovas/Eventiva#800) rather than a static page |

What nobody does that Eventiva can: the agent sources suppliers from the live event plan (dates, site map capacities, budget lines) and the vendor's agent drafts the quote from the vendor's real stock and crew availability, both through the same audited actions.

Sources: [Cvent Supplier Network](<https://cvent.com/event-marketing-management/cvent-supplier-network>), [Cvent venue advertising](<https://www.cvent.com/uk/supplier-venue/advertising>), [Tagvenue: how booking stays free](<https://www.tagvenue.com/blog/how-tagvenue-keeps-booking-free-for-users/>), [Peerspace vs Tagvenue](<https://www.peerspace.com/resources/peerspace-vs-tagvenue/>), [The Knot for vendors](<https://www.theknot.com/content/the-knot-for-wedding-vendors>), [The Knot Worldwide 2025 vendor products](<https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20250724019488/en/The-Knot-Worldwide-Announces-New-Products-to-Help-Wedding-Professionals-Get-Discovered-and-Connect-with-More-Couples>).

## 4. Capabilities as actions

Every operation is one inventory action (Resnovas/Eventiva#807): Effect Schema input and output, typed errors, permission, approval policy and side-effect class. Namespace `directory.`. Permissions in section 9.

| Action | Input | Output | Permission | Approval | Class |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| directory.listing.create | kind (vendor, venue, professional), name, categories | Listing (draft) | listing:write | none | write |
| directory.listing.update | listingId, patch of profile fields | Listing | listing:write | none | write |
| directory.listing.publish | listingId | Listing (published), receipt | listing:publish | confirm | external |
| directory.listing.unpublish | listingId, reason | Listing | listing:publish | confirm | external |
| directory.listing.archive | listingId | Listing | listing:publish | confirm | write |
| directory.venueRoom.upsert | listingId, VenueRoom (name, area, capacities by layout, rig points, power, access) | VenueRoom | listing:write | none | write |
| directory.venueRoom.remove | venueRoomId | void | listing:write | confirm | write |
| directory.offering.upsert | listingId, Offering (name, description, price from, unit, inclusions) | Offering | listing:write | none | write |
| directory.offering.remove | offeringId | void | listing:write | confirm | write |
| directory.media.attach / detach | listingId, fileId ([EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>)), caption, alt text | MediaItem | listing:write | none | write |
| directory.serviceArea.set | listingId, areas (point plus radius or region codes) | ServiceArea | listing:write | none | write |
| directory.verification.request | listingId, trader details | VerificationCase | listing:publish | none | external |
| directory.verification.decide | caseId, outcome, note | VerificationCase | platform:moderate | none | write |
| [directory.search](<http://directory.search>) | query, kind, categories, location, radius, date range, capacity, budget, sort, cursor | Page of ListingSummary plus ranking explanation | public (anonymous allowed) | none | read |
| directory.listing.get | listingId or slug | Listing (public projection) | public | none | read |
| directory.availability.check | listingId, date range, venueRoomId optional | AvailabilitySignal (available, tentative, unavailable, unknown) | public | none | read |
| directory.shortlist.create / rename / delete | eventId optional (F1 Event), name | Shortlist | shortlist:write | none | write |
| directory.shortlist.add / remove | shortlistId, listingId, note | Shortlist | shortlist:write | none | write |
| directory.enquiry.draft | eventId optional, recipients (listingIds), brief (dates, headcount, budget, requirements, attachments) | Enquiry (draft) | enquiry:write | none | write |
| directory.enquiry.send | enquiryId | Enquiry (sent), one EnquiryRecipient per listing | enquiry:send | confirm (always when more than 5 recipients) | external |
| directory.enquiry.withdraw | enquiryId, reason | Enquiry | enquiry:send | confirm | external |
| directory.enquiry.message | enquiryRecipientId, body, attachments | Message | enquiry:respond (either side) | none for humans, confirm for agents | external |
| directory.enquiry.decline | enquiryRecipientId, reason | EnquiryRecipient | enquiry:respond (vendor side) | none | external |
| directory.quote.create / revise | enquiryRecipientId, line items, validity date, terms | Quote (draft, version n) | quote:write | none | write |
| directory.quote.send | quoteId | Quote (sent) | quote:send | confirm | external |
| [directory.quote.compare](<http://directory.quote.compare>) | enquiryId | QuoteComparison (rows per recipient, normalised totals) | enquiry:read | none | read |
| directory.quote.accept | quoteId | Quote (accepted), EngagementHandoff | quote:accept | always | external |
| directory.quote.decline | quoteId, reason | Quote | quote:accept | none | external |
| directory.review.request | engagementId | ReviewInvitation | enquiry:send | none | external |
| directory.review.submit | invitationId, ratings, body | Review (pending moderation) | review:write (invitation holder only) | confirm | external |
| directory.review.respond | reviewId, body | ReviewResponse | listing:publish | confirm | external |
| [directory.content.report](<http://directory.content.report>) | targetRef (listing, review, message), reason, detail | ModerationCase | any signed-in user; anonymous with captcha | none | external |
| directory.moderation.decide | caseId, outcome (keep, edit, remove, suspend), statement of reasons | ModerationCase | platform:moderate | none | write |
| directory.category.manage | taxonomy patch | Taxonomy version | platform:taxonomy | confirm | write |
| directory.insights.get | listingId, period | ListingInsights (views, saves, enquiries, response time, win rate) | listing:read | none | read |
| directory.navigate.\* | screen and record ids | Navigation result | screen permission | none | read |

## 5. Data model

F5 owns these entities. F1 Event and F4 Organisation and Contact are referenced by id, not redefined. Shared columns from Resnovas/Eventiva#809 (tenantId, created, updated, version, deleted).

* **Listing**: tenantId (publisher), kind, slug, name, summary, description (rich text), categories, status (draft, pending verification, published, unpublished, suspended, archived), verification badge, contact channel settings, response-time stat, rating summary, organisationRef (the publisher's own F4 Organisation Party id, per [EVE-65](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-65/f4-contacts-and-crm-people-organisations-relationships-and-history>); legal name, address and contact details are read from it, not copied). One tenant may publish several listings (a company and its venues).
* **VenueRoom** (venue only; named so it does not clash with the per-event F1 Space): listingId, name, area, ceiling height, capacities per layout (standing, theatre, banquet, cabaret, classroom), rigging points and load, power supply, load-in access, step-free access and accessible facilities, floor plan file. Links to an F10 site map when the venue maintains one. F1 references F5 by id only ([EVE-73](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-73/f1-events-and-production-planning-the-event-record-run-of-show>) section 5): Event.venue_ref is a Listing id of kind venue, and an F1 Space may carry an optional venue_room_ref to a VenueRoom; referenced VenueRooms are archived, never deleted.
* **Offering**: listingId, name, description, unit (per event, per day, per hour, per head, per item), price from, currency, inclusions. Professionals use offerings for day rates.
* **ProfessionalProfile** (kind professional): skills, qualifications (references F13 qualification records when the professional is staff of a tenant; self-declared otherwise, marked as such), languages, travel radius.
* **MediaItem**: listingId, fileId ([EVE-25](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-25/port-files-private-attachments-artifacts-and-document-import>)), alt text (required), order.
* **ServiceArea**: listingId, geometry (point plus radius, or region code list).
* **Category**: platform-owned taxonomy, versioned, localised labels ([EVE-28](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-28/port-localization-for-people-and-for-the-agent>)).
* **VerificationCase**: listingId, trader name, registered address, registration number, VAT number, contact, evidence files, outcome, reviewer, decided at.
* **Shortlist** and **ShortlistItem**: organiser tenant, optional F1 Event id, listing ids, notes.
* **Enquiry**: organiser tenant, optional F1 Event id, brief fields, attachments, status (draft, sent, closed, withdrawn).
* **EnquiryRecipient**: the cross-tenant record. enquiryId, listingId, organiserTenantId, vendorTenantId, status (new, viewed, responded, declined, quoted, won, lost, expired), message thread, crmEnquiryRef. On send, F5 calls crm.enquiry.capture ([EVE-137](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-137/f46-capture-enquiries-and-track-opportunities-through-a-pipeline-into>)) in the vendor tenant so the enquiry lands in the vendor's CRM pipeline; F5 keeps the cross-tenant thread and quotes, F4 keeps the lead.
* **Message**: enquiryRecipientId, author principal (person or agent for person), body, attachments, read receipts.
* **Quote** and **QuoteLine**: enquiryRecipientId, version, lines (offeringId optional, description, quantity, unit price, tax rate code), totals, validity date, terms, status (draft, sent, accepted, declined, expired, superseded).
* **EngagementHandoff**: produced on acceptance. Creates in the organiser tenant: an F4 Organisation and Contact link for the supplier (found or created), a booking hold through [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters>) primitives on the F1 Event dates, and a commitment record F11 reads. In the vendor tenant the enquiry already exists as an F4 lead (see EnquiryRecipient); acceptance calls crm.enquiry.resolve (Resnovas/Eventiva#904) with won, and the other recipients' leads are resolved lost with a reason. Both CRM calls run as the F5 directory system principal, scoped in each vendor tenant to crm.enquiry.capture and crm.enquiry.resolve only, and audited with the F5 thread id. F5 owns only the handoff record and its status; the targets are owned by their sets.
* **ReviewInvitation**, **Review**, **ReviewResponse**: review tied to exactly one EngagementHandoff (verified by construction), ratings per dimension, body, moderation status, published at.
* **ModerationCase**: target ref, reporter, reason, outcome, statement of reasons, appeal state.

Tenant scope. Listings, venue rooms, offerings and media are tenant-owned and publicly readable only through the public projection when published. EnquiryRecipient, Message, Quote and EngagementHandoff are two-party records: the row stores both tenant ids, and the authorization rule ([EVE-43](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-43/p14-build-identity-and-access-orgs-authorization-user-profiles-and>)) is "principal belongs to one of the two tenants and holds the enquiry or quote permission there". This is the first cross-tenant record type in Eventiva and needs a test matrix of its own. Reviews are public once published. Moderation cases are platform scope.

Offline sync ([EVE-17](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-17/s4-choose-the-offline-sync-engine-for-record-edits-and-live-text-and>), [EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>)). Synced to device: own listings and children (vendor), own shortlists, own enquiries, threads and quotes (both sides), last search result pages cached read only. Not synced: the public index. Conflict rules: listing scalar fields last-writer-wins per field with version check; listing description is a Yjs text document embedded in the record ([EVE-51](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-51/p112-build-collaboration-yjs-for-text-and-canvas-with-record-sync-and>)) so two staff can edit it together; VenueRoom capacities and Offering prices last-writer-wins per field; quote lines are edited by one side only and a sent quote is immutable (revise makes a new version), so no merge; messages are append-only; status transitions are server-validated state machines ([EVE-42](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-42/p13-build-the-storage-layer-drizzle-on-postgres-and-sqlite-state>)), so an offline transition that is no longer valid is rejected on sync and surfaced to the user. Sending an enquiry, message or quote while offline queues the action and it is executed and authorized on reconnect; the UI shows it as queued, never as sent.

## 6. Screens

All components from Rambo-UI. Each screen declares an Effect Schema screen-context projection (Resnovas/Eventiva#817) and every control binds to an action.

| Screen | Key components | Projection | Controls and actions |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Directory search | search field, filter panel, result list and map toggle, result card | query, filters, visible result ids with rank and reason, selected result | search, filter change ([directory.search](<http://directory.search>)), save to shortlist (directory.shortlist.add), open (directory.navigate.listing) |
| Listing detail (public) | gallery, venue room table, offering list, availability strip, review list, contact button | listing id, visible sections, selected venue room, availability range shown | check availability, add to shortlist, start enquiry (directory.enquiry.draft), report ([directory.content.report](<http://directory.content.report>)) |
| Shortlist | table with compare columns, notes | shortlist id, item ids, selected items | remove, note, enquire selected (directory.enquiry.draft) |
| Enquiry composer | brief form prefilled from the F1 Event, recipient chips | draft fields, recipients, validation errors | save draft, send (directory.enquiry.send) |
| Enquiry inbox (vendor) | list with status filters, thread view | visible enquiry recipient ids, selected thread, unread count | open, message, decline, create quote |
| Quote editor (vendor) | line item table from offerings, totals, validity | quote id, version, lines, totals | add line, revise, send (directory.quote.send) |
| Quote comparison (organiser) | comparison grid, per-recipient thread | enquiry id, rows and normalised totals | accept (directory.quote.accept), decline, message |
| Listing editor (vendor) | form sections, venue room editor, offering editor, media manager, preview | listing id, section, dirty fields, publish blockers | update, upsert venue room or offering, attach media, request verification, publish |
| Reviews (vendor) | review list, response box | visible review ids | respond, report |
| Listing insights (vendor) | KPI tiles, trend charts | period, metric values | change period (directory.insights.get) |
| Moderation queue (platform) | case list, case detail | case ids, selected case | decide, view target |

Public web section: the search and listing detail screens also render server side on the directory web section (own subdomain per Resnovas/Eventiva#779) for anonymous users and search engines, from the same projections and actions.

## 7. Agent behaviour

When asked:

* Organiser: "find three lighting suppliers within 50 miles of the venue for the festival dates under budget line X" runs `directory.search` with filters read from the F1 Event and its unfilled EquipmentRequirement items, the F10 site map and the F11 budget, explains the ranking, and offers a shortlist.
* Organiser: drafts the enquiry brief from the event and attaches the relevant run of show; compares quotes and explains differences in inclusions, not only price.
* Vendor: drafts a quote from offerings, F6 stock availability and F2 crew availability for the requested dates; drafts listing copy and alt text from uploaded photos for the user to approve.

Proactive (behind the flag, opt-in per user):

* Nudge an organiser when a quote is about to expire or a supplier has replied.
* Nudge a vendor when an enquiry has waited longer than their usual response time.
* After an event closes, propose review invitations for every engagement.

Approvals: anything that reaches another business or the public is confirm or always (publish, send enquiry, message as an agent, send quote, accept quote, submit or respond to review). The agent never accepts a quote without explicit approval (always). Bulk enquiry to more than 5 recipients always asks.

Safety: listing text, reviews, messages and quote terms written by another tenant are untrusted data in the agent's context and are marked as such in the projection; instructions inside them are never followed. The agent must not write or solicit reviews (fake review rules, section 11).

## 8. Integrations

Each behind a neutral port in its own integration package; no vendor chosen here, each needs approval on its child issue.

* Geocoding and maps tiles: `Geocoder` port (address to point, region lookup) and map rendering via the F10 map stack. Search by radius works from stored points without a live call.
* Search index: Postgres full text and vector search through the Resnovas/Eventiva#793 search port; geo filtering in Postgres (decision D5-4).
* Business verification: manual moderator review in v1 behind a `TraderVerifier` port, so a registry lookup service can be added later.
* Bot protection on anonymous enquiries and reports: `HumanCheck` port.
* Email and push for new enquiries, replies and quotes: Resnovas/Eventiva#791 notifications.
* Payments: none in v1. Deposits and payment of accepted quotes go through F9 and F11 later.

## 9. Permissions and roles

Permissions: listing:read, listing:write, listing:publish, shortlist:write, enquiry:read, enquiry:write, enquiry:send, enquiry:respond, quote:write, quote:send, quote:accept, review:write, platform:moderate, platform:taxonomy.

| Role | Grants |
| -- | -- |
| Anonymous visitor | public search and listing read; report with human check |
| Organiser tenant member (planner) | shortlist:write, enquiry:read, enquiry:write, enquiry:send, enquiry:respond |
| Organiser tenant approver (budget holder) | above plus quote:accept |
| Vendor tenant member (sales) | listing:read, listing:write, enquiry:read, enquiry:respond, quote:write, quote:send |
| Vendor tenant owner or marketing | above plus listing:publish |
| Professional (single-person tenant) | all vendor permissions on their own listing |
| Review invitation holder | review:write for that one engagement |
| Platform moderator | platform:moderate; no access to private threads except content reported to them |

Cross-tenant rule: a vendor sees only enquiries addressed to their listing; recipients of one enquiry never see each other's identity, messages or quotes. Agents get at most the permissions of the person they act for (Resnovas/Eventiva#810).

## 10. Telemetry and flags

Flag: `directory-marketplace` (default off), with sub-flags `directory-public-web`, `directory-reviews`, `directory-agent-sourcing`.

Events (PostHog, via Resnovas/Eventiva#811 tracking port, pseudonymous ids, no message bodies): directory_search_performed (filters used, result count), directory_listing_viewed, directory_shortlist_item_added, directory_enquiry_sent (recipient count), directory_enquiry_responded (response time bucket), directory_quote_sent, directory_quote_accepted, directory_review_submitted, directory_listing_published, directory_content_reported. Group analytics by tenant.

Success metric: share of sent enquiries that reach an accepted quote within 30 days. Guardrails: median vendor first-response time, report rate per 1,000 listing views.

## 11. Compliance

* UK DMCC Act 2024 and CMA fake reviews guidance; EU Omnibus Directive (2019/2161): reviews only from verified engagements, disclosure of how reviews are collected and checked, no review incentives, no suppression of negative reviews.
* EU Digital Services Act and UK Online Safety Act where applicable: notice and action for illegal content, statement of reasons for moderation decisions, trader traceability (verified trader details before a business can publish to consumers).
* EU Platform-to-Business Regulation (2019/1150): publish the main ranking parameters, and disclose that paid placement does not exist in v1 (or label it if added).
* UK GDPR and EU GDPR: professionals are individuals, so their public profile is published only with explicit consent, can be unpublished and erased; enquiry messages are personal data with retention rules; data subject export covers threads.
* Accessibility: public pages meet WCAG 2.2 AA; venue access information is structured fields, not free text.
* Consumer law: quote terms carry the vendor's identity and cancellation terms; Eventiva is not a party to the contract and says so.

## 12. Acceptance

* A vendor publishes a verified listing with venue rooms, offerings and media; an anonymous visitor finds it on the public web by category and radius.
* An organiser sends one enquiry to three listings from an F1 Event, each vendor sees only its own thread, two quote, the organiser compares and accepts one, and the handoff creates the F4 link, the [EVE-33](<https://linear.app/resnovas/issue/EVE-33/port-scheduling-primitives-for-availability-bookings-and-rosters>) hold and the F11 commitment.
* The same flow runs end to end through the agent with approvals shown on screen and through MCP, with identical audit rows.
* A review can only be submitted from an engagement; a vendor can respond; a reported review goes to moderation with a statement of reasons.
* Cross-tenant negative tests: recipient A cannot read recipient B's thread or quote; a vendor cannot read the organiser's other enquiries; an agent for a planner without quote:accept cannot accept.
* Offline: an enquiry sent offline shows as queued and is sent on reconnect; a quote accepted after it expired while offline is rejected on sync with a clear message.

## 13. Out of scope

Platform payments, deposits, commission or escrow (F9 and F11 later); paid placement and advertising; instant booking without a quote; contract e-signature (port later if needed); ticket resale; hotel room blocks; external marketplace syndication; automated background checks on professionals.

## 14. Dependencies

* Phase 1: Resnovas/Eventiva#807 actions, Resnovas/Eventiva#808 config, Resnovas/Eventiva#809 storage and state machines, Resnovas/Eventiva#810 identity, approvals and audit (cross-tenant rule), Resnovas/Eventiva#811 telemetry, Resnovas/Eventiva#812 change feed (vendor inbox and nudges), Resnovas/Eventiva#813 HTTP API (public web), Resnovas/Eventiva#815 MCP, Resnovas/Eventiva#817 screen awareness, Resnovas/Eventiva#818 collaboration (description text), Resnovas/Eventiva#819 to Resnovas/Eventiva#823 agent.
* Port later: Resnovas/Eventiva#791 notifications, Resnovas/Eventiva#792 files and media, Resnovas/Eventiva#793 search, Resnovas/Eventiva#794 comments, Resnovas/Eventiva#795 localisation, Resnovas/Eventiva#796 agent evaluations, Resnovas/Eventiva#800 scheduling and bookings.
* Feature sets: F1 Event (enquiry context and handoff target), F2 rosters (vendor crew availability), F4 Organisation and Contact (handoff), F6 inventory (quote drafting), F10 site maps (venue spaces), F11 commitments, F13 qualifications, F14 website builder (vendor sites can embed their listing).

## 15. Decisions for Jonathan

Recommended options are the defaults in this spec.

* **D5-1 Who can appear in the directory.** (a) Only businesses and professionals with their own Eventiva tenant, recommended: every listing has an accountable owner and live data. (b) Also unclaimed listings seeded by Eventiva or organisers that owners later claim: faster supply, but stale data and claim disputes.
* **D5-2 Commercial model in v1.** (a) Free listings and enquiries, no payments through the directory; value comes from the platform subscription, recommended. (b) Commission on accepted quotes, which needs F9 payments first. (c) Paid featured placement, which needs P2B ranking disclosure and labelling.
* **D5-3 Reviews.** (a) Verified only, from an engagement made through Eventiva, recommended for DMCC compliance. (b) Also open reviews from any signed-in user, moderated.
* **D5-4 Geo search.** (a) Postgres with PostGIS on Neon, recommended: radius and polygon service areas with indexes; PostGIS is a Postgres extension Neon supports and needs approval as a new dependency on F5.4. (b) Plain columns with bounding-box filters and distance in SQL: no new extension, weaker for service-area polygons.
* **D5-5 Public web.** (a) Public, indexable directory section on its own subdomain, recommended. (b) Signed-in users only in v1.

## 16. Child issues

Hey, I work in software and design consulting and lead the commercial team at an agency. I think it's a real challenge you are facing but there is always a way to make it work by evolving. Some questions: How did you get leads before and what was working for you until recently? I haven't looked at your socials, I know you mentioned being in twitter/x. How are you using those channels, e.g. what are you posting that would catch the attention of a buyer? E.g. running a campaign based on something interesting in your space that will be useful to your target audience. Do you have an ideal client profile and do you already have a sales funnel e.g. how to attract your ICP and take them through a process to closing them e.g. discovery call, proposal deck, pricing and contract etc? Some comments: I'm getting leads every week where a business owner has built and designed something with AI, but what they now need is security, hosting, hardening etc so it could be you may need to move up the value chain e.g. often these pieces of work are poorly designed, no accessibility considerations, not thought to good information hierarchy or UX/UI. I think design led discovery is still valuable; user research, prototypes etc telling businesses the right thing to build in a world where people are just throwing together AI stuff. I would recommend like others to make it clear on your website what you do, why to work with you, how to work with you, and make it easy to get in touch. I think it's worth considering spending a lot of time on sales, e.g. marketing, outbound, referrals, campaigns, build a pipeline and so on. Good luck!

TRACERを正本に統一：Shopify・BASE同期と自動受発注の安全な復旧
## 目的
TRACERを唯一の正本（商品・仕入先・バリエーション・原価/通貨・在庫・販売可否・注文/発注状態）にし、ShopifyとBASEを同一の判定・同期・注文処理で運用できる状態にする。データを無条件に消去せず、既存IDと履歴を保持する。

## 現在確認できている本番状態
- products: 1,618 rows
- supplier_listings: 57,125 rows
- shop_listings: 106 rows
- shop_orders / shop_order_items / purchase_orders / purchase_order_items: 各0 rows
- shop_listingsはバックアップ済み（2026-10-13、106 rows）。products 1,618、supplier_listings 57,125、注文/発注関連テーブルも同日バックアップあり。
- shop_listingsの6件がShopifyまたはBASEの外部IDを持っていた。
- 6件すべて、listing currency=JPYに対しsupplier currency=USD。TRACER側の6件をpublished=false、orderable=false、BLOCKEDにし、ShopifyでACTIVEだった2件をDRAFTへ変更・再取得して確認済み。BASE側の外部状態は未確認。
- 仕入先リストには大多数の未検証データがある。identity/variant/orderabilityの証拠なしに公開・発注してはならない。

## 作業
1. コードの実経路を追い、shopify-publish / base-publish、shopify-orders / base-orders、inventory refresh、dropship execution、supplier order jobsの副作用と共通ゲートを図示する。
2. ShopifyとBASE双方で、TRACERの商品ID・SKU・variant IDを確実に照合する。曖昧/欠落/重複したマッピングは隔離し、勝手に新規商品を作らない。
3. 仕入原価通貨・送料・FXレート・レート日時・売価・粗利の一貫したモデルを定義。USD原価をJPYとして扱わず、JPY原価に換算できない商品は公開/発注不可にする。String(null)等の暗黙変換を禁止。
4. 単一の販売適格ゲートを実装し、両チャネルの公開、在庫更新、注文後の発注で再利用する。少なくとも日本語タイトル/説明、画像、JPY販売価格、原価通貨/換算証拠、利益>0、正規仕入先ID、実際のvariant ID、在庫確認、orderable=true、配送追跡要件、同期可能性を検証。
5. ShopifyとBASEの注文を共通のshop_orders/shop_order_itemsモデルに冪等に取り込み、同一の安全なpurchase order経路へ流す。外部注文IDとチャネルを一意キーにし、再実行/同時実行で二重発注しない。人間の承認・既存ライブ発注ゲートを迂回しない。
6. 販売停止/在庫切れが片方のチャネルだけに反映される問題を防ぐ。TRACERの停止状態を両チャネルに反映し、停止済み商品をcronが再公開しないようにする。
7. 外部APIはモックを用いたintegration testを追加し、実際のアプリ経路を通す。必須ケース：identity missing/ambiguous/mismatch、variant missing/mismatch、USD/JPY mismatch、FX unavailable/stale、margin <=0、out-of-stock、channel API failure、duplicate order webhook/polling、concurrent run、save failure、already-drafted/unpublished item。実データに対するdry-run結果と件数一致を提示する。
8. Cronは、共通ゲートと冪等性テストが通るまで公開/発注の書き込みを増やさない。既存の本番cronを一律停止せず、どのジョブが書き込むか確認し、必要最小限の制御を行う。
9. DB migration/データ変更はバックアップを保持し、まずdry-run、次に検証済みの対象だけに限定して適用する。Shopify/BASEの実商品や顧客注文、履歴を一括削除しない。

## 受け入れ条件
- unit + integration tests pass; build/lint/typecheck pass
- 正常系だけでなく全ブロッカーのテストが実際の経路で通る
- Shopify/BASEの公開候補件数、照合成功/失敗件数、在庫/原価/利益の根拠、dry-runとDBの差分が説明可能
- 外部店舗の実状態をAPIで再取得し、停止/公開の結果を確認
- PRはDraftのまま、証拠とCIがそろうまでmerge/deployしない
- 公開/発注できる商品数が0件なら0件と報告し、数字を捏造しない

## 制約
- 本番商品・顧客注文・履歴を削除しない
- 不確実な商品を自動公開しない
- 仕入先注文を無承認で実行しない
- 英語の顧客向けタイトル/説明を出さない
- Orosyを新規仕入れ経路として追加しない

## Follow-up audit: order pipeline + supplier evidence (read-only, 2026-10-13)

### Order pipeline state
- `shop_orders`: 0 rows; Shopify-linked 0; BASE-linked 0; paid 0; cancelled/refunded 0.
- `shop_order_items`: 0 rows.
- `purchase_orders`: 0 rows.
- `purchase_order_items`: 0 rows.
- `supplier_order_attempts`: 0 rows.

This establishes that these TRACER tables currently contain no order/PO execution history; it does NOT establish that the external stores have no orders. Before declaring auto-ordering operational, fetch external Shopify and BASE orders through their authenticated APIs and reconcile totals, financial statuses, cancellations/refunds, line items, variants and timestamps into a dry-run report. Then test actual application ingestion with duplicate webhook/cron delivery, concurrent processing, cancellation/refund race, and ambiguous supplier timeout without issuing live supplier orders.

### Supplier evidence
- `supplier_listings` total: 57,125 rows.
- CJ variants are split across many states. Read-only grouped query returned 504 CJ rows `verified + supply_discovered + orderable=true + price_confirmed + inventory_confirmed + tracking_available`; another 44 rows have the same positive flags but `verification_status=retryable`; 76 verified rows are explicitly `orderable=false`. These counts are supplier-listing records, NOT unique products or publication-ready listings; they still need exact identity/variant, Japanese copy/image, JPY conversion/FX timestamp, landed cost/profit and active inventory checks.
- Existing `orosy` supplier records: 1,249 rows (`unknown`/`unverified` identity states). User requirement is no Orosy sourcing route. Do not delete these records or use them for new sourcing; identify every ingestion/cron/publish path that can reintroduce/use Orosy and gate it off safely, with regression tests.

### Required fail-closed acceptance gates
1. A `retryable` listing is not treated as verified/orderable just because boolean flags are true.
2. One shared eligibility predicate must reject `identity_status` other than explicitly verified/linked, currency without a recorded conversion basis, missing variant mapping, stale/unconfirmed inventory, invalid Japanese customer copy, missing image, or non-positive contribution profit.
3. No supplier API submission until a unique idempotency key, human approval, exact supplier variant snapshot and safe retry/unknown-result reconciliation are verified.
4. Keep all live supplier submissions and mass publication paused during this audit; no production data deletions performed.

source_text:
F5.12 Build agent sourcing for organisers and quote drafting for vendors
Status: Proposed (2026-11-01), part of Resnovas/Eventiva#833 (F5 Directory and marketplace).

## Goal

The agent sources suppliers from the live event plan and drafts quotes from the vendor's real offerings and availability, using only F5 actions and asking before anything reaches another business.

## Context

* Resnovas/Eventiva#833 section 7 (agent behaviour). The agent loop is Resnovas/Eventiva#819 with actions as tools; durable runs Resnovas/Eventiva#821; external agents over MCP (Resnovas/Eventiva#815) get the same behaviour through the same actions.
* No new actions here: this issue adds agent skills (instructions and evaluated flows) over the F5 actions, plus proactive triggers.
* F1 inputs read by id: Event (dates, venue_ref), Space, EquipmentRequirement (what kit or service the event still needs). F10 site map and F11 budget lines are read when those sets exist.

## Scope

1. Organiser skill "source suppliers": read the F1 Event and its unfilled EquipmentRequirement items, map them to F5 categories, run `directory.search` per requirement with date, location and budget filters, explain ranking, propose a shortlist (`directory.shortlist.add`), draft one enquiry per group (`directory.enquiry.draft`), and ask before `directory.enquiry.send`.
2. Organiser skill "compare quotes": `directory.quote.compare` plus a plain-language summary of differences in inclusions, terms and validity; never calls `directory.quote.accept` without the always approval.

Effect-TS v3; Effect AI only per Resnovas/Eventiva#781 decision; flag `directory-agent-sourcing` default off; no new dependency without Jonathan approving it on this issue; ships to main with `node --run check` results pasted here.

Ask HN: Fake abuse reports keep auto-blocking my site on Cloudflare
I run a small site on Cloudflare's Pro plan. Since 26 September, someone has filed the same fake abuse report against it six times. Each time, Cloudflare automatically puts a "Suspected Malware" warning on my homepage and login pages, and it stays until a person reviews it. The reports are word for word identical. They describe an "order" and product pages that have never existed on my site (they return 404). The file hash in the report doesn't match the hash in its own VirusTotal link, which returns "Item not found". Only the date changes, and twice it's been misspelled ("October 52026", "Octoboer 8 2026"). Cloudflare's team has cleared four of them. The reporter pastes the same text again within a day. The result is that my homepage has been blocked for most of two weeks, my traffic has halved, and Google is indexing the warning page instead of my site. I've opened support cases and requested reviews each time. I've had one reply, on 5 October, and nothing on a lasting fix. I'm not asking for special treatment. I'd like to know:
1. Is there a way to stop automatic mitigations from a reporter or text that has already been shown to be false?
2. Is there a manual-review setting for a domain?
3. Has anyone else seen the abuse form used like this, and how did it end? The same problem is described in my open case with Cloudflare (#02370521). Thanks for any pointers, and if anyone from Cloudflare's abuse team reads this, I'd welcome a reply.

source_text:
Official Docker image 2.43.3 ships @napi-rs/canvas without any native binding → "DOMMatrix is not defined" in all PDF nodes
### Bug Description

PDF parsing fails in the official Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.43.3` with
`DOMMatrix is not defined`. Both independent PDF code paths are affected:

- `n8n-nodes-base.extractFromFile` (operation: `pdf`)
- `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.documentDefaultDataLoader` (dataType: `binary`, loader: `pdfLoader`)

Downloading the PDF (e.g. via HTTP Request node) works fine; the failure
happens only when the PDF is parsed.

**Root cause:** the image contains the JS wrapper `@napi-rs/canvas@0.1.80`,
but **no platform-specific native binding at all**. Neither
`@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl` (which this Alpine/musl x86_64 image would
need) nor any other variant is present. As a result, pdfjs-dist cannot
polyfill `DOMMatrix`, `ImageData` and `Path2D`, and PDF parsing aborts.

This is reproducible in a **pristine** image with no mounts, environment
variables or customizations.

### To Reproduce

1. Check which `@napi-rs/canvas` packages ship with the image:

```bash
   docker run --rm --entrypoint sh docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3 -c \
     'ls /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm | grep -i "napi-rs+canvas"'
```

   Output:

```
   @napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80
```

   Only the wrapper is present; no `canvas-linux-x64-musl` (nor `-gnu`).

2. Try to load the package inside the pristine image:

```bash
   docker run --rm --entrypoint sh docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3 -c \
     'd=$(find / -type d -path "*node_modules/@napi-rs/canvas" 2>/dev/null | head -1); \
      echo "Path: $d"; node -e "require(\"$d\"); console.log(\"canvas OK\")"'
```

   Output:

```
   Path: /usr/local/lib/node_modules/n8n/node_modules/.pnpm/@napi-rs+canvas@0.1.80/node_modules/@napi-rs/canvas
   Error: Failed to load native binding
     [cause]: [
       Error: Cannot find module './skia.linux-x64-musl.node'
       Error: Cannot find module '@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl'
     ]
```

3. In a running instance, execute any workflow that uses Extract from File
   (operation: PDF) or the Default Data Loader with a PDF binary. The node
   fails with `DOMMatrix is not defined`.

### Expected behavior

The image ships the native `@napi-rs/canvas` binding matching its own
platform (`linux-x64-musl`, and `linux-arm64-musl` for arm64 images), so
PDF extraction works out of the box.

### Debug Info

## Logs (running instance)

```
Warning: Cannot load "@napi-rs/canvas" package: "Error: Failed to load native binding".
Warning: Cannot polyfill `DOMMatrix`, rendering may be broken.
Warning: Cannot polyfill `ImageData`, rendering may be broken.
Warning: Cannot polyfill `Path2D`, rendering may be broken.
ReferenceError: DOMMatrix is not defined
```

## Environment

- n8n version: 2.43.3 (self-hosted, `N8N_RELEASE_TYPE=stable`)
- Image: `docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.43.3`
  (digest `sha256:d4eca183959b30fb1ba5ecda7e58363c5be49a7bcf8c0227a6384a47ce2f7a65`)
- Base OS (from image): Docker Hardened Images (Alpine) 3.24
- Node.js: v26.7.0
- Architecture: x86_64
- Running via: Docker, with external task runners
  (`n8nio/runners:2.43.3`, `N8N_RUNNERS_MODE=external`)
- Database / binary data mode: not relevant (reproducible without any instance data)

## Additional context

- Earlier images did contain `skia.linux-x64-musl.node` (see #23754 for 2.0.0),
  so this appears to be a packaging regression: the optional platform
  dependencies of `@napi-rs/canvas` seem to be omitted entirely during the
  image build (e.g. via `--no-optional`, production pruning, or pnpm not
  resolving optional deps for the target platform).
- Related historical reports of the same symptom: #16593, #16438, #16422.
- Possible fix: make sure the Docker build installs the matching platform
  package, e.g. by adding `@napi-rs/canvas-linux-x64-musl` /
  `@napi-rs/canvas-linux-arm64-musl` explicitly, or by configuring pnpm
  `supportedArchitectures` with `os: ["linux"]`, `cpu: ["x64", "arm64"]`,
  `libc: ["musl"]`.
- Current workaround: extract the PDF text outside of n8n (e.g. Python/pypdf)
  and send the text to n8n via webhook.

### Operating System

Debian 13 (host); container: Alpine 3.24 (Docker Hardened Images, official n8nio/n8n image)

### n8n Version

2.43.3

### Node.js Version

26.7.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

TypeError: r.firstEvent.getTime is not a function in WorkflowStatisticsRollupService.foldBatch (Postgres) — logged ~1,400×/hour
### Bug Description

On n8n 2.30.7 (self-hosted, Docker, PostgreSQL) the container log is flooded with:

```
TypeError: r.firstEvent.getTime is not a function
    at src/services/workflow-statistics-rollup.service.ts:126:19
    at WorkflowStatisticsRollupService.foldBatch (src/services/workflow-statistics-rollup.service.ts:124:19)
    at WorkflowStatisticsRollupService.rollup (src/services/workflow-statistics-rollup.service.ts:113:18)
```

Rate: ~1,400 occurrences per hour (~34,000 per 24 h), continuously since 2026-09-29. Without log rotation a single container log grew to ~700 MB. Restarting the container does not help — the error reappears within ~3 minutes (1,340 occurrences in the first hour after a restart).

It looks like `firstEvent` comes back from PostgreSQL as a string (not a `Date`) in the rollup batch, so `.getTime()` fails. Possibly related: #28541, #28640 (same pattern with `dbTime.getTime`) and #40019 (rollup refactor).

### To Reproduce

1. Run n8n 2.30.7 in Docker with `DB_TYPE=postgresdb` (PostgreSQL 17).
2. Have ~50 published workflows with ~1,400 executions per day.
3. Watch the container log — the error is emitted continuously by the workflow statistics rollup.

### Expected behavior

Workflow statistics rollup works with PostgreSQL (timestamps parsed as `Date`) and does not flood the log.

### Debug Info

See the stack trace above.

### Operating System

Linux (Docker host)

### n8n Version

2.30.7

### Node.js Version

Bundled with the official image docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n:2.30.7

### Database

PostgreSQL

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

source_text:
Show HN: Modelpeers – a changelog for the AI models and agents you use
Earlier this year, I had one of my product's features down for 48 hours because Anthropic retired Claude 3 Haiku. In another instance, an API parameter started returning errors. I grew sick of not being able to follow and track the endless changes of AI models every week, so I decided to build Modelpeers. It's basically a feed of all these changes. You can follow models and agents that you use to see what is changing and what you need to do about it. Optionally, you can sign up to get a digest for the models/agents you follow. Every few hours, it downloads and hashes dozens of pages from the prominent AI companies' pages, like changelogs, deprecation pages, status pages, and pricing pages. Then when a page changes, it pulls the diff, validates it with two models, and if validated as true, it posts it to the feed. The feed currently has about 400 changes, 21 of them breaking changes. Fun fact (well, not really fun): OpenAI alone has 12 shutdowns/cutoff planned for the next six months. Would love to hear what y'all think.

Show HN: Go (style) linter for dangling package-level functions
I'm one of those who doesn't like dangling top-level functions polluting the package namespace and has to belong to some type via receiver to make some logical sense and "feel less cluttered" after decade in the other language ecosystems. After leaving this exact complaint (among others) in hundreds of PR reviews, I thought it's going to be fun automating this, as wanted to dig through golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis for quite a while now. It turned out that analysis.TextEdit is more fun than the linter itself, so that fixes could happen automatically and funcs undangle as pointer receiver methods if a concrete func is used just within one type. Give it a spin and tell me what you think. My two hours of internet search didn't yield any similar things out there. As the most of the linters, it's a stylistic choice, that may or may not fit your orgs. Maybe it'll make your life easier. CAUTION: Don't run with `-fix` on non-staged changes yet. PRs are very welcome, especially with more corner-case fixtures.

[GoodBounty-QA]: Bridge-widget QA
# Bridge widget independent QA bounty

Test [PR #266](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodWidget/pull/266) against [issue #257](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodWidget/issues/257), focusing on what users see, understand and do. Deliver an evidence-backed report, not code fixes.

**Independent human testing and a funded live-wallet transfer are mandatory., read below after assignment how to request for testing funds.** Automated tests, fixtures and the author's earlier transfer do not replace them.

Reward: Its part of the main bounty for building the bridging widget. Tiered at: `Mythic`. Read up on reward distribution [here](https://docs.gooddollar.org/for-developers/contributing/open-source-contributors/payments-for-reviews-contributors-and-qa)

## Setup

Follow the [GoodWidget QA guide](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodWidget/blob/main/docs/qa-guide.md) for setup, execution and reporting. Its updated instructions must be committed before relying on them through this link. Record the guide revision used.

The candidate checked on 5 November 2026 is `edehvictor/GoodWidget:fix/bridging-correctness-257` at `8feadd7d59948c924a7d2195a1f556d9355ad4fd`. The Lead must confirm the assigned SHA. Record it, the installed SDK version and environment; keep retests on later commits separate.

Use Storybook runtime fixtures for deterministic/error states that you can not force or replicate through live testing.
Injected Wallet Demo in storybook is for live testing (browser wallet). Currently not yet having a reown wallet-connect story so this is not able to be tested.

Test desktop and 390 px mobile width, including 390 × 504, in light/dark themes. Run the guide's setup/build checks and focused suite: `pnpm test:demo tests/widgets/bridging-widget`. Record blockers and actual outcomes; skipped CI is not a pass.

## Required cases

For each case, record **Pass, Fail, Blocked or Not run**, actual versus expected behavior and fresh screenshots/video or logs. Label evidence live or mocked and human or automated. Expand route-sensitive cases for each agreed route/provider.

### QA01 First use and connection

**How:** Open disconnected; inspect balances and actions, open History/FAQ, connect, then exercise an unsupported wallet network.

**Expected:** Bridge remains visible, balances are placeholders and Connect Wallet is primary. Purpose, next step and network guidance are clear; connection does not leave stale account data.

### QA02 Routes and providers

**How:** Change source/destination independently of the wallet network. Try same-chain/unsupported pairs; inspect balances, quotes, chain names and provider availability.

**Expected:** Values follow the selected source; invalid pairs cannot proceed. Axelar supports Celo↔Ethereum, not Fuse↔Celo. LayerZero choices match supported routes. Selection never prompts a wallet switch.

### QA03 Amounts and fees

**How:** Test typing/paste, MAX, empty/zero/invalid/below-minimum/over-balance amounts and insufficient native balance. Cover Fuse/Ethereum and Celo as source/destination.

**Expected:** 2-decimal Fuse/Ethereum and 18-decimal Celo amounts remain accurate throughout. Invalid amounts cannot proceed. G$ protocol fees, received amount and buffered native-token provider fees are distinct and understandable. Verify live fees using live quotes, not fixture numbers.

### QA04 Review and Confirm

**How:** Select a source different from the wallet network, enter an amount, open Review, then Confirm. Inspect route, provider, received amount, costs and switch guidance.

**Expected:** Selection and Review do not prompt a switch. Confirm switches if needed, refreshes the quote and submits once. The user understands the next wallet action and required network support. See the [confirmed flow](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodWidget/pull/266#issuecomment-6570885978).

### QA05 Rejection and recovery

**How:** In fixtures, reject switching/approval; simulate quote, preparation and submission errors, then Retry.

**Expected:** Rejected switching causes no subsequent quote/submission for that action. Retry uses a fresh quote and submits once. Cancellation, preparation failure and on-chain failure are distinguished, with clear recovery and no false success.

### QA06 Stale state and interruptions

**How:** Change amount/route/source/account during quoting, preparation and mocked switching. Dismiss/reopen Review, change tabs and repeat-click Confirm. After submission, change account/source and fail a history refresh.

**Expected:** Changed inputs invalidate stale preparation and prevent wrong/duplicate submissions. Already-submitted transfers remain available; refresh failure does not erase them.

### QA07 Progress and delivery

**How:** Exercise submitted, pending, failed and delivered states; open source/provider/destination links and Continue in background.

**Expected:** Source confirmation is not destination delivery. Status, remaining steps and return path are clear. Links match the transaction/network; pending or failed states do not imply success.

### QA08 History

**How:** Inspect loading/empty/error/populated/pending states; open pending details. Observe polling, failed status lookup and source selection changes.

**Expected:** Pending details are read-only, without another Confirm action. Polls do not repeatedly rescan every chain or replace the list with a full spinner. Lookup failures retain entries. Amounts, chain names, timestamps and links are accurate.

### QA09 Mobile and accessibility

**How:** Repeat the primary flow at the required viewports/themes. Check keyboard access, control names, Escape/outside-click dismissal, focus return, touch targets and contrast.

**Expected:** Review, switch guidance, Confirm and progress/history links remain readable and reachable, particularly at 390 × 504. Record clipped, inaccessible or misleading UI and its user impact.

### QA10 Design comparison and UI regression

[Bounty #743] Validate /api/upload files and reject missing or dangerous uploads
## Problem

POST /api/upload accepts empty upload requests without a file attachment and returns a 201 Created status code with "no-file". Furthermore, it lacks MIME type whitelisting and file extension sanitation, allowing arbitrary executable scripts (.sh, .exe, .bat, .php) and unbounded file streams that can cause denial-of-service and remote code execution vulnerabilities.

## Requested fix

Harden the upload endpoint in uploadController and uploadRoutes:
1. Reject requests without an uploaded file with a 400 Bad Request error ("No file provided").
2. Enforce a 10MB maximum file size limit.
3. Validate MIME type and file extension against a whitelist of safe document and media types (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif, application/pdf, text/plain), blocking executable and script extensions.
4. Return standard structured response envelopes for success and 400 validation failures.
5. Add focused route integration tests for successful file upload, missing file rejection, oversized file rejection, and dangerous executable file rejection.

This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information.

This issue is created under the Low Handing Fruit Automation bounty. I will submit a PR that references this issue and issue #743.

source_text:
parseRegexLiteral() rejects valid d and v regex flags and silently returns the whole literal as the pattern
### Bug Description

`parseRegexLiteral()` only recognises a slash-delimited regex literal when all trailing flags come from the allowlist `[gimusy]*`. That is the ES2018 set; `d` (hasIndices, ES2022) and `v` (unicodeSets, ES2024) are missing.

When either flag is present the literal is not recognised at all, and the function falls into its "not a literal" branch — returning the **entire input**, slashes and flags included, as the pattern source. The user gets a silently different regex with no error anywhere.

### To Reproduce

1. In any field that accepts a regex literal, enter `/foo/d`.
2. `parseRegexLiteral('/foo/d')` returns `{ source: '/foo/d', flags: '' }`, i.e. it matches the literal text `/foo/d` rather than `foo`.

Expected: `{ source: 'foo', flags: 'd' }`.

The same happens for `/foo/v` and combined flags such as `/foo/gidv`.

### Why this matters

The repo requires Node >= 24 and V8 has supported `d` since Node 16 and `v` since Node 20, so nothing in the runtime prevents these flags. `v` is the modern replacement for the legacy `u` flag and is what makes set notation like `[\p{L}\p{N}]--\p{White_Space}` usable.

The same stale `[gimsuy]` character class also appears in `packages/@n8n/workflow-sdk/src/workflow-builder/string-utils.ts`, so this looks like drift rather than a deliberate restriction.

### Related

Fix proposed in #43021, with regression tests for `d`, `v`, combined flags and `ignoreCase` on top of `v`.

Show HN: Gauge CLI – Open-Source Hillclimbing for Agent Experience
Hi HN! We're releasing an open-source CLI for hillclimbing Agent Experience. That means optimizing your agent-facing surfaces (Skills, CLIs, SDKs, and docs) so that your users' coding agents can easily use your product. Pointing your own agent at the repo is enough to get started.  https://github.com/gauge-sh/gauge-cli  We've found that power users generally want to hand a CLI/MCP to their agents and get started from the terminal. They rarely want to log in and use the web UI themselves. We think developer tools must be agent-friendly to remain relevant. Here are some common findings that Gauge identifies: - agents get confused with CLI/SDK behavior and start source diving
- interactive commands block agents
- agents use deprecated/old CLI commands
- agents don't use Skills when you'd expect
- agents confidently assert limitations that don't exist
- inconsistent terminology confuses agents
- agents can't figure out how commands fit together into a workflow Locally, the Gauge CLI uses Docker containers to run agent harnesses (you can bring your own subscriptions). It finds where agents get confused or stuck and tests changes using your pre-release artifacts (Skills/CLI etc). We normalize events from Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode into standardized transcripts, and store them locally, alongside structured information in SQLite so that your agent can easily analyze the data. This enables automatic hillclimbing toward a great Agent Experience. We also offer hosted compute that enables more features, built on our custom Gateway (for credential brokering and transparent, per-session response rewriting). Hosted compute enables many more concurrent sessions, easier collaboration with teammates, a GitHub App for PR reviews, sessions with logged-in MCPs/APIs, and most importantly it lets you close your laptop while the sessions actually run. You don't need a Gauge account to run the full loop end-to-end though. We expect that local execution with the CLI is enough to find and fix several agent experience issues in a typical project. You'll be able to validate fixes for these issues locally, before publishing new versions (we inject pre-release Skills and code artifacts into the sessions). We would love your feedback!

source_text:
Question: would an AEAP-shaped Execution Receipt fit the approval boundary already in procure-agent?

你好 刘正享,

I came across procure-agent via GitHub search for LangGraph + human-approval workflows and read through the README carefully. The combination of a LangGraph StateGraph with explicit interrupt points, SQLite checkpointer, Decimal-deterministic money arithmetic, and the explicit "approval has checkpoint-version verification; does not execute email or procurement transactions" boundary is unusually careful work. The `BOUNDARY_TEST_RESULTS.json` file in the repo suggests you've already thought about this surface.

My team at Aiyoplane published the first public draft of **AEAP** (Aiyo Execution Authorization Protocol) earlier this month. It overlaps with your approval boundary in a specific, narrow way, so I thought I'd ask rather than guess whether it fits.

**The overlap:**

Your current approval design verifies the LangGraph checkpoint version before an approval can resume execution. AEAP goes one step further: it produces a cryptographically-signed **Execution Receipt** (Ed25519 over an RFC 8785 JCS canonicalized intent) that binds the approver's identity to the exact tool invocation and arguments at the moment of approval. If the plan state changes between approval and execution — even in ways the checkpoint version doesn't detect — the receipt no longer validates and the tool fails closed.

For procure-agent's shape, that would mean: when a human approves a specific quote (报价 A at 1195.00 CNY from a specific supplier), the receipt binds that exact quote-ID + supplier + amount. A later resumed run cannot silently execute against a different quote, even if the LangGraph state looks consistent.

We shipped `aiyoplane-langgraph` and `aiyoplane-langchain` (both Python, Apache 2.0, zero credentials to run locally). Rough shape of what it would look like on your `evaluate_plan` tool:

```python
from aiyoplane_langchain import create_aiyo_langchain, create_local_rdp, BlockedByPolicy, EscalationRequired

authz = create_aiyo_langchain(
    rdp=create_local_rdp(policy=load_policy("procure-policy.yaml")),
    tool_config={
        "evaluate_plan": {"aiyo_gated": True, "action": {"type": "procurement_commit"}},
        "finish_sourcing": {"aiyo_gated": True, "action": {"type": "procurement_commit"}},
        "search_suppliers": {"aiyo_gated": False},
        "request_quote": {"aiyo_gated": False},
        "inspect_offer": {"aiyo_gated": False},
    },
)

@authz.wrap("evaluate_plan")
def evaluate_plan(args, ctx):
    # Runs only on ALLOW. ctx.receipt binds the approver + quote + supplier.
    # ESCALATE → EscalationRequired (fits your LangGraph interrupt pattern).
    # BLOCK   → BlockedByPolicy  (fits your "报告本轮未找到可执行方案" rule).
    return commit_procurement_plan(args)
```

**Three specific questions, since you'd know best:**

1. Is the approval boundary in procure-agent intentionally scoped to checkpoint-version verification only (meaning signed receipts would be out of scope on purpose), or is it a layer you'd consider adding?
2. If it's a layer you'd consider: would the fit be at `evaluate_plan` / `finish_sourcing` (where the plan commits) or at `request_quote` (where each quote is pulled)?
3. For the real-model mode where `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is live, is the "model cannot overwrite the hard rules" invariant something you'd want cryptographically enforced, or is the tool-side forced verification already sufficient for your use case?

If AEAP doesn't fit procure-agent's shape, closing this issue is a perfectly good answer — I'd rather hear "not a fit" than have you consider something that doesn't match.

Spec: [github.com/aiyoplane/aeap](https://github.com/aiyoplane/aeap) · aiyoplane-langchain: [pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langchain](https://pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langchain/) · aiyoplane-langgraph: [pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langgraph](https://pypi.org/project/aiyoplane-langgraph/) · Trust surface, including §15 non-guarantees: [aiyoplane.com/trust](https://aiyoplane.com/trust)

Thanks for the careful work on this surface. The combination of Decimal arithmetic, explicit boundary tests, and the "不执行邮件或采购交易" ("does not execute email or procurement transactions") constraint is a pattern worth more of in agent projects.

— Rashon

Google Mail's $5/seat offering is the first one that comes to mind.     04 May 2011
Google Mail's $5/seat offering is the first one that comes to mind.     04 May 2011
  Starting with Chrome 13, we'll have HTTPS pins for most Google properties. This means that certificate chains for, say, https://www.google.com, must include a whitelisted public key. It's a fatal error otherwise. 

  https://www.imperialviolet.org/2011/05/04/pinning.html
  
ImperialViolet is Adam Langley’s personal technical blog. Langley worked at Google on HTTPS infrastructure and Chrome’s SSL stack. A Tauri app, which is essentially a Chromium browser instance with no address bar and widgets to access browser settings, a Fastmail desktop "app" made with Tauri can potentially even the playing field between Google the Goliath and Fastmail the David on the TLS certificate pinning front. Tauri is like Electron but sucks a lot less.     https://tauri.app/
  
_ > if you've spending tens of thousands of dollars per month Such as, 8,000 users at $40k/month for Google Mail. Yubico has great volume discounts for a part of the CapEx side of a sane deployment of this. The basic WebAuthn/FIDO2-only Yubikeys with a Fastmail logo on them would be, as the kids said a generation ago, "dope". _ > where they have a Helpdesk Quality attention to cicd and artifact release may avoid and potentially reduce conventional helpdesk activity. For individual users of SaaS, provided the .dmg or .msi of the downstream Betterbird/Thunderbird (or other MUA) has sound cicd and decent release attention, no more additional support tickets than reasonable should occur beyond an initial phase. A downstream MUA distro can eliminate manual configuration and superfluous details, such as the shit experience with Thunderbird on macOS (Thunderbird's fault 100%) with Oath2 I saw in the last few months. Such a distro could be tuned with a slew of relatively small adjustments reducing existing support ticket traffic. Startups with headcount of 20 to 30, a good chunk of that being developers, where I have historically preferred to dwell, helpdesk is not there nor wanted for. Higher quality customers are here. _ > and golden image deploys Chromebooks, which not including K-12 did outnumber macOS in non-personal environments around a half-decade ago during that Event 201 thing. Super low IT overhead with those. I have been distant from MIS type of IT for a while but have  heard echoes or binocular'd in a bit and believe the golden image era has quietly passed us. Conventional image pattern shouldn't be necessary anywhere now. Somewhere in 2019, Apple warped native tooling in tandem with device firmware behavior to squeeze out the conventional image pattern ; killed it off. Apple Business now includes built-in mobile device management which can enroll and set up Apple devices then apply standard settings and apps through "Blueprints" ; the .dmg would be trivial to push out. The successor to Jamf. With Microsoft Intune, propagation of .msi packages to enrolled devices is a day-to-day task. Ubuntu, RedHat, SuSE, Qubes, and all related distros, when under IT teams that can code on a rudimentary level, are managed with Ansible or Salt, without the "enterprise tax" part. What all of these have in common is centralized org-wide device management where the ability to push out a .msi or .dmg or .deb/.rpm/.AppImage is there. In similar spirit to certificate pinning, the advanced customers have dedicated private cicd consume source code from the OS vendor. The more advanced are on     Bootstrappable builds: how and why
  https://lwn.net/Articles/1088279/
  
which in tandem with cryptography-grade hashes, has over half way solved the "Trusting Trust" problem that Ken Thompson raised. _ > what other SaaS consumer products use certificate pinning. Slack has the low-hanging-fruit opportunity to with their Electron app, but has reportedly dropped the ball. This is great for tech workers who like to divert all Slack contents to a separate local data sink for archiving and discovery and non-shitty data access. This repo from about seven years ago looks abandoned and inactive, but     https://github.com/myxious/electron-root-ssl-pinning
  
was not necessary for anyone who wanted to do it. _ > let's expand it to banks and government departments in most countries. With the episodic exposure I had with computer vision -> flow chart startups in the SF Bay Area many years ago, relatively ongoing time sinks with some archetypal MBA twat types, and some perceived legendary tier banks running on one of the two legit clouds (neither of which is that Azure garbage), who then fell on customer-facing downtime by not deploying with rudimentary cloud patterns that startups don't fail to do (as we recently found out), I am left feeling not confident that banks can do IT with self-reliance these days. They can still push out .msi and group policy objects though, for sure. From anecdotes I hear of and distant observations of state governments, departments of the big federal government sans some of the cooler TLA, and govs in Europe, I am not optimistic about those. About a decade and a half ago we used to look at these two types of institutions and go "ah, the big guys, in their big buildings, they broker a thing I need, with their marble floors and reassuring smiles, these egregore have got it all figured out". As a staff level DevOps / DevSecOps / whatever who has been along for the ride with a share of Silicon Valley culture-OS startups with enterprise customers, closely followed practices and white papers of hyperscalers and elite security firms, thus can see through any IT product/pattern transparently for its base principles... -- having witnessed various sitcoms, heard of or read over 9,000 of first-hand accounts of such sitcoms, on top of the broadly spread cultural decay we are experiencing in the West upcoming on this Fourth Turning, with the rot of these institutions, and the major cultural shifts on computer illiteracy/obliviousness being normalized among "professionals" observed over the last couple of decades, I think more often than not some scrutiny of IT patterns at these institutions uncovers that they are severely retarded. I suspect on the mid to lower end of the gov side it's just checkboxes, misdirection, and casual corruption almost all of the way down. Anyone who actually gives a shit about IT security and tries to fix things gets railroaded out. The subcontractors who pick up the slack and handle real shit, like SpaceX is something NASA is dependent on (macro example), the upper echelon of the private sector, supranational organizations run by elite characters, are where not the progressive-minded IT teams are found but where IT is treated with some seriousness by leadership. But no transparency into IT patterns will be offered by these outside of talks at cool parties like DEF CON and AWS Re:Invent (shitty DJs but still a great party).

source_text:
Show HN: Chkit – Schema, migrations and backfills for ClickHouse (like Drizzle)
Hey HN, im Marc, co-founder of ObsessionDB.
We are open sourcing ChKit, our tooling to manage schemas, migrations and backfills for clickhouse. I am a big fan of the type safety drizzle provides for the database. Manage the schema in typescript and generate migrations from it is a powerful workflow. I always wished something like it would exist for clickhouse, so we could manage our analytical workloads the same way. It didn't exist, so we build it. We build it after running ClickHouse at petabyte scale in our previous company, were we managed hundreds of tables, MVs and endpoints reading from them. The way it works: 1. You define your schema in typescript, with typed helpers for tables, mv, column types etc..
2. You generate the migration, that contains the DDL, to get your clickhouse instance from status quo to what your current typescript schema defines
3. Your CI can check for drift
4. You run the generated migration against production
5. You use the defined types in your code, to ingest your data while making sure it has the correct type.
   Bonus: if your schema change was BC breaking, we generate the sequence on how to backfill the data, into the intermediate table to migrate (this is quite the hard problem with large tables and schema evolution) In case you have already a clickhouse instance with a schema, you can pull it down and start using ChKit from where you are. Run our generator to setup the boilerplate:     npm create chkit@latest
  
If you folks are running clickhouse in production, I am curious to hear what other challenges you are running into.

I don't really follow the logic in the article at all: The argument is that Unitree's assembly process is currently very manual because there is no in
I don't really follow the logic in the article at all: The argument is that Unitree's assembly process is currently very manual because there is no incentive to automate, which is because labor cost isn't the bottleneck here, where in the US labor cost are much higher, therefore the US will have incentive to automate more. Those are reasonable so far, until you try to use that as a conclusion that this is why the West will win? First of all, what does he think the other 92% of the cost of manufacturing is? A small portion of that is materials and electricity, but the biggest part of the remaining cost is assembly tooling/fixtures for the assembly line, and a fully automated assembly line is much, much more expensive compared to a semi-automated or manual production line. In other words: it's not that Unitree couldn't build fully automated assembly lines if they wanted to, but spending tens of millions of dollars fully automated assembly line that takes up floor space and requires even more labor for manual maintenance for a product that is only being produced by the hundreds to thousands in quantity every month rather than millions simply does not make economic sense to begin with. Second, why is he assuming that a fully automated assembly line will be cheaper to build in the US than in China, especially since he toured a factory with fully automated assembly lines at BYD in China immediately after? And sure, I would absolutely argue that American software engineering is more efficient than Chinese when looked at as a whole, but the cost of programming an assembly line is a minor portion of the cost compared to actually getting the assembly line fixtures and tooling built. Third, his cost estimate is way off if he thinks you can get the same product manufactured in the US for only 50% more. From my own anecdotal experience, a more realistic cost for US manufacturing for pretty much anything is minimum 300% to 1000% more expensive if you are to make the in the US, and the lack of a mature parts supply chain in the US is honestly a bigger issue than worker wage.

source_text:
Microsoft Teams Trigger silently stops receiving messages after ~3 days (Graph subscription is never renewed)
### Bug Description

The **Microsoft Teams Trigger** (channel messages) creates a Microsoft Graph change-notification subscription when the workflow is published/activated, but nothing ever renews it. Graph caps `channelMessage` subscriptions at 4320 minutes (3 days), so the trigger stops receiving messages roughly 3 days after each activation or n8n restart. The workflow still shows as **Active**, no execution fails and no error is raised: the trigger is simply silent. In our case it went unnoticed for 12 days (messages with photos were not processed).

What we observed (delegated OAuth credential `microsoftTeamsOAuth2Api`; first seen on 2.39.10, same node code on 2.42.6):

1. After re-publishing the workflow, `GET /v1.0/subscriptions` listed one subscription for `/teams/{teamId}/channels/{channelId}/messages` with `expirationDateTime` exactly 72 h after creation (2026-10-09T17:13:25Z -> 2026-10-12T17:13:25Z). It was unchanged 3 days later, i.e. no renewal happened.
2. Graph lifecycle notifications (`@odata.type: "#microsoft.graph.subscription"`, only the subscription id present) are delivered to the workflow as normal trigger items shortly before expiry. Nothing handles them (no PATCH, no re-authorize, no re-create); users have to filter them out manually.
3. From reading `MicrosoftTeamsTrigger.node.ts`: `checkExists()` only lists subscriptions and keeps those valid for more than 5 minutes; `create()` creates them and `delete()` removes them. We could not find renewal logic or handling of `reauthorizationRequired` / `subscriptionRemoved`.

Related (not GitHub issues): https://community.n8n.io/t/problem-teams-trigger-webhook/147354 (users report the same ~3 day expiry; workarounds: nightly PATCH or nightly unpublish/publish).

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with **Microsoft Teams Trigger** on a channel (resource: channel message) using a delegated OAuth credential.
2. Publish it and post a message in the channel: the workflow executes.
3. Wait more than 72 hours without republishing the workflow or restarting n8n.
4. Post a message in the channel: no execution is created. `GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/subscriptions` no longer lists a valid subscription for the channel.
5. Unpublish + publish again: it works for another ~3 days.

### Expected behavior

The trigger keeps working indefinitely while the workflow is active, as Microsoft requires apps to renew subscriptions before expiry (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/subscription). Either renew the subscription periodically (`PATCH /subscriptions/{id}` with a new `expirationDateTime`, which also re-authorizes it), and/or handle the lifecycle notifications Graph sends (`reauthorizationRequired` -> PATCH; `subscriptionRemoved` -> re-create) instead of passing them to the workflow as items. At the very least, failing to keep the subscription alive should be visible (workflow status, execution error or log), since today the workflow looks healthy while it receives nothing.

Workaround we use: a separate scheduled workflow (twice a day) that does `GET /v1.0/subscriptions` with the same credential, picks the subscription whose `resource` matches the channel, and `PATCH`es its `expirationDateTime` to now + 4300 min; it alerts if none exists or the PATCH fails.

Allow manual corrections/offer update. Supplier can only view own data; no customer PII/margin/other supplier costs. PO consolidates by SKU, full/partial/unavailable/price-changed, safe award/binding outcome, ready only after awarded commitment (not Hub Received); verify data propagation into sourcing and future stock signal.

**Admin minimal catalog review:** one contextual review surface for pending Candidate/Brand/Line/Ingredient/Media/Publish decisions (no full Admin dashboard expansion). Arabic RTL mobile and desktop, loading empty unauthorized stale 409 retry and file error states; accessibility.

**Acceptance:** fully logged-in supplier imports and verifies real DB changes; owner reviews and publishes candidate; browser refresh persists; wrong-supplier access 403; draft not binding; 2 browser roles and responsive smoke. Cross-link AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#2/115/124/207.

**Execution dependency:** blocked by AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#141. Complete and review previous gate before starting this stage.

### Supplier manual returns / credits — complete only the necessary operational seam

Reuse existing supplier payable / financial reconciliation contracts (see AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#17 and AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#124). Within contextual PO/Supplier and Finance actions, verify that a Hub-accepted customer return sent **physically** to the same supplier with the next purchase delivery is recorded as `SupplierReturn` pending; supplier confirmation yields a verified `SupplierCredit`; applying the credit to the next invoice is a separate, auditable action. Do NOT treat handed-off return as accepted monetary credit, double-deduct purchase COGS, or lower the new PO's genuine gross acquisition cost. Show gross new supplier invoice, credit applied, actual cash paid distinctly. Record a disputed/rejected credit and monthly cutover. If existing APIs cannot support this, report a focused contract gap and add the smallest required API/conditional UI; avoid a separate Returns portal or full accounting suite. Acceptance: supplier next bill 600 EGP minus verified old credit 100 EGP = 500 cash paid, **new goods acquisition cost remains 600**. Backlink to supplier invoice/return and monthly statement.
