Ask HN: Are there AI models for generating sounds based on a text and reference?
I've been having a hard time finding a solution. Is there really no commercialized model that I can feed in a reference sound and text instruction and get another sound out? Right now having a multimodal inputs to image or text output is a commodotized, solved problem. IE you can put a prompt for some image and use a reference image to guide the model on what you want. After all, a picture is worth a thousand words right? Ive also used a text and audio input in order to get a text description or classification out. I cannot for the life of me find a solution for Audio + text -> Audio My usecase is that I'm trying to generate new sound effects based on a source that doesn't have that many clean examples and thought this would be just another solved workflow but I'm not finding much. Tried elevenlabs SFX but it's only text->audio and without the reference, it's hard to guide with just text and recreate a sound with any accuracy. I tried the Stable Audio 3 model which is supposed to do what I want but the results were terrible. This modality seems to be stuck where image generation was in 2016. Is there something else or is this just not a common need?

If you give it a try, and have any suggestions, please let me know! I'm new to open sourcing stuff, so any feedback on how to do that right welcome.

Feat: Gamification & Categorized XP System
### Summary

Expand Donetick’s existing point system to support **Gamification / XP Mode**, including custom **XP Categories** (e.g., *Health & Fitness*, *Learning*, *Chores*) and API endpoints to query user XP totals by type.

---

### 💡 Problem / Motivation

While Donetick currently supports basic points for tasks, standard points don't fully capture different domains of life or personal growth.

Categorized XP (Experience Points) turns task completion into an engaging gamified system. This helps:

* **Increase Engagement:** Gamification makes chores and habits fun for kids and adults alike.
* **Balanced Growth Tracking:** Categorizing tasks allows users to see *where* they spend their effort (e.g., mental vs. physical tasks).
* **Home Automation & Dashboarding:** API access to XP categories enables custom dashboards or smart-home rules (e.g., enabling access to rewards/devices only after earning required XP). this would closes #832 

---

###  Proposed Solution

#### 1. XP / Gamification Settings

* Add an option to toggle display terminology between **Points** and **XP**.
* Allow users/admins to define custom **XP Categories** (e.g., `Health & Fitness`, `Learning`, `Home & Household`).

#### 2. Task Configuration

* When creating/editing a task, allow choosing:
* **XP Value:** (e.g., `50 XP`)
* **XP Category:** (e.g., `Health & Fitness`)



#### 3. API & Integration Support

* Provide REST API endpoints to fetch user XP statistics:
* `GET /api/v1/users/{userID}/xp` – Returns total XP broken down by category.
* `GET /api/v1/circles/{circleID}/xp` – Returns group/circle leaderboard or category breakdown.


* *Example API Response:*
```json
{
  "user_id": "user_123",
  "total_xp": 450,
  "categories": {
    "health_and_fitness": 200,
    "learning": 150,
    "chores": 100
  }
}

```



---

### Example Use Cases

1. **Custom Dashboards:** Display a RPG-style character sheet / radar chart on a smart display or Grafana showing current levels in different life stats.
2. **Smart Home Automations (Home Assistant):** Trigger an automation via Home Assistant (e.g., unlocking a smart lock on a snack drawer or enabling screen time) only after earning a required threshold of *Health & Fitness* or *Learning* XP.

---

P.S. I’m willing to place a $100 bounty on this feature if a maintainer or contributor is open to implementing it and the PR is accepted and merged.

I mean, many companies operate within particular domains but don't have much skin in the domain itself in a way that is meaningful to other participants there -- like Oracle builds software for healthcare, ostensibly, but any actual user of their products will tell you they are nightmarish with regard to usability, and research shows that patients are often harmed as a result. source_text:
Show HN: Lemma, an IDE for reading mathematics (macOS, open source)
I built Lemma while working through The Elements of Statistical Learning (using the Preview app). Kept running into references like "(3.41)" or "by Theorem 2.3" forcing me to scroll back through the entire book. And whenever a proof wasn’t detailed enough, I'd screenshot it, ask ChatGPT to explain, then go back to the PDF to add manual notes. Got pretty annoying. That led me to Lemma: it reads a PDF once (locally), lets you jump around between equations, theorems, etc. without constantly scrolling. I gave it a VS Code look because yes, I'm addicted to VS Code (there are other themes for normal people). A non-exhaustive list of things it can do (right now): - References to theorems, equations, figures, citations and index entries are all clickable (you can peek at them without leaving the page) - You can ask an agent or ChatGPT Web for explanations, longer proofs with one click, save the output in Lemma - When the pdf says “it is easy to show” or “proof left to the reader”, you can write the missing steps in LaTeX, and Lemma checks it on random numerical inputs and gives counterexamples if it’s wrong. You can also fold proofs to try them yourself first, and keep notes attached to specific passages (with exports to Markdown, Anki and Jupyter). Built in Swift/SwiftUI using PDFKit. The analysis runs in a helper process at low priority. No account, no telemetry, and it's GPL.
It’s for macOS 15+ only for now (unless a lot of people find it useful, then I’ll probably do it for other OSes).
It still struggles with some PDFs (scanned ones, other languages, different numbering, etc.) If you try it on whatever you're reading and encounter some problems, feel free to open an issue!

source_text:
Release prep: owner decisions for carlab.rs
Owner-only decisions collected by the carlab.rs pre-release QA loop (branch `carlab-shop`). Everything an engineer could decide is already fixed or defaulted in the code; this list holds only what needs you. The loop appends here each round.

## Decisions

- [ ] **[feature] Parts guarantee / returns wording.** Part pages now show the pickup address and hours next to the price, but no guarantee or return promise (we did not invent one). What do we promise? E.g. "manufacturer's warranty", "doesn't fit your VIN, we swap it", "returns within N days on conditions X". Without an answer the line stays out.
- [ ] **[feature] Reviews / rating on the parts path.** Today we show real Works ("Мы уже подбирали") instead of reviews. Do you want a Google rating or reviews block? If yes: the source (Google Business Profile link) and whether the numbers can be shown.
- [ ] **[feature] Installation service per Category.** «Установить у нас» books: `brake-pads`/`brakes`/`suspension` → brakes-suspension, `engine-parts`/`transmission` → engine-gearbox, `body-parts` → bodywork-painting, everything else (batteries, oils, filters) → servicing. Confirm or correct.
- [ ] **[bug] Social account URLs, incl. the real details.rs Instagram.** `PUBLIC_INSTAGRAM` is no longer read; links come from `packages/brands` `social`. Until you send URLs, details.rs shows no Instagram at all. Need: Instagram/Facebook/TikTok/YouTube per brand (approved.rs, carlab.rs, details.rs).
- [ ] **[feature] Telegram tile on the order confirmation.** It opens the capture bot as a Parts sourcing inquiry. Tying it to the order number needs a capture-bot change (accept `parts-order` as a start slug, show an order screen). Worth it now or after release?

- [ ] **[feature] VIN and decode retention.** The shop stores every VIN a visitor typed (`vin_lookup`) and raw decoder responses, with no expiry. How long may we keep them? Suggestion: 12 months, then delete or anonymise. Needs your call (privacy policy / Serbian data law).
- [ ] **[feature] Where Leads live long term.** All Leads sit in one JSON blob on Vercel Blob, read and rewritten whole on every change. Estimate: fine to low thousands, degrading near 10k Leads or ~1 write/s bursts, unusable at 30-50k (lost clicks/forms). Options: (a) archive closed Leads older than N months to a second blob (cheap, soon); (b) move the store to Postgres (more work, a DB cost). Which, and when? Knowing today's `data/leads.json` size would tell us how close we are.
- [ ] **[feature] VPS sizing.** The shop runs Postgres capped at 512 MB and Node at a 1 GB heap. Fine for the closed beta and the current catalogue; a catalogue in the hundreds of thousands of Parts will want a bigger box. Budget for an upgrade before the full catalogue import?

- [ ] **[bug] Analytics before consent.** Metrika (with Webvisor), GA4 and the Meta Pixel start on page load and stop only if the visitor declines (opt-out, ADR-0033 / ADR-0044). Under GDPR and the Serbian personal data law (ZZPL) tracking cookies usually need opt-in, the Pixel most of all. Show HN: Beolis – Manage your coding AI agents
Hey HN, I'm Fabio, the creator of Beolis. I've built Beolis ( https://beolis.com ) to better handle coding on agentic scenarios. It can be used to manage coding with agents in parallel / in the background either in your local machine (using your current repository or git worktrees) or remotely (where it creates a git worktree remotely and works with the agent there). Although it uses agents you don't need to "chat" with the agent at each step as you usually do when dealing with agents (although you still can), but rather create workflows where you can code the default steps you want. This means that instead of saying 'run the tests' to an agent the idea is that you (or the agent) create code that will actually run the tests and then if it fails it goes to a cheap agent to summarize the failures and then onto a smarter agent to actually do the fixes and work on the problems found -- I find my tokens last much longer given that approach ;) I've been using Beolis to build itself (started back in February) and I believe it's now stable for day-to-day use. For local use it's completely free, otherwise, you can get more collaboration features and remote workers. I'd love to hear feedback.

China Construction Materials Sourcing Expert
Freelance China Sourcing Specialist – Construction & Building Materials

We are looking for an experienced independent freelancer, preferably based in China, to help us research, source and compare construction and building materials from Chinese manufacturers and international suppliers.

This is a remote, part-time position with the possibility of a long-term collaboration.

We are looking for an individual freelancer, not a sourcing agency or company.

1. Required experience and skills

* Native or fluent Mandarin Chinese.
* Excellent written and spoken English.
* Preferably based in China.
* Experience sourcing construction materials, architectural products and interior finishing materials.
* Good knowledge of Chinese manufacturers and suppliers.
* Strong negotiation skills and ability to communicate directly with factories.

2. Materials to research and source

We need someone capable of researching materials, even when we do not know the exact product name or technical terminology.

Examples include:

* MDF, HDF, plywood and moisture-resistant boards.
* Flooring, laminates and wall finishes.
* Roofing membranes and waterproofing systems.
* Rock wool and thermal insulation.
* Aluminium profiles, glass and windows.
* Lighting and electrical products.
* Interior and exterior finishing materials.
* Other construction materials and architectural products.

The ability to identify suitable products and propose alternatives is very important.

3. Sourcing platforms

Experience using the following platforms is required:

* Alibaba
* 1688
* Taobao
* Made-in-China
* Other Chinese supplier and manufacturer platforms.

The freelancer must be able to identify reliable manufacturers, compare products, request technical information and negotiate competitive prices.

4. International logistics knowledge

Good knowledge of international shipping and export procedures is essential.

Experience with:

* Sea freight (LCL and FCL).
* Air and road freight.
* Freight forwarders and cargo consolidation.
* Volumetric weight and shipping calculations.
* Shipping costs and estimated delivery times.
* Incoterms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP).
* Export documentation and customs procedures.
* Import duties, taxes and customs clearance.

Experience shipping construction materials to Cambodia or Southeast Asia is an advantage.

5. Expected deliverables

For each product researched, we expect a clear report containing:

* Direct product link.
* Supplier or manufacturer name and contact details.
* Product specifications, dimensions, thickness, density and weight where applicable.
* Product photos, videos and catalogues.
* Unit price and currency.
* Minimum order quantity (MOQ).
* Production time.
* Estimated shipping cost and delivery time.
* Available technical datasheets and certificates.
* Possible import costs, where these can be verified.
* Your professional recommendation and comparison with alternative products.

We need reliable research and useful recommendations, not just links copied from websites.

6. Payment and working arrangement

We do not pay by the hour.

We prefer a results-based working arrangement with clearly agreed deliverables.

First stage – Paid trial project:

* We will agree on a specific research assignment and a fixed price before starting.
* Payment will be made if the freelancer delivers satisfactory results that meet the agreed requirements.
* The trial will help us evaluate the quality of research, technical knowledge, communication and sourcing skills.

Second stage – Monthly collaboration:

If the trial is successful, we would like to establish a long-term monthly collaboration.

* A fixed monthly payment will be agreed in advance.
* Monthly minimum objectives and deliverables will be clearly defined.
* Payment will be based on the agreed objectives and quality of work, not the number of hours worked.
* The workload and objectives can increase as the collaboration develops.

Please include your proposed fixed price for the trial project and your expected monthly fee.

7. Important conditions

* We are looking for an independent freelancer, not an agency.
* No hourly billing.
* All supplier contacts and original product links must be disclosed.
* No hidden commissions or payments from suppliers.
* We will communicate with and pay suppliers directly.
* Transparency, reliability and long-term cooperation are essential.

8. To apply, please answer the following questions

1. Where are you currently based?
2. Are you a native Mandarin speaker?
3. What is your English level?
4. How many years of sourcing experience do you have?
5. Have you worked with construction materials or architectural products?
6. Which Chinese sourcing platforms do you use regularly?
7. Do you have experience negotiating directly with manufacturers?
8. Do you have experience arranging international shipments to Cambodia or Southeast Asia?
9. Can you provide examples of previous sourcing projects?
10. What fixed price would you propose for an initial trial assignment?
11. What monthly fixed fee would you expect for an ongoing collaboration based on agreed objectives?

We are looking for someone knowledgeable, proactive, detail-oriented and capable of becoming a reliable long-term sourcing partner.
Budget: $30-250 USD

Product strategy: Make FBM a daily-use painkiller, not a vitamin
# Product strategy: Make FBM a daily-use painkiller, not a vitamin

## Product thesis

Free Black Market (FBM) should solve immediate, recurring inefficiencies in how people buy, sell, source, ship, finance, and coordinate commerce. Users should discover a problem with their current model and find a practical solution through FBM.

**Core promise:** FBM makes it easier to buy better, sell independently, save money, build businesses, and participate in a community-driven economy—without sacrificing convenience, price, speed, or usability.

The product should affirm users' good decisions with truthful, evidence-backed feedback. Reinforce concrete benefits (money saved, local producers supported, transparent costs, reduced waste, independent businesses strengthened); do not use empty praise or make unsupported ethical, health, political, or environmental claims.

## Buyer outcomes and habits

Buyers should be able to:

- Understand what they are buying: origin, maker/manufacturer, materials/ingredients, product attributes, provenance, and available verification.
- Assess trust through clear seller histories, reviews, fulfillment records, certifications, and transparent product information.
- Discover seller values, affiliations, and stated political or community alignment through voluntary, clearly sourced disclosures and user-selected filters. Do not infer political beliefs.
- See where their money goes, including seller proceeds, platform fees, payment processing, shipping, taxes, and disclosed impact/community allocations.
- Compare the **full delivered price**, not just the listing price.
- Find the lowest-cost option, fastest delivery, local alternatives, and lower-impact options, with tradeoffs explained rather than hiding them behind one ranking.
- Discover healthier or lower-hazard alternatives using substantiated ingredient/material information. Avoid absolute “chemical-free” claims; communicate specific ingredients, substances, certifications, and evidence.
- Share product links and connect with other buyers to coordinate bulk purchases.

### Buyer-facing product capabilities

1. Competitive Price Index across comparable products and sellers.
2. Full cost breakdown: item price, shipping, taxes, fees, delivery estimate, and total.
3. Cheapest-option and fastest-delivery suggestions, with transparent ranking logic.
4. Local discovery and sourcing alternatives.
5. Product transparency, provenance, seller verification, and trust signals.
6. Healthier/lower-hazard alternatives with evidence and clear limitations.
7. Buyer-to-buyer bulk-buy prompts, group purchasing, and shared shipping opportunities.
8. Money-flow and impact summaries that explain what a purchase supports without overstating impact.

## Seller and organization outcomes

FBM should provide the benefits of an integrated corporate operating system without requiring sellers to become corporate or surrender independence.

Help independent businesses, producers, nonprofits, and community organizations start, operate, and scale through:

- Smooth onboarding and guided setup.
- Modern, approachable business software.
- Low and transparent platform costs and commissions.
- Product, inventory, order, customer, and business insights.
- Marketing plans, competitor marketing intelligence, and practical campaign tools.
- Access to customers, creators, collaborators, and trade partners.
- Multichannel distribution: the ability to sell and manage sales across multiple channels.
- Organized B2B sourcing, procurement, and trade opportunities.
- Alternative financing and capital pathways.
- Business strategies and education integrated into workflows.
- Nonprofit and community-organization workflows, not only conventional for-profit commerce.

### Seller-facing product capabilities

1. Guided business launch and onboarding.
2. A simple business operating hub for products, orders, customers, and performance.
3. Competitive pricing and market intelligence.
4. Marketing strategy, campaign assistance, competitor monitoring, and creator discovery.
5. B2B discovery, sourcing, trade matching, and relationship management.
6. Financing discovery and other capital-access pathways.
7. Multichannel selling and portable customer relationships.
8. Nonprofit/community organization support.

## Problems FBM addresses

- Buyers cannot tell where their money goes or what a product contains.
- Cheap products can become expensive or slow after shipping.
- Independent producers and manufacturers are difficult to find.
- Healthy, transparent, local, and lower-impact options are hard to compare.
- Commerce and business infrastructure are concentrated behind corporate platforms.
- Sellers face high commissions, subscriptions, complex software, platform lock-in, and weak customer access.
- Starting and scaling a business requires too many disconnected tools and too much specialized knowledge.
- Small businesses lack marketing support, social proof, creators, and access to capital.
- B2B systems focus on transactions rather than relationships and coordination.
- Buyers and sellers have too few accessible trade, bulk-purchase, and alternative-financing options.
- Nonprofits and community groups are poorly served by conventional commerce software.
- Low transparency makes it difficult to understand the social, economic, health, and environmental consequences of transactions.

People currently cope by accepting opaque or extractive platforms, paying more for distant shipping, delaying or abandoning business ideas, or choosing employment because starting independently is too complicated. FBM should make viable alternatives easier to act on.

## Habit loops and daily-use behavior

Target frequency should be comparable to the frequency with which people use everyday commerce and gig-economy tools such as Amazon, Shopify, Uber Eats, Faire, and Etsy. Earn this frequency through recurring utility—not artificial engagement mechanics.

### 1. Check the market
Users return to check incoming and outgoing products, orders, shipments, price changes, inventory, business performance, and new opportunities.

### 2. Compare before buying
Make FBM a natural first stop before a purchase: compare delivered prices, speed, local options, product details, and alternatives.

### 3. Share useful finds
Make product links easy to share with friends, customers, groups, organizations, and potential bulk buyers. Sharing should help the recipient make a better decision and create measurable value for the sharer where appropriate.

### 4. Hunt, gather, and discover
Make finding products, producers, suppliers, resources, and trade opportunities feel rewarding—like modern foraging, hunting, and gathering. Discovery should lead to useful action and real-world value.

### 5. Build and improve a business
Give sellers a reason to check FBM frequently for orders, customers, business insights, marketing opportunities, pricing recommendations, suppliers, and financing/trade leads.

Connect commerce activity with well-being through tangible feedback: savings, progress, successful fulfillment, local connections, useful discoveries, and community participation.

## Product principles

1. **Affirm good decisions:** recognize real, measurable benefits; avoid manipulative flattery.
2. **Show the full picture:** disclose costs, money flows, product information, and ranking criteria.
3. **Make better options convenient:** compare price, quality, speed, health-related attributes, locality, and impact without assuming one dimension always wins.
4. **Reduce complexity:** make business ownership accessible to people without business or technical expertise.
5. **Connect rather than isolate:** connect buyers, sellers, producers, nonprofits, creators, investors, and communities.
6. **Reward useful participation:** prioritize economic and community value over empty engagement.
7. **Preserve independence:** provide infrastructure without unnecessary lock-in or surrender of ownership and control.
8. **Be evidence-led:** clearly distinguish verified facts, seller claims, estimates, and unknowns—especially for political alignment, health, and environmental impact.

## Success metrics

Measure repeat utility and user outcomes, not registrations alone:

- Buyer and seller activation and retention.
- Weekly/daily repeat visits tied to useful tasks.
- Product comparisons and share links per active user.
- Conversion from comparison to purchase.
- Verified buyer savings and total delivered-cost differences.
- Delivery speed and fulfillment reliability.
- Repeat purchase and repeat seller revenue.
- Verified-product information coverage and trust outcomes.
- Bulk-buy participation and group-buy savings.
- Local sourcing and supplier discovery.
- Trade matches and completed exchanges.
- Seller time-to-launch and time-to-first-sale.
- Seller acquisition cost, platform fees, and customer access.
- Marketing campaign adoption and measurable results.
- Nonprofit/community organization activation.
- Environmental and health-related indicators only where defensible data exists.

## Implementation approach

Build the initial painkillers before attempting the entire economic ecosystem.

**First-wave priorities**
1. Full delivered-cost breakdown and transparent price comparison.
2. Product/seller transparency and trust information.
3. Local discovery and shipping comparisons.
4. Smooth seller onboarding and a simple operating dashboard.
5. Product-link sharing and basic buyer-to-buyer coordination.
6. Useful buyer and seller activity summaries.

**Next-wave capabilities**
- Competitive Price Index at scale.
- Bulk/group purchasing workflows.
- Healthier/lower-hazard alternatives.
- Competitor marketing intelligence and creator access.
- B2B sourcing, trade, and financing opportunities.
- Multichannel operations and nonprofit/community workflows.
- More complete money-flow and impact reporting.

Treat this as product direction, not a claim that these capabilities are already shipped. Validate each feature against user research, data availability, operational feasibility, and measurable outcomes before promising it.

## Mission

FBM should help more people become entrepreneurs, producers, organizers, leaders, and active participants in a community-driven system that decreases harm. The long-term goal is not merely to move transactions from one marketplace to another; it is to make independent economic participation practical, convenient, and rewarding.

**North star:** People use FBM because it makes their lives easier, and keep using it because it helps them build stronger communities.

Trend Signals for Developers 1. **Privacy‑first tooling is now a blocker.** Multiple repos (Claude Code, OpenCode, Qwen Code) expose leaks in HTTP headers or exported sessions, prompting “privacy‑mod” or sanitisation APIs. Expect forthcoming CLIs to ship **opt‑out privacy layers** as a default. 2. **Headless/daemon operation is a prerequisite for CI/CD.** Issues around `--headless` mode (Claude Code #30447), Windows process‑tree killing (Pi #11854), and sandbox‑free dev modes (DeepSeek #4955) illustrate that teams are moving AI‑assisted coding into pipelines, not just interactive terminals. 3. **Project‑level context and long‑term memory are converging.** From Claude Code’s “Projects” integration to Qwen Code’s durable user‑question feature and Kimi’s knowledge‑plane PR, the ecosystem is coalescing around **persistent, searchable knowledge bases** that survive session restarts. 4. **Token‑budget visibility is becoming a UX pillar.** Token‑inflation bugs (#10287, #102828), auto‑compaction complaints (#4106), and explicit budgeting tools (OpenAI Codex PR #59794) indicate developers need **real‑time cost dashboards** to keep cloud spend predictable. 5. **International‑input ergonomics will differentiate products.** Configurable submit keys (Copilot #1972), IME double‑press bugs (Qwen #16430), and macOS CPU spikes tied to non‑Latin input (Pi #7730) signal that **global developer adoption** hinges on robust IME handling and customizable keymaps. 6. **Modular, plug‑in architectures are gaining traction.** Gemini CLI’s sub‑agent sandbox, DeepSeek‑TUI’s crate‑level decomposition, and Pi’s “durable‑wait” markers all aim for **extensible runtime pipelines**, suggesting future tooling will expose more granular APIs for third‑party plugins (memory stores, custom tools, telemetry). --- ### Bottom Line for Decision‑Makers - **If you prioritize a low‑friction, VS Code‑centric developer experience** – GitHub Copilot CLI offers the smoothest UI, though its open‑source activity is modest. - **Emerging capabilities (project‑aware memory, multi‑backend switching, visual output generation)** are being pioneered across most repos; adopting a tool that already exposes a **knowledge‑plane API** (e.g., Claude Code Projects, Qwen Code durable questions) will future‑proof your workflow. source_text:
> None of which was a good reason to use it on servers. Even if you were familiar with Ubuntu there is very little difference between an Ubuntu server
> None of which was a good reason to use it on servers. Even if you were familiar with Ubuntu there is very little difference between an Ubuntu server and a Debian one. Something to keep in mind is that the term "server" covers a wide range from datacenter beasts pulling kilowatts per node to old desktops running headless to Pi Zeroes and repurposed cell phones, and some of those use cases do in fact benefit from access to proprietary drivers and even hacks like NDISWrapper. Beyond that, I've seen two main reasons to use Ubuntu Server over Debian, and I say this as someone who has administered Ubuntu, Debian, and CentOS systems for years and always chooses Ubuntu or Debian when the options are open. 1. For a while there were commercial software vendors that would release Linux versions only for specific distros, and Ubuntu was on that list a lot more often than Debian, so if you liked Debian-style packaging and wanted to use commercial software there was a reason to use Ubuntu.  Zimbra was one of those when I last used it in the late '00s. 2. There was a time where it seemed like every F/OSS project had a PPA which made it really convenient to install on Ubuntu with automatic updates as part of the system package manager while Debian had to manually load .debs or might not have even had a package due to older system libraries.  For personal toy servers and "pet" dev servers this is wonderful, obviously far less important for well-managed "cattle" servers. Docker, Flatpack, and to a much lesser extent Snap have pretty much eliminated these reasons though.  My home server is still Ubuntu LTS because it's easier than changing it but when it next gets rebuilt things will be changing a lot.  All of my work servers are migrating to Debian, we have one Ubuntu instance remaining that just had its last major service switched away and a bunch of CentOS systems on sites which are getting swapped out whenever our techs happen to visit.

source_text:
Implement Scoped, Expiring Keeper Delegations for Automated Operations
**Description:**
Introduce a delegation primitive that lets an account grant a keeper (the backend operator, a third-party automation service, or a bot) narrowly scoped, expiring authority to execute specific permissioned entrypoints without handing over full admin rights. Automation then runs with least privilege and a hard expiry.

**Problem Statement & Context:**
Several flows are designed to be executed by whoever is around: settling due escrows, executing due timelocked actions, extending TTLs. In practice the backend needs a key that can do these things, and today the only options are an over-broad admin role or manual multisig signing — both unacceptable for routine, high-frequency automation. This is also a prerequisite for unattended operation during an incident.

**Scope & Acceptance Criteria:**
- Add `delegate(grantee, scope, expires_at_ledger, max_calls)` and `revoke(grantee)`, callable by the granting account or its admin.
- `scope` is a checked bitmask of named capabilities (execute due escrow, execute timelocked action, extend TTL, trigger rate refresh), documented in the interface crate.
- Every guarded entrypoint accepts either a direct role holder or a delegate whose scope covers it and whose expiry/max-calls budget is unexpired.
- Delegates can never amplify: a delegated call that internally requires a stronger role fails instead of succeeding.
- Events on grant, use, exhaustion, expiry-triggered rejection, and revoke; view listing a grantor's active delegations.
- Out of scope: delegation of governance voting power (tracked separately) and off-chain key management.

**Implementation Guidelines:**
1. Key Files/Modules: `backstop/src/lib.rs`, `bounty/src/lib.rs`, `grants/src/lib.rs`, `treasury/src/lib.rs` for the guard, the shared interface crate for the scope enum, `tests/` for the authorization matrix.
2. Design/Architecture: a single `require_scoped_auth(scope)` helper backed by persistent delegation records keyed by `(grantor, grantee)`; decrement `max_calls` in the same invocation that performs the guarded action so a failed call does not consume budget.
3. Edge Cases/Constraints: expiry at the exact ledger boundary, revocation during an in-flight execution, scope combinations that are individually harmless but jointly dangerous, and keeping the guard cheap enough not to blow the instruction budget on hot paths.
4. Testing: a full scope x entrypoint matrix, expiry boundary tests, max-calls exhaustion, revocation, and explicit negative tests proving no path escalates to admin.

**Complexity:** Medium (130 points)

source_text:
Show HN: Frink – Desktop-first app for multi-step workflows and parallel agents
What’s up HN?! I'm Benji, and I’ve been building Frink since ~April this year. Frink is a desktop-first, open-source (MIT) app for running coding agents in parallel and multi-step workflows that start on their own. It runs on your machine (macOS and Linux) with your own provider login. It currently supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and OpenCode, but the latter 3 are in preview. No Frink account to use the app. The biggest USP of Frink is workflows: think n8n for agents. You describe a routine in a sentence, for example: "every weekday at 9am, run the tests; if any fail, have an agent fix them, then wait for my approval before it opens a PR." Then, Frink builds it as a workflow (or simply, Flow): a list of steps you can read and change before it runs. A Flow can start on a schedule, from any webhook, or from an event from a third-party such as Linear, Shortcut, ClickUp, Sentry, PostHog, etc. Steps can be agent turns, shell commands, conditions, approval steps that stop and wait for you, or steps you write yourself in code (or ask the agent to write one). Everything that needs you (an approval, an agent's question, a finished task to review) lands in one Work Queue. Other stuff: * Up to four agents side by side, each on its own git worktree if you want. Or, many agents out of direct view. * Every change shows as a diff; there's a code editor, a terminal, etc. * Local-first: chats, Flows and tasks live in SQLite on your machine. * Easier provider parity: currently working on and improving the tooling setup between providers. Once inside Frink, irrespective of what provider you use, the hooks, MCPs, and other tooling work out of the box between providers. Why I built it: I started building it when there weren’t many other competitors; now the industry is swamped with ADEs and harnesses. However, in my opinion, each still lacks good automation for more fine-tuned scenarios. I doubled down on the flows to help me with my actual day-to-day job as a SWE, and over time it’s helped me automate most of the PRs being shipped across my personal projects, team, etc., to the point that it’s a continuous loop and helps a whole ton. Notes: Windows isn't supported yet. Flows only run on Claude Code and Codex for now. It's a solo project, so expect sharp edges.

Optional upstream API supply: original outputs, model costs and evaluation support
Hi Venice team — I’m Yami from ToAPIs. This is a supplier-cooperation proposal, not a bug report.

Venice provides a hosted chat/image/video platform and MCP client with endpoint-specific auth and response-size protections. We prepared original outputs, exact parameters and a dated price sheet for an optional upstream evaluation:
https://github.com/ToAPIs-2025/lower-cost-venice-upstream-toapis

Our international test Key currently quotes gpt-image-2 / 1K at $0.015/image and gpt-image-2.5-flare / 1K at $0.0225/image. Both amounts were confirmed by settled image receipts on October 29. Seedance 2.5 / 720p / one first frame / 4s requested / audio off settled at $0.873 for a decoded 4.04s clip (about $0.216089/s for that example; Key quote $10/1M total tokens). The quotations were checked on October 30; the original settled media are reused October 29 examples, not native acceptance in your product or universal tariffs.

We can support an optional Provider with evaluation credits and hands-on parameter/debugging help, product/documentation sponsorship where useful, or supplementary upstream API supply for your own hosted service. Larger-volume terms can be discussed against your exact models, output specifications and expected demand. Your branding, customer billing and existing suppliers can stay in place.

Any supplier evaluation would first need agreement on your data-processing, retention and region requirements. We do not assume equivalence with your privacy, EU-only routing or TEE commitments.

Would the person responsible for image/video model sourcing be open to reviewing these options? We can follow your supplier process and support a test that addresses an actual requirement from your team.

Thank you,
YamiAnn — ToAPIs Team
yami@toapis.com

AI/semis evening brief, Oct 26: 63 updates, 25 high [part 1/2]
# Anthropic files to go public, and AI supply chains rally on the strength of its spending

**The bottom line:** Anthropic's IPO filing gave markets their first audited look at what a frontier lab spends on compute: $8.9 billion in just the first half of 2026. That spend lands with the chip, memory and optics suppliers. On the same day, Amazon said AWS capacity is sold out through 2027, Lumentum said its optical capacity is booked into 2029, and Celestica guided to roughly doubling revenue next year. Demand is not the open question. Financing is: more of the build-out is now funded by debt and equity raises.

## Anthropic's S-1: a renter of compute, not an owner

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude models, filed its prospectus on Monday to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E8TJMZeVtHs)). The key line for the supply chain is compute and infrastructure expense. It was $7.3 billion for all of 2025 and $8.9 billion for the first six months of 2026. Spending on its own property and equipment was only $482 million. Anthropic rents its compute from cloud providers rather than building it ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E8TJMZeVtHs)).

The headline net loss of $80.7 billion looks alarming but is mostly accounting. A $72.4 billion non-cash charge on convertible notes explains why the company still reported positive operating cash flow ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E8TJMZeVtHs)). Chinese outlet CLS reports H1 2026 revenue up more than 13x year on year ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515964?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

CLS also reports a listing around November 16 and more than $600 billion of future infrastructure commitments ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515835?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Both figures are reported, not confirmed.

On valuation, the last funding round valued Anthropic at $965 billion. Some investors have floated $2 trillion for the IPO. Each of the seven founders holds about 1.4%, worth more than $13 billion apiece ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515861?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Dario Amodei's 2025 pay was about $17.96 million, mostly stock and options ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4042865455502213)).

**Read-through:** Because Anthropic rents its compute, its bill flows to cloud providers such as Amazon (AMZN) and, through them, to GPU, memory and networking suppliers. A successful listing would give the lab public-market capital to keep honouring those commitments. Markets read it that way: SK Hynix rose more than 6% at the open on the filing ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515945?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

## Demand is sold out; the question is who pays

Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said AWS compute capacity is essentially sold out through end-2027, with large orders stretching into 2028 ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516093?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). That is the strongest demand signal of the period.

The funding side is shifting. Meta (META) plans to raise a total of $95 billion for AI infrastructure and its superintelligence push, and its stock fell 1.6% in early trading. Nvidia (NVDA), AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) reportedly expressed interest in buying up to $5 billion of Meta stock ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4043342836798597)). That would be suppliers helping fund a customer's purchases from them.

Sources disagree on the details:
- **Meta:** one report cites up to $950 million via stock sales, not $95 billion ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515966?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **SpaceX:** its GPU financing lease is reported as $40 billion by one outlet ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-27/detail-iniwrkkw2102981.d.html)) and about $400 billion by another ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515966?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

Treat both as unconfirmed until filings appear.

Bank forecasts point the same way. A Yahoo Finance segment puts Big Tech's 2027 AI capex at $1.2 trillion. JPMorgan puts hyperscaler spending above $1.1 trillion, and Goldman Sachs expects about one-third to be debt-funded ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rqlvkSPkTIQ)).

The counterpoint came from Apollo's chief economist Torsten Sløk. He found revenue per worker rising in tech but flat elsewhere, with no margin expansion outside tech so far ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jEwMFxOR0Ls)). If AI buyers outside tech don't see returns, debt-funded capex becomes the weak link.

## Korea's memory makers ride the wave into earnings week

Korean chip stocks rallied hard. Samsung (005930.KS) rose 4.9% and SK Hynix (000660.KS) 7.3% ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-27/detail-iniwrkkw2102981.d.html)), and the KOSPI opened up 3.46% ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515945?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Korean media report that SK Hynix will announce an extra 50–60 trillion won shareholder return plan alongside its October 28 earnings. Samsung reports October 31 ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-27/detail-iniwrkkw2102981.d.html)).

The macro data backs this up. Korea's Q3 GDP grew 1.0% quarter on quarter and 3.4% year on year, beating consensus of 0.8% and 3.1%, on AI-driven chip exports and investment. The Bank of Korea expects growth notably above prior forecasts and updates its outlook on November 26 ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2515916?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The same central bank also modelled the downside. In a pessimistic scenario where US tech giants cut AI capex, Korean chip exports could come in "USD 500 billion to 1 trillion" below forecast ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4043525373285253)). That range looks implausibly large and may be a translation or unit error. The point stands that Korea's growth is now tied to US hyperscaler budgets.

RBC Capital expects the memory shortage to persist through 2027. It sees prices for HBM, the stacked high-bandwidth memory used next to AI GPUs, doubling in 2026, which supports overall DRAM selling prices, with SK Hynix the main beneficiary ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909462843.html)).

Further down the memory chain, Rambus (RMBS) also benefits. It makes interface and power-management chips for server memory modules and licenses memory IP. It posted record revenue of $218.3 million, up 22%, with product revenue of $114.3 million, and guided to "even stronger" Q4 ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/917273/000119312526431918/0001193125-26-431918-index.htm)).

## Optics and server builders: capacity booked for years

Celestica (CLS), a Toronto-based contract manufacturer that builds networking switches and AI server racks for hyperscalers, delivered the period's standout numbers:
- **Q3:** revenue up 83% to $5.83 billion.
- **2026 guidance:** raised to $21 billion.
- **2027 initial guidance:** $40 billion of revenue at a record 9% adjusted operating margin.
- **Beyond:** its CEO said customer forecasts for 2028 are "meaningfully higher" ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1030894/000103089426000049/0001047127-26-000049-index.htm)).

That is a direct read-across to suppliers of 800G and 1.6T networking.

Lumentum (LITE), a US maker of lasers and optical components, went further. Its CEO said capacity is booked through the start of 2029, customers are locking in 2030 supply, and about 70% of 2027 market demand will go unmet even with expansion ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516106?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The comments lifted China's co-packaged optics (CPO) names. CPO puts optical links directly next to the chip. Innolight (300308.SZ), the largest maker of the transceivers that link AI servers, rose 4%+ in Hong Kong trading ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516046?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Ruiyuan's Growth Value Fund raised its Innolight stake by over 80% in Q3 ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909462031.html)).

China's statistics bureau shows how much money this is moving through the supply chain. In January–September:
- Optical fibre manufacturing profit rose 5.7x and optical cable 1.1x, on datacenter construction ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516043?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- Electronic specialty materials profit grew 2.2x and semiconductor discretes rose 51.7% ([Tonghuashun](https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20261027/c681117842.shtml)).
- High-tech manufacturing profit rose 52% ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909251048.html)).

Smaller suppliers are feeling it too. Machine-tool maker Createch (300083.SZ) said nine-month new orders rose 77%. AI hardware, mainly liquid-cooling and optical-module makers, was the largest source at 25.5% of orders ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300083/AN202610271831010970.html)). Guoci Materials (300285.SZ), a supplier of the ceramic powder used in MLCC capacitors (tiny components found throughout every server board), expects batch supply for AI-server grades in Q4 ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909234087.html)).

## Packaging and equipment: bonding is the new battleground

Applied Materials (AMAT) will lift its stake in Dutch assembly-equipment maker Besi (BESI.AS) to about 20%. Besi leads in hybrid bonding, which fuses chips directly copper-to-copper and is key for stacking HBM and chiplets. The partnership extends to thermo-compression bonding and die-on-wafer and die-on-panel integration. Applied says it won't go beyond ~20% or seek a board seat, and the deal awaits US antitrust (HSR) clearance ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/6951/000162828026067303/0001628280-26-067303-index.htm)). Applied is effectively locking in the advanced-packaging toolset that AI chips increasingly depend on.

Not everyone in packaging is keeping pace. Amkor (AMKR), the largest US-listed outsourced chip packager, missed on Q3 sales: $1.99 billion versus a $2.04 billion estimate. Its Q4 guide of $1.9–2.0 billion also trails the $2.05 billion consensus, despite record computing revenue and capex raised to about $2.5 billion ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1047127/000104712726000049/0001047127-26-000049-index.htm)). The mixed result suggests AI gains are not yet offsetting softness elsewhere in its business.

Jefferies expects the equipment boom to persist through 2028. It rates Applied and Lam Research (LRCX) Buy, and ASML (ASML) and Screen Holdings Hold ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909402132.html)). In China, chip-test equipment maker Changchuan Technology (300604.SZ) reported nine-month revenue up 57% and net profit up 104%, and plans a CNY 50–100 million buyback ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909431523.html)).

## China: model exports, compute build-out and robots

On policy, state media say DeepSeek and MiniMax have completed technology-export registration with the Commerce and Science ministries. That clears them for open-source releases and overseas licensing ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610263908186113.html)). Beijing is formalising oversight of model exports rather than blocking them. Hong Kong-listed model maker Zhipu jumped 10%+ ([Tonghuashun](https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20261027/c681118656.shtml)).

Compute is being built close to cheap power. Envision Group delivered phase one of its Ulanqab datacenter in Inner Mongolia. The site is planned for 3GW of load with 80% direct green power, and compute orders are booked into 2027 ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909462262.html)).

Robotics demand is growing, though the evidence so far is thinner:
- **Sales:** China's embodied-AI robot sales rose 22.6% in the first three quarters ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4043296859837574)).
- **ByteDance:** it is hiring across robot hardware, dexterous hands and data ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2516058?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **Toyota:** a single report says it plans to deploy 400,000 humanoids ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610273909419517.html)).

Component suppliers are still mostly at the sample stage. For now, the robot trade runs more on announcements than on orders.

## What to watch

- **SK Hynix (Oct 28) and Samsung (Oct 31) earnings:** HBM pricing commentary and whether the reported 50–60 trillion won return plan materialises.
- **Anthropic's roadshow and pricing, reportedly mid-November:** how the market values a lab that rents its compute, and whether the $600B+ commitment figure is confirmed.
- **Meta and SpaceX financing details:** the reported sizes conflict, and the debt share of AI capex is the key risk flagged by Goldman and Apollo.
- **Bank of Korea forecast update (Nov 26):** an early gauge of how exposed Korea is to any slowdown in US AI capex.
- **Besi deal clearance under HSR:** watch for rival moves to secure hybrid-bonding capacity.

---

# Highlights (25)

Optional upstream API supply: original outputs, model costs and evaluation support
Hi APIDot team — I’m Yami from ToAPIs. This is a supplier-cooperation proposal, not a bug report.

APIDot runs a multimodal API platform with common submission, task polling and webhook examples. We prepared original outputs, exact parameters and a dated price sheet for an optional upstream evaluation:
https://github.com/ToAPIs-2025/lower-cost-apidot-upstream-toapis

Our international test Key currently quotes gpt-image-2 / 1K at $0.015/image and gpt-image-2.5-flare / 1K at $0.0225/image. Both amounts were confirmed by settled image receipts on October 29. Seedance 2.5 / 720p / one first frame / 4s requested / audio off settled at $0.873 for a decoded 4.04s clip (about $0.216089/s for that example; Key quote $10/1M total tokens). The quotations were checked on October 30; the original settled media are reused October 29 examples, not native acceptance in your product or universal tariffs.

We can support an optional Provider with evaluation credits and hands-on parameter/debugging help, product/documentation sponsorship where useful, or supplementary upstream API supply for your own hosted service. Larger-volume terms can be discussed against your exact models, output specifications and expected demand. Your branding, customer billing and existing suppliers can stay in place.

We recognize that public starting prices can refer to different quality/channels. We are not claiming to undercut your current procurement rate; the guide gives exact test-Key specifications so your team can assess a suitable capacity or model gap.

Would the person responsible for image/video model sourcing be open to reviewing these options? We can follow your supplier process and support a test that addresses an actual requirement from your team.

Thank you,
YamiAnn — ToAPIs Team
yami@toapis.com

source_text:
PROC-05A: Governed procurement plan review
# PROC-05A governed plan review — implementation issue

**Status:** Source groundwork authorized; business configuration and live activation remain pending. **Source:** [28-section child specification](PROC-05A-GOVERNED-PLAN-REVIEW.md). **Baseline:** ERP `61d5a608f9cc6069bcf8d06ef51bdca036fd8d47`.

## Problem

The current plan API and UI save, edit, list and cancel owner Drafts only. There is no submission, named independent review, final approval, return/reject/withdraw, active forecast or review history. `ProcurementPlan` has no branch field; existing branchless Drafts cannot safely become branch-scoped by assuming a default branch. The shared Core Approval engine supports generic source records, but its current Procurement executor is purchase-request-specific and its existing delegation record does not establish a working plan delegation path.

## Bounded implementation

- Extend plan records with verified selected-branch ownership and Core organization default currency for new Drafts. Keep old branchless Drafts restricted; add `POST /plans/{id}/claim-scope` with expected version, reason, verified selected branch and explicit confirmation of the stored currency. An organization-wide claim needs an explicit Core permission; no role-name bypass, guessed branch or currency reinterpretation.
- Add explicit, default-ungranted Core plan submission/review/approval/withdraw/read actions and a typed published plan-review policy. No monetary defaults or Finance reservation.
- Open a shared Core approval case with `SourceType=procurement_plan`, pinned plan/line versions and exact values, policy version, branch, maker, named independent assignments and quorum. Use `ApprovalEngine`; do not copy its state machine into Procurement.
- Implement Draft/Returned → Submitted → Reviewed → Active using exactly two initial stage purposes, Review and Final. Business assignees and quorum are configured, never source defaults. Return/reject complete a round and retain it. Withdraw cancels a pending Core case, records a Withdrawn round, and restores the parent plan to editable Draft for resubmission. Final Core Approved decision and Procurement Active state commit together.
- Add actor-bound original-key command receipts, current Core permission/branch/SoD checks, audit/outbox, assigned queue/history and safe error/recovery contracts.
- Extend the original live Plan UI with returned `allowedActions`, plain-language task labels, reason prompts, history and exact-key recovery. Preserve existing Draft CRUD and page layout.
- Treat delegated decisions as unavailable until a separate shared Core current-delegation resolver and denial tests are established. Approved plan-line→PR trace is a follow-on issue.

## Acceptance

Workerless Core maker, reviewer and independent final approver complete one real-cookie private journey on a finite-role PostgreSQL clone. Return/resubmit, reject and Withdraw→Draft→Edit→Resubmit retain previous rounds. Legacy branch/currency claim is explicit, CAS-audited and guarded by owner or separate Core claim permission. Same-key replay returns the original result; changed payload, stale version and concurrent decisions do not duplicate work. Wrong tenant/entity/branch/actor and maker self-approval fail without writes; current revocation is effective. Company All read includes only assigned branches, and all writes use a concrete selected branch. Original business rows and Core identities remain intact; no Finance budget or PO row changes. Original UI actions, denied paths and recovery are exercised with real API, plus source/provider tests.

## Sequence and release hold

1. Review the child spec and resolve business assignee/policy/period choices.
2. Implement domain/API/source tests in a branch based on published ERP main. Do not generate or edit EF migration/snapshot while sourcing B1 owns the schema branch.
3. After B1 is published, generate genuine additive migration from that baseline, test finite roles/ownership/readiness, then private API and original UI acceptance.
4. Release remains default off until reviewed policy, operation evidence and business acceptance exist. No production switch, role grant, Finance posting or external supplier workflow is part of this issue.

Avoid Vizio at all costs! I recently picked one up at Sam's Club. Since my use was only to display an external HDMI source, I never even configured Wi
Avoid Vizio at all costs! I recently picked one up at Sam's Club. Since my use was only to display an external HDMI source, I never even configured Wifi. Unfortunately, they're now wise to this. If it detects its been offline for ten or so start-ups, the TV will 'helpfully' force you into the Wifi config workflow on the next start. It seems to keep an internal counter in flash memory which nothing but a factory reset will clear. In my tests, it seemed like it can be kept offline forever but at the cost of manually dismissing the Wifi config workflow with three clicks on the remote every ~10 power-ons. The TV also will not turn on and just display an external HDMI source even though it has a "Remember Last Source" feature. That feature  does  work as expected with any internal streaming source but external sources must first be manually selected with the remote after each power on (also undocumented in the manual). I figured this out because I bought this small TV to be a wall-mounted screen in the dedicated bathroom of our home theater room. It's only job is to turn on while someone is in the little bathroom and display a copy what's on the main 150" projector screen in the next room, then turn off when they leave. The on/off is handled by a motion sensor and standard Home Assistant automation but after power on it correctly shows the Last Selected external HDMI source for 1 second, then blanks the screen. The source is already selected and working but being blacked out until you manually re-select the same source with the remote (only if it's external). This is clearly an undocumented anti-pattern added specifically to prevent the TV being used unattended as a display screen, picture frame, digital sign etc. Why? Because Vizio (now owned by WalMart) doesn't get rev share if it's: 1) Not online, and 2) Only displaying external sources. That's why it demands manual "proof-of-life" before it'll grudgingly deliver the basic functionality it claims on the box. This made me angry - and the TV was otherwise the perfect size and feature set for my use case. So I programmed an ESP32 with an IR emitter so that every time the TV powers on it sends the remote presses to manually clear the "Please Connect Internet" message and re-select the already-selected external HDMI. Very annoying to be forced to figure this out but now it works fine and no one even sees the annoying messages as they're already gone before by the time we enter and see the screen. So, fuck Vizio :-). Although, I'm pretty sure almost all current consumer TVs now sell all your data exactly the same. The only differences may be the depth of dark patterns they deploy to resist offline usage. To be fair, aside from all the super evil dark patterns, it's a shockingly good quality small TV (24-inch) for $88. Although it's obviously not a high-end display (no native HDR or 24fps), the chipset does do a decent job tone mapping external HDR (and HDR10) sources to SDR and it does proper 3:2 pull-down to display 24 frame external sources at 60fps - which very few TVs in this size do well (or at all). This is why I kept it and spent the time 'fixing' it. Of course, this is only because the TV is subsidized by the $35-$60 avg yearly revenue TV manufacturers reportedly can collect from advertising, app install payments, rev shares and selling all your viewing data. For $88 at local retail, it's probably being sold at a small loss. What's sad is I would have paid double that for the same TV without the dark patterns (in fact, I did buy and return two 24" TVs before this one for $160 and $200 but they couldn't even display external HDR or 24fps sources at all - which was a requirement since this secondary display has to display sources configured for the main projector).

spec automation/service_ledger v3: one door settle_service for the money path (receipt, gate, books, delivery)
Owner's principle of 2026-10-23, in two halves: every service this project sells
emits a receipt, one splitter reads it, and the distribution is decided by rules
alone -- and all the accounting is settled without any person taking part.

This issue closes the money path on paper: service_ledger v1..v3 (four services,
one receipt gate, books derived from entries, and `settle_service` as the single
door), token-wallet v2 (the three-unit trade) and payout's `trade_split_fits`.

## Boundary

- specs/automation/service_ledger.t27
- specs/automation/token-wallet.t27
- specs/verified/payout.t27
- .trinity/seals/automation_automation::service_ledger.json
- .trinity/seals/automation_automation::token_wallet.json
- .trinity/seals/verified_VerifiedPayout.json
- docs/now/

## Goal

One spec-owned door (`settle_service`) that settles any of the four services in a
fixed order -- books-STOP, receipt gate, payout eligibility, books arithmetic,
delivery -- answering SETTLE_STOP / SETTLE_NONE / SETTLE_HOLD / SETTLE_PAY.

## Why this matters

Until v3 the rules lived in separate functions, so a host could call them in the
wrong order (pay before the gate, accrue before eligibility). One door makes the
order impossible to bypass, and HOLD separates "earned but not payable today"
from "not earned".

## Source of truth

- specs/automation/service_ledger.t27 (new)
- specs/automation/token-wallet.t27
- specs/verified/payout.t27

## Deliverable

- specs/automation/service_ledger.t27 v3: `settle_service`, `SETTLE_*` verdicts,
  books (`BOOK_STOP`), accrual only on `payout()==PAY_NORMAL`, flags
  (COMPLETION_HOST_EXISTS=false, BOOKS_HOST_EXISTS=false, TRI_PAYABLE=false).
- specs/automation/token-wallet.t27 v2: TRADE_UNITS 3, SHARE_HOUSE/BOUNTY/REFERRAL,
  trade_charged/trade_share/trade_split_fits.
- specs/verified/payout.t27: `trade_split_fits` refusal (subtract-not-add).
- Seals for all three specs regenerated.

## User Scenarios

Given a course completion receipt that passed the gate and books that read clean,
when `settle_service` runs with TRI_PAYABLE=false, then the verdict is SETTLE_HOLD
-- the accrual stands, nothing leaves.

Given unreadable books, when `settle_service` runs for any service, then the
verdict is SETTLE_STOP before any gate or payout check is consulted.

Given a receipt that payout() refuses (unverified or unreferenced), when
`settle_service` runs, then the verdict is SETTLE_NONE and no book entry exists.

## Requirements

- FR-001: `settle_service` MUST run the chain in the fixed order books-STOP,
  receipt gate, payout eligibility, books arithmetic, delivery, and no caller
  path may reorder it.
- FR-002: an accrual entry MUST exist only where `payout(...)` answers PAY_NORMAL;
  a slash or any refusal MUST accrue nothing.
- FR-003: an unreadable or inconsistent book MUST stop the run (BOOK_STOP /
  SETTLE_STOP) and MUST NOT read as "nothing was owed".
- FR-004: HOLD MUST be reachable only when the books already say PAY; a zero
  balance with a non-payable unit MUST be NONE, never HOLD.
- FR-005: the spec MUST NOT price, promise or mint $TRI; TRI_PAYABLE stays false
  until trust model, settlement path and mainnet are all live.

## Success Criteria

- `./target-bench/release/t27c test-report specs/automation/service_ledger.t27`
  exits 0 with 24 tests and 2 invariants proved, vacuous 0.
- `./target-bench/release/t27c seal --verify` exits 0 for all three specs.
- `t27c validate-seals --pr-files specs/automation/service_ledger.t27,specs/automation/token-wallet.t27,specs/verified/payout.t27` exits 0.

## How to verify

```bash
./target-bench/release/t27c test-report specs/automation/service_ledger.t27
./target-bench/release/t27c seal --verify specs/automation/service_ledger.t27
./target-bench/release/t27c seal --verify specs/automation/token-wallet.t27
./target-bench/release/t27c seal --verify specs/verified/payout.t27
```

## Risks

DESIGN, no host yet: COMPLETION_HOST_EXISTS=false, BOOKS_HOST_EXISTS=false,
LIVE=false, TRI_PAYABLE=false. Must not be sold as live until a host splits a
real charge and a real completion runs through these functions.

- Owner decisions 2026-10-23 (trace in service_ledger.t27 header)
- Host: gHashTag/999-multibots-telegraf (billing-shared.ts, token-ledger.ts)
- Network law: gHashTag/trinity-fpga specs/trinet/settlement_law.t27

AI/semis morning brief, Oct 23: 92 updates, 24 high [part 1/2]
# China's optics makers say AI orders are booked into 2028

**The bottom line:** China's optical-module chain sent one message in a flood of filings. Orders are full, the 1.6T (1.6 terabit-per-second) generation is ramping, and big overseas customers are now giving demand guidance for 2028. Memory is the other pressure point: AI datacenters are absorbing DRAM supply, and phone buyers are paying for it. Beijing's chip ambitions also got fresh fuel from Cambricon's results, DeepSeek's reported record fundraise and a new five-year informatisation plan.

## Optical modules: full order books and longer visibility

Innolight (300308.SZ / 3308.HK), the world's largest maker of the optical transceivers that link AI servers, said orders from its main overseas customers run through 2027. Some key accounts have given 2028 demand guidance ([HKEX](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/1023/2026102300380.pdf)). First-half revenue was CNY 41.78bn, up 182.5%, and net profit was CNY 13.65bn, up 241.7%. The company described pricing as "healthy" and competition as "orderly." It plans to cancel 5.65mn repurchased shares rather than use them for staff incentives ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300308/AN202610231830833072.html)). Next-generation formats, NPO (near-packaged optics) and XPO, will "gradually release."

Its closest rival, Eoptolink (300502.SZ), said 1.6T modules have entered a sustained ramp with shipments accelerating ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300502/AN202610231830831587.html)). It also approved a RMB 800mn–1bn buyback ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300502/AN202610231830831590.html)). Accelink (002281.SZ) reported "ample" orders and no adverse change in trends ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/002281/AN202610231830830889.html)).

The read-through runs upstream to the component makers:

- **Sourcetech (688498.SH)**, which makes the laser chips inside transceivers, guided Q3 revenue up 265–293% and net profit up 579–660%. A second fab phase should add capacity around the turn of the year ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688498/AN202610231830832769.html)).
- **Lianxun Instruments (688808.SH)** tests 800G and 1.6T modules. It forecast Q3 profit up roughly 1,900–2,100% and says it is global number two in 1.6T core test gear ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688808/AN202610231830834114.html)).
- **TFC Optical (300394.SZ)**, a component supplier, reported H1 net profit of RMB 1.2bn on RMB 2.83bn revenue and said its co-packaged optics (CPO) parts are in stable mass production. Its new incentive plan targets net profit up 700% by 2029 versus 2025 ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/300394/AN202610231830833517.html)).

Capital is following. Unlisted Nazhen Technology says its 2027 indium phosphide laser-chip capacity, more than 100mn units, is already covered by orders ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513186?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Shijia Photonics (688313.SH) is seeking up to RMB 2.8bn for chip and interconnect capacity, and itself flags the risk of a shift to silicon photonics and CPO ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688313/AN202610231830848648.html)). Langte Intelligent (300916.SZ), a newcomer to optics, is paying ¥663mn for 51% of a passive-optics maker ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513851?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The 2028 guidance supports the view that hyperscaler capex runs well beyond 2026. The risk is the classic one: a wave of new capacity arriving in 2027 just as CPO starts displacing pluggable modules. Watch whether leaders' "orderly pricing" survives that supply.

## Memory squeeze reaches consumers

A Caixin investigation shows the AI memory crunch now hitting phone shelves ([Caixin Global](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-10-23/in-depth-chinas-smartphones-get-pricier-as-ai-strains-chip-supply-102496477.html)). Price increases before China's National Day included:

- Xiaomi's 18 Pro, up 1,000 yuan
- Huawei's Mate 90, up nearly 28%
- the 2TB iPhone 18 Pro Max, up 3,500 yuan

TrendForce data cited in the piece show server DRAM contract prices rose about 64% in H2 2025, with a roughly 270% cumulative increase projected for 2026. Qualcomm's China chairman said he had never seen memory prices rise 4–5x in a year and expects high prices to persist through 2027. Memory made up nearly 60% of the bill of materials for sub-$400 phones in Q1. Demand is cracking: China shipments fell 4.3% in Q2, the fifth straight quarterly decline.

The article frames this as good for memory makers and bad for low-end handset brands, with scale players best placed. Supplier filings back it up. Baiwei Storage (688525.SH), a Shenzhen memory-module maker, said DRAM and NAND prices rose "significantly" in 2026 and proposed another buyback ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688525/AN202610231830847055.html)). Giantec (688123.SH), which makes the SPD chips on DDR5 modules, grew Q3 revenue 26% as SOCAMM2/LPCAMM2 modules launched. Its chips for CXL memory modules, which let servers pool memory, are now in customer validation ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688123/AN202610231830847992.html)).

China's DRAM champion CXMT voiced "firm confidence" in long-term demand ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906520425.html)). Caixin profiled Micron (MU) CEO Sanjay Mehrotra's push into high-bandwidth memory, the stacked DRAM used beside AI accelerators ([Caixin](https://database.caixin.com/2026-10-23/102496333.html)).

## China's AI chips, models and five-year plan

Cambricon (688256.SH), China's best-known listed AI-accelerator designer, more than doubled Q3 revenue to 3.53bn yuan (+104%). Net profit was 1.40bn yuan (+148%) ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688256/AN202610231830847887.html)). Rival GPU maker MetaX (688802.SH) set incentive targets of 60bn yuan revenue in 2027 and 300bn yuan cumulative over 2027–29 ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688802/AN202610231830849193.html)). These are internal hurdles, not guidance, but they show how much domestic substitution management expects.

DeepSeek reportedly closed a round of about 100bn yuan (~$15bn), a Chinese AI record. CATL and Tencent led, with chip-linked funds also participating ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwfmnk5005978.d.html)). The headline of that report says 10bn, so treat the exact size as unconfirmed.

DeepSeek also open-sourced DeepInfer, the inference framework it uses to serve its own models. DeepInfer runs on both Nvidia GPUs and Huawei's Ascend 950 ([Caixin](https://www.caixin.com/2026-10-23/102496505.html)). That matters for Huawei's ecosystem: software that runs on either chip lowers the cost of switching away from Nvidia. Huawei separately raised a CNY 15bn offshore syndicated loan, its first in six years ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweywq5020293.d.html)).

Policy points the same way. The 2026–2030 Informatisation Plan calls for:

- more advanced-node manufacturing capacity
- high-performance AI chips
- 3D integration and photonics-electronics convergence
- humanoid robots and quantum computing

([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwffek8270214.d.html), [CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2513725?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Shanghai targets 85% AI penetration in industry by 2028, with subsidies of up to 30% on rented compute ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906136377.html)). These are demand-side tailwinds for domestic chips and cloud.

## Datacenter boards and power

High-end circuit boards remain a bottleneck. Shengyi Electronics (688183.SH) guided nine-month profit up 68–75%. It cited growing orders for AI-server and 800G/1.6T switch boards and a "breakthrough" in 1.6T optical-module boards ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688183/AN202610231830847403.html)). Victory Giant (300476.SZ), a key Nvidia board supplier, said some customers have released demand through 2027–28 ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweqhs8199552.d.html)).

Power is next. Megmeet (002851.SZ) showed a liquid-cooled 800V DC power platform with Nvidia at OCP, built into Nvidia's MGX server ecosystem. It also debuted a solid-state transformer module ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906214393.html)). Battery maker XiongTao (002733.SZ) wants to move RMB 336mn from a stalled lithium-battery plant into a RMB 1.5bn AI-datacenter power-supply project. Shareholders vote on 11 November ([filing](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/002733/AN202610231830848099.html)). Datacenter operator Runze (300442.SZ) is taking RMB 4bn from a China Eximbank unit for an AI infrastructure project ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwffen5024680.d.html)), a sign of state-linked money backing compute buildouts.

## Materials and equipment

China Northern Rare Earth (600111.SH), the world's largest light rare-earth producer, grew Q3 net profit 161% on higher prices and volumes ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniweywn8173442.d.html)). That is consistent with tight magnet supply. In the US, the Department of Energy designated helium, essential for chip fabs, as a critical mineral ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-23/detail-iniwfruh5124819.d.html)).

Japan's September chip-equipment orders rose 48.2% year on year ([Wallstreetcn](https://wallstreetcn.com/livenews/3184259)). That is a supportive data point for toolmakers such as Tokyo Electron (8035.T). Quartz Pure Materials (603688.SH), which makes high-purity quartz for fabs, credited semiconductor sales for a 46% Q3 profit gain ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610233906242523.html)).

## What to watch

- **Optics pricing into 2027:** watch Innolight's and Eoptolink's full Q3 reports for gross margins, and whether new laser-chip capacity from Sourcetech, Nazhen and Shijia tightens or loosens component supply.
- **DeepSeek round:** confirmation of the final size, and whether DeepInfer drives measurable Ascend adoption.
- **Memory contract prices:** whether Q4 DRAM quotes keep rising and how far handset demand weakens.
- **Shareholder votes:** XiongTao on 11 November and MetaX on 9 November.
- **Follow-on measures:** detailed rules under the five-year informatisation plan, especially any advanced-node manufacturing support.
