Shopify Flow: inventoryAdjustQuantities, Idempotency & Error Handling for Subscription Bundles
Hello Shopify Community! 
 I’m looking for technical guidance on a Shopify Flow workflow we’ve built for our small soap business. We’ve completed the workflow, but we’re holding off on activating it until we can confirm that inventory adjustments will execute reliably. 
  Our setup:  
 
 Shopify Basic plan 
 Appstle Subscriptions for recurring orders 
 Easify Product Options for customer soap selections 
 13 individual soap products with Shopify inventory tracking enabled 
 Three subscription bundles containing 4, 8, or 12 customer-selected bars 
 
  How our workflow operates:  
 
 Trigger:  Order created  
 Check whether the order has the  FPC-Inventory-Processed  tag. 
 Identify orders containing a Front Porch Club subscription product. 
 Loop through the order’s line items. 
 Identify the subscription line item. 
 Loop through its custom attributes ( Bar #1 ,  Bar #2 , etc.). 
 Match each selected soap name against 13 predefined conditions. 
 Use Shopify’s built-in  Send Admin API request  action with  inventoryAdjustQuantities  to deduct one unit from the corresponding product’s inventory. 
 
 Each soap is mapped to its Shopify Inventory Item ID and our fulfillment Location ID. 
 We’ve tested the workflow using Shopify Flow’s simulation. The conditions correctly identify the selected soaps and reach the appropriate API action. However, the API mutations cannot be simulated, so we haven’t verified the actual inventory adjustments. 
  We have three technical questions:  
  1. Idempotency  
 Our workflow uses API version  2026-07 . 
 The  inventoryAdjustQuantities  mutation requires an idempotency key using the  @idempotent  directive. 
 However, Flow’s built-in Send Admin API request action generates the GraphQL mutation automatically and only exposes an editor for the JSON mutation inputs. 
 Is there a supported way to provide the required idempotency key through this built-in action? 
 If not, does that mean  inventoryAdjustQuantities  cannot be reliably executed through Flow’s standard Admin API request action? 
  2. Accessing mutation errors  
 We understand that a GraphQL mutation can return  userErrors  even when the HTTP request itself succeeds. 
 We attempted to add a Condition immediately after the API request, but  userErrors  wasn’t available as a variable. 
 Can Shopify Flow access the  userErrors  returned by  inventoryAdjustQuantities ? 
 If so, what is the correct variable path or configuration? 
  3. Handling partial inventory adjustments  
 For a subscription containing multiple soaps, some adjustments could succeed before a subsequent request fails. 
 We want to avoid: 
 
 Deducting the same soap twice. 
 Marking an order processed when some adjustments failed. 
 Incorrect inventory counts when a workflow is retried. 
 Problems processing recurring Appstle subscription orders. 
 
 What is the recommended approach for safely handling these situations within Shopify Flow? 
  Our goal  
 Ideally, we’d like to keep this automation within Shopify Flow on our Basic plan rather than upgrade our plan or purchase another app. 
 We’re also open to a lightweight custom integration if the built-in Flow action cannot safely accomplish this. 
 Any guidance from developers familiar with Shopify Flow and the Admin GraphQL API would be greatly appreciated. 
  Thank you!

source_text:
MED-OPEN-001: open health-aid knowledge and medicine dossier provenance
## Objective

Create a reusable, privacy-preserving governance and evidence model for open home health aids and open medicine dossiers across Mycelix, Symthaea, Sol Atlas, and Symtropy.

This is intentionally not a `mycelix-health` implementation task. It belongs in the public Mycelix platform as a domain-neutral provenance/governance contract and should integrate with existing manufacturing work rather than create a duplicate manufacturing runtime.

Related existing owners:
- Symthaea [HEALTH-MFG-000 #5969](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/5969): evidence-bounded health-product manufacturing infrastructure.
- Symthaea [MED-PRODUCT-001 #4727](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/4727): separate wellness and regulated intended-use profiles.
- Mycelix [MFG-001 #4685](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/4685): immutable manufacturing execution and lot evidence.
- Sol Atlas [ATLAS-DSCI-001 #99](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/sol-atlas-leptos/issues/99): licensed scientific evidence snapshots for open pharmaceutical research.
- Symtropy [MARITIME-SIM-001 #1612](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1612) and [ENG-SYNTH #1172](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1172): reuse deterministic engineering simulation/replay substrate for resilience scenarios.

## Scope

Separate four lanes that must never be collapsed into an AI-generated "safe" score:

1. **Open home-care knowledge:** authoritative, versioned first-aid, prevention and care-navigation material with jurisdiction, source, review/expiry, escalation language and correction/withdrawal paths.
2. **Non-medicinal household aids:** open assistive/accessibility designs, care-kit organization and low-risk tools, with materials and intended-use reviews.
3. **Existing medicine access:** link to authoritative medicine identities and local essential-medicine/availability information; preserve licensing, freshness, provenance and quality distinctions.
4. **Open medicine dossier:** public, reproducible scientific and quality documentation for appropriately authorized manufacturers and independent evaluators—product identity, applicable licenses/patents, test-method references, stability/packaging evidence, manufacturing-site qualification references, labeling, pharmacovigilance and recall.

Open licensing does not imply clinical validation, GMP compliance, product authorization, safety for unsupervised use, or permission to manufacture a medicine at home.

## Contract requirements

- Versioned content-addressed snapshot metadata; distinguish URL, publication date, retrieval date, source record identity, dataset version, bytes captured, digest verification, license/terms and redistribution permission.
- License states must include at minimum `KnownOpen`, `AttributionRequired`, `Restricted`, `Unknown`, and `ReviewRequired`. Publicly visible URLs do not grant redistribution rights.
- Preserve separate signed evidence dimensions for clinical benefit/harms, active/product identity and quality, analytical methods, stability, manufacturing capability/GMP, jurisdictional authorization, supply/affordability, safety-event status and recall.
- Use explicit lifecycle states and no implicit promotion: `ResearchOnly`, `SourceLinked`, `ReviewRequired`, `GuidanceApproved`, `ManufacturerQualified`, `ProductAuthorized`, `BatchDispositionRecorded`, `Withdrawn`, `Expired`. Applicable transitions need scoped evidence and accountable owners; states are not a linear clinical score.
- Append-only corrections, retractions, supersession, signing authority, conflicts, provenance edges, and reproducible evaluator receipts.
- Never store patient-identifying clinical data in public medicine dossier records. Separate consented private operational data from public, minimized evidence.
- Keep Mycelix responsible for provenance/authorization/evidence graphs, not for deciding clinical truth; keep clinical and regulatory decision authority with qualified organizations.

## Safety boundaries

No public at-home synthesis/compounding recipes, doses, extraction procedures, sterile/injectable/ophthalmic/inhaled preparations, potent or controlled actives, antibiotics, hormones or other high-risk medicine manufacturing instructions for unqualified users. Do not infer that “natural,” traditional use, an open license, low cost, model confidence or a successful simulation proves efficacy or safety. Traditional knowledge requires consent, rights review and fair benefit sharing.

## First deliverable

A public architecture document and minimal synthetic fixtures defining:
- `EvidenceSnapshotRefV1`
- `RightsAndLicenseAssessmentV1`
- `HealthKnowledgeCardV1`
- `OpenMedicineDossierManifestV1`
- `ProductEvidenceDimensionV1`
- `SafetySignalAndRecallRefV1`
- explicit claim ceiling / non-claims.

Use authoritative links rather than mirroring copyright-restricted clinical guidance. Seed South Africa from current official NDoH STG/EML references and WHO's 2025 Model List as pointers, subject to terms review. WHO says essential medicines should be available, affordable and of assured quality; its 2025 Model List includes over 520 medicines. NDoH's primary-care STG/EML page currently links an eighth-edition file last updated August 2026. Sources:
- https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/essential-medicines
- https://www.health.gov.za/nhi-edp-stgs-eml/
- https://www.sahpra.org.za/document/sa-guide-to-good-manufacturing-practice-for-medicines/
- https://medicinespatentpool.org/progress-achievements/licences

## Acceptance criteria

- Clear boundary between home care, existing-product access and qualified medicine production.
- Exact source and rights metadata without unauthorized corpus copying.
- No single composite evidence score; unresolved, restricted, withdrawn and expired states remain visible.
- Synthetic negative controls for license uncertainty, mismatched product/jurisdiction, stale evidence, retractions, conflicting evidence, unauthorized manufacturer, failed quality evidence and recall.
- Independent checker and exact-head reproducibility evidence.
- Link and reuse existing Mycelix manufacturing/provenance and Sol Atlas evidence semantics instead of creating competing authorities.
- Keep this work in Mycelix/Symthaea/Sol Atlas/Symtropy, not the separate Mycelix-Health application repository.

Short games can be the best experiences. There are a lot of horror titles that barely crack 1 hour and still feel worth the purchase. There is also an argument that this is why PvP multiplayer is so compelling. The game is adaptive in its complexity, and every round of play is a relatively brief, self-contained experience not quite like the others. If you are going for bang-for-buck, it's really hard to beat the emergent properties of a MOBA, BR or RTS. I think those who reject multiplayer games on principle are missing the forest for the dead tree. There is an incredible amount of upside if you can tolerate the occasional bad mood. The dream is when the entire team comes together without any explicit communication and executes perfectly. Nothing beats that sensation. Especially when you can tell that the enemy team is also executing well. I have to seek it out in video games because I can't find it in a real business anymore. Games like League of Legends and CS2 are eternal experiences. I fired up LoL classic the other day and I could easily see myself putting another 5k hours into lux. WoW forever is also looking compelling with its PvP ruleset and unified realm architecture.

Show HN: Delegator – Stop juggling coding-agent sessions
I wanted to share Delegator with the HN community.  delegator gives you a personal inbox to manage your tasks that is completely local to your machine. Backstory: Like everyone else, I've been experimenting with different AI-assisted development workflows.  I realized I was having difficulty with all the context switching between tasks.  Asking agents to develop code ends up taking about 5-10 minutes usually for well-scoped tasks.  At the beginning I would read the AI output as it went along and sometimes interrupt to guide it.  But as LLMs have gotten better, there's less need to do that.  So I would spin up another task during the latency and then another.  (I wrote a little bit about this previously here  https://mattmccormick.ca/we-re-all-managers-now-my-journey-i...  ) Jumping back and forth between terminals with the Agent being at different stages was mentally taxing.  I experimented with some different options and ended up realizing that to avoid the drain of context-switching, what I really needed was a queue. Delegator works by putting all scoped tasks through the system.  It stops when the ready queue has reached your configured limit.  This is to prevent too much work from piling up waiting for review.  It also presents the work from getting too far ahead in case any issues are found as part of development. I also realized that for most tasks, agents can be treated as a background process.  You pass in the work to the process.  It processes it and then gives you an output to review.  All changes are made in git worktrees for safety. Who's it for?  Delegator is for engineers who still want to understand the code and changes.  It's not for vibe-coding or exploratory work.  Don't get me wrong, I'll still spin up an agent session for brainstorming design options.  But once I'm aligned on a direction, I'll then ask the agent to break down the work into "dg tickets".  Since Delegator is a local program, agents can interact with it quickly and seamlessly. Right now it's just CLI based but I'm looking to expand this into a GUI/Desktop App so I would be interested in any feedback you have.  Let me know if you have any questions and I'll respond.  The code is source available so you can check it out at  https://github.com/alcubie/delegator  if you want to check anything.

Clinical: launch decision-maker prospecting pilot with one-product comparison offer
## Outcome
Create a measurable new-clinic acquisition pilot for Lion Elite Clinical. User authorized recording and advancing this strategy on November 3, 2026. This ticket documents executable work; it does not assert that a campaign has launched.

Related: #175 relationship-first positioning, #10 validation framework, #38 coordination hub. Reuse existing BuildPipeline/CRM infrastructure.

## Offer
“Send us the specifications and quantities for one product you already purchase, and we’ll prepare a side-by-side quote with supporting quality documentation.”

Present savings and quality equivalence only when supported for the specific product and comparison. Confirm product availability, intended use, supplier eligibility, documentation, landed cost, and fulfillment terms before prospecting with that offer. Do not market research-use-only products for patient treatment. Keep relationship and long-term service value in the conversation.

## First deliverable: 30 new clinic prospects
- Select one clinic category matched to verified available products.
- Deduplicate against existing CRM and prior outreach; this is a new-prospect pilot.
- Record clinic, official website, service-fit evidence, public business contact path, named owner/purchasing contact where verified, title, source URL/date, verification status, assigned owner, and dated next action.
- A clinic owner is not automatically a confirmed purchasing authority. Mark authority unconfirmed until sourced or confirmed.
- Use business contact channels; do not guess email addresses.
- Keep prospect records, private quotes, supplier economics, and customer details in the private CRM, not this public issue.

## Contact scripts
Routing call:
“Hi, this is Alex with Lion Elite Clinical. Who evaluates suppliers and purchasing options for your clinic?”

First-contact draft:
“Hi [verified name], I noticed [verified relevant service] at [clinic]. Would a pricing and sourcing comparison for one product you already purchase be useful? We can prepare a quote against your specifications and quantities, with supporting documentation, so you can assess whether a switch makes sense.”

Interested reply:
“Which product specifications, order quantity, and delivery requirements should we quote? If you want a savings comparison, you can optionally share your current landed price with identifying details removed.”

After delivering comparison:
Offer a short review with Alex; use the verified scheduling link. Do not invent a calendar URL.

## Pilot execution
- [ ] Verify one fulfillable offer and assemble a comparison template: specifications, quantity, unit/total price, shipping, lead time, documentation, terms, and differences.
- [ ] Deliver 30 evidence-backed new clinic records to the existing private CRM.
- [ ] Confirm purchasing contact or provide a routing-call task for every record.
- [ ] Check sending-domain configuration, delivery/bounce evidence, suppression, and reply capture before launch.
- [ ] Prepare personalized first email and human call task for each eligible clinic.
- [ ] Proposed cadence: day 1 email/routing call; day 3 useful follow-up; day 7 final follow-up. Respect existing frequency rules and stop on reply, opt-out, bounce, or disqualification.
- [ ] Obtain campaign-specific send authorization before releasing external outreach; creating this ticket is not a live-send action.
- [ ] Assign every positive reply an owner and next action within one business day.
- [ ] Review results after the sequence has had time to complete; treat 30 accounts as directional evidence, not a statistically proven winner.

## Funnel and acceptance criteria
Report raw counts and defined rates by campaign/version:
- Attempted, provider-accepted, delivered where confirmed, bounced, unique recipients replying, unique positive replies.
- Reply rate = unique replying recipients / unique delivered recipients; if delivery is unavailable, label accepted-recipient denominator explicitly.
- Positive reply rate uses the same denominator.
- Qualified conversations, comparisons requested/sent, meetings booked/held, orders, and attributed revenue.
- Lead-to-order rate = new purchasing clinics / contacted clinics; report zero denominators as N/A.
- Distinguish automated replies, negative replies, and positive replies.

Done means: usable private CRM records + verified offer + tracked authorized activity + observable outcomes. A ticket, template, or deployed code alone does not constitute campaign success.

## Implementation handoff
Inspect current repository guidance and running systems before changing code. Reuse existing campaign, lead, task, suppression, and analytics components. Post the CRM destination, verified record count, missing fields, evidence of any technical changes/tests, launch status, blockers, and exact next action back to this issue and #38. Do not claim activation from ticket creation alone.


## Verified launch blockers — 2026-11-03
- Owner explicitly requested merge and launch. PR #181 merged after required test job succeeded; merge commit 0a19c92f856c13ad0f5cae78044620a149081944.
- Owner confirmed Render workspace My Workspace (info@lionelitewellness.com).
- Live BuildPipeline GET /api/prospects returned mode=pending, missing CRM_API_BASE, CRM_ADMIN_KEY, CRM_ORGANIZATION_ID. No prospects were imported or contacted.
- Render lists four web services and no Postgres instances in this workspace. This does not rule out an externally hosted database.
- Lion Elite OS /api/gtm-sales/readiness returned launchReady=false, database=false and emailFrom=false. This is a separate service from BuildPipeline; do not conflate their configuration.
- BuildPipeline runs from lionelite/lionelite-lion-elite-business-system/buildpipeline and its CRM adapter targets Lion Elite Intelligence. Repair that actual connection instead of treating the OS documentation merge as activation.
- Next dependency: identify existing private CRM database/organization and securely connect credentials; if none exists, select a persistent database before creating paid infrastructure. Keep secrets out of GitHub and chat.
- Campaign status: NOT LAUNCHED. Campaign launch authorization is now provided; missing configuration and verified campaign inputs remain operational dependencies.

Composer Predictions: pasting into an empty composer fails until a character is typed
### What version of the Codex App are you using?
Not yet confirmed from the About dialog. This report concerns the desktop app, not the CLI.

### What subscription do you have?
Not confirmed for this report.

### What platform is your computer?
macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon (arm64).

### What issue are you seeing?
Pasting a copied prompt into the composer fails when a suggested follow-up prompt (Composer Predictions) is visible. Typing one character first makes pasting work, but leaves an unwanted character before the prompt.

This repeatedly interrupts a workflow involving roughly six concurrent conversations and can alter instructions copied between them.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?
User-reported sequence:
1. Copy a prompt from another conversation.
2. Switch to a Codex conversation with a suggested follow-up prompt visible in the composer.
3. Click the composer and try to paste the clipboard text.
4. The text does not paste.
5. Click the composer, type one character, and then paste: the text is inserted, with that extra character at the beginning.

Whether Cmd+V, context-menu paste, or both are affected remains unconfirmed.

### What is the expected behavior?
Clicking the composer and pasting should insert the clipboard text unchanged, without first accepting/dismissing the suggestion or typing a character.

Suggested regression check: paste into an empty composer while a prediction is visible, including after switching conversations, and verify that the clipboard text is inserted exactly.

### Additional information
This behavior was reported directly by the affected user. The assistant preparing the report could not independently reproduce it because its automation tool blocks control of the Codex app itself. Suggestion/focus interference is a hypothesis, not an established root cause. No private conversations, account email, project files, or logs are included.

The official support chat received this report and directed us to in-app Feedback or an issue in openai/codex for a trackable report; it could not supply a case number through that channel.

Separate product-feedback suggestion from the reporting user: consider credits or recognition for users whose reproducible product bugs are confirmed, and consider this report for such recognition if eligible. This is a suggestion/request, not a claim of existing eligibility or an awarded bounty.

source_text:
Apply evidence, novelty, bounty and submission requirements across all problem work
Establish and apply one evidence and submission standard across **all problem work in grwtsk/math**, including Erdős problems, imported proofs, original results, partial results and computational claims.

User instruction: record the requirements from https://erdosproblemaday.com/guide as a general repository issue, resolve them across our problems, and submit eligible work once a bounty is earned. Submission endpoint: https://erdosproblemaday.com/submit. Read the current destination rules again before any submission.

## Required problem record

- [ ] Record the authoritative problem identity, exact quantifiers/hypotheses, variants, and whether the result is full, partial, conditional or computational.
- [ ] Check current literature and primary sources; retain stable references and dates. Distinguish original contributions from imported proofs, reformulations and formalization bridges.
- [ ] Supply a readable, checkable exposition, citations, artifacts and precise AI-role/version disclosure. Explicitly identify which verification was independent and its limits.
- [ ] For numerical or finite claims, provide reproducible certificates, coverage arguments and independent checks with acceptance/rejection controls where applicable. A finite table does not prove an unbounded statement.
- [ ] Preserve unresolved premises and missing bridges. Avoid claiming human mathematical review when none occurred.

## Repository-specific acceptance

- [ ] Bind every acceptance claim to immutable source commits/blobs, dependency/toolchain identities, exact commands and retained receipt digests.
- [ ] Keep source publication, compilation, fresh kernel checking, transitive axiom audits, expected-statement consumers and host restoration as separate facets; require all applicable facets together.
- [ ] Use explicit NOT_RUN, failed, pending and accepted statuses. Neither progress, a queue completion nor source review establishes acceptance.
- [ ] Follow the paper-to-formalization reference requirements and preserve upstream authorship/licenses. Local content attribution is `grwtsk contributors`. Local automation on behalf of this checkout owner uses `grwtsk <contributors@grwtsk.invalid>`; preserve other contributors’ own author/committer identities and do not enforce or rewrite identities repository-wide.
- [ ] Keep pure mathematics and static acceptance specifications in math; effectful tooling, attempts, receipts, scheduler state and submission machinery belong in grwtsk/noeaaeue.

## Bounty and submission gate

- [ ] Establish the actual prize/bounty terms, eligibility, exact result scope, prior-publication/priority rules and evidence that a bounty has been earned. Kernel verification alone is not bounty eligibility; porting an existing proof is not an original solution.
- [ ] Prepare a complete submission package with exact statement, known work, claimed contribution, readable proof, reproducibility instructions, source pins/verification evidence and AI disclosures.
- [ ] User has authorized submission once a bounty is earned. Preserve that condition; do not submit an unverified result or claim an earned bounty without evidence.
- [ ] The linked submission form requires a reply email and separately offers public-publication consent. Obtain missing contact information when needed; do not infer public consent or invent personal details.
- [ ] Record destination, submitted package identity, delivery/readback, review verdict and subsequent corrections without conflating submission, review, publication and bounty payment.

## Rollout and completion

- [ ] Inventory existing problem entries and classify gaps without upgrading historical evidence.
- [ ] Define a reusable subject-independent checklist/static schema and Noe-owned operational workflow.

title: object.urlEncode() throws on a lone surrogate in the isolated-VM engine but not in the default one
source_text:
object.urlEncode() throws on a lone surrogate in the isolated-VM engine but not in the default one
## Bug Description

`packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts` is a deliberate mirror of `packages/workflow/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts`, and its comment states the intent:

```ts
// DIVERGENCE from packages/workflow/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts:
// The original uses URLSearchParams which is a Web API unavailable inside the
// V8 isolate. encodeURIComponent is an ECMAScript built-in available in all
// V8 contexts, but it doesn't encode !'()~ which WHATWG requires. The extra
// replace step covers those characters to match URLSearchParams output.
```

They do not match for one input class. `URLSearchParams` replaces a lone surrogate with U+FFFD; `encodeURIComponent` throws a `URIError` on it. So the same expression succeeds on one engine and fails on another:

| | `{ v: "\uD800" }` |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/workflow` (URLSearchParams) | `v=%EF%BF%BD` |
| `@n8n/expression-runtime` (encodeURIComponent) | **throws `URIError`** |

## To Reproduce

A lone surrogate is easy to end up with — `JSON.parse` produces one from a `\uD800` escape, and so does slicing a string between the halves of a surrogate pair:

1. Create a workflow with a Code node returning `{ json: { payload: JSON.parse('{"a":"\\ud800"}') } }`.
2. In a following node use the expression `{{ $json.payload.urlEncode() }}`.
3. Run it with `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE` set to the isolate-backed engine, then with the default one.

The default engine returns `a=%EF%BF%BD`. The isolate-backed engine raises `URIError: URI malformed`.

## Scope

I swept every BMP code point through both implementations, as key and as value, plus astral samples:

```
checked 65540 code points as both key and value
distinct disagreement shapes: 2

  workflow: v=%EF%BF%BD
  runtime:  URIError
  e.g. U+D800 as value, U+D801 as value, U+D802 as value, U+D803 as value

  workflow: %EF%BF%BD=x
  runtime:  URIError
  e.g. U+D800 as key, U+D801 as key, U+D802 as key, U+D803 as key
```

4096 disagreements out of 131,076 checks, all of them the 2048 surrogate code points in either position. Everything else is byte-identical, so `whatwgEncode` is right apart from this edge.

## Suggested fix

Make the string well-formed first, which is exactly what `URLSearchParams` does:

```diff
 function whatwgEncode(str: string): string {
-	return encodeURIComponent(str)
+	// URLSearchParams replaces lone surrogates with U+FFFD, while
+	// encodeURIComponent throws a URIError on them.
+	return encodeURIComponent(str.toWellFormed())
 		.replace(/%20/g, '+')
 		.replace(/[!'()~]/g, (c) => '%' + c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).toUpperCase());
 }
```

With that applied the sweep reports **0 disagreements out of 131,076**. `String.prototype.toWellFormed` is ES2024 and available from Node 20; this repo requires Node >= 24.

## A second, related divergence

`packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/number-extensions.ts` carries a similar comment claiming parity:

```ts
// DIVERGENCE ... toLocaleString is an ECMAScript built-in available in all V8
// contexts and produces the same output.
```

`toLocaleString` and `Intl.NumberFormat.format` are indeed equivalent, but the mirror wraps the call in `try { ... } catch { return String(value) }`, and that is not. Where the original raises, the mirror returns the unformatted number:

| call | `packages/workflow` | `@n8n/expression-runtime` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(1234.5).format('en-US', { style: 'currency' })` | throws `TypeError` | `1234.5` |
| `(1234.5).format('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 101 })` | throws `RangeError` | `1234.5` |
| `(1234.5).format('')` | throws `RangeError` | `1234.5` |

A malformed call is silently wrong on one engine rather than reported. I have not touched this one because the catch may be there for a limited-ICU isolate, which I cannot test from outside — happy to follow whichever way you want it to go.

## Operating System

macOS (reproduced against `master` sources directly)

## n8n Version

`master` at the time of writing

## Node.js Version

24

## Database

SQLite (default)

## Execution mode

main (default)

---

CONTRIBUTING.md asks for an issue before a bug-fix PR, so this is that. I have the `urlEncode` change ready with a regression test and will open a PR linking this issue — glad to hold off if you would rather triage first.

# Weekly Digest — 2026-W42

*October 05 – October 12, 2026*

# Weekly Digest: October 05 – October 12, 2026

## Executive summary

This week was dominated by AI platform and agent engineering updates across GitHub and Azure, with major momentum around Copilot controls, local sandboxing, agent governance, evaluation, and new model availability in Microsoft Foundry. Developer tooling also saw meaningful operational changes, especially around Azure CLI/PowerShell authentication and API compatibility, plus new Azure Functions agent capabilities and continued investment in Aspire and VS Code. On the platform side, Azure highlighted Kubernetes, Arc, API Management, and integration scenarios, while Azure Updates carried an unusually heavy retirement signal that teams should review closely. Security and infrastructure coverage reinforced two strategic themes: prepare now for post-quantum and AI-era risk, and modernize observability, networking, and cluster operations before forced transitions arrive.

## GitHub

GitHub’s updates centered on Copilot governance, model rollout, developer experience improvements, and platform-scale security. The biggest themes were tighter enterprise controls, better accessibility and workflow ergonomics, and continued investment in secret detection and agent-scale development infrastructure.

- Copilot for JetBrains added new controls and chat improvements.
- GitHub Copilot weekly releases for October 5 bundled the latest product changes.
- CodeQL 2.27.2 improved analysis for C++, Go, Rust, and JavaScript.
- Copilot code review gained new organization billing options and controls.
- Claude Haiku 5.5 became available in GitHub Copilot.
- Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot reached general availability.
- GitHub introduced a purpose-built model for leaked secret detection.
- GitHub emphasized that secret protection must scale with software.
- Triage role users or higher can now archive pull requests.
- Draft pull requests now count toward pull request limits.

## Data & AI

Azure’s Data & AI news was heavily focused on building, evaluating, governing, and optimizing AI agents in Microsoft Foundry. Alongside new models and retrieval patterns, several posts tackled practical concerns such as evaluation quality, cost efficiency, governance, analytics integration, and database connectivity performance.

- Microsoft-Decision-1 was introduced in Microsoft Foundry for decision and classification workloads.
- Claude Haiku 5.5 is now available in Microsoft Foundry.
- Grok 4.7 was introduced on Microsoft Foundry.
- Microsoft published guidance on closing the AI agent governance gap with Microsoft Foundry.
- Foundry posts explored evaluating voice agents, including Voice User Simulator and multi-turn evaluator reliability.
- Foundry IQ guidance covered metadata-aware agentic RAG when answers are not directly in documents.
- Microsoft shared techniques for making evaluations more cost-efficient.
- A practical guide covered Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding.
- Guidance outlined building production agents in three stages rather than one.
- SqlClient’s new connection pool was introduced for faster parallel connections.

## Developer Tools

Developer tooling updates combined IDE releases, authentication and compatibility changes, new agent-development guidance, and Azure Functions enhancements. The most urgent items are around Azure CLI/Azure PowerShell readiness for Key Vault and Azure AD Graph retirement, while the most forward-looking items focus on agentic development and cloud-native app tooling.

- Visual Studio Code 1.141 and 1.142 Insiders were released.
- Azure Key Vault control plane API changes require upgrades for Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell users.
- Azure AD Graph API retirement requires action for older Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell versions.
- Azure CLI on macOS received a security upgrade with native broker authentication.
- Azure Functions introduced Agent bindings for Python function apps in preview.
- Azure Functions also added managed connectors to connect to more services.
- Hosted Skills in Azure Functions gained dynamic workflows for durable, AI-led event-driven apps.
- Microsoft introduced the Agent Experience practitioner playbook and an explainer on AX.
- Aspire updates added dashboard persistence and brought Native AOT to the dashboard.
- .NET shipped a faster, lighter C# Dev Kit and guidance for UI testing in UWP and WinUI 3 with MSTest.

## Azure Platform

Azure platform announcements focused on application modernization, managed services, governance for AI integrations, and Kubernetes and GitOps operations. The standout items were Anyscale on Azure reaching GA, Arc and AKS management improvements, and growing API Management relevance for MCP and agent governance scenarios.

- Anyscale on Azure is now generally available.
- GitOps with the Argo CD extension for AKS is now generally available.
- Kubernetes clusters can now be onboarded to Azure Arc with the Multicloud Connector in public preview.
- Microsoft Agent 365 and Azure API Management integration was highlighted for MCP governance.
- Logic Apps Automation announced free grant and pricing updates.
- Azure Managed Redis deployment automation was introduced.
- Azure Storage Actions can bulk change blob tiers.
- API Management service tag network rules were updated.
- Azure Integration Services showcased a governed, event-driven AI intake pipeline.
- Azure published a cost-focused look at running Qwen3.8-27B on a $2 H100 Azure Spot VM.

## Azure Infrastructure

Infrastructure coverage was smaller in volume but important for platform engineers operating secure and connected estates. Networking, Key Vault operational lessons, and AKS host-level capability expansion were the main themes.

- AKS multi-NIC support powered by DRANET entered public preview.
- Azure published lessons learned for Key Vault and BYOK deployments.
- Azure VPN Gateway guidance showed how to proactively monitor tunnel disconnections.
- Microsoft highlighted its presence and priorities at OCP Global Summit 2026.

## Containers & Kubernetes

This week’s Kubernetes items were both operationally significant, focusing on lower-level runtime and node behavior changes that can directly affect workload stability and performance. Platform teams should pay attention to cgroup v2 migration implications and the emerging use of node swap.

- Kubernetes published guidance on the shift to cgroup v2 and what teams need to know.
- Kubernetes also covered scaling workloads with node swap.

## Security

Security coverage emphasized readiness for next-generation threats, especially post-quantum transitions and AI-driven vulnerability management. The guidance was strategic but directly relevant to architects planning identity, detection, and risk programs.

- Microsoft urged organizations to start testing certificate ecosystems for post-quantum authentication.
- Microsoft Sentinel introduced the ASIM EmailEvent schema.
- Microsoft shared three lessons from frontier AI vulnerability research.
- CISO perspectives focused on managing vulnerability risks in the age of AI.

## Governance & Operations

Governance coverage was limited this week but useful for teams using deployment analysis to reduce operational friction. The focus was on improving the signal-to-noise ratio in change review workflows.

- Azure Governance detailed noise reduction improvements in Stacks What-If.

## Azure Updates

Azure Updates was heavily weighted toward lifecycle notices, with multiple retirements that could affect platform, data, Java, App Service, Arc, and AKS users. At the same time, several GA and preview launches expanded AKS networking, WAF controls, backup, HorizonDB, and Marketplace and SQL capabilities.

- Retirement: Azure Deployment Environments will be retired on February 22, 2027.
- Retirement: Microsoft Dev Box will be retired on September 18, 2028.
- Retirement: Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters.
- Retirement: Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub.
- Retirement: support for Java 8, 11, and 17 will end on September 1, 2027.
- Generally available: Managed StandardV2 NAT Gateway for AKS.
- Generally available: WAF exceptions for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door.
- Public preview: Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management.
- Public preview: Azure Backup for PostgreSQL flexible server and elastic cluster (v2).
- Public preview: IPv6 support for Application Gateway WAF.

## Ecosystem

The broader ecosystem mix this week included infrastructure-as-code, community DevOps experimentation, and Oracle partnership visibility. While lighter than Azure and GitHub news, these items may still be useful to practitioners watching adjacent toolchains and partner ecosystems.

- Terraform released v1.17.0-rc1.
- A DevOps community post explored using Whisper, FFMPEG, and yt-dlp to analyze sermons for red flags.
- Microsoft promoted its presence at Oracle AI World 2026.

PARTS-EVIDENCE-001 — Exact-model compatibility graph and source resilience
## Why this matters

The existing washer sourcing snapshot can detect that a generic parts-catalogue probe is not proof of fit, but does not yet provide a reusable, multi-family evidence graph for part ↔ exact model/revision ↔ market/serial window relationships. Wrong-fit claims cause wasted shipping, failed repairs and potentially safety-critical substitutions. Similar model names, photographs, seller listings, or shared service contracts do not establish compatibility.

## Paradigm shift

Treat compatibility as a versioned, evidence-backed claim with a scoped predicate—not a property inferred from brand/model similarity. Keep fit, interface/electrical ratings, functional behavior, safety qualification, and configuration/firmware constraints as separate dimensions. Support positive and negative observations; absence of evidence stays unknown rather than incompatible. Permit exact-model manufacturer evidence to establish a catalog/listing relation only, not automatically physical fit, function, or safety qualification.

## Proposed benchmark questions

- How often does a part recommendation produce a false-compatible result on a frozen positive/negative/ambiguous test set?
- What fraction of declared common-repair classes have exact-model/revision evidence, and how stale is the evidence?
- What is the wrong-order/return/rework rate and time to locate a correct part?
- How many genuinely independent sources can supply each critical repair class, after distributor ownership/dependency is considered?
- Are service lead-time and affordability claims based on accepted orders and physical delivery rather than listings and advertising?

## Acceptance

- Strict schema, synthetic-only fixture and Rust auditor integrated into the existing appliance audit CLI/workflow.
- Distinguish manufacturer-listed, seller-claimed, cross-reference-inferred, physical-fit-verified, functional-verified, safety-qualified, verified-incompatible and unknown.
- Model suffix/revision/market/serial applicability and supersession windows are explicit.
- No source counts as independent without a declared supplier/distributor dependency identity.
- Mutation tests prevent seller claims from being promoted to functional compatibility, missing evidence becoming incompatibility, expired evidence being presented as current, and one upstream supplier being double-counted.
- No purchase, fit, repair, or safety claim from synthetic fixtures or schema qualification alone.

Reference context: Open Repair Alliance's Oct 2026 dataset reports 619,875 community repair attempts across 34 countries through July 2026. It is useful for repair-event vocabulary and workflow questions, but does not by itself establish South African large-appliance fault prevalence or model-specific part fit. See https://openrepair.org/announcements/over-half-a-million-records-of-open-data-on-repair/ and https://openrepair.org/open-data/downloads/ .

source_text:
Feature request: Product-specific customer tax exemptions for accurate wholesale and retail checkout
Shopify currently applies customer-level tax exemptions across all otherwise taxable purchases, without allowing merchants to restrict those exemptions to specific products or collections. 
 This creates a significant tax compliance problem for small businesses operating both wholesale and retail sales through one Shopify store. 
  The problem  
 I operate a micro-scale flower farm and retail business in British Columbia, Canada. We sell flowers wholesale to professional florists alongside retail designed floral arrangements, books, pottery and, since we are relying on what we produce at the farm, we also sell fruit and other boutique products with various taxation levels. 
 Some of our wholesale customers qualify for a BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) exemption when purchasing products for resale. However, those same customers occasionally purchase retail products for personal use, which are not eligible for that exemption. 
 Currently, when a customer’s PST exemption is enabled in Shopify, it applies to all their otherwise PST-taxable purchases, regardless of whether the items are being purchased for resale or personal use. 
 For example, a wholesale florist recently purchased a book from our retail boutique. Shopify correctly charged GST but removed PST because of the customer’s account-wide exemption even though the book was for personal use and needed to be taxed. 
  The result is that Shopify’s existing tax settings cannot correctly accommodate a customer who makes both exempt and taxable purchases using the same account.  
   The proposed solution 
 Please introduce  conditional, line-item customer tax exemptions , allowing merchants to specify which products or collections qualify for a particular customer’s tax exemption. 
 When configuring a customer tax exemption, merchants should be able to choose whether it applies to: 
 
 
 All otherwise eligible purchases, preserving the existing functionality. 
 
 
 Specific products selected individually. 
 
 
 Products selected through designated collections, as a convenient way to configure the underlying product-level rules. 
 
 
 The actual tax calculation should occur at the individual line-item level, rather than relying solely on collection membership. 
 For example, a BC PST resale exemption could apply to qualifying products purchased for resale from an approved wholesale collection, while purchases from our retail products would continue to be taxed normally. 
  The exemption should apply only when both conditions are satisfied:  
 
 
 The customer qualifies for the relevant tax exemption. 
 
 
 The purchased product and its intended use qualify for that exemption under the applicable tax rules. 
 
 
 Simply having access to a wholesale collection should not automatically make a customer or transaction tax-exempt. 
 Ideally, Shopify would also allow merchants to use customer and product tags or metafields to configure these rules, making them easier to manage as businesses grow. 
   Essential functionality 
 The proposed system should: 
 
 
 Correctly calculate taxes for mixed carts containing both exempt and taxable products. 
 
 
 Support different tax treatments for the same customer account without requiring separate wholesale and retail accounts. 
 
 
 Preserve existing product tax settings, collection tax overrides and other applicable tax exemptions. 
 
 
 Allow customers to complete their own purchases through the normal online checkout. 
 
 
 Calculate the correct tax amounts before payment, without requiring draft orders, manual adjustments or additional invoices. 
 
 
 Record actual GST and PST amounts accurately in Shopify’s order records and tax reports. 
 
 
 Be available on Shopify’s standard subscription plans, including Basic, rather than requiring Shopify Plus. 
 
 
 The goal is not to create an alternative tax calculation system. It is to make Shopify’s existing customer exemption functionality more precise and compatible with businesses serving different types of customers and transactions. 
   Why this matters to small businesses 
 I contacted Shopify Support and was informed that there is currently no native solution, and that a developer cannot implement this conditional tax calculation on Shopify Basic. 
 The suggested workarounds involve creating draft orders, manually changing customer exemptions or asking wholesale customers to use separate accounts for retail purchases. 
 None of these is a satisfactory long-term solution. 
 These workarounds introduce unnecessary administrative work, create friction for customers, interfere with self-service online ordering, decrease the number of sales, and increase the risk of tax errors. 
 For a micro-business like ours, Shopify Plus is financially impossible. Our monthly sales cannot absorb the cost of that subscription. 
 Small businesses should not need an enterprise-level subscription simply to apply the correct taxation level required by law to run their online store. 
   Why this should be prioritized 
  This is fundamentally a tax accuracy and compliance issue, not simply a wholesale feature request.  
 It affects financial reporting, customer experience, administrative efficiency and the profitability of small businesses. 
 The issue is particularly relevant to businesses serving both wholesale and retail customers, including farms, growers, makers, food producers and other small suppliers. 
 It may also affect merchants in other jurisdictions where tax exemptions depend on both customer eligibility and the nature or intended use of the purchased products. 
 As Shopify continues to support businesses of all sizes, providing accurate conditional tax exemptions on standard plans would be a meaningful improvement. 
  Please consider prioritizing product-level customer tax exemption rules across Shopify plans, including Basic, so merchants can calculate, collect and report the correct taxes automatically without relying on manual workarounds.  
 If a similar improvement is already being considered, I would appreciate having this use case added to the existing feature request. 
 Thank you for considering this request.

Play a prepared Study escape attempt with all three investigators
## Problem Statement

Joel can play the accepted Jacqueline/Patrice skill-test experiment and Tony's prepared turn, but cannot yet coordinate turns across the three investigators and see their combined decisions change the scenario. The next bottleneck is connected party play through the actual rules, tabletop, save/resume and replay paths, while the program handles administration and Joel retains the decisions.

## Solution

Offer a **prepared Study escape attempt** in original The Gathering on Standard. Joel chooses investigator order, investigates, supports tests with other investigators, uses Jacqueline's reaction and weighs Patrice's Lucky! options. At the first fully settled action that gives the party six clues, he chooses whether to spend them and advance Act 1, including its actual map transition. If all investigator turns end first, the attempt finishes without escaping.

The endpoint is visible before play. This is a bounded task from a prepared position, not original scenario setup, a complete investigation phase on every branch, or a complete scenario. It does not force success. Ending the experiment preserves unfinished turns and does not invent defeat, victory or campaign consequences.

Joel accepted the direction, concrete position, endpoint, testing seam and prospective allowance on 2026-10-31, then explicitly invoked `to-spec` to publish this issue. The allowance is **32 aggregate active engineering hours**, including delegated work, source preflight, implementation, asset preparation, verification and review, plus **two owner sessions of at most 20 minutes each**, including retries. No paid services. The ceiling is not a calibrated delivery estimate.

## User Stories

1. As Joel, I want the prepared position and endpoint explained before play, so that I understand the task's limits.
2. As Joel, I want to choose which eligible investigator acts next, so that I can coordinate the party's approach.
3. As Joel, I want each investigator's turn and action allowance tracked separately, so that I do not administer turn order manually.
4. As Joel, I want camera focus to remain independent of the acting investigator, so that looking around cannot change who acts.
5. As Joel, I want each investigator's hand, resources, clues and condition visible, so that I can assess my options.
6. As Joel, I want to Investigate, Draw or gain a Resource with legal costs and consequences, so that I can make genuine tradeoffs.
7. As Joel, I want to end a turn early, so that the program does not force me to spend every action.
8. As Joel, I want unavailable actions refused for their actual rules reason, so that unsupported behavior is not disguised as a legal option.
9. As Joel, I want to choose my own matching commitments, so that I control the resources spent on a test.
10. As Joel, I want other investigators at the location to support a test within their legal limits, so that cooperation matters.
11. As Joel, I want Promise of Power's icons and curse cost administered together, so that its benefit and consequence remain connected.
12. As Joel, I want to choose when Jacqueline intervenes, including an eligible later curse reveal, so that her limited reaction remains my decision.
13. As Joel, I want all legal cancellation choices, including poor choices, so that the program does not choose strategy for me.
14. As Joel, I want random draws to respect physical token multiplicities and held tokens, so that the bag behaves correctly.
15. As Joel, I want each testing investigator's own elder-sign effect, so that Jacqueline helping someone does not replace their identity.
16. As Joel, I want the actual cost and fast timing of Lucky!, so that spending actions to draw it and gain resources is a meaningful alternative.
17. As Joel, I want any reachable Patrice elder-sign choice, including choosing the retained discard, so that optional effects are not silently skipped.
18. As Joel, I want arithmetic, modifiers, costs and outcomes explained in history, so that I can understand the rules without administering them.
19. As Joel, I want to choose whether to spend the six clues, so that the program does not force act advancement.
20. As Joel, I want advancement to move the party and change the map according to the real act, so that cooperation has a visible scenario consequence.
21. As Joel, I want a declined or unsuccessful escape attempt recorded honestly, so that unfavorable outcomes remain valid play.
22. As Joel, I want the experiment to preserve remaining actions and unfinished turns at its endpoint, so that stopping does not invent game effects.
23. As Joel, I want autosave at committed decisions and manual save at pending choices, so that I can interrupt meaningful play.
24. As Joel, I want a fresh launch to restore the exact choice, state and randomness, so that resuming does not reroll or repeat effects.
25. As Joel, I want a failed save to leave live play unchanged, so that retrying cannot duplicate costs or consequences.
26. As Joel, I want undo only before new hidden information, so that I can correct decisions without rewriting revealed outcomes.
27. As Joel, I want stored replay moments with Next, Previous and camera control, so that I can narrate the attempt without new randomness.
28. As Joel, I want replay navigation to preserve the live session and original recording, so that inspecting the past cannot change the match.
29. As Joel, I want readable substitutes when art is absent, so that missing artwork does not prevent play.
30. As Joel, I want earlier Tony/Jacqueline saves and recordings preserved and accessible, so that this experiment does not invalidate accepted work.
31. As Joel, I want prior attempts preserved when starting another, so that trying another approach does not destroy evidence or recordings.
32. As Joel, I want corrupt or incompatible records refused without modification, so that recovery remains possible.

## Implementation Decisions

### Prepared position

| Element | Selected value |
| --- | --- |
| Context | Original Gathering, Standard, three investigators; Act 1 Trapped and agenda 1, with no pending trigger or doom threshold. |
| Start | Start of the investigation phase, before choosing its first investigator; no pending action or test. |
| Map and clues | All three investigators in revealed Study, shroud two; six clues on Study, zero held by the party. Only Study is in play. |
| Investigators | Printed attributes, health and sanity; zero damage. Tony and Patrice zero horror; Jacqueline two starting horror from two Arcane Research permanents. |
| Resources/discards | Zero resources and empty discard piles for all three. |
| Threats/assets | No enemies or threat-area cards; Internal Injury is not in play. Tony has Bounty Contracts with six bounties and no target. No other relevant assets beyond Jacqueline's two permanents. |
| Turns/limits | Each investigator may take one turn with three ordinary actions. Tony's restricted extra action is available but has no eligible Fight/Engage target. Jacqueline's reaction is unused this round. |
| Chaos bag | Original Standard composition: +1; two 0; three −1; two −2; −3; −4; two skull; cultist; tablet; auto-fail; elder sign. No initial bless/curse tokens. |

| Investigator | Initial hand | Fixed hidden draw prefix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tony | On the Hunt `03263` ×1 | Guts `01089` ×2, then On the Hunt `03263` ×1 |
| Patrice | Promise of Power `07032` ×1 | Lucky! `01080` ×2, then Unexpected Courage `01093` ×1 |
| Jacqueline | Clairvoyance `60408` ×1 | Clairvoyance `60408` ×1, then Eyes of the Dreamer `11067` ×2 |

Preserve the pinned starting-list quantities in the remaining hidden inventory. Do not replace unknown cards with playable inert cards. Unresolved basic-weakness slots remain outside reachable behavior and do not constitute completed campaign preparation. This arranged position does not prove that preceding legal campaign play reaches it. Fixed hidden deck order is fixture input, not player knowledge. Ordinary chaos draws are random and unbiased across physical tokens; privileged deterministic draws belong only to verification fixtures.

### Choices and stopping boundary

Offer Investigate, Draw, Resource, eligible commitments, optional abilities and voluntary End turn under the actual rules. One investigator finishes their turn before the next is selected. Preserve same-location eligibility and the ordinary one-card limit for each supporting investigator; the testing investigator may commit appropriate cards under the normal rules. Refuse invalid targets, unaffordable costs, inappropriate commitments and stale revisions without mutation.

Jacqueline may react to any investigator's eligible test at her location. Declining an initial reveal does not consume her reaction or suppress a later eligible curse-reveal opportunity. Preserve the round limit, all legal cancellation choices, additional draws, held-token custody and token cleanup. Resolve the testing investigator's own elder-sign effect. Support Lucky!'s original fast timing, cost and +2 effect without automatically selecting it.

Ordinary play stops at the **first fully settled action/test leaving six clues held by the group**. Complete commitments, token cleanup, mandatory consequences and legal after-test choices before presenting the closing decision:

- **Advance Act 1:** perform the group clue-spending decision, spend six, execute the full reverse, and expose Act 2. Put Hallway, Cellar, Attic and Parlor into play; discard every enemy in Study (none in this position); place all investigators in Hallway, revealing it; remove Study. Stop before further actions.
- **Finish the attempt without advancing:** preserve the resulting position and record the declined advancement. Do not invent a defeat or scenario resolution.

If all investigator turns finish before six clues are gathered, stop at the investigation-phase boundary before the enemy phase. Saving/closing may interrupt any pending decision without advancing it.

Ending this task does not end an unfinished investigator turn: preserve remaining actions, limits and game state. Keep the post-action player window even when the sixth clue comes from the third action. The endpoint is an explicit experiment boundary, not a rule forbidding further action after six clues. There is no continuation beyond this endpoint or migration promise into a future campaign implementation.

### Reachable-content closure

The following independent arguments define this prepared task. They must be challenged during verification; they are not permission to filter out legal choices:

1. Only ordinary successful Investigate tests gain clues, one at a time. Before the sixth discovery, every pre-reveal test window has fewer than six held clues. That test then settles and ordinary play stops before another begins. Thus no supported test loses its target to mid-test act advancement. General advancement during tests remains legal outside this selected task.
2. No enemies means no Fight/Evade/Engage target, opportunity attack, friendly fire or Gathering tablet damage. Study has no available movement destination before advancement. No Injury means no Injury action or turn-end damage.
3. Tony can draw at most three cards. Guts has no matching intellect icons and no willpower test occurs. On the Hunt can be committed to Investigate; its encounter-draw event timing does not occur.
4. Jacqueline draws at most three cards: either three ordinary Draw actions, or at most two plus one canceled-elder-sign draw during her own test. Helping another investigator uses that investigator's elder-sign effect. Her selected non-Fast assets cost at least three; gaining those resources from zero and playing an asset needs at least four actions. Their intellect icons remain usable.
5. Patrice cannot draw Lucky!, gain its one-resource cost and use it during a test before her third action. Unexpected Courage is reached only by a third Draw action. Before a non-final own test, at most her initial Promise can be in her discard, so her elder sign cannot shuffle a nonempty subset while leaving one card. On a final test, an eligible actual shuffle remains available, including selecting the retained card and persisting randomness. No later own Draw remains, and the selected partners' cards cannot draw for her. Later supporting commitments may change her discard without causing another test for her.
6. Only one Promise is reachable. Its commitment introduces one curse. Support real additional reveals, cancellation and token destinations. Ten-curse overflow and additional replacement assets are unreachable.
7. The Standard bag contains one physical cultist, held until test completion even if Jacqueline leaves two resolving tokens. At most one cultist horror per test and three own tests gives Tony at most three horror, Patrice three, and Jacqueline five including her starting horror. No damage is reachable. Defeat is therefore unreachable; no immunity is introduced.

New draw/resource gifts, extra actions/tests, enemies, pre-test clue gains or later phases invalidate these bounds and require scope review.

### Rules, continuity and presentation

- Use one local party session and its own supported record scope. Reuse existing production helpers and shared interactions when their contracts agree. The existing experiment states and token resolvers are deliberately narrow; changing an actor identifier does not establish correct party behavior. No general engine or interpreter is selected.
- Preserve the production **player observation → revision-bound choice → save candidate → install** authority boundary for both native UI and player driver. Observations and histories do not reveal future deck order or random state. The first risk-bearing check must exercise a real multi-investigator commitment/reaction and its continuation through this same boundary, against the independent expectations below.
- Autosave committed decisions and permit manual save at pending choices. Save the candidate before installing or displaying consequences. Persistence failure leaves live state, pending choices and future randomness unchanged; retries must not duplicate costs, tokens, clues, shuffles or map effects.
- Fresh-process reopen restores the exact state, held tokens, commitment/cancellation/fast-effect/after-test/closing choice, limits and randomness. Interrupted presentation has no rules authority. Records identify their required input, rules and application versions.
- Keep undo barriers at committed hidden revelations, including card draws and token reveals, not animation completion. An unobserved Patrice shuffle alone reveals no hidden information; undo can restore its prior state and randomness if it crosses no intervening revelation, but cannot cross the preceding test's token reveal. Retain intelligible undo history and preserve exported recordings.
- Replay consumes stored events/observations without new randomness or applying current rules. Next/Previous navigate meaningful moments with automatic camera direction and manual override. Returning to live play preserves the live session. Replay cannot overwrite a live save or rewrite the match.
- Preserve earlier experiment saves and recordings through retained compatible modes or an explicit tested compatible path. Refuse corrupt/incompatible records visibly with original bytes intact. Starting another attempt preserves previous records. No automatic migration is promised.
- Preserve the scenario area, investigator areas, test area, actor-versus-camera distinction, shared contextual controls, inspection, commitment markers, reveal shortcut, reduced-motion behavior and manual camera control. Explain costs, arithmetic, timing and consequences in readable game language. Show the actual map transition and honest completion state; do not expose fixture machinery as player controls.
- Prepare and verify selected new artwork before relying on it. Preserve the source archive and prior prepared collections. Runtime uses only the selected prepared asset collection, remains usable with readable substitutes, and works offline. Personal configuration, saves and recordings remain separate from portable artwork. No third-party payloads enter Git.
- All project-owned executable logic, tools and tests follow the accepted Rust implementation-language contract. Internal naming, decomposition, algorithms and reversible adapters remain delegated engineering judgment.

## Testing Decisions

Use the **existing highest behavioral seam: player observations and submitted revision-bound choices through the same rules authority as the native UI**. Joel accepted this seam with the coherent scope; no further interview is needed. Test available choices and observable consequences, not private types or implementation output used as its own oracle.

Prior art is the existing Jacqueline decision tests, Tony decision/continuity tests, actual driver-process reopening tests, and production tabletop registration checks. Cover the new party rules, persistence/replay integration and affected native controls through these established boundaries. Source-derived expectations remain independent of both old resolvers and any secondary implementation.

| Case | Independent expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Turn order and early End | Each investigator takes at most one turn; unused actions do not transfer. Camera focus never selects the actor. End cannot skip a pending test or consequence. |
| Shared commitment | A same-location supporting investigator contributes at most one appropriate card; Patrice's Promise adds four wild icons and one curse, then is discarded at test completion. Preserve legal decline and reject excess/invalid commitments. |
| Tony arithmetic | Intellect 3 with −2 fails Study shroud 2; one On the Hunt intellect icon changes the result to success. |
| Lucky tradeoff | Patrice Draw + Resource + Investigate can pay one for Lucky on eligible failure. Intellect 2 with −1 gives 1; Lucky gives 3 against difficulty 2. Lucky has no commitment icons. Decline remains legal. |
| Cultist and Lucky | Original Standard cultist is −1. Patrice's 2 − 1 fails at 1; Lucky brings it to 3, succeeding and preventing the failure-only horror. |
| Combined cancellation/curse | Jacqueline with Clairvoyance's intellect icon and Patrice's Promise has intellect 8. Reveal auto-fail, curse, 0; cancel auto-fail, then reveal −2: resolve total −4 and succeed at 4 against 2. Cancel curse and 0 instead: auto-fail remains, no clue is discovered. |
| Standard symbols and order | Skull is −X for Ghouls at the location, hence 0 here; cultist is −1 and causes 1 horror only on failure; tablet is −2 with damage only if a Ghoul is present, hence none here. Exercise every face, additional curse draws, legal multi-token resolution order and cleanup. |
| Investigator elder signs | Apply Tony's original Contracts effect, Patrice's original after-test shuffle option, or Jacqueline's own canceled-elder draw according to who tests. Jacqueline reacting on Tony/Patrice does not grant her own elder effect. |
| Patrice final shuffle | After a final test with an eligible discard, choose the card retained and actually shuffle the rest into her deck. Persist exact continuation; no fourth ordinary action or later draw is offered. |
| Prefix/asset closure | Support all three possible prefix draws and matching commitments. Refuse asset play due to actual action/resource insufficiency. No hidden tail card is revealed on any supported path. |
| Sixth clue on third action | Fully settle the test and after-test choices, then retain the final player window and closing spend/decline choice without artificial turn ending. |
| Advance/decline | Spend exactly six and complete the map transition, or retain Study and held clues. Neither branch silently continues to another turn/phase or invents campaign results. |
| No escape | If all turns end below six clues, finish without victory, defeat, enemy phase or scenario resolution. Preserve poor choices and unfavorable draws. |
| Undo | Permit only reversals that do not cross committed hidden information; preserve limits, previous state/randomness and recorded history, including after reopen. |
| Failed-save retry | Inject failure before installation, retry, and match an uninterrupted control: no duplicate effect, changed next draw or partially installed transition. |
| Fresh-process resume | Interrupt and reopen at commitment, cancellation, Lucky, final-shuffle and final-spend choices. Match pending choices, committed outcomes and unrevealed continuation against uninterrupted play. |
| Recorded replay | Navigate actual stored moments forward/back, then return to unchanged live state. No new randomness, recalculated outcome or save from the past. |
| Legacy/refusal | Earlier experiment records reopen through their supported paths; corrupt/unsupported records are preserved with a clear refusal. New attempts preserve prior records. |

Run the repository's required Rust/hygiene checks and proportionate affected native-path checks using isolated saves/settings and the existing verified tools. Exercise real artwork and readable substitutes. Existing test counts, screenshots or synthetic input do not establish rules fidelity or owner experience beyond the behavior actually exercised.

Owner acceptance uses **at most two sessions of 20 minutes each, including retries**:

- Session 1 exercises cooperation, interruption/resume and an escape attempt.
- Session 2 changes investigator order/ability allocation, includes decline or unsuccessful completion as needed, and narrates stored replay.

Prepare technical evidence before consuming owner attention. Outcome luck does not mandate another run. Joel judges clarity, pacing, control burden and whether this task is worth playing; automation cannot supply that verdict. These checks do not establish recurrent-use fitness or the complete lifecycle of any investigator.

## Out of Scope

Full scenario setup or complete The Gathering; enemy/upkeep/mythos phases; play after the declared endpoint; movement/actions in newly revealed locations after advancement; combat or defeat machinery unsupported by this position; full-deck shuffling/drawing beyond the bounded Patrice continuation; actual random-basic-weakness preparation; upgrades and successor decks; arbitrary content support; runtime LLM adjudication; general engine/DSL/framework; automatic record migration; unrelated refactors or new diagnostic tools; video encoding/upload/publication; paid services; redistribution of source assets.

The original Night of the Zealot campaign remains the complete-delivery goal and remains unmet. Acceptance of this attempt cannot be used as proof of a complete scenario, campaign, reusable engine or normal randomly prepared deck play.

## Further Notes

### Authority, classification, appetite and stopping

- Owner and acceptance authority: Joel (`joeloverbeck`). Baseline: `7083162607cc910632d1aaedbc2a82581fe54282`.
- The incumbent is the accepted isolated test and Tony-turn paths; they remain available. This work uses the smallest local party implementation needed for the selected real-card task, rather than building general infrastructure first.
- This is a **decision-only gameplay experiment** for judging connected party cooperation and first-act progression through the real player, persistence and presentation paths. Its defining result is Joel completing or intentionally terminating this exact task and judging its clarity/burden. It does not confer product-like authority on a broader engine or establish campaign readiness. Later promotion/reuse beyond this scope requires the applicable evidence and acceptance.
- This one issue owns the selected increment. It displaces full-scenario implementation until this bounded party path is inspected. No separate maintenance, architecture or tooling lane is activated. The existing closed #1, #2 and #22 are accepted evidence, not open blockers.

No paid services. These are prospective ceilings, unconsumed by implementation at publication, not delivery promises. Earlier allowances do not reset or transfer here.
- First exercise the multi-investigator commitment/reaction and save/reopen path against the worked cases before expanding presentation. Keep the default early stops: two active hours without an inspectable acceptance-bearing increment; three failed repair cycles at the same boundary; three review passes expanding an open semantic family; approximately doubled expected surface; an unapproved capability/pipeline; or any effort/human-burden limit. Investigate findings and distinguish implementation defects from invalid expectations before repair.
- Stop on unverifiable governing inputs, a material unresolved source interpretation, or failed reachable-content closure before implementing around it. Report the exact evidence and recommend the smallest correction or reduced promise. No silent unsupported behavior, automatic extension or fresh adjacent lane follows. At the limit, preserve the candidate and return for adopt/reject/narrow/park/reframe or explicitly authorized continuation. Unadopted or failed experimental behavior must not gain authoritative dependents/default-path publication through inertia.
- `ready-for-agent` records bounded readiness. This publication does **not** activate implementation, unattended continuation, native sessions, commit/push, PR, merge or owner acceptance. Future implementation activation and exact production publication retain their separate authority. Recheck baseline, issue state and source identities before execution. Record effort, review cycles and remaining owner allowance here during authorized execution; unattended work additionally requires the repository's durable-state requirements.
- The source set, precedence, finite obligation bounds, independent expectations and input identities below support constructing this bounded candidate. They do not assert that it has run. A local prototype or secondary implementation must not substitute for the intended Rust/native consumer's checks.

### Source set, precedence and custody

Use the accepted Chapter One/original English baseline: applicable errata and the pinned taboo overlay; specific card/scenario exceptions over general rules; absolute prohibitions and applicable encounter-over-player precedence; Rules Reference over Learn to Play; expansion rules for bless/curse. source_text:
Show HN: ArchDocs – Shared context and verification for engineers and AI agents
Hi HN, My name is Aylon and I'm building ArchDocs. I started building ArchDocs in late 2024 as an architecture diagramming tool with reusable references and objects (still exists today and is usable). As I've been using AI to code more and more, one of the things I've run into is that my agent doesn't have enough context around past decisions or findings that could affect an implementation, causing some nasty side-effects like redundant investigations, incorrect assumptions, repeating previously caught mistakes and ultimately wasting precious tokens. Let's say for example, you need to do a migration that affects 10 backend services. Your agent starts working on the first one and during the implementation and verification process, it discovers an issue that will undeniably affect the other 9 services. The next agent can start on the second service without knowing what was learned on the first. There's another problem I run up against time and time again. I need a dependable way to verify and log what an agent has done, the outcome of that and any deviations or issues that arise from it, so I can tell whether the change actually did what I intended. Enter Design Docs inside ArchDocs. The workflow is simple. You or your agent can craft a spec and ask questions for people to answer. Writing the implementation plan comes next, followed by doing the actual work. While you or your agent works, you track important milestones, deviations, decisions and more in the work log. Need to pause or have someone else do the work? No problem, craft a handoff or let ArchDocs AI do it for you. Finally, you or your agent logs a summarized version of what was done and how it was verified in an evidence of work submission. In that migration example, your agent can mark the issue in the work log as a "finding" and that will then be surfaced when future agents execute on the other 9 services. On the verification side, you may ask, "How does this help if the agent or engineer is just writing down their verification?" This is a good question and that's only one part of the verification. We have this concept of Agent attested (paired with human verified) and human attested. The last pillar and the most important is ArchDocs' own independent, automated verifications. Right now, we just have GitHub tracking for check results but we will soon be expanding this into so much more. Imagine one of the automated verifications is that a specific log with a specific attribute shows up in Datadog. Maybe even a specific event showing up in PostHog. There's a lot of ways we're going to take this and we're excited to share them once done. You can explore an example design doc without signing up. It includes the spec, implementation plan, work log and verification evidence:  https://archdocs.io/templates/design-doc-example
