## Evidence needed for every product before announcing "cheapest" or accepting payment

- [ ] Authenticated supplier, exact SKU/variant, in-stock inventory and permissible U.S. destination route, with timestamped source.
- [ ] Supplier cost, verified destination ZIP freight and expected total delivered cost. Include payment processing, tax/duty where applicable, return reserve, refund liability and any seller-funded handling.
- [ ] Same-model competitor price comparisons with live dated links, pack size, variant, availability and comparable shipping terms. No claim to world's lowest price on category-level research.
- [ ] Existing commercial-margin policy passed, with dollar profit per order and owner-reviewed proposed retail. Never slash prices below fulfillment cost to win a headline.
- [ ] Current product safety/compliance documentation when relevant. Particularly electrical chargers, lighting, battery products and garment-steaming devices.

Show HN: Hurston-1 open source TTS that speak Southern American and Afro-English
Hey HN, I’m open sourcing my Hurston-1 narrowband TTS model (Apache-2.0). It is very good with American English and does especially well with Southern American and Regional African English accents. Destined AI is based in Atlanta, and I built this because I’m amazed by what AI can do, and I wanted to help introduce and welcome more people to feel comfortable using and interacting with AI. Since 2021, I’ve been collecting fully consented voice data from over 20,000 people, 1M audio recordings, and over 1,800 hrs of audio captured to date. For this model, I used a small part of the data, 136 hrs, to finetune Maya1 and expand it’s capabilities. Hurston-1 is a narrowband TTS model that focuses the output on telephone use because that is still where most of these voices will be heard. I’ve used it to support customers such as Amazon and Salesforce and generated over half-mill revenue with it. Now I’m open sourcing it to help unlock opportunities for others as well. Limitations: this model doesn’t maintain the exact same voice across prompts and doesn’t support voice cloning. For many use cases, this is fine but maybe not so - if you’re creating podcasts. This is the first release - I’m already working on the next version with improvements. I would appreciate, if anyone is interested in this space, download the model from huggingface, check it out and let me know any feedback. Also, open to connecting with others in this space as well.

source_text:
Edit value, footprint, sourcing and DNP for many parts at once
**Why:** Getting a schematic ready for a BOM or PCB means setting the same footprint, manufacturer or DNP flag on many parts, such as all ten 0603 resistors. Today the Inspector only shows Size when several parts are selected, so you have to click and type into each part one at a time. Bulk editing makes that a single edit.

**Spec:** When the selection holds two or more components, MultiPanel (src/ui/Inspector.tsx ~L1027) shows only SizeField. Add a 'Part details' Section to MultiPanel that is visible when at least 2 selected components are real parts (hasPartFields(def), using getSymbol/instanceSymbol as the existing code does). It contains:
1. A 'Value' TextInput.
2. One TextInput per PART_FIELDS entry (footprint, manufacturer, mpn, supplier, supplier_pn, datasheet).
3. A 'Do not populate' Toggle.

How it behaves:
- If every targeted part has the same value for a field, the input shows that value. If the values differ, the input is empty with the placeholder 'Mixed'. An empty field with nothing set on any part shows the normal f.placeholder.
- Typing into an input writes that value to ALL targeted parts in ONE mutate() call, so a single undo reverts every part. For PART_FIELDS, use the same rule as PartDetails.setProp (L369): trim the value, and delete the prop when the value is blank. For Value, write c.value as typed, matching ComponentPanel L647.
- The DNP toggle shows 'on' only when every targeted part is DNP. Turning it on sets props.dnp = '1' on all targeted parts. Turning it off deletes props.dnp from all of them.
- Targets are only the selected components whose symbol hasPartFields. Labels, rails, no-connect flags, wires and shapes in the same selection are left untouched. The section summary says e.g. '7 parts' and, when some selected components are skipped, adds '· 2 labels skipped'.
- Locked parts are edited too. This matches the single-part inspector, which already lets you edit props of locked parts. Locking only blocks geometry changes.
- Custom fields and Add field are out of scope (later slice).

Put the logic in pure helpers in src/model/partFields.ts so it can be tested without React:
- `sharedValue(comps: ComponentItem[], read: (c) => string): string | null` returns the common trimmed value, or null when the values are mixed. An empty list returns ''.
- `applyPartField(doc: CircuitDoc, ids: string[], key: 'value' | PartFieldKey | 'dnp', v: string | boolean): void` mutates a draft doc, applies the rules above, and skips ids that are missing, not components, or not hasPartFields.
The UI calls `mutate((d) => applyPartField(d as CircuitDoc, ids, key, v))`.

Add a new test file src/__tests__/partFieldsBulk.test.ts. Build a small doc the way the existing tests do (see netlistExport.test.ts or groupScale.test.ts for doc/component helpers). Cover:
- sharedValue for same, mixed and empty input.
- applyPartField sets the footprint on all parts.
- A blank footprint deletes the key on all parts.
- DNP on and off.
- A net-label/rail component in ids is untouched.
- Value is written to all parts.
- An unknown id is ignored without throwing.
- toBomCsv on the result groups the now-identical parts into a single row with Quantity = n.

Update the README line under 'Part details and manufacturing' to mention that selecting several parts lets you set their value, footprint, sourcing fields and DNP together.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] src/model/partFields.ts exports sharedValue and applyPartField. applyPartField only touches components whose symbol passes hasPartFields, and ignores missing ids.
- [ ] MultiPanel in src/ui/Inspector.tsx renders a 'Part details' Section with Value, the six PART_FIELDS inputs and a DNP toggle when 2 or more selected components are real parts.
- [ ] Each edit from that section goes through exactly one mutate() call covering all targeted parts (confirm by reading the code), so one undo reverts them all.
- [ ] Mixed values show an empty input with the 'Mixed' placeholder. Values shared by every part are prefilled. The DNP toggle is on only when every targeted part is DNP.
- [ ] Blank PART_FIELDS input deletes the prop (same as single-part PartDetails). DNP off deletes props.dnp.
- [ ] New test file src/__tests__/partFieldsBulk.test.ts covers same/mixed/empty sharedValue, set/clear footprint, DNP on/off, label components untouched, unknown id ignored, and BOM grouping after bulk footprint set. `npx vitest run src/__tests__/partFieldsBulk.test.ts` passes and `npx tsc -b` reports no new errors.
- [ ] README mentions bulk editing of part details. Total diff stays under ~350 changed lines.

_Proposed by the go-agents planner. A PR follows; it is not auto-merged._

source_text:
Launch HN: Respan (YC W24) – Open-source Rust AI gateway built around plugins
Hey HN, this is Andy from Respan ( https://www.respan.ai ). We are building an open-source Rust AI gateway. It is a decoupled gateway, so everything is a plugin, including different providers, protocols (MCP, voice), modalities (images, videos), and gateway features (fallbacks, PII redaction, smart routing). Instead of packaging tons of providers and features into one gateway, Respan provides a small core and public interfaces that teams can use to assemble the AI infrastructure their application needs. That way, users can build their own features as additional plugins without having to change the gateway's core. Here’s a video demo:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pVv2ibXiTXM  There are countless LLM gateways and most of them solve a common problem: calling different providers from a single endpoint. However, adding new features can become prohibitively difficult. So developers can end up building another gateway to solve a specific problem. We've been building our gateway based on LiteLLM since 2024, and now it's providing services for thousands of orgs. Each org needs different API key settings, routes, and limits. To support that, we kept wrapping LiteLLM, adding more features to it, and at one stage, our wrapper code exceeded 100,000 lines. This January, a routine LiteLLM upgrade caused intermittent connection errors, and we had to roll back. We still haven't figured out the cause, but since then, we no longer upgrade LiteLLM directly and instead manually backport upstream fixes. These experiences made us realize that continuing to patch LiteLLM is not a sustainable long-term solution, and we had to redesign the gateway ourselves. While redesigning our gateway, we wanted to make it easier to add features without breaking existing ones. Inspired by Nginx, we think an AI gateway should have a really small core, only responsible for dispatching events. We believe that everything should be a plugin in our gateway, including providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), protocols (chat, realtime voice, MCP), modalities (images, videos), and gateway features for reliability and security (smart routing, fallbacks, and PII redaction through example plugins). Beyond that, we want developers to be able to easily extend the gateway's capabilities by adding their own plugins, without touching the core. Adding a provider, even your own, is dead simple, because quirks are plugins too and there’s nothing magical about them. A provider is a short file, Mistral’s is 22 lines, and each quirk, like Groq putting token usage in its own field, gets its own test. Respan Gateway does more than let you call Claude or Gemini models from the OpenAI SDK. It handles tools, images, and reasoning protocols automatically: an application based on the OpenAI Realtime API can also use Gemini Live through the gateway, though not every feature translates. A simple chat app can use MCP tools configured in the gateway, without implementing MCP itself. We also parse requests into a shared structure. When the client and provider use the same API, we preserve provider-specific fields in their native format, even if our shared structure doesn't have a field for them. That way, the gateway can write them back instead of dropping them. Here’s how it works: An adapter hands each HTTP or WebSocket connection to the first client format that recognizes it. The format exposes the request as a two-way stream of typed input and output events. The core runs plugins in registration order, allowing them to choose a provider, filter or wrap either stream, make additional calls, return a response, or refuse the request. A provider format then opens the upstream connection. If the client and provider use the same format and no plugin changes the payload, the original bytes and protocol-specific fields can pass through unchanged. When formats differ, they translate through shared types for messages, tool calls, results, streams, and usage. This stream model can represent both one-shot HTTP requests and long-lived bidirectional sessions. The gateway is open source at  https://github.com/respanai/respan-gateway  under the MIT or Apache-2.0 license. You don't need to use Respan's hosted platform and can run it directly on your local machine. Build it from source, add your provider keys, and swap the base URL in a supported client. You can keep using the API your client already speaks. It's still pre-alpha. We make money from our hosted platform ( https://www.respan.ai/pricing ), which runs the gateway for you with native observability and evals, along with unified billing. If you’re building routing, tools, filtering, observability, or security for agents, we'd love to see it as a plugin. PLUGINS.md in the repo explains how to write one and links to the plugins we’ve created so far. Turning that into an ecosystem is basically our roadmap, and we welcome you to contribute your own plugins. We'd love to answer any questions and hear your feedback!  https://github.com/respanai/respan-gateway

source_text:
Looking for a tech job is a helpless data-entry nightmare
I spent hundred of hours (distributed over many days) filling my resume data to freshly developed forms made specifically to the hiring process of one or two companies, even though I feel like I have a top 10% resume and years of in hands-down software development experience. I love solving problems, it's part of me. I know it has got a lot harder to land a development gig but I've worked with modern stuff like AI-generated briefs for meetings, bug logs automatically sent emails to responsible developers, at a point I had an Agent dedicated to verifying how well our code was written so I feel like I've kept up with the innovations, and skills. But I have no idea how to land a job in software development anymore: nothing seems enough. I have tried for over a year and the only reason I can withstand this much waiting while seeking a job in that field is because of my exceptional employment history (including working to Silicon Valley companies), but it has got to a point I am worried. I've asked my friends who are also developers and they feel similarly, we do not know where to dedicate our effors, as if the competency of software engineers were transformed irrelevant because of AI. We know what happened, we just don't know what to do with all the competency we embody. I've taken a liking to working as a bartender in my local city, because that's kind of the only job I can land lately, but as soon as my degree in Computer Engineering is mentioned I'm set aside as a anti-social computer expert who will never take a low-paying job like "this". (Secretly I found it very fun, fullfilling in a way I never thought I needed because money was my priority at the beggining of the carreer) How the hell do we transform this competency and learning ability of software engineers into desireable company-adding value skills? (I swear this is not generated by AI, I don't even know how to prove anymore)

### Bug Description

When you click **+** in the sidebar and hover an option like **New workflow**, a submenu opens with a "Create in" heading above the list of projects. This heading is written in English directly in the code, so it does not get translated. The same heading shows up for workflows, credentials, variables, data tables and agents.

https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/58f11bf0cf5e384efa7f6818fc940ff5ed8200a9/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/app/composables/useGlobalEntityCreation.ts#L130

Everything else in these submenus is already translated, for example `projects.menu.personal` and `projects.menu.create.workflow`.

2. Set the UI to a language other than English.
3. Click the **+** button in the sidebar.

The heading shows in the selected language.

### Debug Info

I found this while reading the code on `master` (2.45.0). The text is written into the code, so it happens on every setup.

### Environment

- Operating System: macOS (platform independent)
- n8n Version: 2.45.0 (`master`)
- Node.js Version: 24.x
- Database: n/a
- Execution mode: n/a

### Note

The fix is in #41773.

source_text:
Editor shows a deleted credential as valid when another credential has the same name, but execution fails with "Credential with ID ... does not exist"
### Bug Description

When the credential referenced by a node is deleted and a new credential with the same name and type is created, the editor treats the node as correctly configured. The credential selector shows the new credential as selected, with a check mark, and no credential issue is raised on the node.

The workflow, however, still stores the old, deleted credential ID. Any execution (manual "Execute step", manual workflow run, or a production trigger of the published version) fails with:

Credential with ID "0Snu055DhBPxJwpy" does not exist for type "httpBasicAuth".
Selecting the same credential again in the dropdown does not fix it. The stored ID stays the old one, so the user has no visible way to repair the node from the credential selector.

As far as I can tell, the cause is that the frontend and the backend resolve the credential differently:

Frontend: useNodeHelpers.getNodeCredentialIssues first looks up the stored ID. If that fails, it falls back to a name match. When exactly one credential matches by name, no issue is reported: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/ddfafbfbeb61bf45d5b46085e0f194df87369a3c/packages/frontend/editor-ui/src/app/composables/useNodeHelpers.ts#L645-L690
Backend: CredentialsHelper.getCredentialsEntity looks up by ID only and throws CredentialNotFoundError: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/ddfafbfbeb61bf45d5b46085e0f194df87369a3c/packages/cli/src/credentials-helper.ts#L348-L366
So the node looks valid in the editor but cannot run.

My guess about the dropdown (not verified): the selector already shows the same-name credential as the current value, so clicking that option does not emit a change. onCredentialSelected / replaceInvalidWorkflowCredentials then never run, and the stale ID is never replaced.

With the draft/publish model the problem gets worse. Even after the draft is repaired, the published version keeps the deleted ID until the workflow is published again. Scheduled runs keep failing in the meantime, and the editor gives no hint about it.

### To Reproduce

1. Create an HTTP Basic Auth credential named Login API.
2. Create two workflows. Each one has a Schedule Trigger and an HTTP Request node (Authentication: Generic Credential Type → Basic Auth) using Login API. Publish both.
3. Go to Overview → Credentials, delete Login API, and create a new HTTP Basic Auth credential with the same name, Login API.
4. Open workflow 1 and the HTTP Request node.
- The Basic Auth field shows Login API, and the dropdown has a check mark on the new credential.
- The node shows no credential issue or warning.
5. Select Login API again in the dropdown, close the node and save.
6. Click Execute step (or run the workflow).
- It fails with Credential with ID "<old id>" does not exist for type "httpBasicAuth".
7. Export the workflow, or read it through the API. The node still has "credentials": { "httpBasicAuth": { "id": "<old id>", "name": "Login API" } }.
8. The published version keeps the old ID too, so production/scheduled executions fail as well.

Workaround: change Generic Auth Type to a different type, switch back to Basic Auth, select the credential (now the change really happens), save, and publish the workflow.

### Expected behavior

One of these:

- The editor flags the node with a credential issue when the stored ID does not exist, even if a credential with the same name exists ("Credential 'Login API' was deleted, select it again"), and selecting a credential in the dropdown always writes its ID to the node, even when it already looks selected.

- When the editor resolves a missing ID by a unique name match, it writes the resolved ID back to the node (marking the workflow as changed), so that what the user sees is what gets executed.


Also nice to have: a warning when deleting a credential that is still used by published workflows, listing the affected workflows.

isBetween() with date-only string bounds drops the written day in non-UTC workflow timezones
### Bug Description

In a workflow expression, `DateTime.local(2023, 6, 16, 23, 0).isBetween('2023-06-16', '2023-06-17')` returns `false` when the workflow timezone is west of UTC (for example America/New_York), even though 23:00 on June 16 is inside the written range. Date-only string bounds go through `new Date()`, which parses them as UTC midnight; converted into the workflow timezone, `'2023-06-16'` becomes June 15, 8:00 PM in New York. East of UTC the bounds land mid-day instead of midnight. The same shift affects partial date-only strings (`'2023-06'`, `'2023'`).

I reproduced this in n8n's own expression test suites (`packages/workflow` and `packages/@n8n/expression-runtime`): a regression test with the expression above fails on current master in the default America/New_York test timezone.

### To Reproduce

1. Set a workflow's timezone to America/New_York (workflow Settings).
2. Evaluate `{{ DateTime.local(2023, 6, 16, 23, 0).isBetween('2023-06-16', '2023-06-17') }}` in an expression, for example in a Set node.
3. The result is `false`.

### Expected behavior

`true`. Date-only string bounds should mean midnight in the workflow timezone, the same way `.toDateTime()` already parses `'2023-06-16'` (`tryToParseDateTime` uses `DateTime.fromISO`, i.e. local midnight).

### Debug Info

Reproduced on current master (2.45.0) through the test suites above (Node 24). I did not run a separate UI test; the steps above are the reproduction path for the same code. Related: #42064 reports the same class of bug for String.toDate - this is a different code path (isBetween bounds via convertToDateTime), not covered by its PR #42065.

Zenvocloud: zero-cost first-customer acquisition sprint
## Goal
Acquire the first verified paying B2B customer for Zenvocloud/TaskForge, with $0 upfront spend and no invented leads or revenue.

## Current verified baseline (2026-10-12)
- Production homepage and 11 other intended routes return HTTP 200.
- `/api/lead` rejects GET (405) and invalid POST (400); valid submission, storage and notifications not yet verified.
- Upwork freelancer profile is active but positioned primarily around financial planning and unrelated skills; 0 Connects. Do not buy Connects or claim applications were submitted.
- Cloudflare production deployment is successful; do not assume all premium redesign elements are live.

## Work packages (execute, verify, record evidence)
1. Verify the valid lead intake end-to-end using an isolated staging environment and synthetic data; remove test records; verify notifications and avoid any live false leads.
2. Check all visible CTAs and customer paths for broken links, quote request friction, honest service claims, and privacy compliance.
3. Build a concise B2B offer sheet for inventory/CSV cleanup, CRM data quality, and operational automation with truthful sample work and scoped deliverables. Do not invent testimonials or guaranteed outcomes.
4. Prepare free-channel distribution: portfolio pages, relevant communities/directories where business posts are permitted, and compliant, tailored outreach to genuine buyer requests. No mass unsolicited spam.
5. Audit Upwork positioning and draft a factual replacement headline/bio/skills for user confirmation. Do not edit profile without platform-required approval; no paid Connects.
6. Verify merchant checkout and fulfillment independently before accepting payment; keep unverified gates closed.
7. Track weekly metrics: qualified prospects discovered, relevant outreach sent, replies, quotes, verified payments. Report zeros explicitly.

## Acceptance criteria
- Evidence links for each completed action.
- One successful isolated end-to-end synthetic lead test, with cleanup evidence.
- At least one honest, discoverable offer and one verified permitted zero-cost acquisition channel.
- No spending, fabricated customer records, or unauthorized outreach.

[GoodBounty-QA] Live test the GoodReserve widget on XDC
## Summary

Independently test the GoodReserve widget through real human use on XDC production, including one small live buy and one small live sell. Check the full experience, stale-quote fixes and recovery paths, then submit a reproducible report with evidence. Developer self-tests, automation and fixture results support this work but do not replace the tester's own live use.

## Request and scope

- **Implementation:** [GoodWidget PR #280](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodWidget/pull/280).
- **Revision to test:** `570eb00392dcba8d5862056be09f455b9d06869e`. Record the exact checked-out SHA; confirm any replacement revision with the maintainer before testing it.
- **Original requirements:** [GoodWidget issue #279](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodWidget/issues/279).
- **QA guide:** [GoodWidget QA guide](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodWidget/blob/main/docs/qa-guide.md).
- **Report format:** [GoodBounties reusable QA report](https://github.com/GoodDollar/.github/blob/master/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/GoodBounties-QA-Template.md), used below for the tester's submission.
- **Bounty-Tier:** Common

Comment with your ETA and intended browser/wallet coverage. Wait for assignment and confirmation that the PR is ready for QA before starting.

The required transaction scope is **XDC mainnet, chain ID 50, production contracts**, with the environment fixed throughout testing. Development-contract transactions, redesign and new wallet integrations are outside this task.

## Setup and test funds

1. Read the PR, original requirements, review discussion and QA guide. Identify existing evidence and known gaps. Ask the maintainer about missing or conflicting requirements rather than assuming they passed.
2. Check out the named revision and run:

   ```sh
   git rev-parse HEAD
   pnpm install
   pnpm build
   pnpm storybook
   ```

3. Open `http://localhost:6006` and select **Widgets → GoodReserveWidget → InjectedWallet**. Use a dedicated injected browser wallet on XDC. This story uses the widget's default production environment; keep it fixed. Record the installed widget and reserve SDK versions, browser/version, OS, wallet/version and viewport.
4. Before signing anything, contact the team in [GoodBounties Telegram](https://t.me/gooddollarbounties/4115) to request test funds and confirm the production token/reserve addresses, spender, XDC gas funding and approved buy/sell amounts. If these are unavailable or unclear, mark the affected cases **Blocked**.
5. Check the wallet's network, token, spender and amount before each approval or transaction. Stop on any mismatch. Never share private keys or seed phrases, and redact sensitive data from evidence.

The **Interactive** story uses a custodial fixture wallet. Do not fund it or use its results as evidence of your own live-wallet QA. Optional automated checks, such as `pnpm test:demo tests/widgets/goodreserve-widget`, must be reported separately with the tested version, actual outcome and run evidence.

## Required cases

Record each subcheck separately when outcomes differ. Include expected and actual behaviour, who performed the check and supporting evidence.

1. **QA-01 Connect and recover.** Connect the wallet and verify the displayed address, XDC network and balances. Disconnect/reconnect and refresh. The widget must recover with the correct current state.
2. **QA-02 Change accounts.** Switch accounts, including while a quote is loading and while confirmation is open, without signing. Previous-account balances or quotes must not remain actionable. Return to the funded account and verify fresh state.
3. **QA-03 Amount validation and MAX.** Try empty, zero, non-numeric, fractional and insufficient amounts. Invalid amounts must not enable Review. Valid fractional amounts must retain the correct units and precision. MAX must not exceed the available balance. Do not execute a MAX swap unless that full amount is approved.
4. **QA-04 Quotes and fees.** Check both USDM → G$ and G$ → USDM. Verify token labels and decimals, estimated output, rate, slippage, minimum received and exit contribution. Main-view and confirmation details must agree, allowing for display rounding. Record wallet gas fees separately.
5. **QA-05 Changed inputs and delayed quotes.** Change amount, direction and slippage after receiving a quote. The previous quote must stop being actionable while a replacement loads. Try rapid edits and confirm that an older response cannot replace the latest quote. Record any timing scenario you could not exercise.
6. **QA-06 Unchanged inputs.** After a valid quote loads, press MAX twice, reselect the active slippage preset and enter a character removed by amount sanitisation. When the effective input is unchanged, the widget must not clear the quote and remain stuck without a replacement.
7. **QA-07 Live buy.** Complete one small approved USDM → G$ buy. Verify any token approval, confirmation details, pending/success states, the XDC explorer link and resulting balances. Repeated clicks must not create duplicate submissions; do not approve extra transactions to test this. Include the swap transaction link and any approval link.
8. **QA-08 Live sell.** Complete one small approved G$ → USDM sell. Verify approval if requested, exit contribution, minimum received, pending/success states, explorer link and resulting balances. Include the swap transaction link and any approval link.
9. **QA-09 Cancel and retry.** Cancel the widget confirmation, then separately reject a wallet request and retry. Neither cancellation may appear as success or leave the widget stuck. Report any other errors encountered and whether recovery works.
10. **QA-10 Expired quote.** Leave a confirmation quote open for more than 60 seconds. Attempt to continue without approving a stale transaction. The expired quote must refresh and require review again before signing.
11. **QA-11 Network changes.** Switch away from XDC while a quote is loading and, separately, while confirmation is open, without signing. Old quotes must stop being actionable. An unsupported network must show the switch-network state rather than become stuck fetching a quote. Return to XDC and verify fresh balances and a current quote. No transaction on another network is required.
12. **QA-12 Layout and exploration.** Test desktop and mobile viewports, including 390px. Check readable copy, reachable controls, loading/error states and console/runtime errors. Explore beyond the checklist and report confusing or inconsistent behaviour. State whether mobile coverage used a resized browser or a physical device. Compare with the linked written requirements; include reference and implementation evidence for visual discrepancies.

If available, repeat connection and quote checks with a second compatible injected wallet. Identify that as additional coverage and state if it was not attempted.

## Required QA report

Follow the GoodWidget [QA guide’s](https://github.com/GoodDollar/GoodWidget/blob/main/docs/qa-guide.md) reporting and retesting instructions. Post your report on PR #280 and link it from this issue. Include both live XDC swap transaction links.

## Testing funds.

Once assigned please reach out on telegram to request for testing funds. you can reach out through the goodbounties channel:

First-Dollar Mission: qualify and complete the first paid AI-assisted repair
## Objective
Get BountyForge's **first legitimately paid AI-assisted coding repair**, then repeat toward a **$2,000/month gross** target. This is a private income-generation operator, **not a SaaS to sell**. Optimize for accepted work and net receipts, not developmental test counts.

- $0 additional spending; no paid APIs, runners, infrastructure, application credits, or subscriptions.
- Never use the owner's Mac; don't interfere with Phase 15 or either existing draft PR.
- No Reddit and no phone-dependent outreach.
- Do not accept third-party code, tokens, personal information or customer credentials into the public runner or current unadmitted sandbox.
- Do not submit bids, send messages, claim bounties, accept terms, deliver external work, enable scheduled inference, collect money, or promise results without the owner's explicit approval.
- Respect venue rules on automation and AI use, US eligibility, funding, and payout/KYC. A posting is not an offer or escrow.

## Live research checkpoint, 2026-10-23
1. **Upwork candidate A (research only): $70 fixed**: [Improve existing Python AI document-extraction tool](https://www.upwork.com/freelance-jobs/apply/Python-Developer-Improve-Existing-Document-Extraction-Tool_~022111905971757282297/). Published Oct 18; PDF→JSON extraction, missed fields/layout differences and inconsistent structure. Potentially bounded if sample PDFs, expected outputs and tests are supplied. Published Sep 29; login/signup, Airtable lookups, session/auth. Requires private code/credential-safe test harness; current bidding availability, AI permission and source custody **unverified**. Public page direct fetch blocked with 403.
3. **Reject**: [tscircuit/dsn-converter#54](https://github.com/tscircuit/dsn-converter/issues/54). Algora shows several nominal open bounty amounts, but original issue was **closed** when checked Oct 23.
4. **Reject**: [tscircuit/jlcsearch#92](https://github.com/tscircuit/jlcsearch/issues/92). Algora still lists it, but original issue was **closed** when checked Oct 23.

- [Upwork Help: Connects](https://support.upwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/211062898-Understanding-and-using-Connects): applications may consume Connects and purchases cost money. Do not buy any. Use only existing/free credits if platform terms and account permit; available balance and listing-specific required Connects remain unknown.
- [Opire official payments](https://docs.opire.dev/rewards/pricing): claiming/creating a bounty **does not cause automatic payment**. The bounty creator separately reviews and arranges payment. Reject any repository claiming guaranteed automated Opire payout until independently substantiated; for example, claude-builders-bounty/claude-builders-bounty#4 currently states automatic payout on merge in conflict with Opire's own policy.
- Existing owner-only [Hatchable BountyForge dashboard](https://leftsock-bountyforge.hatchable.site) read-only status on Oct 23: 25 discovered candidates, zero verified funded and zero third-party repair attempts; the discoverer is not commercial admission.

- Check whether A and B still accept proposals in the owner's authorized platform account, whether application requires paid Connects, whether AI-assisted work is permitted and whether the client accepts an explicitly bounded paid milestone. **Do not spend to apply.**

- If no task passes, publish a specific **blocked** verdict with evidence, not a synthetic success.

PROC-SOURCING-001: authorized acquisition receipts to attributable sourcing candidates
## Purpose

Define the Symthaea-side adapter between evidence-first external acquisition and Mycelix's capability-first sourcing evaluator ([Mycelix PR #5072](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5072)). Reuse existing OSINT/tool-selection, provenance, component identity and Mycelix execution receipts; do not create another browser/network authority path.

## Existing owners to compose

- Symthaea RES-OSINT-001 / #5417: bounded investigation state machine and search-plan semantics.
- Symthaea RES-OSINT-TOOL-001 / #5440: reasoning-only tool/source adapter selection.
- Symthaea RES-SEC-001D / #5569: retire legacy direct WebResearcher egress from the cognitive authority path.
- Symthaea ROB-CATALOG-001 / #4877: physical component, datasheet, BOM and substitution identity.
- Symthaea provenance/revocation contract, PR #7553: source/publisher identity, revision/digest anchors, retrieval time, integrity result, lifecycle, rights, and claim-validity semantics.
- Mycelix #1110 and #5005: supply-chain traceability bridge and versioned logistics standards registry.
- Mycelix #5037 / #5072: need-to-fulfilment and capability-first sourcing comparison.
- Sol Atlas PR #101: geographic/supply-network and disruption context, with explicit evidence maturity.

## Core boundary

```text
candidate search plan
  != permission to disclose query

authorized external execution receipt
  != evidence truth

supplier page / parsed offer
  != verified stock

engineering component
  != merchant listing
  != purchased article

sourcing frontier
  != winner
  != purchase authorization
  != order dispatch
```

Symthaea should reason about source and method selection, consume exact authorized-acquisition receipts, and emit attributable candidate projections. It must not instantiate a raw network client from a cognition path, self-mint disclosure permits, interpret no result as proof of absence, or route a candidate directly to checkout.

## Candidate projection contract

A first reference adapter should preserve, without promoting caller claims into verified facts:

- source/receipt identity, exact retrieval or observation time, source locator, content digest and integrity-verifier reference;
- acquisition and extraction profile identities and versions;
- supplier/listing identity separately from physical component identity;
- manufacturer part number/revision, exact variant and capability-profile reference when available;
- quote currency/unit, per-unit price and quantity basis, minimum-order/pack-size semantics, shipping/tax/fees, quote validity;
- inventory quantity, inventory-specific observation time, expiration/currentness and evidence origin/status;
- declared lead time, geography and evidence provenance;
- explicit unknown/contested/unavailable fields rather than fabricated defaults;
- reviewed substitution mapping reference and version, when a listed item differs from the requested canonical capability.

ValueFlows, GS1 EPCIS/CBV and UBL/OCDS are mapping targets where applicable—not permission to conflate intent, commitment, provider claim, observed event, supplier listing, shipment and physical truth.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inventory the exact existing source-receipt/provenance/component contracts before adding types.
2. Define a read-only projection from qualified receipt + field-level extraction evidence into the Mycelix sourcing offer input.
3. Keep extraction, evidence integrity, issuer trust, quote/stock currentness, capability equivalence and procurement authority as separate gates.
4. Add offline fixtures for price/stock timestamp divergence, source-content mutation, redirect/new-origin mismatch, hostile page instructions, unit/currency mismatch, pack-size/MOQ, substitution drift, duplicate listings, stale credentials, unknown fields and exact replay.
5. Add a separate oracle that validates projection completeness and rejected/indeterminate cases without importing the production adapter implementation.
6. Only later, wire an RFQ/purchase-order draft flow through Mycelix. Transactional execution must remain in its separately authorized gateway.

## Proposed acceptance targets (not measured)

- 100% of emitted offer fields map to an explicit field-level evidence reference or an explicit unknown state.
- Zero unverified/stale/conflicting quote or stock observations promoted to eligible.
- Zero implicit unit/currency/pack-size conversions.
- Zero substitutions admitted without a matching versioned capability-equivalence reference.
- Zero cross-origin or redirected external destinations treated as authorized by the original request.
- 100% duplicate/replay fixtures deterministic; source mutation invalidates the relevant digest binding.
- No cognitive-path network/credential authority; only the exact authorized execution receipt may advance acquisition state.
- Measure projection latency separately from network acquisition and sourcing evaluation; freeze host, corpus and toolchain before reporting.

## Scope ceiling

This is not a browser rewrite, a general supplier registry, a product crawler, a truth oracle, an automatic public-sector integrity finding, or purchase execution. Do not duplicate Mycelix's canonical EPI, supplier, component or logistics semantics. The first deliverable is a read-only, effects-disabled projection plus adversarial fixtures.


## Procurement portfolio/recourse integration (2026-10-17)

Compose with the new Mycelix portfolio and adaptive-recourse slices rather than building an independent supplier-ranking or execution path:

- [Mycelix #5088 — portfolio sourcing](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/5088), [PR #5099 — bounded exact portfolio allocator](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5099), and [PR #5108 — scenario-specific adaptive recourse](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/pull/5108).
- [Mycelix #5109 — ex-ante selection of flexible/backup commitments](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix/issues/5109) is a separate follow-on task; #5108 evaluates a fixed baseline and already-committed option set.
- Candidate projections should preserve normal/base allocation versus flexible/backup option semantics, capacity-pool identity and snapshot, reservation/activation fees, activation lead plus transit time, quote/qualification/capacity freshness, and declared parent/site/sub-tier/route failure domains.
- Do not let a Symthaea forecast become a verified capacity observation. Do not count source-name diversity as resilience when the sourced dependency graph overlaps.
- Emit attributable, advisory candidate/forecast records with source, model, timestamp, uncertainty and input-manifest identities. Mycelix remains the authority/evidence record owner; actual contract changes and purchases require a separate authorized workflow.
- For first evaluation, use Mycelix's frozen synthetic scenarios and compare forecasts against later observed outcomes. Keep synthetic scenario results separate from live-domain source evidence.

1. A pure decision contract: only authoritative, fresh, fully bound per-lot `PASS_TO_TS` enters TS research. `HOLD_NATIONAL`, `SKIP`, missing evidence, and manual K-column values without source verification never enter automatic supplier research. No `GO` inferred.
2. Define typed normalized result shape for: lot identity/announcement, original TS source/link/hash and criteria list, actual candidate Brand+Model+Partnumber, criterion-by-criterion evidence and `TS_COMPLIANCE_100_PERCENT` (never fabricated), three distinct supplier quotes with price/date/stock/lead time evidence, delivery/taxes/certifications/fees/contingency, total landed cost, net profit, margin, markup, break-even, and GO/REVIEW/NO-GO. Missing cost items -> REVIEW; `GO` only when margin >=20% *net*, all proofs present, acceptable competition/legal constraints and TS compliance=100%.
3. Offline tests for malformed/duplicate TS criteria, weak price sources, outdated quotes, missing costs, optimistic profit assumptions, contradictory supplier stock, national gate UNKNOWN/YES, replay/idempotency and zero Sheets/Secrets mutations.

- Do not fake product matches, suppliers, quoted prices, 100% TS or profit. No direct external purchases/bids.
- Keep `FULL_SCAN_DISABLED`, no daily trigger, no API key change, no Apps Script publish, no autonomous writes to Google Sheets or `NATIONAL_GATE`.

- Distinguish **verified wedding-ready** from existing RoamWise stays; do NOT auto-label hotels as wedding-ready without capacity, event permission, pricing and owner consent.
- Venue cards: rooms, guest capacity, lawn/banquet, indoor rain backup, parking, road access, music cutoff, accessibility, noise limits, indicative prices, cancellation/deposit and GST disclosure where applicable.
- Vendor match with human approval. Ailon Tusk should collect brief, create budget ranges with assumptions, show only verified offers, route quote requests, maintain enquiry state. Never hallucinate availability or accept payments without valid backend integration.
- Admin CRM for lead sources, unique enquiry IDs, consent, status, owner, quote response SLA, deposits, revenue/commission, disputes. Scoped staff access; founder final approval.
- Start as lead/referral model; no involuntary payment collection and no dependency on Cashfree production until sandbox webhook/reconciliation/idempotency checks pass.
- Add schema.org metadata, wedding SEO destinations pages, analytics funnel visit -> lead -> qualified -> venue quote -> booking -> gross margin.
- Include wedding-day traffic and shuttle coordination; small curated celebrations as signature offering.

Venue commission 5–8% where signed; vendor referral 8–12% where signed; transport 5–10% margin; planning coordination fee quoted transparently. No double-charging; written vendor/referral terms and clear customer pricing, T&Cs, cancellation, GST.
Existing stay commission terms remain unchanged until signed amendment.

- Mobile Android Chrome (Moto G64), desktop, keyboard/screen-reader basics.
- End-to-end submitted lead appears in admin, is deduped, can be assigned, followed up, closed, and exported without leaking personal information.
- Wedding vendor onboarding needs photo permissions, owner consent, verification status, and ability to upload real images.
- No fake testimonials, fabricated prices, unsupported inventory or automatic claims of partnerships.
- Feature flag OFF by default until smoke tests and founder review; no production write or live charge without separate approval.

## Launch KPI
30-day goal: 20 verified suppliers, 30 qualified leads, >=5 signed quote requests, >=1 confirmed paid booking, measured verified net contribution, with acquisition spend capped.

Python API Integration Bot
I need a reliable Python-based bot whose single purpose is to integrate several external APIs and keep the data flowing between them without manual intervention. The core of the job is to build clean, well-structured code that can:

• Authenticate against each service (OAuth2, token, or key as required)  
• Schedule and trigger calls at configurable intervals  
• Parse and combine the responses into a single, usable JSON payload  
• Log every request/response and gracefully handle time-outs, rate limits, and other common errors

If asynchronous techniques (aiohttp, asyncio) or task queues (Celery, RQ) would improve performance, feel free to include them. Well-written docstrings, a short README, and concise setup instructions are part of the final hand-off so I can extend the bot internally later.

I’m open on exact tooling, as long as the end result is a self-contained script or small package I can drop onto a Linux server and run with a single command. Please include a brief outline of your proposed approach and any past projects where you wired multiple APIs together successfully.

source_text:
Show HN: RDST – A local agent that watches Postgres/MySQL for query regressions
We noticed during the course of many many years of DBA related work that fixes to database issues and queries are always reactive. An entire database can fall over extremely quickly when an unbounded query grows without warning. Traditionally, DBAs hear complaints of slowness and follow a methodical process: 
- manually browse pg_stats or other database related performance internal tables 
- see which queries are slowest
- figure out what indexes are missing
- figure out which indexes are actually bad and slowing down writes
- painstakingly implement a fix In the age of cheap intelligence, we decided that there is no reason we can’t have an always-on agent that is designed to do this job for you.  Databases need something or someone that is always watching with a massive amount of contextual understanding to be able to take quick actions.  We’ve watched the alternative play out repeatedly. One of our users’s checkout page went from loading instantly to taking 11 seconds in a single night with no code change.  How? Well somehow their order table grew by 40M rows because BI team had injected historical data and suddenly postgres started doing full table scans. Sometimes routine operations have unintended results and can easily destroy your database. We wanted to catch these kinds of regressions instantly. So we built RDST. RDST is a desktop agent that runs on your PC and connects to PostgreSQL / MYSQL (read only) and compares every query against its own performance every minute. Every expensive query is automatically EXPLAIN ANALYZED, stripped of PII and sent to U.S. based frontier or open model providers to analyze which indexes are missing, how the query could be rewritten, and provides the fix.  We then run a classifier model (JEV) to decide if you should be notified (is this standard behavior for this particular query?), and the full history of the query performance is kept for years.  RDST also keeps track of your entire database health in general, and recommends more fixes than simply bad queries. Since it runs locally we can keep the database credentials stored in your OS Keychain (RDST never keeps them in its own storage layer), and the connection goes straight to your database (using a jump host or SSH tunnel for private connections). You can read more about how we handle data especially as it pertains to LLM use here.  https://readyset.io/docs/readyset-ai/rdst/desktop/privacy  We really want feedback from the community from people running Postgres and MySQL in production. We are giving inference away completely for free. Just as a reminder, RDST will NOT run any updates or indexes against your database at this time.  We are considering a fully autonomous auto-pilot mode in the future, but for now we are leaving the actual fixes in your hands. Let us know what you think!

source_text:
Show HN: Overtone – Transcribe, correct and cut captions for any screen shape
Hi HN, I'm Ruud, co-founder of Lont. We turn company emails into personalized videos. Video captions cost us manual work twice: fixing misheard words, then fixing layout, like lines ending on “the”. Overtone uses multiple models to listen to the audio: gpt-transcribe, Azure STT, and Elevenlabs Scribe. When they return conflicting results, Overtone sends small clips to the models again, and then lets an LLM decide what was actually said. The LLM is like a human doing a sanity check on the transcription model. Humans would easily recognize a word to be different based on context. The LLM basically does the same, using an optional context prompt + its world knowledge. Because of this the Word Error Rate (WER) on many test files is lower when using Overtone, compared to just using a model without it. Sure, the cost is higher because we use up to 3 different STT models + an LLM, but it still removes mistakes, reducing the time needed to fix captions to a minimum, and reducing the chance you'll miss something. For us it's worth it. For ultra high volume use cases it may not be. The rules-based cutter nicely cuts the transcript into captions that look good, depending on screen size: 16:9 is different from 9:16, and the Overtone Format we created supports any type really. Pauses become breaks, captions are grouped per speaker, and names/numbers are never spread out over multiple captions. How to add these captions to your videos? A videojs plugin can do this automatically, so you don't burn in your captions. The plugin lets you cycle between styled captions, plain captions, and off. You can burn them into an MP4 file with overtone burn. Quickly try it out just the cutter? Try:     npx overtone-captions recut yoursub.srt
  
Transcribing audio with API keys works too. Use --dry-run to show a cost estimate before you send. We open-sourced this first version (MIT) because we believe many people can benefit from this, especially if your captions just need to be good. There's plenty of room to improve though, so we've made it easy to help contribute to add style packs, languages, and providers/models. You can find a demo at:  https://overtone.lont.ai/  Find the code and benchmarks here:  https://github.com/lonthq/overtone-captions

source_text:
Golden Client E2E — parcours boutique→retrait, preuves documentaires B2C/B2B et recette humaine
## Objectif produit
Transformer la Golden actuelle (cockpit 10 frontières, commande synthétique créée déjà payée) en **recette complète boutique → client final → finance**, comprenant **documents clients + preuves B2B et contrôles agents**. Un seul fil `market + order_reference + trace_id` lie Playwright, verdicts humains, écrans réels, documents et oracles backend. Ne pas refaire les centaines de tests existants ; les réutiliser.

## État vérifié sur main au 13/10/2026
- `public/golden-e2e-cockpit.html` offre 10 étapes et les boutons `golden-create` / `golden-advance` ; il commence sur une commande **déjà préparée**, pas sur la visite client/OTP/checkout. `services/golden-e2e-cockpit.js` projette les faits métiers, pas les documents.
- Le cockpit peut actuellement afficher `Golden certifié` sur **10 clics humains** indépendamment des preuves backend (faux vert).
- Route `/admin/golden-e2e` présente dans `bootstrap/html-routes.js` ; entrée de menu Canonical à confirmer/brancher sous autorité admin.
- `routes/admin-order-360.js` : POST `golden-create` / `golden-advance` sont **interdits en production** (garde NODE_ENV). Ne jamais contourner cette garde.
- `features/documents.feature.js` / `routes/documents.js` : accès privé client sous `/api/auth/me/documents` ; actuellement la liste client expose factures et reçus de remboursement. `transaction_documents` contient aussi des justificatifs internes. Aucune URL documentaire publique, aucun PDF envoyé via WhatsApp.
- Réconciliation Hub distincte du fulfillment ; réception réelle validée par agent Hub ; remise client distincte de disponibilité relais.
- Source : `docs/doctrine/DOCTRINE_DOCUMENTS_TRANSACTIONNELS_KOMERCE.md` et `docs/audits/KOMERCE_E2E_CERTIFICATION_GAP.md` (audit point de départ, à réévaluer sur HEAD).

## Scénario fil rouge — automatisation puis recette humaine
1. **Client navigateur réel** : market KM/CM/CG, catalogue sourcé et affichage en français, fiche produit/variante/prix/stock, panier individuel ou liste figée.
2. **Client authentification OTP** : émission réelle sur sandbox contrôlé, réception/validation, expiration, erreur, tentative concurrente. Pas de faux « OTP reçu » à partir d'une simple réponse simulée.
3. **Checkout** : choix relais, devise, prix figé, création commande depuis la vraie boutique (pas d'INSERT préalable). Variantes wallet, cash relais, PSP sandbox si disponible, Mobile Money selon market/capacité.
4. **Confirmation** : événement de paiement confirmé (pas simple `pending`), commande/reçu, **facture client** (PDF immuable privé, bon destinataire), historique / Mon Komerce / notification.
5. **Achat fournisseur** : `purchase_lines` → PO SKU/SOI exact, groupement, doublons/concurrence, fournisseur/quantités/devise. Contrôle du bon de commande B2B (trame/état réel, PDF seulement si un système en produit un).
6. **Exécution fournisseur** : preuve de commande et de paiement fournisseur, confirmation/accusé externe **si réellement accessible**, matching/rejeu.
7. **Expédition fournisseur** : numéro tracking, preuve d'expédition / BL ou facture fournisseur si transmis ; aucun document présumé présent ; suivi fournisseur ne signifie **pas** réception Hub.
8. **Réception physique Hub** : agent Hub confirme unité/quantité/état sur vraie surface autorisée ; pièce de réception / écart / réserve rattachée à la PO. C'est le Hub qui confirme physiquement.
9. **Transit → douane → relais → remise** : pièces de transport/douane (si requises), réception relais réelle, scan QR/code/autorisation, preuve de retrait client ; disponible ≠ remis.
10. **Clôture** : coûts achat/transport/douane, cash garde si applicable, réconciliation et règlement Market (si applicable), documents comptables, absence d'écart non soldé.

### Variantes intégrées au même moteur
- Client individuel / liste partagée figée / deux sessions concurrentes.
- Paiement réussi, échoué, expiré, callback dupliqué/désordonné, annulation et remboursement.
- Stock limité et 2 achats simultanés ; divergence réservation / commande payée.
- KM/CM/CG, devise/prix/catalogue/français/relai, desktop et mobile ; ne promettre un PSP ou provider L6 que si sandbox réellement accessible.
- PO groupées/partielles, manque fournisseur, réception Hub partielle, incident douane, colis endommagé, échec document, retrait non autorisé.

## Matrice documentaire obligatoire et agent responsable
| Transition | Justificatif à contrôler | Source/autorité | Si absence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paiement confirmé | facture B2C PDF privée (après événement confirmé) | documents + orders | BLOQUANT, diagnostic Finance/Documents |
| Remboursement confirmé (variante) | avoir / reçu remboursement privé | refunds/documents | BLOQUANT |
| PO créée | PO persistée + représentation B2B si disponible | purchasing | agent Achats : vérifier génération/export ; ne pas inventer un PDF |
| Fournisseur confirmé/payé | référence fournisseur + preuve de débit + accusé/facture si disponible | purchasing/provider | agent Achats : récupérer/rapprocher ; contrôle manuel traçable |
| Fournisseur expédie | fulfillment / tracking + BL ou preuve transport **si fournie** | provider/purchasing | agent Achats ou Logistique : demander pièce, tracer absence |
| Hub reçoit | réception physique horodatée/quantités/agent + preuve de réception | Hub | agent Hub : contrôle réel, écart/réserve, BLOQUANT si absent |
| Douane/transit | déclaration / facture douane / justificatif transport selon exigibilité | logistics/customs | transitaire : rapprocher ou déclarer manquant |
| Relais reçoit | scan / statut réception physique réel | Relay | agent relais : contrôle, anomalie si non reçu |
| Client retire | scan de retrait autorisé + `pickup_proof` si émis | Relay/documents | agent relais : corriger ou signaler |
| Finance clôture | rapprochements coûts/règlement/cash, pièces nécessaires | Finance | comptable : investigation ouverte, aucun faux vert |

**Statuts documentaires** : `NON_DU`, `ATTENDU`, `DISPONIBLE_A_VERIFIER`, `VERIFIE`, `CONTROLE_MANUEL_REQUIS`, `MANQUANT_BLOQUANT` (projection de recette, pas cycle métier parallèle). Pour chaque pièce : événement déclencheur, exigibilité selon market/provider, source canonique, référence/URL authentifiée ou identifiant, horodatage, acteur, hash si disponible, verdict, raison d'absence, tâche agent / preuve d'intervention ; `non applicable` ne vaut pas `verifié`. Ne jamais fabriquer de PDF externe, de BL ou de facture fournisseur.

## Lots de livraison (PRs petites, gouvernées)
- [ ] **A — accès / cadrage** : menu admin Canonical → /admin/golden-e2e avec vérification des droits, scénario client réel distinct du parcours synthétique de frontière ; rendre visibles le market et les niveaux de preuve L0–L6.
- [ ] **B — client Playwright / humain** : réutiliser E2E boutique+OTP+checkout+partage, sessions clients et vrais écrans ; opérateur vérifie la continuité, sans injection directe de commande payée.
- [ ] **C — documents** : projection read-only par fil/order/PO : document source, éligibilité, statut, URL privée autorisée, responsable d'une preuve fournisseur absente ; distinguer B2C et B2B.
- [ ] **D — terrain** : cliquer sur les **actions réelles** avec rôle agent Hub/transitaire/relais (ou simulator non-prod explicitement étiqueté) ; pas de mutation depuis un écran de projection ni bypass de permissions.
- [ ] **E — verdict de certification** : `VERT` uniquement si preuves backend canoniques + documents obligatoires + étapes automatiques réellement exécutées + validations humaines + absence d'incident bloquant ; `NON EXECUTE`/mock/staging absent restent visibles, aucun faux vert.
- [ ] **F — scénarios négatifs et marchés** : concurrence, remboursements, webhooks, plusieurs marchés, mobile, documents conditionnels, rapport exportable et liens vers vraies interfaces.

## Garde-fous / définition de fini
- **Playwright avant humain** : l'humain joue d'abord le client (catalogue→OTP→paiement→confirmation), puis l'agent aux seules frontières physiques autorisées. La suite du client après paiement est essentiellement notification et suivi, pas clic forcé.
- Aucun reset destructif ; fixture dédiée, environnement isolé ; aucun achat/fonds réels ; aucun accès client à une pièce B2B ou fuite inter-market.
- Tests L3 mockés != L4 réel navigateur+serveur+DB != L5 staging != L6 prestataire sandbox. Afficher ces niveaux explicitement.
- Un `golden-create` ne remplace pas un vrai checkout ; les 10 étapes actuelles restent utiles comme **sous-recette**.
- S'assurer que les anomalies cash collections / statut shipping décrites par l'audit historique sont vérifiées sur main et corrigées si encore présentes.
- Avant modifications : `npm run agent:context -- --pack ui --feature dashboard`, `npm run agent:context -- --pack service --feature documents`, `npm run arch:impact -- ...`, tests ciblés, **`npm run pr:preflight` vert avant chaque PR**, CI et merge selon `AGENTS.md`.
- Terminé seulement quand une commande issue du navigateur traverse les vraies frontières jusqu'au retrait/clôture, que les documents sont consultables sous permissions correctes ou qu'un contrôle agent explicite résout leur absence, et que le verdict refuse tout faux vert.

## Amendement P0 — Sourcing et Raffinerie obligatoires avant la vraie boutique (13/10/2026)

La Golden complète ne démarre **jamais** d'un produit artificiellement injecté dans le catalogue. Chaîne requise : SOURCE FOURNISSEUR → SOURCING RÉUSSI → RAFFINERIE RÉUSSIE → REMISE AU CATALOGUE → PUBLICATION ET VENDABILITÉ MARKET → VRAIE BOUTIQUE → CLIENT → ACHAT → FOURNISSEUR → LIVRAISON → CLÔTURE.

Le sourcing et la raffinerie peuvent avoir déjà eu lieu avant l'ouverture du navigateur ; la Golden doit alors vérifier leurs faits persistés, leur identité et leur provenance. Un parcours acheté sur un produit préexistant est une certification partielle, et pas une certification complète de la source au client.

### Quatre preuves bloquantes

- SOURCE_PROVED : source réelle identifiée, capture/observation fraîche, identité exacte Offer/Unit/SOI, et passage sourcing réellement attesté, pas un seed.

- REFINERY_PROVED : passage et résultat réels, contrôles qualité et données produit/variantes/images, décisions de rejet ou d'acceptation journalisées, pas de bypass.

- CATALOG_RELEASE_PROVED : remise au catalogue par l'owner, SKU/variante exacts, publication et vendabilité Market, prix/devise/relais corrects, observés dans la boutique réelle.

- CUSTOMER_ORDER_PROVED : filiation jusqu'aux order_items et purchase_lines/PO, correspondance exacte product_sku_id et supplier_unit_ref/SOI, aucune substitution de SKU similaire.

### Cockpit et tests

Ajouter des étapes et des liens directs Sourcing → Raffinerie → Catalogue → Produit 360 → Boutique → Commande → PO fournisseur ; exposer verdict et preuve propre à chaque frontière. Rejeter une Golden complète si preuve absente, produit seed direct, raffinerie non attestée, publication simulée ou SKU/SOI divergente. Cas négatifs : source inconnue, article rejeté, stock/prix évoluant après sourcing, Market non publié, concurrence et replay. Ne pas relancer du sourcing pour chaque achat : proposer une exécution contrôlée séparée pour certifier la source au client avec vrais faits persistant sur environnement isolé. Réutiliser les propriétaires Sourcing, Raffinerie/Catalogue, Purchasing sans créer une vérité parallèle. Aucun achat, publication externe ou paiement live sans autorisation.

## Décision — Assainissement préalable des produits de test
Avant une Golden source→client, inventorier les produits actuellement créés directement par les tests ou seeds Sourcing, en distinguant environment, market_id, product_id/SKU, provenance et liens avec commandes/PO/paiements. Ne JAMAIS effectuer de DELETE global ni de RESET, ni toucher à la production. En DB éphémère dédiée de recette, retirer seulement les fixtures identifiées explicitement, via les services propriétaires et le mécanisme de nettoyage approprié ; si un produit a des liens métiers ou historique, le désactiver/écarter de la Golden plutôt que le supprimer. Vérifier les FK et le nombre avant/après, conserver les sources et traces d'audit. Dans la Golden, la liste de produits éligibles doit être vide au départ puis peuplée exclusivement par un sourcing réel + passage raffinerie + publication Catalogue attestés. Fournir d'abord inventaire et dry-run chiffré pour validation avant toute action destructive ; aucune suppression exécutée par la présente issue.

source_text:
Schedule Trigger runs daily workflows twice on DST fall-back night (Europe/Berlin)
### Bug Description

On 25 Oct 2026 the clocks in Germany went back (03:00 CEST to 02:00 CET). Every daily Schedule Trigger I have at 03:xx ran twice, one hour apart:
- Days interval at 03:00: 01:00:58Z and 02:00:58Z
- Days interval at 03:45: 01:45:57Z and 02:45:57Z
- cron `0 15 3 * * *`: 01:15:00Z and 02:15:00Z

The first run falls in the repeated hour (the second 02:xx), the second one is the real 03:xx. All 8 of my daily triggers at 03:xx did this, in interval and in cron mode. A daily trigger at 02:45 ran once, and the triggers at 04:xx and the hourly ones ran normally. Both runs have mode trigger and the same seconds offset.

I run the legacy scheduler (N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED not set), which uses cron 4.4.0 with luxon 3.7.2. My image is the official one plus a few patched OS and npm packages (not cron or luxon). This looks like the same bug as:
- https://github.com/kelektiv/node-cron/issues/1087 (see the comment from 4 Oct about daily jobs in the hour after the repeated hour)
- https://github.com/nestjs/schedule/issues/2389 (same double run, same date and timezone, cron 4.4.0)
cron 4.4.0 is still the latest stable release, so there's no fixed version to upgrade to yet. The comment on kelektiv/node-cron#1087 also shows this for America/New_York with daily jobs at 02:xx. US clocks go back on 1 Nov 2026.

Workaround: I moved the jobs where a second run hurts to 04:xx.

### To Reproduce

1. Self-hosted n8n with GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Europe/Berlin and TZ=Europe/Berlin, N8N_SCHEDULER_ENABLED not set.
2. Activate a workflow with a Schedule Trigger that runs daily at 03:00.
3. Let it run through a DST fall-back night (or fake the clock).
4. On 25 Oct 2026 it ran at 01:00Z and again at 02:00Z.

### Expected behavior

One run per day, at 03:00 local time (02:00Z on 25 Oct).

`tools/sourcing_data/mfr_aliases.json` lets a supplier's manufacturer name stand for the library's. [VULNERABILITY] Medium: Unclamped one-sided re-entry tick range in RevertHookAutoLendActions triggers InvalidTick and drops automation triggers near tick bounds (revert-finance/v4lend)
# [VULNERABILITY] Medium: Unclamped one-sided re-entry tick range in RevertHookAutoLendActions triggers InvalidTick and drops automation triggers near tick bounds (revert-finance/v4lend)

### Target Information
- **Repository**: `revert-finance/v4lend`
- **Impacted Files**: `src/hook/RevertHookAutoLendActions.sol` (lines 411–446), `src/shared/planning/AutoLendLib.sol` (lines 13–36)
- **Component**: AutoLend One-Sided Re-Entry Planning & Tick Normalization
- **Severity**: Medium ($1,500 ~ $2,500 USDC / Cantina Audit Tier)
- **Settlement Wallet**: `0x3a5E08708dd1CF22AAe94f913Ab69b17b80a3dC5` (Base / EVM USDC)

---

### Executive Summary
When `AutoLendLib.planOneSidedReentry` plans a new one-sided Uniswap v4 position when `addToExisting == false`, it computes the new tick boundaries by adding or subtracting `tickSpacing` and `tickWidth` relative to `baseTick`. 

In `AutoRangeLib.plan` (following the fix in `V4LE-74`), all planned ticks are strictly clamped against `TickMath.minUsableTick(tickSpacing)` and `TickMath.maxUsableTick(tickSpacing)`. However, `RevertHookAutoLendActions._processLendWithdraw` takes `plan.newTickLower` and `plan.newTickUpper` without normalization or boundary clamping and passes them directly to `_mintPosition`.

When `_calculateLiquidityForRange` calls `TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick(newTickUpper)`, if `newTickUpper > TickMath.MAX_TICK` (or exceeds the pool's usable tick range), `TickMath` reverts. Because this occurs inside `_processLendWithdraw` after the swap callback has already popped the trigger from the active trigger list, the trigger is permanently consumed and destroyed while the position remains stranded out of range.

---

### Technical Vulnerability Details

#### 1. Unclamped Boundary Tick Computation in `AutoLendLib`
In `src/shared/planning/AutoLendLib.sol` (lines 27–33):
    if (isToken0) {
        newTickLower = baseTick + tickSpacing;
        newTickUpper = newTickLower + tickWidth;
    } else {
        newTickUpper = baseTick - tickSpacing;
        newTickLower = newTickUpper - tickWidth;
    }

When market price approaches the edge of the allowable tick space (e.g. during extreme volatility or in wide-tick pools), `newTickUpper` can exceed `TickMath.MAX_TICK` (887272) or `TickMath.maxUsableTick(tickSpacing)`. Similarly, `newTickLower` can fall below `TickMath.MIN_TICK` (-887272).

#### 2. Trigger Drop and Revert in `_processLendWithdraw`
In `src/hook/RevertHookAutoLendActions.sol` (lines 420–445):
    _mintPosition(
        plan.poolKey,
        plan.newTickLower,
        plan.newTickUpper,
        liquidity,
        ...
    );

Uniswap v4 requires that `minUsableTick <= tickLower < tickUpper <= maxUsableTick`. If `newTickUpper` violates this invariant, `TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick` reverts unconditionally.

Because `RevertHookCallbacks._afterSwap` removes the position from the active trigger list before executing `_dispatchAutomationAction`, the failed re-entry permanently destroys the trigger. The position's capital is permanently stranded out of the pool with no re-entry trigger scheduled.

---

### Impact & Blast Radius
- **Permanent Automation Trigger Destruction**: Positions configured in volatile pairs or wide-tick pools that trigger near tick bounds suffer irreversible trigger loss.
- **Stranded Capital**: The position fails to re-enter the AMM, stopping fee generation and requiring manual intervention by the position owner.

---

### Remediation Diff

Enforce tick boundary clamping in `RevertHookAutoLendActions._processLendWithdraw`:

In `src/hook/RevertHookAutoLendActions.sol`:
    --- a/src/hook/RevertHookAutoLendActions.sol
    +++ b/src/hook/RevertHookAutoLendActions.sol
    @@ -420,6 +420,13 @@ abstract contract RevertHookAutoLendActions is RevertHookExecution {
                 int24 tickSpacing = poolKey.tickSpacing;
    +            int24 minTick = TickMath.minUsableTick(tickSpacing);
    +            int24 maxTick = TickMath.maxUsableTick(tickSpacing);
    +            if (plan.newTickLower < minTick) plan.newTickLower = minTick;
    +            if (plan.newTickUpper > maxTick) plan.newTickUpper = maxTick;
    +            if (plan.newTickLower >= plan.newTickUpper) revert InvalidTickRange();

---

Selling wholesale on Shopify: how do you notice when a B2B buyer stops reordering?
For those selling wholesale or B2B on Shopify: how do you catch a regular buyer who has quietly stopped ordering? 
 Shopify B2B covers companies, catalogs and payment terms, but I haven’t found anything built in that flags “this account usually orders every 3 weeks and it’s been 7”. What I mostly see is someone exporting orders now and then, sorting by last order date and emailing whoever looks late, which tends to slip on busy weeks. 
 Disclosure: I build n8n automations for Shopify B2B, and while testing a reorder reminder two things surprised me: 
 
 A fixed rule like “remind after 30 days” fits almost nobody. Buyers have very different rhythms, so using each buyer’s own typical gap between past orders worked much better. 
 Buyers whose last order hasn’t shipped yet should be skipped. A “time to reorder?” email while they’re still waiting for the last delivery looks careless. 
 
 Curious how others handle it: 
 
 Do you track reorder timing per buyer, or just by a fixed number of days? 
 Does the follow-up come from sales personally, or an automated email? 
 Has anyone found that a pre-filled “reorder the same items” link actually gets used by B2B buyers?

# BLOCK OWNER & ACCEPTANCE GATE — 2026-10-19

Single acceptance umbrella for all sub-issues in this project. **Do not treat the project as complete because upload/PO screens work or previous feature tickets are Done.** This parent should remain open until verified end-to-end.

## Business outcome

Supplier login → source file received under supplier scope → format recognized/AI-assisted one-time reviewed mapping → row validation + brand/line eligibility → exact Product/SKU matching → (existing) cost/availability/quantity offer update OR (new) ProductCandidate → reusable Brand/Line/Ingredient facts + trusted research + routine metadata + content/packshot/appropriate derived imagery → authorized final review, dedup and publish → linked SupplierOffer → Supplier PO confirmed/Ready with source and quantity truth. Independent audit covers skip/reject/review paths.

## Six milestones, in order

M0 code/test/security audit; M1 source-neutral intake and schema/row pipeline; M2 identity + offer consistency; M3 knowledge/product enrichment; M4 actual browser review/publish and supplier work; M5 cross-domain negative tests + real-export pilot. Linked subtasks define each gated deliverable. Block next phase until current stage evidence passes, but allow selective AI work independent of validated known-offer updates.

## Acceptance (all required)

* Exact supplier-scoped content dedup and correct **format fingerprint** vs Product/SKU fingerprint; versioned approved profile; unknown mapped semantic cost never auto-applies.
* Full and partial imports handle missing vs zero qty and price-only; incomplete full never mass-deactivates; old accepted POs intact.
* Known rows safely update only supplier offers, out-of-scope skip with reason, ambiguous size/variant reviewed, no duplicate product.
* Eligible new candidate acquires verified Product facts and reusable Brand/Line/Ingredient knowledge and formula-aware routine metadata, not invented medical claims or brand logos; source vs derived images clearly distinguished.
* Authorized review/publish creates exact Product/SKU and links supplier, not retail pricing automatically; results visible on storefront and sourcing when sellability/listing prerequisites satisfied.
* Real business UI, tenant isolation, retry/idempotency, concurrency, old-file and AI/media outage; actual DB evidence + signed QA.
* Synthetic tests are developer proof only; real file pilot from launch-relevant supplier software and owner approved mapping semantics required before production go/no-go.

## Execution protocol

Only ChatGPT/owner access Linear, not coding agents. One sequential repo/branch agent scope with clean git audit before touching files; read current code, reuse existing AI FastAPI/Prisma/NestJS/storage; no speculative rewrites, no new ERP integrations, no filler UI. After each stage: changed paths, tested commands/results, schema/API evidence, known blockers, safe restart instruction. No implicit "done" on report alone.

AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#1, AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#2, [GLO-75](https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-75/implement-product-ingestion-workflow-and-review-state), [GLO-77](https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-77/implement-product-candidate-review-and-publish-apis), [GLO-97](https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-97/implement-brand-productline-management-apis), AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#8–124, AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#90, AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#3, AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#93. Existing states are historic not end-to-end proof.

## Owner inputs that cannot be fabricated

Sanitized real export samples and exact header meaning per supplier; authoritative brand/line allowlist; supplier purchase-cost and discount rules; source license/verified brand logos, genuine product packshots; working research/media API keys and budget as verified from environment. Do not put keys into Linear or public logs. Claim external pilot BLOCKED until real data and approved semantics exist.

**AI image generation is DEFERRED, NOT a release/hard-gate blocker.** The Supplier + Product Knowledge pipeline must fully work without paid image generation. Required: verified exact product packshot/source image (or explicit missing-image editorial hold where identity evidence is insufficient), brand logo from authorized source, image storage/transformation, ingredient/Brand/Line facts, text, routine, and honest UI. Ingredient conceptual visuals/lifestyle illustrations are optional and can remain NOT_GENERATED. Choice of a specific model to be benchmarked and enabled only with explicit owner approval near/after production. All existing acceptance criteria about generated visuals are conditional on enabling that future capability; lack of optional generated visual cannot block catalog publication otherwise satisfying factual/media identity rules.

Owner asked about cost-free/deferred image generation. MVP Gate requires the provider-neutral media workflow and **verified** packshot/logo/derived transformations; optional AI educational ingredient imagery, product lifestyle/editorial art and **paid Google/OpenAI provider activation** are DEFERRED until owner budget/production decision. API keys and paid image smoke tests are not prerequisites to close this block. All product fact/research/routine/content/media approval and storefront truthful publication remain required.
