How does the crowding out work here? I'm not being pedantic, I'm genuinely curious about the dynamics as you see them. My experience in the publishing
How does the crowding out work here? I'm not being pedantic, I'm genuinely curious about the dynamics as you see them. My experience in the publishing world is that there is already an infinite supply of writing. Lots of things serve as filters, some for better and some for worse, but ultimately the quality of the writing (however we define that) vs. the field is part of that filter. There is a competition for our limited little attention spans and finite waking hours, and writing better suited to our tastes tends to win out. I don't see how that dynamic changes with AI. If all writers have more or less equal access to AI, some writers will use it in ways that result in writing I enjoy more than others. Some won't use it at all and still write work I really like. The majority of people writing with or without AI, just as today, won't write stuff I really want to read. I don't know if I've ever read a piece of SEO-driven content marketing and thought it was particularly profound or that it made an impact on me. Or that I really had an inherently meaningful connection to the author. I sort of don't care if people generate 100x more of that sort of thing. It makes Google searches less effective, I guess? Or it may make my For You Page on Instagram less human-rich? I've read some nice poetry though. I usually go looking for it. There are a handful of authors I tend to like consistently. The overall volume of poetry published (it's quite a lot!) doesn't really have an effect on my preference for their work. If there was 1,000,000 times more poetry published because of AI, I don't think it would prevent me from seeking out new poems from writers/publishers/curators I like, nor would I probably really notice.

source_text:
Gamma roadmap: intelligent starter actions, multimodal documents, safe Excel, tool-first architecture
# Gamma architecture roadmap — tool-first, not reinventing the wheel

**Status:** Planned only. **Gate:** Complete controlled human Beta and document-retrieval validation before implementing Gamma. This issue is a durable planning record; it authorizes no changes to main, production, billing, or user data.

## Product principles
- Gemini remains the reasoning/orchestration brain. Understand intent in DE/FA/EN (extensible to more languages); use tools only when useful.
- Evidence priority: verified internal living archive and standards -> general reasoning -> public web where appropriate; preserve deterministic safety/standards verification, precise citations for verified claims, uncertainty on insufficient evidence.
- **Use -> Extend -> Build**: evaluate native ChatGPT/OpenAI capabilities, GitHub integrations/actions, established libraries and APIs before building bespoke implementations. Avoid duplicating PDF reading/summarization, OCR, Excel execution, document parsing, search, and file management.
- Review newly available tools and connector capabilities at implementation time against cost, security, privacy, vendor lock-in, quality, and maintenance. Do not assume a capability exists or is free until verified.
- Keep elevator.help technical assistance separate from the later commercial **Elevator Agent AI** supplier/parts marketplace. Provide a future handoff interface, not premature marketplace implementation.

## Six starter actions and expected behaviors
1. **Troubleshoot a fault**: ask manufacturer/model/fault code/context; optionally analyze photo/document; provide evidence-based, safety-conscious diagnostics.
2. **Search technical documentation**: retrieve relevant verified internal documentation first; provide grounded answer and citation where permitted; fallback appropriately.
3. **Ask about EN 81-20 / EN 81-50**: retrieve authoritative text, verify clause/numbers deterministically, fail closed on unverified normative claims.
4. **Plan shaft dimensions**: gather capacity, lift type, building constraints; provide clearly labeled preliminary guidance, not certified design.
5. **Send a photo**: inspect image, identify visible objects/labels and uncertainty; ask *what the user wants to do* (identify component, troubleshoot, find manual, find spare part, find supplier). Never infer unseen technical properties.
6. **Upload a document**: securely parse PDF/images/office files as supported, extract text/tables, summarize, answer user questions grounded in the uploaded file; ask intent when ambiguous.

## Proposed phased Gamma work
- **Gamma 1 — Intent and UX:** intelligent starter actions, intent router, follow-up questions, multilingual behavior, mobile scroll/input, clear answer feedback (like/dislike), observability. Reuse existing code.
- **Gamma 2 — Multimodal and documents:** photo analysis, PDF reading/summarization/Q&A, secure temporary uploads, consent for storage, per-user isolation, retention/deletion, size and rate limits, GDPR/privacy and cost budgets. No automatic ingestion of user uploads into shared/public archive.
- **Gamma 3 — Safe calculations:** run approved archived Excel calculation models and user-supplied spreadsheets in sandboxed, isolated execution; validated inputs, formulas, outputs, provenance, resource/time limits; never execute untrusted macros or arbitrary code. Use mature spreadsheet engines/libraries first.
- **Later:** validated Answer Catalog / canonical FAQs with versioned standard revalidation, quotas/metering and optional billing, My Elevator product finder. Supplier/spare-part sourcing remains a future Elevator Agent AI integration via an explicit tool contract.

## Acceptance / design gates
- Real-document end-to-end Living Archive test before Gamma.
- Human Beta test set: technical fault cases, verified standard clauses, ordinary conversational follow-ups, DE/FA/EN, mobile login and Google OAuth, performance/security/cost.
- For each new feature: inventory existing OpenAI/ChatGPT, GitHub, Gemini, Cloudflare and OSS tools; choose use/extend/build with rationale, measured costs and security review; add offline regression tests and production smoke checks.

source_text:
String .toDate() returns the previous day for a date-only ISO string west of UTC
### Bug Description

`String.toDate()` returns the day **before** the one written when the string is a date-only ISO date (`"2023-06-16"`) and the n8n process runs west of UTC (any `America/*` time zone, for example).

`toDate()` parses with `Date.parse()`, which reads a date-only ISO string as **UTC** midnight, and then forces "00:00h" with `date.setHours(0, 0, 0)`, which works on the **local** fields. In `America/New_York`, `2023-06-16T00:00Z` is `2023-06-15 20:00` local, so `setHours(0, 0, 0)` lands on `2023-06-15 00:00` local. East of UTC (and in UTC) the local day already matches, so the bug only shows up for instances west of UTC.

Other date-only forms such as `"June 16, 2023"` parse as local midnight and are not affected.

The same code is in `packages/workflow/src/extensions/string-extensions.ts` and its mirror in `@n8n/expression-runtime`.

### To Reproduce

1. Run n8n with `TZ=America/New_York` (or `GENERIC_TIMEZONE`/system time zone west of UTC).
2. Evaluate `{{ "2023-06-16".toDate().toDateString() }}` in an expression.
3. You get `Thu Jun 15 2023`.

Minimal Node reproduction of the same steps:

```sh
TZ=America/New_York node -e 'const d = new Date(Date.parse("2023-06-16")); d.setHours(0, 0, 0); console.log(d.toString())'
# Thu Jun 15 2023 00:00:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time)
```

### Expected behavior

`Fri Jun 16 2023`: local midnight of the day that was written, in every time zone.

### Debug Info

Found by reading the code on `master`, and reproduced with a unit test that calls `stringExtensions.functions.toDate` directly with `process.env.TZ = 'America/New_York'`.

### Operating System

Ubuntu Linux

### n8n Version

master (current HEAD)

### Node.js Version

20.19.2

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
I'm curious how people on HN are using AI day to day, and came up with a list of questions I thought could be interesting to know. No need to answer every question of course, just wanted to get a gut feel how people are using AI. 1) What AI subscriptions are you personally paying for? (Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Cursor, etc) - Which tiers? - Have you purchased multiple subscriptions from the same provider (eg two Claude accounts)? 2) Are you using models outside (or instead) of those subscriptions? For example, pay-as-you-go APIs, OpenRouter, or locally hosted models. - Which models and providers? 3) What coding harnesses and interfaces are you using? Are you sticking with the default CLIs or IDE integrations, or using alternatives like OpenCode, Pi, Aider, Muse Code, or custom-built harnesses? - What made you switch harnesses (if you switched)? 4) Are you using any agent orchestration or swarm tools? - For example, Munder Difflin, Gas Town, Ruflo, or something custom. 5) Are you using broader agent platforms like OpenClaw / Hermes Agent / Grok bot / Dots / Muse? - If you are using them, what are your main use cases? ----- I know my workflow has differed significantly from a year ago, and so it would be interesting to capture a snapshot today of what people are using and why.

source_text:
Spec: carlab.rs polish around two touchpoints, parts-sourcing case studies, incremental builds and cross-site debts
## Problem Statement

carlab.rs now has its own parts catalogue (PR #357), but the site around it was built before the catalogue existed and has gathered loose ends:

- A visitor comes for one of two things: to book the car service, or to find a part. The homepage and the site structure do not put both paths in front of them with equal weight, and neither path is tuned to end in a contact.
- The visual language drifts: inputs are slightly rounded while buttons are full pills, icons sit on some submit buttons and not on others (#37).
- CarLab now sources parts for customers, but there is no way to show a successful parts-sourcing job as a case study: "parts sourcing" is not a CarLab service, and a case study (Work) cannot name the parts it used.
- Several small defects and debts are open across the three sites: "My garage" remembers VINs the shop could not resolve (#430), wrong price and Serbian on live approved.rs and CarLab case studies (#279), em dashes and Ё in source copy (#278), trust boundaries still without zod (#38), `llms.txt` never audited and no agent catalogue (#285), no social links (#39), the Offer cart and checkout logic spread across routes (#388, #389, #390).
- Every carlab.rs build re-renders every page even when one Part changed, and the real Vercel build of the catalogue was never measured (#380, #40).
- The local-SEO keyword method was only applied to carlab.rs (#268).

## Solution

One pass that leaves carlab.rs coherent and the three sites tidy:

- carlab.rs is restructured around two first touchpoints with equal weight, service booking and part search, each ending in a contact, and a part search leads naturally to booking its installation. The current visual style stays and is polished into consistent rules (one radius scale, one button style, icons only where a button navigates).
- Parts sourcing (the existing VIN parts inquiry) becomes a CarLab service with its own page. A Parts sourcing case study is drafted from a completed shop Order with one button in the shop admin, lists the Parts that Order sourced, and shows its total; Work pages link to those Part pages and Part pages show the Works that used them.
- A shop Order becomes completed when staff mark its Lead won in the CRM bot; ❌ lost in the bot and a cancel in the shop admin cancel each other (ADR-0053).
- A Part that cannot be bought at once shows «Заказать», which opens a Parts inquiry with the owner's wording; every Part shows its supplier photos, or its Category's picture when the supplier has none.
- The listed defects and debts are fixed.
- carlab.rs builds incrementally: a page whose data did not change is not re-rendered; the first real Vercel build is measured.
- approved.rs and details.rs get the corrected keyword research and copy review.

Tickets folded into this spec: #430, #380, #279, #388, #389, #390, #289 (rescoped: polish, not a redesign), #37, #278, #268, #285, #39, #38, #40, plus the new parts-sourcing case studies. Each item below is marked [feature] or [bug].

## User Stories

Site structure and design (#289, #37) [feature]

1. As a driver who needs a repair, I want to see on the first screen of carlab.rs that I can book the service, so that I do not have to hunt for it.
2. As a driver looking for a part, I want the search box on the first screen and in the header of every page (a field on desktop, an icon on phones), so that I can type a VIN, a part number, a name or my car right away.
3. As a visitor on a phone, I want both paths visible without scrolling past marketing copy, so that I reach what I came for in one tap.
4. As a service visitor, I want each service page to show what the service includes, how long it takes and how to book, so that I can decide and book on the spot.
5. As a parts visitor who found a part, I want to see its price or «Заказать», each with a clear next step, so that I know how to get it.
6. As a parts visitor, I want to book the installation of the part I found in the same flow, so that I get the part fitted without a second enquiry.
7. As any visitor, I want the contact options (form, Telegram, WhatsApp, Viber, phone on touch devices) at the end of every path, so that leaving a contact is always one step away.
8. As the owner, I want every path to end in a contact, so that no visit leaves without a way to follow up.
9. As a visitor, I want inputs, buttons and cards to share one radius scale and one button style, so that the site looks deliberate.
10. As a visitor, I want arrow icons only on buttons that take me somewhere, not on buttons that submit a form, so that buttons say what they do (#37).
11. As the owner, I want the design kept in its current style and only polished, so that the brand stays recognisable.
12. As a details.rs visitor, I want the same button rule on details.rs, so that the sister site follows it too (#37 covers both).

Parts sourcing and case studies [feature]

13. As the owner, I want Parts sourcing («Подбор запчастей», today's VIN parts inquiry) to be a CarLab service with its own service page, so that it is sold like the other services.
14. As staff, I want a «Сделать кейс» button on a completed Order in the shop admin, so that a case study starts from a real deal.
15. As staff, I want the button to create an unpublished draft Work in Keystatic with the Order's car (make, model, year), its Parts (brand and number, several of them) and its total in RSD already filled in, so that I only write the story and add photos.
16. As staff, I want the draft committed with my own Keystatic login, so that the shop server never holds a key that can change the repository.
17. As a customer, I want my VIN, name and contact never to reach a case study, so that my deal can be shown without exposing me.
18. As staff, I want the draft's data copied once and editable in Keystatic afterwards, so that the case does not change when the shop does.
19. As staff, I want the button only on completed Orders, so that a case study is always a deal that happened.
20. As a visitor reading a Parts sourcing case, I want each listed Part to link to its Part page when it has one, and to show its brand and number otherwise, so that I can order the same Parts.
21. As a visitor on a Part page, I want to see the case studies where we sourced that Part, so that I trust we have done it before.
22. As a visitor, I want the case to show the price the customer paid, so that I can judge what sourcing costs.
23. As a visitor reading a Parts sourcing case, I want its enquiry form to be about Parts sourcing, so that my enquiry reaches the right person.
24. As the owner, I want Parts sourcing cases translated to sr and en like every Work, and the service in `llms.txt`, the sitemap and the service list, so that every locale, search engine and agent finds them.

Completed orders [feature]

25. As staff, I want marking an Order's Lead ✅ won in the CRM bot to complete the Order in the shop, so that I mark a deal in one place.
26. As staff, I want ❌ lost in the bot to cancel the Order, and cancelling the Order in the shop admin to mark its Lead lost, so that the two never show different outcomes.
27. As staff, I want a status change that could not reach the other side to be retried, so that the bot and the shop end up in step.

Part cards [feature]

28. As a visitor looking at a Part that cannot be bought at once (no Offer yet, or the shop still in closed beta), I want a «Заказать» button instead of «Цена по запросу» or «Узнать цену», so that I can act on it.
29. As that visitor, I want «Заказать» to tell me plainly that the shop is new, works directly with the best suppliers to get good prices, that this number is most likely available but needs checking, and that they will buy it or offer an equivalent once I leave a contact, so that I know what happens next.
30. As a visitor on any Part page, I want «Установить у нас», with the installation price shown where it is set, so that I can have the Part fitted.
31. As a visitor, I want every Part to show a picture: the supplier's photos where they exist, otherwise the Category's picture marked as an illustration, so that no Part looks empty and no Part shows a wrong photo.

Small defects [bug]

32. As a visitor whose VIN the shop could not resolve, I want "My garage" not to remember that VIN, so that the site does not show me a car it cannot match (#430).
33. As a visitor whose VIN resolved, I want "My garage" to keep remembering it, so that I do not retype it.
34. As an approved.rs visitor, I want the bmw-x1-2 case to show 47,000 EUR everywhere, so that the price is consistent (#279).
35. As a Serbian reader, I want the four wrong Serbian phrases in the approved.rs and CarLab cases fixed, so that the text reads correctly (#279).

Copy hygiene (#278) [feature]

36. As the owner, I want no em dash and no Ё in the Russian source copy of the three sites, so that the copy does not read as machine-written.
37. As the owner, I want a check that fails when an em dash or Ё is added to Russian source copy, so that it does not come back.
38. As a content editor using the content skill, I want the rules written into the skill, so that new copy follows them.

Agents and search (#285, #268) [feature]

39. As an AI agent, I want each site's `llms.txt` to follow the format (title, summary, grouped links, a bounded size), so that I can read the site efficiently.
40. As an AI agent, I want carlab.rs's catalogue entries in `llms.txt` to fit the budget, or the overflow to be a recorded choice, so that the file stays usable as the catalogue grows.
41. As an AI agent, I want `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` on all three sites, so that I can discover what each site offers.
42. As the owner, I want approved.rs and details.rs keyword research done with the corrected method, so that their meta copy targets what people search for.

Social links (#39) [feature]

43. As a visitor, I want to find each brand's social accounts somewhere more visible than the footer, so that I can follow the brand.
44. As the owner, I want the account links to be configuration per brand, so that I can add them when I send them.
45. As the owner, I want a social link not to count as a contact click, so that contact analytics stay clean.

Trust boundaries (#38) [feature]

46. As the owner, I want every remaining trust boundary listed in #38 validated with zod, so that bad input fails loudly instead of slipping through a cast.

Shop internals (#388, #389, #390) [feature]

47. As a developer, I want one reader for Offer cart and order lines, so that line metadata is typed once.
48. As a developer, I want the Offer cart operations behind one module, so that each store cart route is validation plus one call.
49. As a developer, I want checkout to go through one entry point and a pure judge, so that every refusal is decided in one place and unit-tested.
50. As a shopper, I want the cart and checkout to behave exactly as today, so that the refactor changes nothing I see.

Builds (#40, #380) [feature]

51. As the owner, I want carlab.rs to skip re-rendering pages whose data did not change, so that a Publish after a small catalogue change builds fast.
52. As the owner, I want a layout or config change to still rebuild everything, so that incremental builds never serve stale markup.
53. As the owner, I want the first real Vercel production build of the catalogue measured (time, output size), so that we know the margin to the limits.
54. As the owner, I want approved.rs and details.rs build times measured before deciding on incremental builds there, so that we adopt it only where it pays.

## Implementation Decisions

Structure and design (#289, #37)

- The homepage, header and service/part flows are reworked around two equal entry points: service booking and the one search box (`<catalogue-search>`, #428). On phones the search comes first with the services and «Записаться» right under it, both on the first screen. The header carries the search as a field on desktop and as an icon on phones on every page. Both paths end in the existing contact controls and lead form; no new contact mechanism.
- A Part page offers booking its installation where the Part has an installation price, reusing the existing installation data and the lead form with the service the installation maps to.
- The visual polish stays inside carlab.rs's own design system: one radius scale and one button style defined as the app's tokens (never in `packages/site-kit`, per AGENTS.md); which radius and whether buttons stay pills is the designer's call within the current style, as is the arrow rule for buttons (#37, also on details.rs) and where the social links sit (#39).
- Design goes through the `ui-designer` agent and the `frontend-design` skill, mobile first; the parked six-direction redesign is not resumed.

Parts sourcing case studies

- Parts sourcing is the existing `vin-parts-inquiry` service (Glossary: Parts sourcing), promoted into `SERVICE_SLUGS_BY_BRAND.carlab` with its label in `@podbor/brands`, so it gets a service page, appears in the Keystatic multiselect and can be a Work's `servicesApplied`. `parts-order` stays the Lead service of shop Orders.
- The Work schema gains optional sourced Parts (Brand name and part number, normalised with the catalogue contract) and an optional price in RSD shown only on Parts sourcing works; the Keystatic form gets matching fields; neither is translated.
- A completed Order's card in the shop admin gets «Сделать кейс». It opens a page on carlab.rs beside Keystatic (the approved.rs case-photo pattern) that fetches a privacy-filtered summary of that Order from the shop (car as make, model and year; Brand-numbers; total in RSD; never VIN, name or contact) and commits an unpublished draft Work with the staff member's Keystatic GitHub login. The shop holds no repository write token. The draft is a one-time copy; the site build never reads the Order.
- At build time each listed Part resolves against the catalogue snapshot: a Part with a page renders as a link through `PathBuilder`, anything else as brand and number text. Part pages list the Works that reference their Brand-numbers. A missing shop or catalogue never breaks a Work page.
- A Parts sourcing Work's closing lead form posts the Parts sourcing service.

Completed orders (ADR-0053)

- Marking a `parts-order` Lead won in the CRM bot completes its shop Order (picked up and paid); there is no completion from the shop side.
- Lost in the bot cancels the Order; cancelling the Order in the shop admin marks its Lead lost.
- The bot reaches the shop through an authenticated admin route and the shop reaches the bot through the Lead route it already uses; a failed call is retried so the two converge. Glossary: Completed order.

Part cards and images

- Wherever a Part cannot be bought at once (no Offer, or `SHOP_OPEN` unset), the price block shows «Заказать», opening the Parts inquiry form with the owner's copy (new shop, direct work with the best suppliers, availability checked, this Part bought or an equivalent offered, leave a contact). Russian source copy only; the translate job fills sr and en.
- Every Part page offers «Установить у нас», showing the installation price where the Part has one.
- A Part with no supplier photo shows its Category's picture marked as an illustration; supplier photos stay first wherever they exist.

Defects

- #430: the rule "remember only a VIN the shop resolved" lives in one place, inside the site-kit "My garage" element or the code that knows the VIN resolved; site-kit stays at 100% coverage and any site using the element gets the rule.
- #279: price set to 47,000 EUR in the case's structured price and in the FAQ; the four Serbian fixes are hand translations committed on their own, never with a Russian edit (AGENTS.md).

Copy (#278)

- Em dashes and Ё are removed from the Russian source copy of all three sites with the content skill; `translations` blocks and structured fields are not hand-edited (the translate job refreshes them).
- The content skill gains the em-dash and no-Ё rules.
- A check in the `check` job fails on an em dash or Ё in Russian source copy (i18n YAML and Work/case Russian fields), alongside the existing YAML validity check.

Agents and SEO (#285, #268)

- `llms.txt` of all three sites is audited against the format; carlab.rs's catalogue entries fit the budget or the overflow is written down as a choice.
- `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` is served on all three sites through one shared helper next to the shared `llms.txt` renderer, each site supplying its data.
- WebMCP is not part of this spec (#431).
- #268 is an owner task: it needs live Keyword Planner and Search Console access. The agent side is writing up the research per site and applying the agreed meta copy once the owner supplies the data.

Social links (#39)

- Account URLs are per-brand configuration; placement is decided in the design polish (more visible than the footer); social links never carry the contact-click attribute.

Trust boundaries (#38)

- Every open item in #38's register gets a zod schema at the boundary; schemas for browser code sit beside the browser module, not inside it, so zod does not enter the client bundle (AGENTS.md).

Shop internals (#388, #389, #390)

- One line reader types Offer cart and order line metadata (offer id, parent offer id, add-on kind, in stock, lead time) and the handoff state; add-ons link to their Part by the parent's Offer id; one readiness schema replaces the two copies; beta orders carrying both parent keys still render.
- The Offer cart becomes one module; each store cart route is request validation plus one call.
- Checkout has one entry point and a pure judge returning a refusal code or repriced lines; Medusa sits behind an adapter and Medusa's own completion route uses the same judge.
- These no longer wait for the shop to open: they change no behaviour.

Builds (#40, #380)

- carlab.rs turns on Astro's `experimental.incrementalBuild` (Astro 7.2). Every catalogue page (Part, Model, Vehicle, Model x Category, Category, make hubs) returns a `cacheKey` from `getStaticPaths` that is a digest of exactly the data the page renders, so an unchanged page is skipped and a changed one re-rendered. Astro already invalidates everything on a config, lockfile or module-graph change.
- `build.concurrency` stays at 1 (the cache is off above 1).
- CI persists Astro's cache directory between carlab.rs builds (an Actions cache keyed per branch), since `vercel build` runs on a fresh runner; an empty cache renders everything.
- The decision is recorded in an ADR, including how a stale cache is avoided.
- approved.rs and details.rs: CI build times are measured; incremental builds are adopted there only if the measurement shows a gain worth the `cacheKey` plumbing, and the decision is recorded in #40.
- #380: the first real Vercel production build of the catalogue is measured after the shop's first deploy and the result posted on #380.

## Testing Decisions

A good test drives the feature through its public interface and asserts what a caller sees: page data, element behaviour in the DOM, HTTP responses, stored rows and Leads, committed files. Never internal calls. Seven seams, all existing patterns:

1. Storefront page data through the catalogue snapshot, paths, sitemap and `llms.txt` tests: Works linking to Part pages and plain text for Parts without one, Part pages listing their Works, the Parts sourcing service in `llms.txt`/sitemap/service list, «Заказать» wherever a Part cannot be bought, the Category picture for a Part without photos, `cacheKey` stability (same data, same key; changed rendered data, new key), `ai-catalog.json`. Prior art: `catalogueSnapshot.test.ts`, `catalogue.test.ts`, `llmsTxt.test.ts`, `paths.test.ts`.
2. Browser elements under jsdom in `packages/site-kit` (100% coverage): "My garage" stores only a resolved VIN (#430).
3. Shop admin and store routes through `medusaIntegrationTestRunner`: the privacy-filtered Order summary behind «Сделать кейс» (no VIN, name or contact), completing and cancelling an Order when the bot asks, the shop marking the Lead lost on a cancel, and the cart and checkout refactors (#388-#390) with today's specs passing unchanged plus unit tests for every refusal code of the pure judge. Prior art: the offer-cart, checkout and carlab-orders specs.
4. Content schemas and copy: the content and i18n tests for the Work schema (sourced Parts, price) and the new service; the em-dash/Ё check with its own test; the YAML validity check. Prior art: `content.test.ts`, `.github/scripts/yaml-content-valid.ts`.
5. Design (#289, #37, #39 placement, header search): no automated tests; a `ui-designer` pass with mobile-first screenshots of the homepage, the header on phone and desktop, a service page, a Part page with «Заказать» and «Установить у нас», and a Parts sourcing Work.
6. The CRM bot's won and lost handlers in `packages/lead-crm` (100% coverage) with a stubbed shop: won completes the Order, lost cancels it, a failed call is retried, a non-Order Lead calls nothing. Prior art: the bot callback and `afterStatusChange` tests.
7. The carlab.rs route that commits the draft Work, against a stubbed GitHub and a stubbed shop summary: one unpublished Work file with car, Parts and RSD total, committed with the caller's Keystatic token, refused without one. Prior art: approved.rs's case-photo routes and `githubContents.ts` tests.

## Out of Scope

- Firing the shop funnel goals (`add_to_cart`, `begin_checkout`, `purchase`) and registering conversions (#384-#387): they ship with opening the shop (#382, #383).
- Opening the shop itself (#382, #383) and its legal blockers (#76, #79).
- On-demand rendering of catalogue pages (#423, deferred).
- WebMCP (#431).
- A full redesign or a new visual direction for carlab.rs (#289 is rescoped to polish).
- Collecting the social account URLs (the owner supplies them).

## Further Notes

- Grilled on 2026-10-30 (decisions recorded in GLOSSARY.md: Parts sourcing, Parts inquiry, Completed order; CONTEXT.md: Case study; ADR-0053).
- Owner decisions on 2026-10-30: #289 is polish of the current style around two touchpoints (service booking and part search) that both end in a contact; parts sourcing becomes a service and Works list sourced parts with two-way links; the funnel stays with opening the shop; #37 follows the design polish's button rule; social accounts exist and links come later.
- #268 needs the owner's Keyword Planner and Search Console access; #380's last step needs the shop's first production deploy.
- The folded tickets should be closed with a pointer to this spec once their part lands.

Junior Python LLM Bot Developer
I need a junior-level Python developer who is excited about building automation bots powered by both offline and online large-language models. The immediate task is to create bots that streamline routine processes for my company and then connect those bots seamlessly to our existing web apps, a couple of legacy desktop tools, and several cloud services we already use.  

You should already be comfortable spinning up SaaS-style back ends (FastAPI, Django, or a similar stack is fine) and have at least tinkered with frameworks such as LangChain, [login to view URL], or the OpenAI API so you can switch between local and hosted LLMs when needed. A solid grasp of common automation libraries—think Selenium, Playwright, PyAutoGUI, or REST hooks—will also make the work smoother.  

Deliverables I expect:  
• A working automation bot (or small fleet of bots) that can log in, collect data, act on it, and hand results back to our web, desktop, and cloud environments without manual intervention.  
• Clear, concise setup instructions and inline code comments so another developer can extend the project later.  
• A brief hand-off call or screen-share so I can see the bot in action and ask final questions.  

If you enjoy experimenting with LLM prompts, integrating APIs, and turning repetitive tasks into one-click workflows, you’ll be a great fit. Let me know what similar projects you’ve already built, especially any that bridged multiple platforms the way this one will.
Budget: ₹1500-12500 INR

[software-development-practices:nist-ssdf] github/gh-aw-firewall repository guidance Repository-observable SSDF controls for `github/gh-aw-firewall` are generally strong at commit `360f0f904b1824dbffa1288d8dee58db94e903ab`: pinned GitHub Actions, scheduled CodeQL/dependency/supply-chain scans, SBOM/cosign coverage for container images, and regression-oriented test gates are all present. The main evidence-backed gap is release integrity for non-container CLI assets: I found checksum validation for `awf-*` binaries and `awf.tgz`, but not a repo-observable signature or provenance verification path for those assets themselves. This review is advisory and non-binding; it does not prove security, compliance, certification, endorsement, or SSDF conformance. **Action:** Maintainer should assign this issue to Copilot to add signed or attested verification for CLI release assets and update installer/docs; accept when a release publishes verifiable signatures or provenance for `awf-*` binaries and `awf.tgz`, `install.sh` or setup paths validate them, and release documentation shows the verification flow. - Critical finding: container release integrity is stronger than CLI release integrity today (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, `docs/image-verification.md`, `install.sh`, `docs/releasing.md`). - Critical finding: repository-observable detection and prevention controls are broad and active in source (`.github/workflows/codeql.yml`, `dependency-audit.yml`, `supply-chain-scan.yml`, `test-coverage.yml`, `.github/dependabot.yml`). - Critical metric: 1 promoted backlog item met the threshold for an evidence-backed repository change in this run.
Agent prompt Implement a release-integrity improvement for `github/gh-aw-firewall` focused on SSDF PS.2.1 / PS.3.1 / PS.3.2. Requirements: 1. Extend the release pipeline so `awf-linux-x64`, `awf-linux-arm64`, `awf-darwin-x64`, `awf-darwin-arm64`, `awf-bundle.js`, and `awf.tgz` ship with verifiable signatures or provenance that is generated in CI and published with the release. 2. Update `install.sh` and any setup/install path that currently trusts only `checksums.txt` so it validates the new signature/provenance material before installation, while still failing closed on mismatches. 3. Update release/install docs to show how users verify the CLI assets, parallel to the existing container-image verification guidance. 4. Add or update focused tests that cover failure paths for tampered assets/metadata. 5. Keep existing container signing/SBOM behavior intact. Deliverables: - Workflow changes in `.github/workflows/release.yml` - Installer/setup changes (`install.sh`, `action.yml`, or both as needed) - Documentation updates (`docs/releasing.md`, `README.md`, `docs/image-verification.md` or a better-named CLI verification doc) - Tests proving the verification path fails closed
Assessment metadata, scope, and limitations ### Metadata - Target repository: `github/gh-aw-firewall` - Analyzed commit: `360f0f904b1824dbffa1288d8dee58db94e903ab` - Target snapshot source: local `target/` checkout plus bounded GitHub metadata reads - Source verification date: `2026-10-13` - Final SSDF baseline used: `NIST SP 800-218 Version 1.1 (final, February 2022)` - Official URLs: - `https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/ssdf` - `https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final` - `https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.800-218` - Machine-readable marker: - `` ### Scope and assumptions - Repository-observable review only: committed files in `target/` and bounded accessible GitHub metadata. - Assessed against the current final SSDF baseline above. The NIST SSDF project page also references `SP 800-218A` as a final SSDF community profile for generative AI and dual-use foundation models, but it augments `SP 800-218` and was **not** treated as a replacement baseline for this repository review. - Findings are risk-based and scoped to evidence visible in this repository snapshot; absence of repository evidence is **not** proof that an organizational control does not exist. ### Inaccessible or non-repository evidence - Branch protection / rulesets details were not readable with the available credential (`gh api repos/github/gh-aw-firewall/branches/main/protection` returned `403 Resource not accessible by personal access token`). - GitHub security feature state, private security alerts, secret-scanning alerts, advisories, internal training records, personnel/process evidence, and private incident-response artifacts were not assessed. - Workflow files provide evidence of intended controls, but this run did not establish historical execution success for every workflow.

MongoDB Chat Memory node doesn't set driverInfo, unlike the other MongoDB nodes
### Bug Description

The MongoDB Chat Memory node creates its `MongoClient` without `driverInfo`, so its connections don't identify themselves as n8n in the MongoDB connection handshake.

n8n's other MongoDB integrations already set this:

- The MongoDB node sets `driverInfo: { name: 'n8n_crud', version: <node version> }` in `packages/nodes-base/nodes/MongoDb/GenericFunctions.ts`.
- The MongoDB Atlas Vector Store node sets `driverInfo: { name: 'n8n_vector', version: <node version> }` in `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/vector_store/VectorStoreMongoDBAtlas/VectorStoreMongoDBAtlas.node.ts`.
- The MongoDB Chat Memory node, in `packages/@n8n/nodes-langchain/nodes/memory/MemoryMongoDbChat/MemoryMongoDbChat.node.ts`, only passes pool settings (`minPoolSize`, `maxPoolSize`, `maxIdleTimeMS`).

As a result, connections from the Chat Memory node can't be told apart from generic Node.js driver traffic in MongoDB Atlas, unlike connections from the other two nodes.

### To Reproduce

1. Create a workflow with a Chat Trigger connected to an AI Agent, then add a chat model and a MongoDB Chat Memory node using MongoDB credentials.
2. Send a chat message so the memory node opens a connection.
3. While the connection is open, run `db.currentOp(true)` in `mongosh` against the same deployment, and find the operation from n8n.
4. See that `clientMetadata.driver.name` is only `nodejs`, with no n8n entry.

### Expected behavior

As with the MongoDB and MongoDB Atlas Vector Store nodes, `clientMetadata.driver.name` should include an n8n entry for this node (for example `nodejs|n8n_memory`), and `clientMetadata.driver.version` should include the node version (for example `6.21.0|1.1`).

### Debug Info

Not available. This was found by reading the source on `master` (commit 4b5ea1de), and the same code ships in n8n@2.46.6. It applies regardless of environment.

### Operating System

macOS (Darwin 25.6.0); not environment-specific

### n8n Version

2.46.6

### Node.js Version

24.1.0

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted

Show HN: Koody for Business – AI bookkeeping for people who aren't accountants
Hi HN, I'm Hallie, founder of Koody. Today, I'm launching Koody for Business: AI-powered accounting, bookkeeping, and tax prep software for sole proprietors and small businesses. For years, I used accounting software for my business. I went into it to create invoices, categorize and reconcile transactions, and work with my accountant to prepare our books. I often dreaded having to do it. There were so many transactions to get through in a handful of different currencies, and I found the whole process draining. The software I used (and refuse to name) worked really well. It was capable accounting software, and I'm not trying to suggest otherwise. But for me, accounting had become a bit like going to the dentist. You know it's necessary and useful, but that doesn't stop you from feeling anxious about it or wishing you didn't have to go. What makes this personal is that I've always been good at accounting. Throughout secondary school, I was the best student in every financial accounting class. I was also the class prefect, so I would regularly collect everyone's homework and take it to the staff room for submission. My accounting teacher used to ask me to put mine on top because she used it as a marking guide. I then went on to study finance in undergrad and eventually earned an MBA. So accounting isn't an unfamiliar subject to me, yet dealing with my own books made me extremely sad and anxious. I'm building Koody for Business because I want business owners to see accounting through my original lens: something simple and enjoyable that doesn't require a degree to understand. Koody automatically categorizes business income and expenses and uses those transactions to produce cash flow insights, profit and loss reports, and records for Schedule C and tax prep. There are two workspaces: personal and business. The business workspace lets you manage your business finances separately from your personal finances, even when you use the same bank account for both, as many sole proprietors do. You can keep each transaction in the appropriate workspace, so personal spending stays out of your business reports. You can use Koody just for your business, just for your personal finances, or for both. Give Koody for Business a try at koody.com/business. I'd love to hear what you think.

TradeLink SEO automation — living project status, decisions and blockers
# Living project checkpoint: TradeLink SEO automation

_Last status checkpoint: 2026-10-16, late evening (Claude session, production-readiness pass). This issue is the canonical **working status** for future assistant/Claude handoffs. It is not authorization to publish. The detailed checkpoint is in the latest comment below._

## Objective and permanent operating rules
- Build a **real research-driven SEO agent** for TradeLink (`usetradelink.com`), combining Google Search Console, Semrush, verified competitor research and authentic TradeLink product facts.
- Prioritize **qualified traffic, conversions and measurable results**, not page count, keyword stuffing or AI-detection evasion.
- When authorized, the agent researches, audits, drafts, tests, proposes and creates PRs automatically. **Every public website change requires a new, specific human approval** before publication.
- Keep `PUBLISHING_ENABLED=false` until every step before step 15 of [`docs/ops/activation-checklist.md`](https://github.com/ThomasPeakBot/usetradelink/blob/claude/festive-lamport-7ttt72-release-automation/docs/ops/activation-checklist.md) is done.
- Never expose secrets, spend more API units, merge, or deploy public website changes without explicit authorization. **Semrush: no further billable requests.** Every path is now fail-closed (see #19).

## Evidence and review
- [Full-repository audit, issue #10](https://github.com/ThomasPeakBot/usetradelink/issues/10)
- Test results come from Claude's local runs (Postgres 16) **and** GitHub Actions CI.
- The **real-deployment check** (`deploy-verify`) runs on GitHub's runners against the actual Cloudflare preview of each PR.
- Railway, Slack, Search Console and live Semrush are **not** verified: Claude's sandbox cannot reach them.

## Release structure: merge only these, in order (all drafts, unmerged)
| PR | Contents | Base | Notes |
|----|-------|------|----|
| [#18](https://github.com/ThomasPeakBot/usetradelink/pull/18) | **Site release**: #13 + #15 + #17, plus real deployment verification and the Semrush MCP lock for assistants | `main` | **Changes the public site.** Merge after Cloudflare is switched to `_site` |
| [#19](https://github.com/ThomasPeakBot/usetradelink/pull/19) | **Automation release**: #8 + #9 + #11 + #12 + #16 on top of #18, the Semrush lockdown, engine fixes, campaign 1, activation checklist | #18 | Retarget to `main` after #18 |
| [#20](https://github.com/ThomasPeakBot/usetradelink/pull/20) | SEO proposal 1: one page answers "how to copy trade on Tradovate" (480/mo) | #18 | Content |
| [#21](https://github.com/ThomasPeakBot/usetradelink/pull/21) | SEO proposal 2: answer "how to copy trade on Topstep" (140/mo) | #18 | Content |
| [#22](https://github.com/ThomasPeakBot/usetradelink/pull/22) | SEO proposal 3: source and date `/futures-trade-copier/` (140/mo, KD 6) | #18 | Content |

#8, #9, #11, #12, #13, #15, #16 and #17 are fully contained in #18/#19; `git merge-base --is-ancestor` was checked for every head. Do not merge them separately. Close them once #18 and #19 are merged.

## Activation status (full ordered list: `docs/ops/activation-checklist.md`)
- **NEEDS MY APPROVAL:**
  - Cloudflare build → `_site`
  - Merge #18, then #19
  - Proposals #20–#22
  - Arm publishing
  - Engine-opened PRs
  - Semrush budget
  - Claude drafting
  - Product-claim decisions
- **NEEDS CONFIGURATION:**
  - Import the `main` ruleset
  - Railway source branch `main` + Wait for CI + PR Environments off
  - Create `seo-engine` and `seo-dashboard`
  - Read-only DB role
- **BLOCKED (owner must confirm):**
  - Current Railway variables
  - Search Console service-account access
  - Slack PB Assist round trip

## Product-owner decisions needed
1. **NinjaTrader:** the homepage FAQ says it's supported; everything else says Tradovate only. Blocked in the facts registry.
2. **"Ten protection rules":** on the homepage, in `llms.txt` and in the TradeSyncer comparison. #20 removes it from the Tradovate guide. The quality gate now catches it in table cells too.
3. **Competitor claims:** re-verify the TradeSyncer trial and annual discount, and the Tradecopia trial, then cite each one inline. Campaign item 5.
4. **Tracking/consent:** unchanged; needs a separately scoped approval.

## Handoff convention
For **each substantive project update made with an assistant**, update the status in this issue:
- date
- factual code and deploy state
- linked PR, CI and evidence
- decisions and approvals
- unresolved blockers
- next action

When a prior status becomes outdated, update it rather than representing it as current. Never claim work was applied if it was only proposed, and do not assume future automatic updates from other sessions or tools.

Hybrid already owns every piece of a machine bug-hunter except the machine. A grammar-driven generator can synthesize well-formed `.hy` programs by the million; `hyb check` filters the ones it ACCEPTS; the emitter lowers them; `go build` is an independent oracle that requires zero trust in our own code; a delta-debugging shrinker reduces any accepted-but-unbuildable program to a minimal repro automatically. Chain those five stages and the Tier-0 BUILDABLE guarantee stops depending on humans noticing violations: every violation becomes a one-command, minimized, self-filed issue — the first night it runs, the pipeline does mechanically the work of every soundness report filed here so far. It doubles as a regression gate in CI (fuzz for N minutes per PR) and as the corpus's missing half — the corpus proves the checker is right where we looked; the fuzzer proves it is right where we didn't. Any second oracle (`go vet`, the ownership runtime's own assertions, a checker derived from GUARANTEES.md rows) turns the same shape into a differential soundness engine.

### Which assumption it breaks

Two sacred cows. (1) *"Reproduction is the only door to a payout"* — the door today is a human-written repro; this removes the human from the loop, so reproduction becomes the toolchain's own output, not a reporter's skill. (2) *"A green corpus is our evidence of soundness"* — a fixed corpus only samples the program space; a fuzzer searches it, so the evidence stops being "we checked these programs" and becomes "we continuously searched for counterexamples and found none (N programs, M CPU-hours, coverage X)". The BUILDABLE claim in GUARANTEES.md goes from asserted to falsified-or-surviving, in public, with a number attached.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

Every issue in this tracker is a human finding a hole once, a fix closing it, and the next hole waiting for the next human. This changes what the project *is*: soundness stops being a property people verify occasionally and becomes a property the toolchain attacks continuously. It also inverts the trust debate the other wildcard families are having — capabilities (W-001–W-004), the untrusted emitter (#345), native-Go analysis (W-011–W-013) all argue about which component to trust; a pipeline checked against the real Go toolchain is the only argument that does not have to trust the checker, the emitter, or the alias graph *at the same time*. A normal feature bounty would reject it — no user-visible feature, pure tooling; this track exists exactly for that.

**Why now — receipts from this repo's own week.** Three distinct defect classes slipped past the standing evidence base — 191 unit tests, ~60 integration suites, a 1523/0 battery, a 109/109 differential corpus: (a) the sub-64 constant-conversion over-rejection pinned by `tests/const_conversion.rs::sub64_integer_overflow_folds_and_stays_accepted` — it broke while sitting in an open fix PR (#907); (b) pointer-parameter auto-addressing pinned by `tests/pointer_borrow_chains_issue_131.rs` — same story (#911); (c) the four range-bound bypass classes of #827. Each surfaced only because a human happened to write one more case — and two of them survived even the fix authors' own validation loops until a full-suite run forced them out. `check → emit → go build` finds every one of these classes mechanically, before a fix ships, on every commit. Meanwhile the tracker is absorbing waves of instant, unverified issues (dozens per afternoon): triage bandwidth, not report supply, is the bottleneck — and the pipeline's output is the opposite of that noise: every auto-filed report arrives already verified (accepted + unbuildable) and delta-minimized.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

Preregistered spike, scoped to `spikes/<id>-self-submitting-pipeline/` (ID from triage):

1. **Build** (no checker/emitter changes): grammar+corpus-seeded generator, driver, delta-debug shrinker.
2. **Budget**: ≥3 nights × ~16 CPU-hours — order 10^4–10^5 fully-compiled programs (check → emit → `go build`) and ~10^6 checker-only programs per night.
3. **Negative control first**: seed the pipeline with the known pre-fix vectors (#827's six loops, the sub64 accept set) against the pre-fix commit — it must re-find them; without this, a silently broken oracle reads as saturation.
4. **SUCCESS** = ≥1 accepted-but-unbuildable minimal repro on current main — filed immediately as a first-reporter soundness issue (P0-class insights bypass the review calendar per MOONSHOT.md).
5. **SATURATION** = 0 findings after the full budget — the first *measured* bound on how saturated the checker is, something no fixed corpus can state. Either outcome publishes as the M2 learning; both are paid.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

No checker or emitter code changes — external tooling only (generator, driver, shrinker, ~1–2k lines) plus CI wiring. What breaks: CI minutes (tunable N per PR), triage load (needs a dedup label and a rate cap, e.g. ≤5 auto-filed issues/week), and Go becomes a CI dependency for the oracle (already pinned: go1.26.9). User-facing migration: none.

### Track terms

- [x] I understand no prototype is required and failure-with-knowledge is a valid, paid outcome
- [x] I understand all outcomes (including declines and failures) are published in MOONSHOT.md

source_text:
Free Shopify CSV checker — catches the import that silently deletes your variants
I build free Shopify tools, so I have a bias here, but I kept running into the same problem and wanted to share what I built for it. 
 A product CSV can look completely valid and still delete data when you import it. The one that catches people out is in Shopify’s own import docs: if your file has a SKU or Weight column but not both the Option1 Name and Option1 Value columns, the import creates a new default variant and deletes your existing variants. There’s no error and no warning, so you only find out after. 
 So I made a checker that reads your CSV in the browser and flags that before you upload, plus a few other quiet ones: 
 
 SKUs that Excel turned into scientific notation (7.05E+11), where the real value is already lost 
 Blank or inconsistent handles that split one product into several 
 Prices with a currency symbol that import as 0.00 
 Image URLs Shopify can’t download (http-only, login-gated, or ending in _thumb/_small/_medium) 
 Encoding issues like a UTF-8 BOM that hides your Handle column 
 
 Each finding is ranked worst-first with why it matters and how to fix it. It reads only the file you give it, nothing is uploaded, there’s no account, and it doesn’t call any AI. Once the page loads, you can even use it offline. 
 It’s free with no limit. If you import products in bulk, I’d like to know if it catches something useful, or if you have a CSV that breaks it: 
 
   
       

       Extensions Market 
   

   
       

  Free Shopify Product CSV Checker — Catch Errors Before You Import  

   Some 'valid' CSVs delete your variants on import. This free checker flags those, plus handle, price, image, and encoding issues. In your browser, nothing uploaded.

KairoSphere architecture and runtime audit — prioritized repair plan
## Objective
Perform a repository-wide architecture and runtime audit of KairoSphere and deliver an evidence-backed, prioritized repair plan. Do not begin broad refactoring before the audit findings are recorded.

## Known baseline (verify against current HEAD)
- Vite build tool and development server.
- Native JavaScript ES modules; no React/Vue/Angular dependency was present in the previously inspected root package.json.
- Supabase client dependency and Supabase project files.
- Vite config previously set the production base path to `/laughing-waffle/` and development base to `/`.
- Local browser previously failed to render the app at localhost:5173; root cause was not established.
- Prior repository inspection did not include a live local process, browser console, network trace, or full test/build execution.

## Audit workstreams (priority order)

### P0 — Runtime boot and reproducibility
- Inspect current branch/commit, package.json, lockfile, Node engine, Vite config, HTML entry, source entrypoints, and scripts.
- Reproduce startup using the documented Node version and a clean dependency install where possible.
- Check port 5173 occupancy, Vite host binding, strictPort behavior, process exit/logs, and whether Vite silently falls back to another port.
- Verify both localhost and 127.0.0.1 responses, HTML entry, module loading, asset paths, and browser console/runtime exceptions.
- Determine whether the observed browser frame error is caused by server absence, wrong port/host, startup failure, or application runtime failure. Attach exact evidence.

### P1 — Frontend architecture and application integrity
- Map the actual application boot sequence, modules, routing/navigation, state ownership, UI composition, and dependency graph.
- Identify dead, duplicated, conflicting, stale, or unreachable files and scripts.
- Verify responsive behavior and core dashboard/navigation flows.
- Check error boundaries/fallback behavior, loading/empty/error states, and console warnings.
- Distinguish deliberate architecture from accidental complexity; recommend simplification only where supported by evidence.

### P1 — Supabase and security
- Trace client initialization and environment-variable usage; verify no secrets are committed or exposed.
- Inspect auth/session restoration, sign-in/sign-out, protected access, and failure handling.
- Review database schema/migrations, CRUD paths, validation, and Row Level Security policies against actual client queries.
- Check anonymous/public access, ownership constraints, and data isolation. Do not weaken RLS to make the UI work.
- Verify missing/malformed environment configuration fails safely and is documented.

### P1 — Build and deployment
- Run automated tests and production build; record exact commands, exit codes, and relevant output.
- Validate GitHub Pages base path, asset URLs, SPA refresh/navigation behavior, and deployment workflow consistency.
- Compare local development and production preview behavior.

### P2 — Quality, maintainability, and performance
- Check accessibility basics, mobile layout, semantic structure, bundle size, unnecessary dependencies, and avoidable runtime work.
- Assess logging/diagnostics and add only high-value observability recommendations.
- Identify obsolete patterns and unused data/code; propose cleanup separately from necessary repairs.

## Required deliverables
1. Architecture map: entrypoints, major modules, data flow, external services, build/deploy path.
2. Runtime diagnosis: reproducible steps, root cause(s), logs/network/browser evidence. Mark anything not testable in the available environment as NOT VERIFIED.
3. Findings register with severity (P0/P1/P2), affected file/line, impact, evidence, and recommended fix.
4. Prioritized repair plan: smallest safe repair first, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and rollback considerations.
5. Test matrix: startup, both loopback URLs, browser render, auth/session, CRUD/RLS, tests, production build, deployed base path.
6. Explicit list of proposed removals/refactors and why they are safe; do not delete or migrate data during the audit.

## Execution constraints
- Audit first; do not make broad architecture changes or destructive cleanup as part of diagnosis.
- Preserve user data and secrets. Never print secret values.
- Do not change repository ownership/access, security settings, billing, or deployment/publication settings.
- If repair is straightforward and non-destructive, propose the exact patch and test it on a separate branch or local working tree; do not merge or deploy.
- Do not claim a test passed unless it was actually run. Separate VERIFIED, FAILED, and NOT VERIFIED.
- If local terminal/browser access is unavailable, complete the static repository audit and provide exact commands for the local operator to run.

## Final report format
- Executive status (Healthy / Degraded / Blocked)
- Confirmed root causes
- P0/P1/P2 findings table
- Architecture map
- Prioritized repair sequence with acceptance tests
- Commands/tests run and results
- Remaining blockers and owner/action needed

source_text:
AI Agent: Anthropic thinking block is duplicated across parallel tool calls, Anthropic API rejects the next turn with 400 "Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block"
### Bug Description

When an Anthropic Chat Model with thinking enabled (explicitly, or by default on Claude Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.x, which think adaptively when no `thinking` field is sent) returns **one `thinking` block followed by two or more `tool_use` blocks in the same response**, the AI Agent node (Tools Agent V3) fails on the very next model call:

```
400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"messages.1.content.3: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to \"drop_block\". That setting requires the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` value in the `anthropic-beta` header. This request has content before this block that was not present when it was created, first at `messages.1`."}}
```

Surfaced in n8n as `NodeOperationError: Bad request - please check your parameters` on the AI Agent node, thrown from `ToolsAgent/V3/helpers/executeBatch.ts`.

Turns with a single tool call work. The failure only happens when the model issues parallel tool calls, so it is intermittent and depends on the model's choice.

### Root cause (verified in source on master @ 40094e3, 2026-10-15; reproduced on 2.42.7)

The model returns a single assistant turn shaped like `[thinking, tool_use A, tool_use B]`. The thinking block carries a signature that Anthropic binds to that exact turn.

When the agent rebuilds the history after running the tools:

1. `createEngineRequests.ts` → `extractThinkingMetadata()` (line 43) copies the same `thinkingContent` / `thinkingSignature` into the metadata of **every** tool action of the batch. In the saved execution both actions carry an identical `metadata.anthropic.thinkingSignature`.
2. `buildSteps.ts` → `buildSteps()` (line 345) builds the steps. For Gemini it detects parallel calls sharing a thought signature and merges them into one assistant message via `buildSharedGeminiAIMessage()` (lines 288 and 389–412). There is no equivalent branch for Anthropic. Each Anthropic tool call goes through `buildIndividualAIMessage()` (line 236) → `buildAnthropicContentBlocks()` (line 93), which always returns `[thinkingBlock, toolUseBlock]` (line 126).

The history sent on the next call is therefore:

```
Human: ...
AI:   [thinking(sig S), tool_use A]
Tool: result A
AI:   [thinking(sig S), tool_use B]      <- same signature S, replayed under a different prefix
Tool: result B
```

Anthropic now validates that a signed thinking block is replayed under the prefix it was created with. The second copy is preceded by `tool_use A` and `result A`, which did not exist when the signature was minted, so the request is rejected. The comment above the Gemini branch in `buildSteps.ts` describes exactly this problem ("Splitting into separate model turns invalidates the signature"); the Anthropic path simply never got the same handling.

### Related

- #40360 (open) touches the same Anthropic replay path in `buildSteps.ts`.
- #38302 (merged) made empty-text thinking blocks survive the round-trip. This report is the next failure after that fix: the block survives, but it is duplicated.
- #37730 / #37954: explain why thinking is on by default for Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 when Thinking Mode is unset.

### To Reproduce

1. Workflow: Manual Trigger → **AI Agent** (Tools Agent, typeVersion 3.1).
2. Chat model: **Anthropic Chat Model** (typeVersion 1.6), model `claude-opus-5-5` (or `claude-sonnet-5`), **no Thinking Mode option set** (so the model thinks adaptively), or Thinking Mode: Adaptive.
3. Attach two independent tools, e.g. two HTTP Request Tool nodes, or one MCP Client Tool exposing several tools.
4. Prompt with something that invites two lookups at once, e.g. "Look up the user with email X AND search for similar tickets about Y, then summarise."
5. When the model answers with one thinking block and two `tool_use` blocks, both tools run, and the next Anthropic Chat Model call fails with the 400 above. Open the execution → Anthropic Chat Model → second run → input: the history shows `AI: [thinking][tool_use]` twice with the same signature.
6. Prompt it so that it only calls one tool per turn: works.
7. Set Thinking Mode: Disabled, or switch to the OpenAI Chat Model: works.

In my instance this hit 5 production runs in ~24 h on a support-ticket agent with an MCP Client Tool (`get-user` + `find-users`, `get-user` + `get-invoices`, `find-users` + `find-teams`, …). In every failing run, both actions in `subNodeExecutionData.actions[].action.metadata.anthropic` had the identical `thinkingSignature`.

### Expected behavior

Parallel Anthropic tool calls from a single thinking turn should be replayed as **one** assistant message `[thinking, tool_use A, tool_use B]` followed by the tool results, the same way `buildSharedGeminiAIMessage()` already does for Gemini thought signatures. Alternatively, the thinking block should be attached only to the first tool call of the batch and omitted on the others.

### Workarounds

- Set **Thinking Mode: Disabled** on the Anthropic Chat Model node (works since #37954; not possible on models that cannot disable thinking).
- Use a different chat model node.

source_text:
BENCH-SPACE-004: quantify supplier concentration versus cislunar service resilience
## Research basis

The OECD's 2026 Space Economy at a Glance assesses a space economy whose access has broadened while launch activity, orbital infrastructure and supply chains remain concentrated. It reports that four providers accounted for more than four-fifths of orbital launches in 2025 in one commonly used metric and highlights single-country dependencies in crucial space-related inputs. See https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/the-space-economy-at-a-glance-2026_cbf9b240-en/full-report/managing-vulnerabilities-dependencies-and-sustainability-risks-of-the-space-economy_4d97ef6d.html

These real-world observations motivate this benchmark; the fixture values below are synthetic and must not be presented as the OECD's provider shares or as an actual procurement dataset.

## Paradigm shift

Treat supplier diversity as a measurable resilience attribute with an explicit cost—not as a slogan and not as a proxy for arbitrary failure probabilities. Compare the cost of a concentrated procurement portfolio with the additional cost of a portfolio that can still meet its service floor after any one supplier fails.

## Synthetic reference case

Required service demand: 70 normalized capacity units.

- Concentrated portfolio capacities: 50, 20, 15, 15 (total 100); listed lifecycle procurement cost: 100 synthetic cost units; portfolio HHI: 3,350 using the sum of squared percentage shares.
- Diversified portfolio capacities: 25, 25, 25, 25 (total 100); listed lifecycle procurement cost: 118 synthetic cost units; portfolio HHI: 2,500.
- Under concentrated sourcing, losing the 50-unit provider leaves 50, below the demand floor of 70 (shortfall 20). Losing any smaller provider leaves at least 80.
- Under diversified sourcing, losing any one 25-unit provider leaves 75, satisfying demand 70.

The 18% diversification premium is the explicit trade-off in the toy case, not a real cost estimate. Deterministic fault cases do not imply that outages are equally likely or independent.

## Required invariants

1. Compute HHI from the fixture's declared capacity shares; require shares to be non-negative and sum exactly to 100% (or use an explicitly documented normalized unit).
2. Run every single-supplier failure as a separate deterministic case; do not assign outage probabilities without evidence.
3. Calculate remaining capacity, unmet demand, lifecycle cost and the service-floor result for every case.
4. If N-1 supplier resilience is a hard requirement, mark the concentrated option infeasible before ranking price; select the cheapest feasible option only after gates.
5. Report cost, HHI, capacity and service separately—no composite score may hide a hard shortfall.
6. A higher HHI is not itself proof of market power or a causal failure probability; this is a procurement exposure metric over the specified candidate portfolio.
7. Reject a claimed robust portfolio if demand is raised above the remaining capacity after its weakest single-supplier failure.

## Acceptance targets

- 100% of named single-supplier fault cases have an independently recomputed remaining-capacity result.
- Zero infeasible options may win a hard N-1 gate on the basis of lower price.
- Exact HHI outputs match the analytical oracle (3,350 and 2,500 for the frozen fixture).
- Zero probabilistic-risk claim from deterministic fault coverage.
- Reports show diversification premium, capacity shortfall and HHI side-by-side.

## Composition

This is a new synthetic portfolio slice linked to the [Space Economy Reference Benchmark Suite PR #1736](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/pull/1736) and the [common-cause resilience work #1749](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symtropy/issues/1749). It should compose with Symtropy's deterministic market/logistics models and Mycelix provenance, with Symthaea comparing policies and Sol Atlas projecting supply and dependency context. It is not a second generic market engine.

source_text:
Show HN: Flopper is a hardware explorer for AI infrastructure and beyond
Hello! I built Flopper to make it easier to compare GPUs and understand the tradeoffs for workloads for AI and beyond. When researching GPUs from say Nvidia, AMD, and Huawei, I kept running into the same problem: specs were scattered across datasheets, and matching them to available configurations, vendors, and prices was cumbersome and a bit weird and frankly annoyingggg! AMD made me make an account :( So I started a place to bring that information together. Flopper lets you compare GPU specs, including TDP and compute throughput in terms of flops/tops, alongside estimates for AI workloads or other compute workloads (say, ~FP32 based) I recently added pricing data from dozens of providers to help track how prices change over time. Getting reliable quotes for systems like the NVL72 is still particularly difficult tbh, not sure how I can tell you how much that costs easily due to them being behind large procurement contracts and big multi-nationals. One thing that's become fairlyyyy clear is the interest in consumer cards and local LLMs. The bigger challenge is connecting advertised specs to real-world performance. In our testing so far, I’ve seen roughly 85% of advertised throughput, but that’s a ballpark observation for the workloads I’ve tested, not a general rule and so variable (power, cooling, workload etc). I'm considering a CLI that lets people run benchmarks and submit results, potentially using MLPerf as an automation? That way, we can all compare quoted performance with the workload, configuration etc. I'd love feedback: what information is missing, how can I improve it? And what would you need to see to trust a community-submitted benchmark? Corrections and additions also very welcome - some of the measurements are best efforts (and simple multiplications) but I hope it's of some use. Thanks for looking :)

DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY: evaluation material and an evaluator adapter
## What this is
`DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY` is on the mandatory Intent list for Season II. To rank its miners fairly, the network needs two things:

- **Evaluation material**: examples the network tests answers against.
- **An evaluator adapter**: the piece that scores each answer.

This Issue asks for both.

What the catalogue says it is for: Confirms driver dispatch route scheduling, customer delivery appointment slots, and signature requirements.

## The Intents
Work only on these exact names.

| Intent | What it asks |
|---|---|
| `DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY_GENERAL` | Query asks what delivery appointment window, route slot or signature requirement a dispatch system has committed for a stop or order. |

## Who needs it
No app idea in the Season II brief needs it yet. It's a Telegraph Intent, so the network should be able to rank it when one does.

Missions it serves: Consumer Platform, Consumer Automation.

## Part 1: Evaluation material (anyone can help)
**Question pairs.** Questions people would really ask this Intent, each with a better answer and a worse answer.

The network only uses an Intent's material once enough different people have contributed. So this part needs several of you, and every person counts.

How:
1. Read [Contribute Evaluation Data](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/contribute-evaluation-data). It has the row format, the limits and the reasons a row gets turned down.
2. Sign in to Anjoman and open [Evaluate](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/eval). Add your material under the Intent's exact name from the table.
3. Check your rows. Each one should end up `eligible`. If one is `rejected`, it says why.

What makes it good:
- Use real questions people would ask this Intent.
- Make the worse answer believable but wrong, about as long as the better one, and different every time. Repeated stock answers get thrown out.
- Add the link a row came from when you can.

## Part 2: An evaluator adapter (for builders)
An adapter is a small model, packed into one `.wasm` file, that reads a question and an answer and scores the answer. You register it on the family `DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY`, and it scores every Intent under it.

How:
1. Train and package it with [Train an Evaluator Adapter](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/train-a-scoring-adapter). The kit and every command are there.
2. Register it and follow its status with [Build an Evaluator Adapter](https://anjoman.ai/docs/scoring/build-a-scoring-module). You can publish it from [Evaluate](https://anjoman.ai/dashboard/eval) in Anjoman.
3. The network tests it on this family's evaluation material, so it can only be judged once that material is in. It goes live only if it passes the network's checks.

## Rules
- Work only on the Intents in the table.
- Network details (contracts, node, chain): [Addresses & Parameters](https://anjoman.ai/docs/protocol/addresses-and-params). How Intents and families work: [Intents](https://anjoman.ai/docs/using/intents).
- Nobody from Telegraph will ask for your private key or for money.

## Done when
- [ ] Evaluation material: the network has accepted material for every Intent in the table and uses it for ranking. A maintainer ticks this once it is verified.
- [ ] Evaluator adapter: one is live on `DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY` and scores its Intents. A maintainer ticks this once it is verified.

Your own part counts once your rows are `eligible`, or once your module passes the network's checks. Say which in your `/submit`.

## Reward
**Unfunded.** No money or tokens are paid for this Issue. The protocol's own evaluator rewards are separate: see [Tokenomics](https://anjoman.ai/docs/protocol/tokenomics). Hackathon prizes are set by the H2 rules.

## How to join
- Several people can work on this at the same time. Comment `/claim` to join. Everyone who joins is listed.
- Post `/progress <what you did>` at least every 72 hours, or your claim lapses. Other people's claims stay.
- When your part is done, comment `/submit` with your contributor address or your module's registration id, and a line on what you added.
- A maintainer checks each submission on its own. The Issue closes only when every box under "Done when" is ticked, so one part alone doesn't close it.

source_text:
Automation instructions that start with "/" or "$" reach the agent as empty text
🤖 _The AI agent says:_

## What happens

An automation instruction that starts with `/` or `$` reaches the agent as empty text.

Steps to reproduce:

1. In `/m`, create a schedule automation with the instruction `/summarize the support tickets from yesterday`.
2. Run it, or wait for the schedule to fire.
3. Open the session of that run.

Expected: the agent's first message is `/summarize the support tickets from yesterday`.

Actual: the agent's first message is empty.

The same thing happens to one part of an event automation's instruction. When the instruction is `/summarize {{Title}}`, the agent receives only the title. Text such as `$100 bounty` at the start of a part is also lost. The "What the agent gets" preview and "Run now" still show the full text, so the preview does not match what the agent receives.

## Why it happens

Automations build the agent's input with `resolve_target_fields` in `sdks/python/agenta/sdk/utils/resolvers.py`. That function passes every string in the stored mapping through `resolve_json_selector`.

`resolve_json_selector` treats any string that starts with `$` as a JSON Path, and any string that starts with `/` as a JSON Pointer. It does not check whether the string is meant as a selector. When the path finds nothing, it returns `None`, and the message text becomes empty.

The instruction text and the selectors live in the same strings. A selector is a whole text part, such as `$.event.attributes.title`. A plain sentence that starts with `/` or `$` looks the same to the resolver. The stored format also has no way to escape a literal `/` or `$`.

## What a fix needs

- The resolver must tell a selector apart from plain text. One option is to read only `$.` and `$[` as JSON Path inside message text parts. A second option is to read `/` as a JSON Pointer only outside message text.
- `resolve_target_fields` has other callers, such as webhooks. A fix must keep their behavior, or change it on purpose and test it.
- The frontend preview uses the same rule in `@agenta/entities` (`resolveSelectorPreview`), and it must change with the backend so that the preview still equals what the agent receives.

This bug existed before the event field picker, and it affects schedules today. It was found during the review of #7913.
