source_text:
How Does the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT NAND Flash Memory Work?
NAND flash memory is an essential technology in modern electronic systems, providing non-volatile data storage that retains information even when power is disconnected. It is widely used in embedded systems, automotive electronics, industrial equipment, and digital devices that require reliable memory solutions.
The Micron [MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT](https://globx.eu/products/micron/mt29f1g08abafah4-aatf) NAND Flash Memory is a 1Gb single-level cell (SLC) NAND flash memory device designed for applications that need dependable data storage and parallel memory access. With an 8-bit data bus, a 3.3V I/O interface, and an operating temperature range of -40°C to +105°C, it is suited to demanding embedded and automotive environments.
Understanding how this NAND flash memory works helps engineers select appropriate storage components for electronic system design, firmware storage, and industrial applications.

**What Is the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT?**
The MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT is a non-volatile [NAND flash memory](https://doodleordie.com/profile/globxoffical) component manufactured by Micron Technology. It stores digital information in memory cells that retain their programmed state without continuous electrical power.
The device provides a 1-gigabit storage capacity, organized as 128M × 8 bits. Its parallel interface allows a compatible processor or memory controller to transfer data through an eight-bit bus.
Unlike volatile memory such as SRAM and DRAM, NAND flash memory preserves stored information when the system shuts down. This makes it useful for storing firmware, configuration data, and other information required when an electronic device starts operating.

**How Does NAND Flash Memory Work?**
NAND flash memory stores information by controlling the electrical charge within specialized semiconductor memory cells. These cells represent digital data through different electrical states.

The MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT uses single-level cell technology, meaning each memory cell stores one bit of information.
Its operation can be understood through three main processes.

1. Storing Data in Memory Cells
During programming, the memory device applies controlled electrical conditions to place charge into the storage structure of selected memory cells. The resulting electrical characteristics represent the programmed data.
In SLC NAND flash, each cell represents either a logical 0 or a logical 1. Because each cell stores one bit, SLC technology offers a straightforward storage arrangement compared with multi-level NAND technologies.
This design is useful in embedded applications where predictable memory behavior and endurance are important considerations.

2. Reading Stored Information
When a processor needs information, it sends the appropriate command and address to the NAND flash memory. The device accesses the selected location and determines the stored bit values by sensing the electrical characteristics of the memory cells.
The retrieved data is transferred through the eight-bit parallel interface.
A compatible controller or processor coordinates the read operation and uses the returned information for tasks such as loading firmware, accessing configuration settings, or retrieving stored program data.

Single-level cell NAND flash stores one bit per memory cell. Other NAND technologies, including MLC, TLC, and QLC, store multiple bits per cell.
The main difference is how many electrical states each cell must distinguish.
SLC NAND uses two principal states, making the interpretation of stored data simpler than in technologies that use more states per cell. SLC memory is therefore often selected for applications that prioritize endurance, reliable operation, and consistent embedded storage behavior.

---

## PAYMENT SCOPE CORRECTION — 15 OCT 2026

Owner confirmed ShinaCare must account for **COD, Visa/Mastercard and Vodafone Cash**, not assume COD is the only future checkout payment method. **C1 backend exit remains a REAL COD Cart-to-Cash E2E**, PLUS a tested lean payment-method-aware core/guardrails under [GLO-241](<https://linear.app/ahme-hassan/issue/GLO-241>). This DOES NOT claim card or Vodafone Cash checkout is LIVE without an Egypt-compatible provider, merchant account, API credentials, signed callback verification and real sandbox evidence. Do not invent provider integrations or require keys for COD acceptance. For online methods keep unverified attempts PENDING, never synthesize paid/cash/settled, and avoid creating COD driver obligations. Separate provider settlement/payout from payment confirmation. Actual provider integration requires explicit owner approval and remains a later milestone.

---

## Goal (owner directive 15 Oct 2026)

BACKEND ONLY. Demonstrate one persisted Cart→quote→COD order→durable sourcing→consolidated supplier PO/confirmed allocations→Hub receipt→barcode-verified preparation+packing documents→driver run/custody/delivery→door-cash declaration→physical cash count→single correct settlement. Include availability/return/refund/support and supplier payables. No Storefront/Business Workspace design or implementation in this phase.

This is an **acceptance gate, not duplicate implementation**; work in linked existing canonical W issues and any verified missing backend task. Existing C0 cross-workspace UI acceptance (AhmedHassanDev1/shena-care#118) is explicitly deferred, NOT Done.

## Required reproducible test evidence (same identifiers throughout)

- [ ] Real PostgreSQL test DB (\*\_test), migrations, scoped actor accounts for customer/guest/admin/supplier/hub/driver/cashier; no Neon/shared/production DB.
- [ ] Server-only cart quantity/revision, catalog sellability/prices, authoritative quote, price-change 409/requote, idempotent COD order, persisted confirmed address + geo pin, Cairo/Giza serviceability and role-safe pin access.
- [ ] Durable order.placed handoff/recovery, idempotent supply plan; supplier+SKU aggregated PO with N:1 quantity-aware PO-line-to-allocation mapping and deterministic partial/fallback; no late duplicate supply.
- [ ] Real Hub receiving quantity vs supplier Ready, correct source links, scan mismatch blocked, packed unique shipment identity and printable thermal receipt/slip data (physical printer testing deferred).
- [ ] Driver-only assigned manifests with secured coordinates/stop ordering, handoff scanning, dispatch atomic order+shipment effects, delivered/failed/retry/return consistency and safe replay.
- [ ] Expected COD vs declared door cash vs counted cashier cash vs settled; driver/courier/hub scope; zero duplicate/failed/undelivered settlement; explicit short/over variance; exact Decimal arithmetic.
- [ ] Supplier payable based on correct received/approved qty/cost snapshot, EGP, race-safe idempotency; cancellation/refund/manual COD refund evidence, support escalation and event/outbox truthfulness.
- [ ] Query/read APIs for role-scoped operational inboxes (no UI), RBAC/IDOR/PII negative HTTP cases, concurrency/transaction failure recovery.
- [ ] Single full-backend C2C automated integration suite, including critical negative cases; exact Git SHA, commands, passed/failed/skipped counts, DB target; no simulated success evidence.

## Acceptance

Backend PASS requires one replayable HTTP/API→DB run from cart to settled money, accurate cross-domain state, and documented negative/authorization/concurrency tests. Manual physical cash, printer, real supplier and all role UI acceptance are separate later operational gates; do NOT misrepresent them as backend-proven. Keep this issue In Progress until all backend bullets pass. No fixed date.

## Execution guardrails

Reuse implemented modules (do not rewrite Cart/Quote/Shipping/Scan/Settlement blindly); inspect HEAD, staged 26 deletions and private uploads before touching code; never broad-stage/reset; one coding agent at a time; scoped commits; no merge without owner approval. Claude may only update progress/evidence statuses and comments, not owner scope/dates/priorities.

source_text:
Show HN: Daisy – macOS software KVM with native trackpad gestures
I have three laptops on my desk most days.  Each laptop is used for different work, that I need to keep separate.  (Day job, advisory work, personal.)  When I went looking for a software KVM, the only free one that correctly handled trackpad gestures was Apple's Universal Control but that requires using the same iCloud account on each system, which is a non starter. I had planned to just contribute to something else but the best option I found was intended to be a universal software KVM and had already rejected OS specific features.  I get the thinking and don't begrudge the devs at all but I needed something that supports my workflow.  Thus, Daisy (as in "daisy chain"). Daisy is a FOSS software KVM for macOS that doesn't need an iCloud account and handles gestures the way I want it to.  You arrange the displays to match your physical desk, move the pointer across an edge, and control follows it to the next machine. Nothing leaves the local network (unless you want auto-updates) and there's encryption all the way around anyway. It turns out that getting the trackpad working is somewhat non trivial. macOS doesn't expose Spaces and Mission Control swipes through the public gesture events. They arrive as private DockControl events, which meant figuring out how to capture the gesture phases, progress, and velocity, transport them, and replay them on another Mac. There's a fair amount of undocumented macOS behavior involved, and I've documented what I figured out in the repo. Beyond gestures, the key things I wanted: - Capable of handling a large chain (8), with a layout tool that that makes it easy to arranges systems the way they exist on my desk
- Copy/paste across machines for images, files, and folders
- No accounts or other external dependencies
- Keeping displays active across the whole chain when you're doing work, without violating the intent behind screen locking
- No single machine acting as the control system that all peers must negotiate with for trust (the machine you're typing on is always the control system) It's not quite 1.0. Occasionally the layout UI loses track of a peer even though the connection is fine, input can sometimes get jerky, and I still need to beat on file transfers more. I use it daily, though, and it's reached the point where I find it genuinely useful. It currently requires Apple silicon and macOS 26 or later. I've tested on 26 and 27. Code, downloads, and the technical documentation are here:
 https://github.com/misfitdev/daisy  I'd be particularly interested in hearing from anyone who's fought with macOS input events or tried to solve the same problem. And if you give Daisy a shot, I'd like to know what breaks. I'm also really happy about the security design and I'd love for people to poke holes in it. :)

## Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime (WPF). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability.

WPF XPS synthetic hyperlinks exposed through UI Automation can bypass restrictive navigation checks and reach attacker-controlled content, enabling remote code execution after user interaction.

## Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/471

source_text:
[wildcard] Kill the hand-written behaviour repro: an execution-oracle fuzzer (INVARIANT 5 — accepted ⇒ runs clean under `-race`)
### The idea, in a paragraph

Hybrid already checks buildability by machine (W-023's INVARIANT 4: accepted ⇒ `go build` succeeds) and checks *behaviour* by hand: the differential harness compares `build+run` outcomes on a curated set of hand-authored pairs, and every race/P0 report in this tracker was found by a person writing one more racing program. That asymmetry is the hole. Buildability is decidable by a compiler; **soundness itself** — "this accepted program does not race, does not panic, does not write the wrong element" — is only ever *observed* when a human hand-writes the witness. The proposal is to make execution the oracle: grow `tools/fuzz/hyfuzz.py` a **semantics leg** — generate programs, let `hyb check` accept-gate them, emit, `go build`, then **execute the emitted Go under `-race`** (plus the runtime's own guards); classify divergence (race | panic | guard violation | wrong value | none); delta-debug-shrink anything that diverges; self-file it with the witness. The static claims the checker makes for a program (loan spans, no cross-task aliasing, single-writer windows) become *hypotheses* that the execution leg adjudicates. The first iteration needs no semantic model at all: race reports and panics are unambiguous, and they are exactly the **P0 ladder class** — an accepted program that builds and then races is the most expensive bug in this repo.

### Which assumption it breaks

Two. (1) *"Evidence about behaviour must be hand-authored."* A curated corpus proves the checker right on the programs someone chose; a fuzzer searches the space nobody chose. Behaviour evidence stops being a list and becomes a measured quantity (N executions, M CPU-hours, residual per rule family) — the semantic twin of what W-023 did for buildability. (2) *"The runtime is only the untrusted half."* Today the Rust runtime/bridge is the thing the checker's proofs are supposed to protect; here the runtime becomes the **judge** of those proofs. This is a genuinely different oracle from a compiler check: `go build` answers "is this well-formed Go"; `go run -race` answers "does the program behave the way the checker said it would". When the race detector fires inside a program the checker proved non-aliasing, something is wrong — the checker's proof or the runtime's enforcement — and the divergence is the finding. (Honest limit: the runtime cannot certify itself; the two sides are adjudicated against each other, and each divergence is triaged as P0-class evidence, not as a verdict about which side is wrong.)

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

Receipts from this repo, not theory. W-023's build oracle drove the build residual 38.03% → 2.78% and left *semantics* untouched — the open P0 family is precisely the set that **builds fine**: #970 (a slice-element loan survives re-binding → OOB store-back panic + silent wrong-element write), #946 (map-slot loans bypass E3102 across move/re-loan, concurrent map writes), #953 (`emit_match` drops the O8 store-back on `else_arm`), #966 (self-shadowed bindings allow concurrent map writes after a move), #971 (bare expression statements / deferred calls discard values past the front-end), #974 (clobbered return-origin and multi-return alias tracking). No amount of build-fuzzing moves those numbers; execution-fuzzing can. **The size of the untouched half** is measurable today: 84 of the 178 open issues in this tracker carry `soundness` in the title (`is:issue is:open soundness in:title`) against 192 open PRs — and the behavioural ones among them are, by construction, programs the checker *accepts* and the compiler *builds*; the build-side family is the one machine sweeping has already taken. And the project's own spike protocol already proves the oracle works — the wildcard spikes are *race-verified* by running them under the detector. Today that verification happens once per idea, by hand, at PR time; this makes it a standing nightly leg, and turns "we once verified a spike" into "we continuously attacked the checker with executions". A normal feature bounty would reject it (no user-visible feature, pure tooling) — which is what this track is for.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

Pre-registered spike, scoped to `spikes/<id>-exec-oracle/` (ID from triage), results committed before they are judged:

1. **Build** (no checker/emitter/runtime changes): semantics leg in the fuzzer + driver (`hyb check` → emit → `go build` → `go run -race`), divergence classifier, delta-debug shrinker, auto-filer with a shrink-normalized dedup key.
2. **Budget**: ≥3 nights × ~16 CPU-hours. Race-instrumented runs are 5–20× slower, so the semantics leg sees far fewer programs than the checker-only leg — the *ratio* is pre-registered with the budget, not the raw count.
3. **Negative control first**: seed the pipeline with the known P0 shapes at their pre-fix commits (#970's three repros — OOB reslice panic, silent wrong-element write, append-realloc — plus #946, #953, #966, #971, #974). It must re-find every one; without this a silently broken oracle reads as saturation.
4. **SUCCESS** = ≥1 *new* accepted-but-unsound minimal repro on current main, filed immediately as a first-reporter P0-class issue (MOONSHOT.md: P0-class soundness insights bypass the review calendar).
5. **SATURATION** = 0 findings over the full budget ⇒ publish the first measured **execution-residual table** per rule family (build + race + panic + guard violations) — a number no fixed corpus can state, and the first measured bound on how saturated the checker is *semantically*.

Either outcome is the M2 learning; both are paid.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

- **Slow by construction**: `-race` makes the semantics leg roughly an order of magnitude more expensive per program than the build leg; the claim is deliberately per-execution, and the ratio is pre-registered so nobody mistakes a small sample for saturation.
- **Nondeterminism**: the first iteration counts only unambiguous classes (race reports, panics, runtime guard violations) and skips model comparison for programs whose output is not deterministic; "wrong value vs a model" is an explicit later, opt-in stage, so no soft claims enter the record.
- **Triage load**: auto-filed reports need the dedup key plus a hard rate cap (e.g. ≤3/week) — otherwise the pipeline becomes the noise problem it exists to solve.
- **Dependencies**: the pinned Go toolchain (go1.26.9) is already a CI dependency, `-race` needs nothing more, and the spike requires **zero** checker/emitter/runtime edits — tooling only (generator leg + driver + shrinker, ~1–2k lines).
- **Relation to existing entries, stated up front**: this is the *semantic twin* of W-023 (#565 / spike #577, buildability) and the *execution half* of #939 (reproduction automation: shrink → dedup → auto-file). The generator/harness would be shared with both; the oracle, the falsified claim, and the defect class are different (buildable vs behavioural). If the maintainers prefer to fold this into W-023 or into #939 with credited authorship, that is a perfectly good outcome — the deliverable is the runtime leg and the numbers it produces.

### Track terms

- [x] I understand no prototype is required and failure-with-knowledge is a valid, paid outcome
- [x] I understand all outcomes (including declines and failures) are published in MOONSHOT.md

# Spike pre-registration — execution-oracle fuzzer (INVARIANT 5)

**Status:** pre-registered draft, written *before* any run, to be committed as
`spikes/<id>-exec-oracle/HYPOTHESIS.md` once triage assigns the `<id>`.
**Claim under test:** "accepted ⇒ runs clean" is falsifiable *by machine*, and
the machine finds accepted-but-unsound programs that the build oracle (W-023)
cannot see.
**Pre-registered by:** Dimany4 (issue #1011). Nothing below is edited after
results exist; deviations are appended, never rewritten.

## H — hypothesis

H1. A generator + accept-gate + emit + **execute** pipeline, seeded with the
known pre-fix P0 shapes, re-finds **all** seeded shapes and finds at least one
**new** accepted-but-unsound minimal program on `main` within the budget.

H0 (the null, published if it wins). Zero findings in the full budget. The
result is then the first measured *execution-residual table* per rule family —
a number, not a claim.

## Falsifier design (what would make H1 false)

- F1. Any seeded shape is **not** re-found ⇒ the leg is broken; the run is void
  until fixed (this is the negative control, run first, before any budget is
  spent on generation).
- F2. A "finding" cannot be reproduced by a human in <10 minutes from the
  shrinker's output (i.e. the minimization is not actually minimal) ⇒ counted
  as a tooling defect, not a finding.
- F3. A divergence disappears when the same program is built with the pinned
  toolchain in a clean tree ⇒ classified as environment noise, discarded.

## Budget (committed in advance)

- 3 nights × ~16 CPU-hours on the developer machine; pinned toolchain
  (go1.26.9 + rust 1.99.0 as per repo pins).
- Pre-registered **ratio**, not raw counts: for every 1000 programs that pass
  the accept-gate, report how many reach execution (build + `-race` start) —
  the build leg's throughput is not the claim, the *execution* leg's is.
- Findings cap: at most 3 auto-filed reports per week across the whole run.

## Measurement (what gets published, either way)

| Stage | Metric |
|---|---|
| generate | programs emitted, accept rate (accepted / generated) |
| build | INVARIANT 4 residual (buildable failures) — W-023 comparison baseline |
| execute | programs executed, wall-time per execution, `-race` overhead factor |
| classify | divergence counts: race / panic / guard violation / nondeterministic / clean |
| attribute | per rule family: executions, divergences, execution-residual rate |
| file | auto-filed issues, dedup hits, human-reproduce time for each |

The published learning is the table above plus the status of H1 — success
(new P0-class repro filed) or saturation (measured residual per family).

## Out of scope in this spike (deliberately)

- No semantic model comparison for nondeterministic programs (a wrong-value
  claim needs a model; the first iteration refuses to guess).
- No checker/emitter/runtime source changes: the leg is external tooling.
- No CI wiring beyond an opt-in per-PR job with a wall-clock budget (wiring is
  the M2 deliverable, not the spike's).

## Relation to other entries (stated up front)

- **W-023 (#565 / spike #577)** — same generator/accept-gate skeleton, oracle =
  *compiler*. This spike's oracle = *execution*. Their residual is buildability;
  this one's is behaviour.
- **#939 (this author)** — reproduction automation (shrink → dedup → auto-file).
  The spike reuses that plumbing; the claim here is the oracle, not the filing.
- If maintainers prefer one merged entry with credited authorship, that is an
  acceptable outcome; the artifacts above stay the deliverable either way.

Show HN: Confetti – Start designing hardware with plain English prompts
Hey HN! We're Tianyi and Lucas from Confetti (YC F26) ( https://confetti.build/ ).  We’re building a platform that helps you turn your ideas into physical things using plain English. Take a look at a quick demo video here:  https://youtu.be/UhtAs4mg5O8  Making hardware has always required layers of expertise: learning modeling software, sourcing compatible components, designing enclosures, wiring, firmware, and finding someone to manufacture it all. We experienced this firsthand while prototyping a home AI device we wanted to build. We didn't have too much experience in hardware and every step opened up more questions. We spent so much time figuring out the process before we could make progress on the thing itself, so we built Confetti to make it easier to get started. Confetti puts the whole process on one platform, driven by natural language: - CAD: generate and edit 3D designs from text or image prompts - Electronics: automatic sourcing for compatible off-the-shelf parts, wiring, and firmware - Manufacturing: get quotes and place orders to get parts sent straight to your doorstep - Community: share, remix, and personalize builds from other makers for yourself In the same way that AI has made it much easier for people to build software, we think that we can use AI to enable a lot more people to start building the ideas they have for physical projects too. We would love to hear feedback that you have, what sort of bugs and issues you run into, and features you'd like to see!  https://confetti.build/

source_text:
Culinary review required before restoring Dfina and Babbouche cooking cards
PR #29 reconciles ten dish pages with the recipe archive. Two definitions can be published, but the full cooking instructions and Recipe structured data need the following editorial decisions.

### Dfina, recipe 56

The canonical record specifies a 10-minute full stovetop simmer followed by 12–16 hours in a covered 225°F/107°C conventional oven, a check before bed or after the first three hours, and boiling water if ingredients become exposed. The existing presentation packet instead specifies 100°C for 10–12 hours without opening the pot. USDA’s general home conventional-oven guidance gives 325°F as the minimum setting. Its 140°F guidance concerns holding already-cooked food. Neither source validates the temperature history of this particular covered pot of beef, shell-on eggs and legumes.

A qualified culinary food-safety reviewer should document the tested equipment, quantities, initial cook, measured internal temperatures, transition to overnight holding and liquid checks, or approve a separately tested method. A change of oven set point alone is insufficient. Preserve the original record and its Sabbath context until the decision is recorded.

[Canonical record](https://github.com/Oak-Main/medina/blob/d8ca704bdba73b9e532b9c6ba85f7d3091f28015/lib/data/recipe-details.json) · [USDA conventional ovens](https://ask.fsis.usda.gov/article/What-is-the-lowest-temperature-you-can-set-the-oven-to-for-and-safely-cook-food) · [USDA hot holding](https://ask.fsis.usda.gov/article/At-what-temperature-should-I-hold-hot-foods)

### Babbouche, recipe 15

The archive uses food-grade live land snails, a 10-minute initial boil and skim, and a covered two-hour simmer at 190°F/88°C. It also specifies an unidentified sprig of dried wormwood and describes the broth as medicinal. The U.S. natural-flavoring standard specifies a thujone-free finished food for Artemisia. The record gives no supplier specification, species or finished-food evidence. This is a sourcing and formulation question; there is no finding that a tested sample of this broth was unsafe.

Verify a suitable food-use ingredient and preparation or approve a documented, tested botanical change. Reconcile the supplier-directed preparation language with the generic home purging instruction and remove the unsupported therapeutic description before restoring the full card. Preserve the recorded simmer and the use of food-grade snails.

[21 CFR §172.510](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-172/subpart-F/section-172.510) · [CDC guidance on edible snails](https://www.cdc.gov/angiostrongylus/prevention/)

Restore each method independently after sign-off. Check the visible ingredients, method, FAQPage and Recipe JSON-LD on the built route, then update its publication-state regression.

BETA MASTER — Community Clout Championship v1: one verified event bridge, fair daily/weekly/quarterly/annual ranks, permanent 365-day Moonpet (NO DRIFT)
# BETA MASTER PLAN — Community Clout Championship v1 (16 October 2026)

> **STATUS: SPEC / ISSUE ONLY. NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT LIVE, NO MERGE/DEPLOY AUTHORIZATION.**
> **Owner decision:** GK delegated selection of the best *next build design* for the private/community beta. Primary goal is enjoyable **24/7 engagement and online clout**, **not money**. The task authorized here is to document the plan and dependencies. Do **not** create a PR, change main, migrate production D1, deploy Workers/Pages/VPS, change Telegram menus/secrets, enable cash/token/real-world prizes, or silently rewrite existing award rules just because this issue exists.
>
> **Scope owner:** this issue owns the **cross-ecosystem Clout receipt adapter + competition projection and UX**, *not* game engines, Moonpet economy, Arcade accuracy, GK Radio event builder, Dead Run campaign expansion, wiki lore, or existing currency ledgers.

## 0. Why this issue / outcome

A private community should be able to play whenever it wants, switch activities during game-specific cooldowns, and compete for badges, status and bragging rights. Make a **single understandable, auditable, non-spendable championship** across eligible Moonpet, Telegram, website and Arcade activities **without flattening distinct existing XP systems or rewarding fake browser numbers**.

**The chosen product model:** Moonpet's **permanent, approximately one-year Legendary journey is the long-term achievement anchor**. Shorter competitions are **daily (UTC), weekly (ISO/Monday UTC), quarterly (Moonpet competition calendar), and annual (UTC calendar year)**. The user's same pet continues across every competition reset. Nobody must already own a Moonpet to enter daily/weekly Clout.

**This is deliberately NOT a casino/bank-grade rebuild.** Reuse Cloudflare D1/Workers, signed Telegram identity and current source receipts. Protect rankings against easy farming and duplicate claims, but keep unlimited *gameplay* and reasonable budgets. Do not build new realtime infrastructure, alternate accounts, wallet/currency or a massive event bus.

## 1. Mandatory existing issue map — avoid duplicate agents and precedence drift

| **#1478** — MoonPet master roadmap | Moonpet UX/economy/content, Hxx provenance, existing 7 daily missions / weekly Journey / 365-day progression | Use existing accepted Moonpet event, Crest, Growth Mark, Contract, completion and quarter evidence | Add pet gameplay, change costs, delete/retire pets, merge weekly/daily Journeys, restart old Hxx work |
| **#903** — Production HUD + Arcade OS | Shared navigation/identity/proof-event presentation and cross-game UX architecture | Put Championship Clout into existing HUD/System Hub shell and central player identity | Create a rival shell, duplicate nav, bespoke unrelated game HUDs |
| **#1458** — CANON LOCK | Lore/product authority and W81 continuity | Preserve current canon and distinguish in-game clout from crypto/real-world rewards | Change lore/rights/economic promises |

| **#1202** (closed) | Historical 90-day Moonpet-era plan | Treat as superseded where current runtime differs | Restore obsolete 90-day pet retirement, older unlock prices or 60/10 Legendary gates |
| **#843** (closed) | Wiki likes/citation/comment missions | Reuse current source-backed awards; add true page/citation validation if used for championship | Reimplement wiki mission wiring |

Reference issue links: #1513, #1478, #903, #1458, #1259, #1266, #1069, #1071, #1072, #1226, #1253, #1202, #843. **The master issues stay open.** Child PRs must cross-link exactly which work they consume or defer. Recent issue comment claims/old PR snapshots are not proof of today's deployed versions.

## 2. Audited code baseline (revalidate before ANY implementation)

Source snapshot observed from default main on 2026-10-16: **2777337b6d7a0124483aec5a1843068b323a166c**. Source evidence != production Worker/D1/Telegram signed-in QA.

| Existing source | What code currently establishes | Integration status |
|---|---|---|
| workers/moonboys-api/pets/content/evolutions.json; pets/season-completion.js | Final Legendary stage **365 ownership days, 240 distinct-day Growth Marks, 44 distinct-week Crests**, plus level/boss/relic/material gates. Earlier age gates 7/28/84/182. Completion marker durable. | **Reuse unchanged** |
| pets/ownership-period.js; pets/season-authority.js | Pet lifetime journey continues after creation quarter; **competition quarters are calendar Jan–Mar/Apr–Jun/Jul–Sep/Oct–Dec**. Pet/source identity never resets on competition rollover. | **Reuse unchanged** |

Meta score submission accepts client figures. Aggregate sums incomparable raw best scores and uses top-100 per-game lists. | **Historical/display-only until a trusted receipt exists** |
| workers/moonboys-api/worker.js | /arcade/progression/sync derives Community/Arcade XP from client raw_score/meta_points after signed Telegram auth, cooldown and rate checks; /faction/earn, /faction/signal/contribute, /player/mastery/update and /player/daily-missions/progress accept client-declared contributions/progress. | **Do not treat as independent Clout authority** |
| worker.js wiki engagement | Linked comments/likes/citation votes can award per-page daily Community XP through source evidence, but accepted page_id/cite_id are not consistently checked against canonical published inventory. | **Clout only after authentic source validation** |
| docs/moonpet-source-of-truth.md | Newer permanent-pet year-long model | **Authority for pets** |
| docs/pet-game-seasonal-model.md, docs/moonpet-season-economy-calibration.md | Some earlier passages still say 90 days / 60 Growth Marks / 10 Crests | **Stale-doc reconciliation needed; never change current runtime to match old copy** |

Pre-change audit must classify every source **EXISTS / PARTIAL / MISSING / LIVE BUG / NEEDS DESIGN / VERIFIED IN PROD** with code path, exact deployed build, signed Telegram test and the authoritative receipt/table. *A passing fixture is not a verified real player run.*

## 3. LOCKED product/canon invariants (hard fail if violated)

1. **Moonpet permanence:** same pet_id, original ownership season, earned XP, level, evolutions, 240 Marks, 44 Crests, lifetime completion, identities, spaces and saved reward receipts persist across UTC days, weeks, competition quarters and years. No quarterly pet reset/retirement. Keep 1,000 **lifetime earned Arcade XP** first-pet entry gate (not spent); max 3 active pet spaces; existing 500 / 1,000 **spendable Arcade XP** additional-space costs; preserve grandfathered owned/history rows.
2. **Never merge currencies:** Arcade lifetime/spendable XP, Community XP/telegram_users.xp, Pet XP, Block Topia XP, Faction XP/Clout, Moon Gold/Crystals/Gems, Style Tokens, game raw score, and new **Championship Clout** are distinct. UI must name each. Nothing silently converts one to another or assumes that all game XP must be the same balance.
3. **Championship Clout is NON-SPENDABLE STATUS ONLY:** no cash, crypto, NFTs with promised value, withdrawal, transferable balance, store prices, player-to-player trade, pet-slot purchases, real-money equivalents, or bridge to existing Arcade spendable wallet. Rewards v1 are visible badges, champion titles, profile honors, event shout-outs and annual Hall of Fame **only**.
4. **Do not confuse existing Battle Chamber faction clout** with the new player Championship Clout. Different owner, source table/API/UI label, rank and reconciliation. Do not feed faction totals from arbitrary browser signals.
5. **24/7 participation:** do not hard-stop game access for hitting a leaderboard threshold. Existing per-source XP caps, care timers, safety restrictions and ranked eligibility remain until a separately reviewed balancing PR. Endless practice remains available; only count distinct qualifying official championship evidence, not every refresh/click.
6. **Verified linked identity:** use signed Telegram credentials and authoritative link checks for permanent rank. Guests can play and see public boards, but do not gain permanent competitive Clout. No forced Telegram location/GPS permission for general participation.
7. **No retroactive laundering:** a historic browser score, locally saved mission, old KV rank or unverified submission is not silently promoted into verified Clout. Preserve it with a clear legacy/practice source label until independently validated.
8. **No broad rollout by one PR.** No Worker deployment, D1 migration, bot menu change or score/payment flag change without explicit release checkpoint after review and tests.

## 4. Separate time scales: Moonpet JOURNEY vs Community COMPETITION

| Plane | Window/owner | Resets | Must not reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| Permanent Moonpet Journey | Pet-specific age from recorded adoption; roughly **365 days minimum** | **Never** | pet ownership/history, 240 daily Marks, 44 weekly Crests, XP, evolutions, achievements |
| Daily Championship | 00:00:00–next 00:00:00 **UTC** | Daily board | pet/day receipts, currencies, weekly/season/annual history |
| Weekly Championship | **Monday 00:00 UTC–next Monday** | ISO week board | underlying receipts and pet progression |
| Quarterly Championship | **Calendar quarter UTC** (Q1 Jan–Mar etc.), matching current Moonpet competition quarters | Quarter board | lifetime pet journey and independent legacy 90-day Arcade boards |
| Annual Hall of Fame | UTC Jan 1–Dec 31 | Annual leaderboard (archive winners) | lifetime profile awards/history |
| Existing Arcade 90-day windows | Anchor 2024-01-01; distinct from calendar quarter | Existing legacy schedule stays initially | **Do not repurpose or silently move existing stored boards** |
| Existing Community Season | Configured active telegram_seasons dates | Existing authority stays initially | all-time Community XP |
| Moonpet Weekly Journey | Per-pet creation-week clock, not always ISO week | Objective period only | previously earned pet Crest/evidence |

**Decision:** NEW Championship Clout quarter follows Moonpet calendar quarters; **do not change pre-existing Arcade or Community season authorities in this issue**. Show any differing period dates visibly. A later separately approved normalization/migration may replace legacy boards only after archived snapshots and proof.

For source-to-Championship attribution, default to immutable **server-earned timestamp** of the qualifying source event, not request-supplied time or retry time. Preserve each existing source's documented exception if its original receipt uses a settled period. Apply a single normalized UTC interval calculation inside the new Clout projector; prevent backdating, forward dating, late-insert rank movement after final freeze except explicit audited corrections. Publish exact board end and claim-freeze rules.

## 5. Selected fair *v1* scoring model — simple, small-audience-friendly

**Do not sum raw scores across Snake, NBG, Dead Run, Kaiju, Moonpet etc.** Different games have incomparable numerical ranges. A 100,000-point easy score must not defeat a technically difficult 3,000-point score simply due to scale.

**Championship Clout daily budget: 100 possible non-spendable ranking points from proven actions** (this is a competition scoring formula, NOT a cap on gameplay, earned Pet XP or shared Arcade XP):

| Bucket | Up to | Calculation / source policy |
|---|---:|---|
| **Skill** | **40** | The best **up to 3 distinct eligible games** that day. Game-specific server-verified performance maps to a versioned 0–100 skill rating. **Monotonic v1 rule:** Skill Clout = floor(40 × min(100, best_verified_rating + 0.10 × second_best_rating + 0.05 × third_best_rating) / 100), with missing games contributing zero. A newcomer with only one title can still earn the full 40; playing a weaker second game can NEVER reduce existing Clout. Keep only the best verified rating per title. No repeat-run sum. |
| **Daily/Weekly mission evidence** | **25** | Server-defined mission IDs and target definitions. Mission completion credits only if owned source event(s) qualify; daily objectives and once-per-week journey proof. Allocate exact points by public policy registry, not client target/amount. |
| **Variety / activity switching** | **15** | Three 5-point unique eligible categories or games within the UTC day (requires at least one **verified completed** action for each). Rotation should not require paid features or location permissions. |
| **Community engagement** | **10** | First approved/valid linked engagement actions, e.g. legitimate wiki like/comment/citation or bot daily claim, with daily dedupe and canonical page/citation verification. Not points-per-page, arbitrary votes, browsing seconds or spammable comments. |
| **Streak / scheduled event** | **10** | Server-backed attendance across distinct days and/or official scheduled event proof. No idle-online timer rewards; missed day cannot mint an invented proof. Event score overrides require an explicit approved rule. |

**TOTAL** = integer 0–100 daily Championship Clout. Daily board compares this day's total. Weekly = sum of its distinct official UTC days; quarterly = sum of its days; yearly = sum of its days. Retain underlying event evidence, but materialize small derived period totals for cheap reads. Duplicate syncs cannot increase the daily score, replays/returns cannot consume multiple slots, and points may only increase after server-verified improvement of an eligible best result until a period closes. For a tiny player base, use **fixed/versioned per-game skill thresholds and minimal valid gameplay**, not raw live-percentiles that wildly fluctuate with 2–5 participants.

**Tie breakers:** higher verified total; then more distinct eligible gameplay titles in period; then more verified active days; then earliest final qualifying server timestamp; then stable verified Telegram ID. The source policy version and actual tie rules must be stored with the archived board. A private test cohort must verify fairness before production activation.

This is the **default non-economic Championship formula selected for beta build planning**. Numbers may be tuned from sample gameplay, but never silently during an active competition. Commit a named immutable policy version and apply scoring changes at **next period boundary** (or explicitly announce/archive a beta reset). Economy impacts outside this non-spendable Clout ledger still require #1513/#1478 authorization.

Keep separate existing **Best Run / Overall / Accuracy** specialist boards from #1513 A01/A02. This 0–100 Clout championship is an additional *cross-game* layer, not an alternative accuracy implementation.

## 6. Verified source registry (authoritative eligibility matrix)

Each adapter MUST read a **server-owned immutable event/receipt**, prove the linked owner and a real qualifying outcome, and declare its verification class. First release should prioritize sources that already have receipts.

| Source | Provenance/adapter requirement | Initial Clout disposition |
|---|---|---|
| **Moonpet care, Daily Journey, Weekly Journey** | Accepted telegram_pet_events + source pet_id, owner, saved day/week/season; read Growth Mark/Crest unique awards where relevant. Per-pet week is not ISO Clout week. | **First pilot**: mission/variety, never raw Pet XP → raw Clout |
| **Moonpet Contracts / bosses / final Legendary** | Verified saved completed run / boss result / permanent progression receipt; no reward on failure/abandon. Year-long Legendary success is permanent Hall of Fame honor; optional one-off quarterly recognition. | **First pilot** for receipt-backed completions; preserve existing unlimited Contract *plays* |
| **Telegram /daily** | Existing awardCommunityXp daily_claim once-per-UTC-day receipt; accepted and linked. | **First pilot** in small engagement budget; does NOT grant 1,000 Arcade XP |
| **Website wiki interactions** | Genuine signed linked user, real published page registry + actual citation ID; moderation/validity and unique source receipt. No fictional page_id/cite_id spam. | **After page/citation validity gate**, limited engagement credit |
| **Dead Run** | Active server-ended ranked session, settled score and verified movement/action evidence, one best qualifying result per title/day. Handle spoofable GPS cautiously; optional game, never mandatory for broad Clout. | **Next pilot after abuse/sync tests** |
| **NBG London** | Saved replay-verified run, server-computed XP/time, finish receipt; ensure input replay cannot be trivially reused for fresh receipts, and reconcile trusted_xp/verified_run_count vs total_xp/run_count before any *prize* logic. | **Next pilot after replay-reuse regression**; NBG game XP remains game metric |
| **Eight main Arcade games** | Game runtime acceptance + independent challenge/run proof or server-signed single-use trusted source receipt. Telegram auth alone and a submitted high score do not prove play. | **Read legacy boards; NO new official Championship points** until their individual proof adapters pass |
| **Block Topia Street Signal independent board** | Separate KV leaderboard; signed identity != server-verified skill. Require genuine run authority; no double credit for the same Arcade action. | **Not eligible initially** |
| **Faction contributions / faction XP / player mastery / generic daily progress APIs** | Currently accept client numbers in important routes. Cannot use as Championship source without verifiable upstream events; do not infer official receipts from acceptance alone. | **Excluded until secured or strictly derived** |
| **Future #1069 Kaiju group / #1071–#1072 World War/Plague / #1513 events** | Provider owns match/event settlement and emits immutable result ID; Clout reads and validates. | **Interface only**, no gameplay implementation here |

**Source definitions must include:** source system, source event type, canonical owner ID, accepted state, durable event ID, first earned timestamp, verifier version, rule/policy version, source score/metric, optional pet_id, source season key, provider's receipt/cap semantics, Clout categories it may qualify for, invalidation state and audit reference. No session-token or Telegram secrets in public Clout rows.

Do not reinterpret verified Moonpet XP as Arcade XP, or Dead Run's game-local XP as Community XP. Existing Community and Arcade balances continue behaving under their own contracts.

## 7. Lightweight D1 Championship event bridge (not a replacement game engine)

**Recommended implementation:** one additive, minimal, append-only Championship source-claim table + daily/weekly/quarterly/annual projections in current production D1. Exact SQL is a child PR deliverable after inspecting existing schemas and migration numbering. No new KV or queue unless measured.

Required properties:

- Unique authoritative key **(source_system, source_event_id, owner_telegram_id, policy_version, qualifying_effect)** or equivalent fixed natural key. A retry returns the same verdict; no double Clout or duplicated badge.
- Worker recomputes score effects from a **D1 source receipt/approved provider record**, checks account ownership + anti-cheat, status and real window; browser payload is a *request for synchronization*, never a clout_delta/mission_target/raw score source.
- If effect maps to multiple declared buckets, separate effect keys make each explicit and idempotent; same source may satisfy a mission AND skill policy where documented, not multiplied arbitrarily.
- For counters/bests store source identity, policy_version, validated score and maximum eligible best. Corrections/revocations must be explicit, audited and recalculated atomically; prevent unordered replay regressions.
- An accepted source receipt and Championship effect must commit atomically **where one D1 writer owns both**, or use read-and-claim with a guarded exactly-once projection where the event already committed. Fail closed on missing/unavailable source, partial row or banned identity.
- Batch/D1 uniqueness protects simultaneous different devices. Store audit timestamp and original source timestamp. Preserve past periods; never delete old score rows or retroactively re-award spendable XP.
- Aggregations must read D1 indexed by (period_type, period_key, telegram_id) or preaggregate deterministically; avoid reading every game history on each public page view. Keep leaderboard queries cheap for a small community; cache public reads briefly only if invalidated/TTL clearly defined.
- No per-frame server calls, constant re-polling, daily N×users cron or long-running database scans. Include inexpensive recovery/reconciliation for interrupted one-off projections.

**API contract (names illustrative, review existing route collisions before choosing):**
- GET public/current Championship season metadata with UTC reset deadlines and policy version.
- GET public daily/weekly/quarterly/annual board with ranking basis, source status, player name and no sensitive IDs.
- POST linked /me or state read with signed Telegram proof; returns eligible sources, current verified Clout, badges and next available suggestions.
- Optional POST sync for a *reference to an existing authoritative receipt only*; no direct award, score, claim amount, or mission target field.
- Admin-only archive/recompute/audit endpoints only if genuinely necessary; do not expose a client-settable admin/manual top-up.

## 8. Repair obvious competition-write authority weaknesses — SCOPE / compatibility

**Before an official source is eligible**, address or isolate these current endpoints. Preserve existing client compatibility and historical balances; do not zero wallets or withdraw rank without a transparent beta provenance policy.

- workers/leaderboard-worker.js POST score + meta: accepts verified Telegram identity but client-provided score/meta/timestamp; does not attest to actual completed gameplay. Do not count those rows as verified Championship Clout, even when returning accepted=true.
- workers/moonboys-api/worker.js POST /arcade/progression/sync: validates auth and anti-farm/caps, but accepts raw_score, meta_points and client_run_id; these are not official proof. Restrict new competitive authority to server-issued receipt, migrate clients safely; do not suddenly strand legitimate current players.
- worker.js /faction/earn, /faction/signal/contribute, /player/mastery/update and /player/daily-missions/progress: browser-supplied numbers can alter standings/claims. Make Championship rewards derive only from **actual source actions**. Separate current/future security remediation for legacy systems with regression coverage.
- workers/blocktopia-leaderboard/worker.js: independent score API also accepts signed user-declared score; preserve its existing specialist board but do not mark as proof without a trusted game source.
- NBG: no switch enabling prizes based solely on flags; verify replay uniqueness, period trust fields, and full real-browser run before integrating. Keep NBG_LONDON_PRIZES_RELEASED false until separate explicit sign-off (and decide whether any old spendable XP prize model is being retired in favor of badge-only competition).
- Website wiki: validate real page/citation catalogs and approved linked action before rewarding Clout. Existing wiki 10 Community XP mission rule is separate and should not silently change.

**Anti-cheat proportionate to private beta:** unique source receipts, signed owner, realistic per-game proof where needed, minimum gameplay duration/action evidence, no score timestamps from client, diminishing rank effect for repeated easy events, manual moderator review for abuse. Do **not** add costly fraud vendors, complex real-time telemetry for every game, IP-derived identities, forced GPS, or punitive global XP wipes. Record suspected fraudulent/unverified separately, and allow appeals/corrections.

## 9. Retention loop and UX (24/7 engagement, not compulsory online timers)

Player-facing loop: **play eligible game → saved/verified result → daily mission + Clout credits → visible next action during cooldown → weekly/quarterly progress → badge/Hall of Fame**.

- One daily "Today's Clout" widget on existing System Hub / Games / Moonpet Missions summary / Telegram bot entry, not four competing HUDs. Link through existing site-shell (issue #903). No new duplicate navigation.
- Give **three server-selected daily objectives** across available activities, and weekly goals, but do **not** replace Moonpet's 7/7 checklist, 3/5 Daily Journey, 5/5 Weekly Journey, Moonpet bounties, or #1513's planned shooting accuracy missions. Use one qualifying-event registry and display exactly which already-existing objective it also satisfies.
- During a Moonpet cooldown, recommend the next eligible available action from *current server cooldown and receipt state* (e.g., Arcade title, NBG, wiki, Moonpet Contracts, another allowed pet activity), and show exact cost/eligibility/claim/no-claim, reset countdown. An unavailable app or GPS-only mode never blocks all progress.
- Continue to let players play after XP caps: explain "practice / verified result / XP at cap / Clout best already counted / next reset" instead of hiding the game or promising unlimited awards.
- UI states: **practice only**, **verified**, **saved**, **already counted**, **awaiting verification**, **not eligible**, **blocked**, **unavailable/retry**. Never label stale localStorage preview as "live". Keep full reward/history semantics.
- Responsive 360px/390px and desktop; readable color-independent rank/status, keyboard/Telegram mini-app navigation, short polling, offline fallback. Public anonymous scoreboard reads only. No token/precise GPS exposure.
- One shared "How Points Work" source-of-truth guide is **already owned by #1513 B02**. Supply this issue's Clout formula and reason codes as inputs; do not create a competing guide route.
- Event or accuracy UI from #1513 A01–A03 should reuse this projection interface **once shipped**, without double counting or bypassing its existing organizer/moderator gates.

## 10. Delivery: small independent PRs, in this sequence

### PR 0 — Evidence/contract and beta decisions (NO production mutation)
- [ ] Rebase on current main; read AGENTS.md, #1513, #1478, #903, #1458 and both Moonpet current docs; reconcile stale 90-day/60/10 statements against current 365/240/44 runtime before modifying public copy.
- [ ] Audit actual D1 schema, receipt ownership, Worker flags/deployed version, current player-visible boards, representative new + returning signed Telegram test account (do not expose identifiers).
- [ ] Publish source eligibility table with **EXISTS/PARTIAL/MISSING/LIVE BUG/NEEDS DESIGN/VERIFIED IN PROD**, route proof, count/window semantics, code and screenshot references.
- [ ] Record final approved Clout v1 weights/eligibility and no-financial-prize commitment; reserve unique API/table names avoiding faction clout collisions. **No gameplay code in this PR.**

### PR 1 — Additive Championship Clout ledger + deterministic read-only projector
- [ ] Versioned source registry, reusable receipt-validation helper, single-use effect keys, D1 uniqueness, small source/period indexes, dry-run policy calculator, public scoring contract.
- [ ] UTC day/week/calendar-quarter/year buckets, active/current + archived leaderboard reads, tie breakers, deterministic reload and idempotent backfill **only of explicitly validated** historic evidence (prefer start-from-launch for ranking; grandfather old records as legacy-visible).
- [ ] Migration preflight, compatibility and rollback test; **do not apply production migration inside PR**. No Arcade/Moonpet XP rate changes.

### PR 2 — Verified core pilot, available to newcomers without a pet
- [ ] Server-receipt integration: existing Telegram /daily claim; Moonpet accepted Daily/Weekly Journey/Contracts/verified boss or milestone sources; genuine validated wiki sources (after page/citation guard).
- [ ] Feature flag; include a non-Moonpet participation path (linked Telegram action + eligible wiki) for players below the 1,000 lifetime Arcade XP adoption gate.
- [ ] Live test duplicate awards, switch pet, old-quarter claim and same source across missions; no interference with 3 pet slots, wallet or existing 7/7 and 3/5 and 5/5 counters.

### PR 3 — Trusted scored games (separate source adapters, NOT rewrites)
- [ ] NBG: one-replay-per-accepted-run tests, prevent cheap reused input sequences; period trust-field parity; read-only existing game boards preserved; **no spendable prize payout**.
- [ ] Dead Run: true ranked/final settled source; best-per-player metric projection; no GPS requirement to participate in the broader Championship; no duplicate XP or spurious Community XP conversion.
- [ ] Main eight-game Arcade + independent Block Topia: adapters only when real run verification/receipt issuance exists; coordinate directly with #1513 A01/A02 rather than independently implementing it.
- [ ] Each source has explicit enabled/disabled status. Do not fake a combined board from client-submitted numbers while adapters are incomplete.

### PR 4 — Clout leaderboards, badges, Hall of Fame and cooldown-aware guidance
- [ ] Present compact daily/weekly/quarterly/annual standings and rank basis, "My Clout" break-down, badge/titles, period end/reset and history.
- [ ] Keep specialist Moonpet/NBG/DeadRun/Arcade ranks; don't hide old boards. No double labels "XP" for non-spendable Clout.
- [ ] Cooldown-specific next action using existing server states; clear Claim/Recorded/Unverified notices, don't reward screen time or page reloads.
- [ ] Coordinate shared HUD with #903; guide with #1513 B02; Moonpet menus with #1478; no competing menu/framework.

### PR 5 — Production verification, canary and controlled activation
- [ ] Run existing domain CI, issue-required targeted regressions, D1 SQLite concurrency/rollback tests, Worker+Pages provenance checks, 360px/390px/desktop browser tests, real signed Telegram new/returning account smoke.
- [ ] Backup & record current D1 + KV/score history; deploy migration only after reviewed PR and **before** matching Worker; stage/read-only flags first; activate pilot only after explicit GK release approval.
- [ ] Check live accumulation/rollover at UTC day, ISO week, calendar quarter, leap year, year end; old pet and legacy Arcade 90-day windows remain intact.
- [ ] Observe lightweight error logs, reconcile 3 sample verified user journeys, verify no unexpected Arcade spendable or Community XP award, publish rollback strategy and what has/has not been released.
- [ ] Add links to child PRs and production evidence here; keep this issue open until GK confirms all selected phases or deliberately defers any remaining adapters.

**Parallel work:** agents may work independently on issue inventory/tests or per-game adapter design, but one designated owner coordinates the **D1 schema + shared reward authority**. Any two PRs touching the same Worker route/ledger must sequence through review; no simultaneous competing migration or direct edits to main.

## 11. Acceptance tests (must be executable, not checkbox theatre)

### Trust/abuse
- [ ] Browser sends invented million-XP or forged meta and claims a fresh client ID: **zero new Championship Clout**, no extra Community/Arcade XP or faction power.
- [ ] Repeat exact source event 100 times, across browser sessions and concurrent requests: exactly **one** effect per declared category; stored period total unchanged by repeats.
- [ ] Different Telegram account submits another account's run/pet/mission receipt: rejected; no cross-account membership or pet ownership leakage.
- [ ] Tampered mission ID, target, amount, fake game score, fake date, stale/expired Telegram link: cannot mint Clout.
- [ ] Nonexistent published-page slug or nonexistent citation ID cannot generate wiki Championship Clout.
- [ ] No signed identity: public boards visible; no permanent score mutations.
- [ ] Rate-limit and ban-state unavailability fail closed; corrected score/ban status supports audited rollback/recalculation without double points.

### Gameplay fairness
- [ ] Heavy player repeats one easy action 1,000 times: can still play; no unlimited new daily Championship points.
- [ ] Skilled player with one verified game qualifies and can place; variety bonus rewards diversity without requiring Moonpet/GPS/paid item.
- [ ] Two games with vastly different native point scales produce comparable **versioned normalized** skill values.
- [ ] Moonpet lifetime and all event receipts survive a quarter boundary; daily/weekly/Crest/Mark attribution follows original source time, not delayed retry time.
- [ ] A non-Moonpet newcomer can join and rank, while the 1,000 lifetime Arcade XP pet-entry gate stays unchanged.
- [ ] Moonpet year-long Legendary remains 365/240/44; after quarterly reset the same pet retains all Marks/Crests/evolution, achievements and optional future annual Hall of Fame.
- [ ] Existing NBG gameplay score can be saved without enabling its spendable Arcade prize cron; duplicate/reused replay does not create new eligible prize proof.
- [ ] Dead Run independently credited Arcade wallet remains unchanged; no new Community XP is silently added just from displaying Clout.
- [ ] Legacy unverified Arcade/meta score stays visible in existing specialist boards, but does not become "verified" Championship score without a source event.

### Calendar/UX and budget
- [ ] Day 23:59:59.999 UTC vs 00:00:00.000, week Sunday→Monday, Mar31→Apr1, Dec31→Jan1, source earned-at vs delayed claim all allocate to documented periods with stable ties.
- [ ] 2-user and 10-user boards behave sensibly (no live population percentile instability); stable top-three/badge snapshots settle once.
- [ ] Same action contributes at most its declared effects to Clout, missions and faction proof; no accidental "triple Community XP".
- [ ] On cooldown, shown alternative action is actually eligible when tapped; server remains final authority; no forced online screen-time grind.
- [ ] No duplicate NAV or pages, infinite timers, per-frame API traffic, D1 full history scan per public GET, novel vendor/billing dependency, or leaking private Telegram/GPS data.
- [ ] UI explains precisely when counts are practice, verified, already counted, inactive or waiting for the next UTC reset.

## 12. Release and handoff protocol (all agents MUST follow)

For every child issue/PR post a short status comment **to THIS issue** using:

~~~text
Work package: PR N / source ID(s) / overlaps #1513 Axx Bxx DRxx, #1478 Hxx
Current main SHA; Worker/Pages provenance; prod D1 migration ledger status:
Status: EXISTS | PARTIAL | MISSING | LIVE BUG | NEEDS DESIGN | VERIFIED IN PROD
Authoritative source row + receipt ID type + owner + UTC period:
Exact game/API/DB/JS files touched:
In scope / out of scope and canonical rules preserved:
Fraud/replay/double-award/clock/cross-account tests:
Test commands + observed results; CI run links:
New D1 migrations? backup/apply/ledger order:
Worker deploy? Pages deploy? VPS? Telegram menu?:
Live signed Telegram verification and actual result (or UNVERIFIED):
Economic/score-policy change? Approved source issue / decision:
Rollback + old balance/history preservation:
Open conflicts / next work package:
~~~

Mandatory repository checks: AGENTS.md, current CI workflow and the correct Worker runbooks. Workflows/PR labels don't prove production deployed. Changes that touch Arcade XP, Moonpet Gold/costs, faction influence, prizes or legacy score calculation require the separate approval/QA required by #1513/#1478. Do not change protected wiki lore or brand canon under #1458.

**Agent STOP conditions:** missing source-owner proof; unclear currency vs Clout scope; D1 migration not on current migration head; reward/period ambiguity; read failure being treated as zero; missing real Telegram auth; conflicting PR touching same Worker; changes to permanent pet lifecycle, pet-entry/slot costs, 90-day legacy ranking, live spendable XP payout or new real-value reward. Stop, annotate here, and request a narrowly scoped decision. Do not invent a resolution.

## 13. Definition of done

- [ ] At least newcomer/Telegram + genuine Moonpet + one server-verified scored game have **live verified** points on a single Daily/Weekly/Quarterly/Annual non-spendable Championship Clout board; unsupported game adapters show honest "not yet verified".
- [ ] Cross-game source event dedupe, one-owner proof, fair normalized skill, clock/freeze and history-preserving rollback pass deterministic and signed production smoke tests.
- [ ] Moonpet 365-day Legendary path (240/44) and quarter-competition separation stay intact; zero lost/duplicated Pet XP, Arcade XP, Community XP, wallet balances, Marks, Crests or pets.
- [ ] No non-economic Clout points leak into spendable Arcade XP, Gold, wallet or other in-game economies; NBG's legacy XP prize cron remains locked unless separately approved.
- [ ] Players can play 24/7, clearly understand skill/mission/community contribution and see useful available cooldown alternatives.
- [ ] No duplicated implementation of #1513, #1478, #903 or new future games; canonical guides and handover comment include exact status and final provenance.
- [ ] All child work is merged/deployed **only after review/approval**, with rollback and real signed-account results. No claims of "complete" until those steps are documented.

### Owner intent / final product definition

**One identity, distinct XP systems, one non-spendable Championship Clout ranking based on genuine saved achievements. Moonpet is the permanent year-long anchor; daily/weekly/quarterly/annual competitions reset only standings, never pets. Endless play is welcome; fake credits and score replays are not. Low-cost, small-community beta — no casino, no real-value prize system, no infrastructure overbuild.**

**This is the authoritative planning issue for the *Clout integration layer only*. Issues #1513 and #1478 remain owners of their existing gameplay and economy roadmaps.**

source_text:
N8n + MirrorFly Developer for Video Conferencing Automation
Hi everyone, 
 I’m looking for an experienced automation developer who can help me build a video conferencing automation system using n8n + MirrorFly + API integrations. 
 This is a paid freelance project with clear requirements and a defined scope. 
 I’ll keep this as concise and technical as possible so you know exactly what’s involved. 
   Project Overview 
 I need to build an automated video conferencing workflow using n8n and MirrorFly that will: 
 
 
 Create video meetings automatically based on predefined triggers. 
 
 
 Generate meeting details and share them with participants. 
 
 
 Schedule meetings using calendar integrations. 
 
 
 Send meeting invitations and reminders through email or messaging services. 
 
 
 Manage meeting related events through webhooks and APIs. 
 
 
 (Optional add-on) Automate meeting recordings and post meeting notifications. 
 
 
 All of this needs to run through n8n workflows, with MirrorFly providing the video conferencing capabilities. 
   Core Requirements 
   1. MirrorFly Video Conferencing Integration 
 
 
 Integrate MirrorFly Video Call API and SDK. 
 
 
 Create and manage video meetings through supported APIs. 
 
 
 Generate or retrieve meeting joining details. 
 
 
 Handle meeting events through webhooks or callbacks where supported. 
 
 
 Support one to one and group video calls. 
 
 
 Connect MirrorFly with n8n using HTTP requests, webhooks, or a custom integration where required. 
 
 
   2. Meeting Scheduling and Management 
 
 
 Trigger meeting creation from form submissions, CRM updates, or other events. 
 
 
 Integrate with Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar scheduling services. 
 
 
 Send meeting invitations to participants. 
 
 
 Schedule automatic reminders before meetings. 
 
 
 Handle meeting cancellations and rescheduling. 
 
 
   3. Automated Notifications 
 
 
 Send meeting details through email or supported messaging services. 
 
 
 Notify participants when a meeting is scheduled, updated, or cancelled. 
 
 
 Send reminders at predefined intervals. 
 
 
 Support optional Slack or Microsoft Teams notifications. 
 
 
 Use structured data to pass meeting details between workflows. 
 
 
   4. CRM Integration 
 Integrate with HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive to: 
 
 
 Trigger meeting workflows based on CRM events. 
 
 
 Associate meetings with relevant contacts or deals. 
 
 
 Update CRM records when meetings are scheduled or completed. 
 
 
 Store meeting details and supported recording links. 
 
 
   5. Post Meeting Automation 
 
 
 Trigger workflows when a meeting ends, using supported events or callbacks. 
 
 
 Send follow up emails to participants. 
 
 
 Update CRM records with meeting status. 
 
 
 Store meeting metadata and recording links when available. 
 
 
 Trigger additional workflows based on meeting outcomes. 
 
 
   6. Optional Premium Feature: Meeting Recording and Streaming 
 If you have experience with video recording and streaming integrations, please mention it. 
 This feature may include: 
 
 
 Automating meeting recording through supported MirrorFly capabilities. 
 
 
 Retrieving recording details or links. 
 
 
 Triggering workflows when recordings become available. 
 
 
 Integrating supported RTMP or HLS streaming workflows where required. 
 
 
   Tech Stack 
 You must be comfortable with: 
 
 
  n8n:  Webhooks, HTTP Request nodes, conditional logic, API integrations, and asynchronous workflows. 
 
 
  MirrorFly:  Video Call API, SDK integration, and supported meeting capabilities. 
 
 
  Calendar APIs:  Google Calendar, Calendly, or similar services. 
 
 
  CRM integrations:  HubSpot, Salesforce, or Pipedrive. 
 
 
  Backend development:  JavaScript or other technologies when a custom integration is required. 
 
 
   Deliverables 
 
 
 Fully configured n8n workflows. 
 
 
 MirrorFly integration with the required video conferencing functionality. 
 
 
 Automated meeting scheduling and notification workflows. 
 
 
 Documentation for future maintenance. 
 
 
 One handover and training session. 
 
 
 30 days of bug support after delivery. 
 
 
   Budget 
 The budget is flexible depending on experience, but roughly: 
 
 
  Base system:  £800–£1,000 
 
 
  Advanced features and integrations:  £800–£1,200 
 
 
 Payment can be arranged through an agreed platform. 
   How to Apply 
 Please reply with: 
 
 
 Your experience with n8n and API integrations. 
 
 
 Your experience integrating video conferencing APIs or SDKs, preferably MirrorFly. 
 
 
 Examples of similar automation projects. 
 
 
 Your availability. 
 
 
 Estimated delivery timeline. 
 
 
 Your pricing for the base system. 
 
 
 Your pricing for advanced features and integrations. 
 
 
 I’m ready to start immediately with the right developer. 
 Thanks!

source_text:
Gmail Trigger skips emails when Gmail's internalDate is in the future (follow-up to #24539)
<!-- Please follow the template below. Skip the questions that are not relevant to you. -->

## Describe the problem/error/question

The Gmail Trigger silently skips emails when Gmail's `internalDate` of an incoming email lies in the future. This is the same bug as GitHub issue #24539 (closed by the stale bot; the reporter confirmed on 2026-09-22 it still happens on 2.39.9). The cursor logic is unchanged on current `master`.

The trigger sets `staticData.lastTimeChecked` to the newest date among the messages it fetched:

```ts
let effectiveLastTimeChecked = Math.floor(Math.max(lastEmailDate, +startDate)) || +startDate;
```

`getEmailDateAsSeconds()` already prefers `internalDate` over the `Date:` header, but that does not help: Gmail itself can set `internalDate` in the future. In our case a customer replied from a gmail.com address to our Google Workspace mailbox, and the sender's clock was about 10 minutes ahead:

| Source | Value (UTC) |
|---|---|
| `Received:` by mx.google.com | 14:04:51 |
| `X-Received:` | 14:04:50 |
| Trigger poll that picked it up | 14:05:18 |
| `Date:` header | 14:14:50 |
| `internalDate` returned by the Gmail API | **14:14:50** |

From then on every poll queried `after:<14:14:50>`, which returns nothing. All Gmail Triggers on that mailbox were blind for ~10 minutes, and every email that arrived in that window was never processed. The cursor recovered by itself once the clock passed 14:14:50, but the skipped emails are never picked up again. With a larger clock skew the gap grows: we saw 72 minutes in an earlier incident, and #24539 reports several hours.

**To reproduce**
1. Activate a workflow with a Gmail Trigger (v1.4, poll every minute).
2. Send an email to that mailbox from a client whose system clock is ahead (e.g. 15 minutes), for example via an IMAP/SMTP client against a gmail.com account.
3. The trigger fires once for that email. `lastTimeChecked` in the workflow's static data is now in the future.
4. Send a normal email before that future time. The trigger never fires for it.

**Expected behavior**
The cursor should never move past the time of the poll, for example:

```ts
const nowSeconds = Math.floor(+now);
effectiveLastTimeChecked = Math.min(effectiveLastTimeChecked, nowSeconds);
```

`possibleDuplicates` already covers the boundary, so the email with the future date would not be emitted twice.

## What is the error message (if any)?

None. That is the core of the problem: the trigger produces no executions and no errors while it skips emails.

## Please share your workflow/screenshots/recording

Any workflow with a Gmail Trigger reproduces it. Minimal example (credentials removed):

```
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "parameters": {
        "pollTimes": { "item": [{ "mode": "everyMinute" }] },
        "filters": {}
      },
      "type": "n8n-nodes-base.gmailTrigger",
      "typeVersion": 1.4,
      "position": [0, 0],
      "name": "Gmail Trigger"
    }
  ],
  "connections": {}
}
```

## Share the output returned by the last node

Trigger output for the offending email (simplified, other fields omitted):

```json
{
  "id": "1a178873d42e1349",
  "internalDate": "1793024090000"
}
```

`1793024090000` = 2026-10-26 14:14:50 UTC, while the email was received at 14:04:51 UTC and picked up by the poll at 14:05:18 UTC.

Static data of every trigger on that mailbox right after that poll:

```json
{ "lastTimeChecked": 1793024090 }
```

Beyond the Furrow: How the Modern Agricultural Oil Supplier Keeps British Farms Moving Forward
Agriculture in the UK represents one of the most demanding commercial environments in the country, where unpredictable weather, strict seasonal deadlines, and heavy machinery converge. Tractors, combine harvesters, grain driers, and processing equipment cannot afford unexpected downtime when crops are ripe or fields require urgent preparation. Securing a dependable agricultural oil supplier ensures that daily work never grinds to a sudden halt, keeping British food production resilient, efficient, and prepared for future operational challenges.

### Dependable Bulk Deliveries Across British Farmland
Timely [farm fuel delivery](https://compassenergy.co.uk/agricultural-fuel-supplier/) serves as the backbone of modern agribusiness. When harvest windows open under clear skies, machinery runs around the clock, consuming vast amounts of fuel at an intense pace. Partnering with a dedicated bulk farm fuel specialist provides continuous access to the vital energy reserves needed during peak cultivation and harvest windows. An established agricultural diesel supplier understands these agricultural cycles intimately, scheduling red diesel delivery routes to match local harvest patterns so storage tanks never run dry.

Choosing an experienced farm fuel supplier means gaining a partner that monitors regional supply chains, anticipates market volatility, and navigates narrow rural roads with suitable tankers. Efficient fuel delivery guarantees that every field tractor, telehandler, and irrigation unit maintains uninterrupted momentum throughout every planting and harvesting campaign.

### Enhancing Performance and Protecting Expensive Machinery
Modern engines demand high standards of cleanliness and thermal stability. While standard UK farming fuel provides the necessary combustion, integrating premium farm fuel additives into bulk storage tanks significantly extends machinery longevity. These specialist additives combat common issues such as condensation build-up, microbial contamination, and injector fouling, ensuring tractors perform at peak torque while keeping fuel consumption economical.

Protecting expensive capital investments requires clean fuel systems, especially during prolonged winter storage periods. With high-grade red diesel suppliers offering advanced additives pre-mixed or in bulk containers, farm managers can prevent costly injector repairs, reduce unburned emissions, and maintain high thermal efficiency across their entire fleet.

### Embracing Cleaner Alternatives with Low-Emission Solutions
Environmental stewardship is reshaping agriculture in the UK, urging producers to lower their carbon footprints without sacrificing mechanical output. Forward-thinking farming operations increasingly turn to hydrotreated vegetable oil as a fossil-free substitute for conventional gas oil. Sourcing from an accredited [HVO Fuel Supplier](https://compassenergy.co.uk/hvo-fuel/) allows farm managers to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by up to ninety percent using existing diesel engines without costly mechanical conversions.

Integrating renewable HVO Fuel into everyday operations demonstrates how farming in the UK continues to evolve, balancing high output with environmental care. A trusted agricultural oil supplier provides both standard gas oil and paraffinic alternatives, giving agricultural businesses the flexibility to transition smoothly toward net-zero targets at their own speed.

### Integrated Distribution for Barn, Mill, and Family Home
Many British holdings are diverse businesses encompassing livestock barns, grain drying complexes, processing units, holiday lets, and residential farmhouses. A comprehensive industrial oil supplier meets this diverse demand by providing specialised industrial heating oil alongside commercial lubricants and gas oil. Commercial grain drying facilities, workshops, and livestock sheds depend heavily on consistent deliveries of heavy-duty industrial heating oil to maintain steady temperatures and protect grain stores from spoilage.

At the same time, maintaining farm life extends beyond the fields to the farmhouse itself. Choosing an agricultural distributor that doubles as a dependable domestic oil supplier simplifies logistics by combining farm and household energy management into one trusted relationship. Instead of coordinating multiple delivery companies, estate managers rely on one consolidated domestic oil delivery for domestic heating oil and domestic fuel delivery. Reliable domestic oil suppliers understand that keeping farm cottages and family dwellings warm through harsh winter freezes is just as crucial as keeping harvesters active across the fields.

### Cultivating Lasting Reliability Across Modern Operations
Success across British farms rests on dependable operational partnerships that deliver year after year. Sourcing all liquid energy through a dedicated agricultural oil supplier ensures complete transparency, superior product consistency, and rapid delivery when seasonal schedules tighten. From high-grade tractor fuels and eco-friendly renewable alternatives to heating solutions for rural homesteads, dependable distribution keeps farm businesses robust, productive, and equipped for every season ahead.

- [x] Correct the **N4-backed, N8-titled** original hidden trial listing before any public use.
