[Warehouse] P9-05 · Sourcing — RFQ to many suppliers, vendor quotations with versions, comparative statement with L1 and the approved award
Part of #547 · Module **`warehouse-trade`** · Migrations **V550040, V551050, V551051** · Screens **WS-288 RFQs**, **WS-289 Vendor Quotations**, **WS-290 Comparative Statements**

Contract: [`docs/contracts/trade-rfq-award.contract.md`](../docs/contracts/trade-rfq-award.contract.md). Mirror rows M7–M12 (the sales side is p9-08).

## Scope
- Tables per contract §0 (`V550040`).
- RFQ issue renders **one print job per invitee** (`TRA-UNR-01`); response tracking; close bids.
- Vendor quotation capture with versions (`supersedes_id`), charges, alternatives, free-of-charge;
  supplier document attachment through platform documents.
- Sealed mode (`warehouse.trade.rfq.sealed_until_due`, default false, `OD-37`): masking happens in the
  **backend response**, not in the page.
- `ComparativeStatementService` computes the matrix (`TRA-T4-01`) including vendor grade (blank until
  p9-12) and contract rate (blank until p9-06); refresh on staleness (`TRA-T4-02`). **One statement per
  RFQ × currency** (`currency_code`, partial uk among statements not `REJECTED`); quotations in another
  currency are shown unranked and are awardable only on their own currency's statement (`TRA-GRD-10`).
- Award editor, split award, reasons; `TradeApprovable` for `CS` with `non_l1_award` condition. Exits:
  rejected → `REJECTED` (terminal, RFQ back to `BIDS_CLOSED`, a new statement may be prepared,
  `TRA-T1-13`); returned → `DRAFT` (`-14`); an input change on a `SUBMITTED` statement returns its request
  (`TAM-T1-08a`). RFQ cancel is allowed from `BIDS_CLOSED` / `EVALUATION` with no approved statement.
- Vendor quotation revise is allowed from `SUBMITTED` **and `EXPIRED`** (a validity extension, `TRA-T1-08`).
- Award targets include an **OPEN PO** (rate fixed, quantity open) as well as FIXED / BLANKET PO and a rate
  contract (`TRA-T4-03`).
- `AwardService.onApproved` drafts targets (`TRA-T4-03`) — FIXED / OPEN / BLANKET PO need p9-07, rate
  contract needs p9-06; a target type whose task has not landed is not offered.
- `TradeRfqJob` (`TRA-T3-01`…`-03`), settings `warehouse.trade.rfq.min_suppliers` (3), `rfq.reminder_days` (2).
- Prints `RFQ`, `COMPARATIVE_STATEMENT`: this task seeds their minimal default templates (FR-615); p9-14 adds final layouts.
- Permissions / menus (*Purchasing — Sourcing*) / grids / scopes / caches (`V551050`, `V551051`).
  `wht_comparative_statements:approve` approves the award — **no `:award` verb** is seeded.
  Notification kind `TRADE_VQ_EXPIRED` and the RFQ reminder kinds (FRD-TRADE §12b).

## Requirements closed
`FR-562` `FR-563` `FR-564` `FR-565` `FR-566` `FR-567` `FR-568` `FR-569`

## Scenarios closed
`WH-SC-485` (invite half) `WH-SC-505` … `WH-SC-514` · `WH-SC-566` `WH-SC-573`

## Closes
`RM-002`

## Traps
- **Ranking is backend-only and per currency** (`TRA-UNR-02`); the page renders the payload, it does not sort prices.
- Landed price excludes tax (`TRD-06`); charge allocation basis per charge.
- A revised quotation after CS preparation makes the CS stale; submitting a stale CS is refused.
- An alternative item never displaces the RFQ item in rank.
- The CS detail is a matrix — not a `DynamicDataTable`; the list page is.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Every `TRA-*` row tested; `WH-SC-510` arithmetic asserted to the paisa
- [ ] Sealed masking verified at the API (a second buyer's GET returns no price)
- [ ] Award approval moves PR allocations exactly (`TRA-T4-04`)
- [ ] Prints carry only the invitee's name

## Blocked on
`p9-02`, `p9-03`, `p9-04`. Award targets: `p9-06`, `p9-07`.

## Definition of done
Merged; reviewer + functional-reviewer clean against `trade-rfq-award`.

**Railway Electrification and Energy Storage Requirements Support Market Growth**

The growing emphasis on railway electrification and energy-efficient transportation is creating demand for advanced battery technologies. Railway operators and rolling stock manufacturers are evaluating energy storage solutions that can support operational flexibility and improve the efficiency of railway systems. Lithium battery technology is attracting attention because of its potential applications in modern railway traction and onboard energy management.

Railway traction systems operate under demanding conditions, requiring batteries capable of delivering dependable power across varying operational cycles. Factors such as charging performance, energy density, operating temperature, service life and safety characteristics influence technology selection. Manufacturers are therefore focusing on battery solutions that can address the technical requirements of railway applications while supporting reliable long-term operation.

Another important consideration is the development of railway systems operating across different infrastructure environments. Battery-based traction technologies can provide an alternative energy source in applications where conventional electrification infrastructure may be limited or where additional operational flexibility is required. Their suitability depends on route characteristics, energy requirements, charging infrastructure and rolling stock configuration.

The increasing adoption of advanced railway technologies is also encouraging manufacturers to improve battery integration, monitoring and management capabilities. Battery management systems, thermal management and charging controls are important elements in ensuring reliable operation. These technological considerations are expected to remain relevant as railway operators assess the role of lithium battery systems in future transportation infrastructure.

• Demand for energy-efficient transportation: Railway operators are exploring technologies that can improve energy utilization and operational efficiency.
• Battery-powered rolling stock: Interest in battery-based railway applications is creating opportunities for lithium battery system suppliers.

The market also faces challenges. Railway traction applications require batteries to meet demanding safety, durability and reliability requirements. Battery performance under changing temperatures, frequent operating cycles and demanding power requirements also remains an important consideration for manufacturers and railway operators.

The railway traction lithium battery system market is associated with the broader railway energy storage and electrification ecosystem. Market opportunities are influenced by rolling stock modernization, railway infrastructure investments, battery technology development and the operational requirements of railway networks.

Lithium battery system adoption depends on factors such as traction power requirements, energy storage capacity, charging arrangements, battery management technology and compatibility with railway equipment. These considerations influence product development and procurement decisions among railway operators and rolling stock manufacturers.

Regional market development is influenced by differences in railway infrastructure investment, electrification programs, transportation modernization priorities and the availability of supporting battery technologies. Countries investing in railway upgrades and advanced rolling stock present opportunities for manufacturers developing lithium battery solutions. However, adoption levels depend on infrastructure readiness, project economics, regulatory requirements and technical suitability for individual railway applications.

The competitive environment includes established battery manufacturers, railway technology providers and companies developing advanced energy storage solutions for transportation applications. **Key companies** covered in the report include **Saft, Forsee Power, Leclanché, Toshiba, Turntide Technologies, Siemens Mobility, Hitachi Rail, Stadler Rail, Alstom and CRRC**.

Companies operating in this market compete through battery technology development, product reliability, system integration capabilities, safety performance and long-term service support. Battery manufacturers focus on developing solutions that meet the demanding operational requirements of railway applications, while railway technology companies contribute through rolling stock development and system-level integration.

The presence of both specialized battery suppliers and established railway equipment manufacturers highlights the importance of collaboration across the value chain. As railway operators evaluate advanced energy storage technologies, suppliers with strong engineering capabilities, railway application expertise and dependable product performance are positioned to participate in emerging market opportunities.

> You don't actually have to handle I/O with the async runtime if you don't want. You _could_ just poll the futures yourself in a loop, which is rough
> You don't actually have to handle I/O with the async runtime if you don't want. You _could_ just poll the futures yourself in a loop, which is roughly the same as what happens if you just call the transition function in a loop for a manual state machine. How would the future get the I/O result then? > And likewise if you just keep calling the transition function with empty input you'll also busy-loop. This makes no sense, why would I ever want to do that? > but if you've got your own external notion of that That's a very big if. I said "easily" and this is not easy at all. Moreover it ignores the context: the SansIO/async/await code is generally a library written by a user, while the code that wants to use it is written by someone else entirely. Good luck sharing this external notion between the two! --- I agree that it would be ideal to have a way to automatically generate the state machine from straightforward looking code, and async/await kinda does this, but this usecase requires more flexibility than what async/await provides.

source_text:
I see a bit of a split in people in creative roles of all kinds (and this is something I had noted before LLMs made the contrast more stark). some peo
I see a bit of a split in people in creative roles of all kinds (and this is something I had noted before LLMs made the contrast more stark). some people get into it because they like the  process  of making the thing that they are making (in whole or in part). Others get into it because they have a thing that they want to exist in the world but no-one else has made it (I would also split this into people who just want the thing, or people who want to make something that crosses many domains and so want custom things that will fit into the whole). The former group tend to react with revulsion to automation, because it removes the part they like (though it may depend on what part is automated: most people will find some part of their work necessary but tedious). The latter are usually much more willing to embrace it, because it's the end result that they care about moreso than the process.

## 1. Exact KPI meaning

For every autonomous Matrix worker, including Librarians, **65% of the worker's evaluated performance/KPI** measures attributable contribution toward verified money-in or the evidenced removal of a real blocker on that path. The remaining **35%** measures the worker's existing governed mandate and responsibilities.

This is a performance-accountability weight, **not a 65% wall-clock, time, compute, staffing, activity, or blanket sales quota**. It does not expand a worker's mandate or transfer ownership. Contribution must be attributable, observable, and evidence-backed.

## 2. Outcome truth

Keep these states separate:
- **Verified money-in:** received/withdrawable funds or settlement independently verified.
- **Lifecycle progress:** qualified response, accepted work, contract, invoice/receivable, submission/award, delivery acceptance, or another source-backed state change.
- **Attributable enabling progress:** a worker removes a specific evidenced blocker directly preventing a money path.
- **Activity only:** wake, report, prompt edit, candidate list, draft, raw application, nominal bounty value, unaccepted deliverable, or unverified payment claim.

Activity alone is not money-in. Enabling progress must be labelled as progress, not cash. Do not double-count one outcome or assert causality without evidence.

## 3. Keep the 60/20/20 sourcing allocation separate

The existing **60/20/20** rule applies only to effort within opportunity sourcing/search:
- 60% real-value/direct-buyer work;
- 20% qualifying Micro-Matrix work;
- 20% maximum recruitment/platform-led sourcing.

It is not the 65% KPI or a Matrix-wide time/compute quota. Inbound and accepted offers are outside the sourcing allocation; do not delay them because a sourcing slice is full. Progress each from its furthest source-verified lifecycle stage using existing iSCOPE → PRI → Banker ownership where applicable.

## 4. Every-flight reporting

The current Blue State requires every run to state its objective, why it matters now, and its observable pass test before material work. Every post-flight report must state **PASS or FAIL**, why, proof/readback, the 65% KPI result, and one concrete next action. PASS requires all mandatory tests and independent readback. Any unmet or unknown required test means FAIL. Each run also includes the existing FORX 13-head review and routes its actionable results through existing Root Intake as Category B.

## 5. Existing ownership and acceptance conditions

- **ROOT/T-GOV:** governs/dispositions the supersession and keeps Blue State, this issue, and Intake Index aligned.
- **MASTER/LIBRARIAN + FORX:** verifies per-worker receipt and behavior samples; no universal-adoption claim from prompt text alone.
- **Each existing worker:** applies 65/35 semantics within its own mandate and separates activity, enabling progress, lifecycle progress, and money received.
- **Existing commercial owners:** preserve 60/20/20 and progress existing inbound/accepted opportunities truthfully.
- **Acceptance evidence:** current Blue State and this issue read back as 65%; Index points to the 65% artifact; Registry v1.2 root and all registered mandate payload hashes remain unchanged; per-worker behavioral samples are read back; money-in is credited only on independent settlement evidence.

**Current status:** Blue State and the 65% artifact are written and independently read back. This issue is being updated to the 65% target. Index and ROOT issue #31 must be read back after their updates. Matrix-wide worker adoption is not yet proven. No revenue is claimed from this governance change.

**Historical supersession chain:** 25%/75% → 33% request → 45% Owner request → **65% current Owner direction**. Historical artifacts are not deleted or rewritten to hide prior states.

This updates the existing Category A request, not a new queue or worker. The country-origin/legitimacy rule is applied only to income opportunities; it does not constrain continuity-drive mapping/noding/weighting.

Do not advance them unless sponsor/payer origin, live deadline, rules and payout are verified and expected net value beats direct buyer work.
- A PeoplePerHour AI automation listing advertising about USD $374 was not independently inspectable because the page served an anti-bot interstitial; the accessible card alone did not establish the buyer/payee identity or funding/escrow state. After that bounded verification attempt, **DISCARD rather than leave active HOLD**. No bid was made.
- Recent Reddit “for-hire” search results were supply-side developer adverts, not buyers offering to pay. Excluded as non-opportunities.

### Existing global crypto inventory
Latest confirmed first-party Agent Bounties snapshot in the existing Category A record is dated 11 Oct: 0 claimable, 0 verification-ready and $0 funded USDC; some nominal items were explicitly not verifier-ready. The 12 Oct external refresh was not independently read back in this run, so this remains **stale prior evidence, not a claim about today's inventory**. Do not count nominal mirror/feed entries until current primary inventory, eligibility, payout and settlement route are independently read back.

- Existing canonical opportunities remain the priority: Kingston Stanley ($99 / 48-hour sourcing overflow pilot) and Xubio ($49 / 48-hour onboarding support pilot) already sent and followed up once; OnTrack Mulching cleanup offer sent; JobNect/KJ Plumbing remain delivery-delayed; Colonia Estudio, Cork City Gaol and Cuina Teva were rejected/closed to unsolicited follow-up; MPRTC route is known wrong/unmonitored. Respect each record's current contact state—do not re-contact merely because revenue is slow.
- The two existing Upwork briefs (USD $700 RAG/CRM build and USD $1,000 WhatsApp/GHL agent) remain gated on a truthful live demo/source proof and authorized authenticated proposal route. Do not call either applied or qualified.
- The public searches in this bounded run produced no additional direct buyer brief that met all requirements (identifiable payer, live scope, feasible route from South Africa and credible short path to withdrawable payment). Supply-side posts and expired posts were excluded. This is not a claim that no such buyer exists; discovery remains open.

### Execution/acceptance report
- **New routes fully qualified as near-term withdrawable money:** 0.
- **New Web3 route held for one bounded verification / capability gate:** 1 (1inch Infrastructure Bounty).
- **Rejected as non-cash, stale/ineligible, unverifiable, or supply-side noise:** multiple, as above.
- **Applications, bids, outreach, purchases, wallet transactions or paid tasks executed in this research pass:** 0.
- **Revenue or Owner repayment evidenced by this pass:** $0. No repayment is claimed.
- **Next actions:** maintain focus on current warm/direct pilot responses and current unblocked paid-task gates; recheck live microtask availability via first-party routes; get current funded/claimable bounty inventory via its authorized API surface; only retain Web3 candidates with scope fit and transparent payer/control/settlement. Continue to reject unverifiable offerings after one bounded public-source check.

The 33% allocation remains a governance request until ROOT/T-GOV disposition and per-worker consumption/behavioral receipts are read back. @claude

# Revamp /punish With Automatic Escalation, Rule Keywords, and Staff Permissions

For ban-evasion, use safe existing-ban extension logic.
Never shorten an existing punishment.

All punishment tiers must be configurable.

==================================================
5. AUTOMATIC OFFENSE TRACKING
==================================================

Track punishment history by player UUID.

Each offense must store:
- Unique incident ID
- Player UUID
- Rule ID
- Canonical keyword
- Readable display name
- Gamemode
- Punishment scope
- Timestamp
- Issuing staff UUID
- Staff permission level
- Previous qualifying offense count
- Applied punishment tier
- Punishment type
- Duration
- Evidence or incident reference
- Enforcement status
- Appeal/reversal status

Example:

Steve has three previous Spam offenses.

Staff runs:
/punish Steve spam

System determines:
Rule: Spamming
Offense: 4
Punishment: 1-Hour Mute

After successful confirmation, record the offense.

The next qualifying spam violation receives Tier 5.

Use a configurable 90-day escalation window for minor offenses.

Serious offenses should use a longer configurable window.

Keep audit records regardless of escalation-window expiration.

After Tier 5, continue applying the configured Tier 5 punishment unless an authorized policy specifies otherwise.

==================================================
6. CONFIRMATION GUI
==================================================

Running /punish must NOT immediately punish the player.

Open a confirmation GUI.

Example:

JOSHYMC PUNISHMENT CONFIRMATION

Player: Steve
Rule: Credit Voucher Abuse
Gamemode: Survival
Previous Offenses: 1
Current Offense: 2
Punishment: 14-Day Ban
Staff: ExampleAdmin

Buttons:
- Confirm Punishment
- Cancel
- View History

For serious penalties, require an evidence/reference or written justification before confirmation.

The confirmation must:
- Be bound to the initiating staff UUID.
- Use a unique ID.
- Expire after a configurable period.
- Be single-use.
- Recheck staff permissions.
- Recheck the player's offense count.
- Recheck punishment scope.
- Reject stale confirmations.

==================================================
7. GAMEMODE AND NETWORK SCOPE
==================================================

The system must function on BOTH Survival and Lifesteal.

Support:
- Survival-only punishment
- Lifesteal-only punishment
- Network-wide punishment

Default to the gamemode where the violation occurred.

Store the gamemode with each offense.

History should be accessible network-wide to authorized staff.

Qualifying offenses for the same rule may count across both gamemodes.

Example:

Steve spams on Survival:
Tier 1 = Warning

Steve later spams on Lifesteal:
Tier 2 = 10-Minute Mute

The mute applies to Lifesteal, not automatically to Survival.

Normal network-wide bans require Manager-or-higher approval.

Admins may issue emergency network-wide suspensions lasting up to 24 hours, requiring senior review within six hours.

Do not allow automatic escalation to bypass these approval requirements.

Validate whether a rule applies to the gamemode before enforcement.

==================================================
8. DUPLICATE PUNISHMENT PREVENTION
==================================================

Prevent:
- Double-clicking the confirmation GUI.
- Reusing confirmation IDs.
- Two staff punishing one incident twice.
- Concurrent commands incorrectly increasing offense tiers.
- Retry operations duplicating punishment records.
- Restarts replaying completed punishments.
- Aliases creating separate rule histories.

Use:
- Unique incident identifiers.
- Database transactions.
- Idempotent punishment execution.
- Safe concurrency controls.
- Persistent execution state.

If punishment execution fails, do not falsely mark the action as completed.

==================================================
9. APPEALS AND REVERSALS
==================================================

Integrate with existing moderation and appeal systems.

When a punishment is overturned:
- Preserve the audit history.
- Mark the offense overturned.
- Remove invalidated offenses from future escalation counts.
- Restore applicable access.
- Record the authorized reversing staff member.
- Preserve a reason for the reversal.

Existing unmute, unban, and unwarn functionality must continue working according to staff permissions.

Do not erase the historical incident.

==================================================
10. CORRECTIVE ACTIONS
==================================================

Some violations may require:
- Removal of duplicated items.
- Reversal of exploited money.
- Removal of illegitimate Credits.
- Rank corrections.
- Reversal of bounty farming.
- Leaderboard corrections.
- Restoration of protected builds.

Do not automatically wipe player inventories or balances solely because a rule was selected.

Corrective actions require proper authority, evidence, and audit logging.

==================================================
11. COMMANDS AND GUI
==================================================

Required commands:

/punish <player> <rule>
/punish history <player>
/punish history <player> <rule>
/punish preview <player> <rule>
/punish rules
/punish rules <category>
/punish confirm <id>
/punish cancel <id>
/punish reload

Preserve existing compatible legacy commands, including relevant unban, unmute, and unwarn operations.

Tab completion must:
- Display canonical hyphenated keywords.
- Show only authorized rules.
- Exclude informational rules.
- Support offline player resolution where applicable.

The rules GUI must organize offenses by category and show readable rule names.

Every command and GUI action must enforce server-side permissions.

==================================================
12. STAFF AUDIT LOGGING
==================================================

Log:
- Staff UUID
- Target UUID
- Rule ID
- Rule keyword
- Readable rule name
- Gamemode
- Punishment scope
- Previous offense count
- Applied tier
- Punishment type
- Duration
- Confirmation
- Execution outcome
- Evidence/reference
- Reversal or appeal state

Also log:
- Failed enforcement.
- Permission denials.
- Tier overrides.
- Duplicate incident prevention.
- Administrative corrections.
- Network-wide approvals.

Use the existing tamper-resistant moderation audit infrastructure where possible.

==================================================
13. EXISTING SYSTEM COMPATIBILITY
==================================================

Inspect the existing JoshyMC punishment implementation before making changes.

Preserve:
- Existing active bans.
- Existing active mutes.
- Existing warnings.
- Existing appeal records.
- Existing moderation history.
- Existing staff group permissions.
- Existing gamemode isolation.
- Existing network moderation behavior.

Do not create a second incompatible punishment backend.

Do not invent previous offense counts when historical records cannot reliably be mapped to specific rules.

Do not modify unrelated commands, gameplay mechanics, rank rewards, or economic systems.

==================================================
14. TESTING REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Test command parsing:

/punish Steve spam
/punish Steve hacking
/punish Steve claim-abuse
/punish Steve credit-voucher-abuse
/punish Steve combat-logging

Verify player-facing reasons:

spam -> Spamming
hacking -> Hacking or Cheating
claim-abuse -> Claim Abuse
credit-voucher-abuse -> Credit Voucher Abuse
combat-logging -> Combat Logging

Never display raw keywords in ban reasons.

Test all five tiers of spam:

1. Warning
2. 10-Minute Mute
3. 30-Minute Mute
4. 1-Hour Mute
5. 6-Hour Mute

Test every staff rank:
- Trainee
- Helper
- Jr Mod
- Mod
- Lead Mod
- Jr Admin
- Admin
- Sr Admin

Verify:
- Rank inheritance works.
- Trainees can only issue warnings.
- Helpers can only issue warnings/mutes.
- Jr Mods cannot issue bans.
- Mods cannot exceed 7-day bans.
- Lead Mods cannot exceed 30-day bans.
- Jr Admins cannot permanently ban.
- Admins can handle all enforceable rules.
- Sr Admins can review serious cases.
- Developer gains no unintended moderation authority.
- Unauthorized rules are hidden from suggestions.
- Manually typing unauthorized keywords still fails.

Test:
- Offline punishment targets.
- Persistent history after restart.
- Escalation expiration.
- Shared history across gamemodes.
- Correct gamemode punishment scope.
- Network-wide approval restrictions.
- Duplicate confirmations.
- Concurrent moderation actions.
- Appeal reversals.
- Database failures.
- Permission changes before confirmation.
- Enforcement failures.
- Informational rules cannot trigger punishment.

==================================================
15. IMPLEMENTATION AND PR
==================================================

1. Read CLAUDE.md.
2. Inspect existing moderation architecture.
3. Implement rule registry and readable names.
4. Implement hyphenated command keywords.
5. Implement five-tier punishment configuration.
6. Implement eight rank-specific permission nodes.
7. Implement inherited staff authorization.
8. Implement persistent automatic offense tracking.
9. Implement punishment confirmations.
10. Integrate Survival/Lifesteal and network scope.
11. Integrate existing ban/mute/warn/kick backend.
12. Implement duplicate protection.
13. Implement appeal and reversal handling.
14. Add audit logging.
15. Add relevant automated tests.
16. Run ./gradlew build.
17. Fix implementation-related build failures.
18. Commit and push completed changes.
19. Open a PR referencing this issue.

Do not merge automatically.

Because this issue is large, preserve incremental completed work on the remote branch.

If blocked, document the blocker and preserve the branch instead of silently abandoning the implementation.

==================================================
EXPECTED RESULT
==================================================

A Helper executes:

/punish Steve spam

The system:
- Finds Steve's previous spam violations.
- Determines the next punishment.
- Checks Helper permissions.
- Displays confirmation.
- Applies the punishment if authorized.
- Records the incident.

An Admin executes:

/punish Steve credit-voucher-abuse

The system:
- Recognizes Credit Voucher Abuse.
- Calculates the correct tier.
- Checks Admin permissions.
- Displays confirmation.
- Executes the punishment.
- Records the offense.

Steve's ban screen displays:

Reason: Credit Voucher Abuse

NOT:

Reason: credit-voucher-abuse

The completed system must support both gamemodes, automated escalation, the eight staff permission nodes, secure confirmations, persistent tracking, appeal compatibility, and complete audit logging.

Implement, test, build, push, and open a PR for review.

source_text:
Agent.run(output_type=...) fails on the console channel because of the 'openminion: ' prefix
**Environment:** openminion 0.1.17 (PyPI), Python 3.12.9.

`Agent.run(output_type=Model)` cannot be used on the console channel: the runtime validates the channel-rendered text, which starts with the literal `openminion: ` prefix, so valid JSON never parses.

**Minimal reproduction**

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from openminion import Agent

class Answer(BaseModel):
    ok: bool
    value: int

with Agent(instructions="Answer in JSON.", output_type=Answer) as agent:
    result = agent.run('Return {"ok": true, "value": 42}')
```

**Observed**

```
AgentOutputValidationError: Reply did not validate against Answer:
  Invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1
  input_value='openminion: {"ok": true, "value": 42}'
```

The body is valid JSON. The literal `openminion: ` added by the console renderer is what breaks `json.loads`. Without `output_type`, `result.text == 'openminion: {"ok": true, "value": 42}'` and `result.raw["body"]` has the same prefix.

**Cause**

`api/agent.py::_coerce_output` validates `reply_text` as returned by the console channel without stripping that channel's render prefix.

**Workaround**

Do not use `output_type`. Parse `result.text` after stripping `openminion: `, markdown fences, and an optional top-level array. A small helper is in `SC0d3r/bounty-scout` (`scout.agent.parse_json_object`).

**Suggested fix**

Strip the channel prefix before coercion, or return the raw body to the Python API and keep rendering in the CLI layer. At minimum, document that `output_type` is not usable on the console channel.

This matters for automation: typed output is the natural way to build tool-driven agents, and the failure mode points at the JSON payload rather than at the renderer.

source_text:
Agent v3.1 cannot execute Tool HTTP Request: "has a supplyData method but no execute method"
## Environment

- n8n 2.45.0, self-hosted (Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.45.0`)
- AI Agent node `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent` v3.1
- Tool HTTP Request `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.toolHttpRequest` v1.1
- OpenAI Chat Model `@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChatOpenAi` v1
- Model endpoint: any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (the failure happens when the model asks for the tool, before the HTTP request is made)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Add a Manual Trigger, then an AI Agent node (v3.1).
2. Attach an OpenAI Chat Model as `ai_languageModel`.
3. Attach a Tool HTTP Request (v1.1) as `ai_tool`, with any URL (e.g. `https://example.com`).
4. Give the agent a prompt that makes the model call the tool.
5. Execute the workflow.

## Expected

The tool performs the HTTP request and returns the response body to the agent.

## Actual

The tool node fails with:

```
The node "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.toolHttpRequest" has a "supplyData" method but no "execute" method.
```

The AI Agent node itself reports `success` and hands an empty tool result to the model, so from the agent's point of view the tool returned nothing. The execution status is `error` only because of the tool node's error.

## Control

The same workflow with the AI Agent node set to v2.2 works: the HTTP request is made and the response (including headers) reaches the model.

So on 2.45.0 `toolHttpRequest` is usable with agent v2.2 and unusable with agent v3.1.

## Additional note

The silent part matters on its own: when a tool fails, the agent does not surface the failure to the model and still finishes `success`. Anyone relying on the model to notice a failed tool call needs to inspect the tool node's `runData` instead.

## Evidence

Local 2.45.0 instance, agent v3.1 workflow:
- execution id 885: `Tool` node `error` with the message above, `Agent` node `success`, agent output `TOOLSAW:""`.
- control execution 890 (agent v2.2, same tool pointed at a closed port): tool node `success` and the model receives `There was an error: "connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9"`.

Happy to retest against a newer build or provide the exported workflow JSON.

source_text:
MED-PRICE-001: build quality-gated global medicine affordability and procurement model
## Goal

Design and prototype an open, auditable decision-support system that helps participating health systems obtain essential medicines at the **lowest sustainable, quality-assured landed cost** while improving reliable availability and equitable access.

The objective is not to optimize purchase price alone. A low unit price that creates stockouts, short shelf life, unsafe product quality, concentrated supply, expensive distribution, or unaffordable patient co-payments is not a good outcome.

## Why this matters

WHO says essential medicines should be available at all times, affordable to people and health systems, and of assured quality; the 2025 WHO Model List contains over 520 medicines, including 374 for children:
https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/essential-medicines
https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/B09474

Proven mechanisms already exist:
- WHO recommends quality-assured generics/biosimilars, price transparency, tendering and pooled procurement among the policy tools countries can combine: https://www.who.int/teams/health-product-and-policy-standards/medicines-selection-ip-and-affordability/affordability-pricing
- The Global Fund's Pooled Procurement Mechanism managed about US$1.02 billion in orders for implementers in 81 countries during 2025: https://www.theglobalfund.org/en/sourcing-management/procurement-tools/
- UNICEF publishes multiyear-agreement antimalarial price data: https://www.unicef.org/supply/documents/antimalarials-price-data
- The Medicines Patent Pool tracks licensed product access, registrations and supply readiness: https://medicinespatentpool.org/accesspal
- South Africa's National Department of Health publishes a medicine-price database including Single Exit Prices and logistics fees: https://www.health.gov.za/nhi-pee/
- WHO prequalification provides a quality benchmark for products eligible for its programme: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/prequalification-of-medicines-by-who

## V1 scope

Start with an offline, synthetic-data-first procurement simulator for a small set of essential generic medicines; do not ingest patient-level data.

### Required data contracts

1. **Medicine presentation identity:** INN/active ingredient, strength, dosage form, route, package size, target FHIR/ATC/other coding systems only where correctly mapped, country/jurisdiction, registration status, and licensed market scope.
2. **Price observation:** currency, observation date, unit basis, public/private or tender channel, supplier, price type (ex-manufacturer/SEP/tender/landed), contract duration, volume tier, tax/duty/logistics inclusion, source locator, exact capture digest and source-specific licensing/reuse status.
3. **Quality/admission evidence:** regulator registration and status, WHO prequalification or an accepted stringent/regional/national approval criterion for the intended procurement channel, GMP/quality-system evidence, product identity and strength match, recall/alert state, and expiry/shelf-life conditions.
4. **Supply offer:** supplier and manufacturing site, offered volume, production capacity evidence, lead time, delivery reliability evidence, minimum order, shelf life at delivery, temperature/cold-chain needs, API/key starting material dependencies when known, and contract terms.
5. **Demand scenario:** aggregate demand by period and geography, uncertainty range, seasonality, service-level target, current stock, lead-time demand, and shortage/expiry costs. Use synthetic aggregates until lawful and governed operational data is separately qualified.
6. **Decision/award record:** input-manifest and policy digests, eligibility gates, scenario assumptions, candidate offers, selected allocation, dissent/counter-evidence, conflicts of interest, reviewer approval, and reasons for excluding offers.

Keep raw patient or beneficiary identifiers out of public artifacts and procurement receipts.

## Optimization objective

Minimize total expected lifecycle cost, not just quoted price:

`expected_total_cost = acquisition + freight + insurance + duties/tax + quality testing + storage/cold-chain + financing + expiry/wastage + shortage/stockout impact`

Subject to hard constraints for lawful market access, product quality, approved/authorized use, capacity, lead time, available budget, shelf life, and required service level. Also constrain supplier concentration and maintain minimum resilience (e.g. qualified second source or safety stock) where supply risk justifies it. The model may display trade-offs but cannot relax safety or quality gates to achieve a lower score.

Fairness requirements: report price and availability separately by country/channel and date; distinguish absolute price from affordability relative to local public-health budgets and household burden; model tiered prices and cross-subsidies transparently; do not infer willingness to pay from sensitive individual data or use identity/reputation scores to allocate medicines.

## Mechanisms to compare

- pooled/regional procurement and standardized tender lots;
- multi-winner tenders and volume commitments that preserve qualified backup suppliers;
- quality-assured generic and biosimilar uptake;
- transparent price comparisons and lifecycle cost-plus analysis;
- patent-pool/voluntary licence and regulatory-registration availability mapping;
- demand pooling, forecasting, order consolidation and inventory optimization;
- regional manufacturing/technology transfer when scale, quality systems and delivered total cost support it;
- public R&D and purchasing agreements with access and transparency conditions;
- packaging, formulation, distribution and cold-chain efficiency;
- appropriate tax/markup and patient co-payment policy scenarios.

No claim that all interventions lower prices in every context: the simulator must show assumptions, uncertainty, market concentration and failure modes.

## Luminous stack integration

- **Mycelix:** authoritative provenance/snapshot/selector references, licence and eligibility evidence, supplier/contract decision receipts and correction history. No universal trust score.
- **Symthaea:** demand forecasting, scenario analysis, sensitivity/uncertainty and counterfactual ranking against simple baselines. Advisory only.
- **Sol-Atlas:** map and timeline of price observations, registrations, licence territory, shortage risk, evidence gaps and scenario results. Visualization confers no authority.
- **Mycelix-Health:** medicine presentation / procurement domain contracts, quality gates, safety/recall integrations and qualified human award workflow.
- **Nix/CI:** pinned toolchains, immutable public synthetic corpus, reproducible scenario manifests and exact-head results.

Do not mix clinical efficacy/safety evidence, medicine registration, supply eligibility, tender eligibility, price observation and contract award into one Boolean or reputation score. Each requires a separate state and source.

## Required adversarial tests

- Same presentation but different strength/form/pack cannot compare as the same unit.
- Same named price with different unit basis, currency, observation date, tender channel or included logistics is not directly comparable without explicit normalization.
- Missing/unknown licence territory or registration does not become eligible.
- Low-price offer fails hard quality gate -> never wins.
- Price-only winner causes high stockout risk -> report total-cost/resilience trade-off and eligible alternatives.
- Single supplier concentration breaches policy -> infeasible or explicit exception with accountable human approval.
- Stale price/recall/registration evidence -> Indeterminate/review-needed.
- No offer or missing price data never appears as “free” or a successful procurement.
- Different FX rates / freight / expiry assumptions produce a traceable changed scenario.
- Unsupported data licence means no unlicensed redistribution; metadata-only evidence remains metadata-only.
- Model's selected offer is not itself a contract, purchase order or payment instruction.
- Simulated savings cannot be represented as realized/clinical outcomes.

## Deliverables and acceptance

1. Versioned Rust input/output types and synthetic dataset.
2. Deterministic baseline for eligible-offer filtering and cost normalization.
3. Small exact/transparent allocation optimizer with budget, service-level and concentration constraints; compare against lowest-price-only baseline.
4. Scenario report for purchase price, landed cost, service level, expiry, supplier concentration, uncertainty and access/affordability by geography.
5. Independent checker recomputes eligibility and cost from immutable inputs, separate from the optimizer.
6. Tests and replay receipt demonstrate deterministic output for the same input manifest/policy.
7. No purchase/execution authority; final award stays with an accountable buyer under local law and procurement rules.

## Initial demonstration

Use synthetic offers for 10–20 generic essential-medicine presentations across 3–5 hypothetical regions. Then adapt public price observations from WHO/UNICEF/Global Fund/South African NDoH only when the exact source, date, unit, licence and comparability conditions are recorded.

## Non-goals

- No unsupervised procurement, prescribing, therapeutic substitution, or patient-level allocation.
- No bypassing patents, marketing authorization, import controls, GMP, pharmacovigilance or procurement law.
- No treating WHO prequalification as automatic legal authorization in every country.
- No claim of realized savings or patient outcomes from a simulator.
- No assumption that local manufacturing is always cheaper than pooled imports.

source_text:
Organic Fragrance 101: What Product Developers Need to Know
The word organic gets used loosely across the fragrance industry, and that looseness causes real problems for brands trying to make accurate claims. A product developer sourcing an organic fragrance for the first time needs to understand that organic is not simply a softer version of natural. It is a specific, certifiable standard, and treating it casually can expose a brand to compliance risk long after a product has shipped. This article breaks down what organic fragrance actually means, how it differs from natural, and what to check before committing to a formulation.
Organic Is a Certification, Not a Vibe
In the fragrance world, an organic fragrance refers to a formulation built from raw materials that are certified organic under a recognized standard, such as COSMOS or USDA organic guidelines, depending on the market. This means the plants used to produce the essential oils and aromatic extracts were grown without synthetic pesticides, synthetic fertilizers, or genetically modified inputs, and the supply chain carries documentation proving that chain of custody from farm to final blend.
This is a meaningfully higher bar than natural. A natural fragrance can be built from naturally derived raw materials without any certification behind the farming practices. An organic fragrance requires that certification trail, and a formulator working in this space needs to source accordingly, which usually means a smaller, more carefully vetted pool of raw material suppliers.
Why Product Developers Get This Wrong
The most common mistake is treating organic and natural as interchangeable marketing language. A brand that labels a product organic fragrance without the underlying certified raw materials and documentation is taking on legal risk, since regulatory bodies and consumer protection agencies in several markets have started enforcing organic labeling claims more aggressively, particularly in personal care and home fragrance categories.
The second common mistake is assuming an organic claim can be made for the whole product based on just the fragrance component. Depending on the market and the certifying body, an organic fragrance oil used at a small percentage in an otherwise conventional formulation may not be enough to support a broader organic product claim. Brands need to understand exactly what percentage and what certification level is required before building marketing language around it.
What Goes Into an Organic Fragrance Formulation
Formulating with organic fragrance oils is more constrained than working with conventional naturals, simply because the raw material pool is smaller. A formulator has to work within what certified organic growers and distillers can actually supply, which affects everything from consistency of supply to cost. Essential oils like organic lavender, organic bergamot, or organic rose generally cost more than their non-certified counterparts because the farming and documentation requirements are stricter and yields are often lower.
Batch-to-batch consistency is also a bigger challenge with organic raw materials than with conventional ones, since certified organic farms are often smaller operations more exposed to seasonal and regional variation. A fragrance house experienced in organic formulation builds blending strategies that manage this variability while still holding the final scent profile consistent for the brand's customers.
Questions to Ask a Potential Supplier
Before committing to an organic fragrance program, product developers should ask a supplier for the specific certification standard being used, documentation proving the certified organic status of each raw material in the formulation, and clarity on what percentage of the final product needs to be certified organic to support the label claim in the markets where the product will be sold. It is also worth asking how the supplier handles supply disruptions, since organic raw material shortages are more common and can affect production timelines if a backup sourcing plan is not already in place.
Where Agilex Fits In
Agilex Fragrances supports brands building organic and organic-adjacent fragrance programs with documented raw material sourcing, formulation expertise across personal care, home care, and candle applications, and the compliance knowledge needed to make accurate label claims. Details on the organic and natural aromatics portfolio are available at [organic fragrance](https://www.agilexfragrances.com/naturals/), including guidance on which certification pathway fits a given product category.
Getting It Right From the Start
Organic fragrance is a genuine, defensible positioning when it is built correctly, and it can be a strong differentiator in categories where consumers are paying close attention to ingredient sourcing. The brands that succeed with it are the ones that treat organic as a sourcing and compliance discipline from the earliest stages of product development, rather than a label applied after the formula is already locked. Getting a qualified formulation partner involved early is the difference between a claim that holds up under scrutiny and one that creates problems down the line.

Show HN: Optio – A self-hosted orchestration platform for AI agents
Hey HN! I shared Optio here back in March. Originally it was focused on getting swarms of coding agents (claude code/codex) to drive PRs towards a merge by automatically resuming them on CI failures or PR comments. Since then, I've reworked the project to be a general platform for running any kind of AI workflow on your infra by allowing users to configure each component of a possible workflow: When: On demand, a cron schedule, or triggered by external events such as a webhook, slack message, ticket (jira/linear/gh), pagerduty/datadog/alertsmanager/pylon/sentry. Where: In a k8s pod or any machine you have installed the optio daemon on (I use my laptop). Who: Any harness you prefer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, etc.) What/Why: You can format parameters from the triggers directly into the prompts and then configure if the agent should exit, be resumed automatically, or be persistent. You can either define workflows in the web ui or as yaml files that get synced to the orchestrator (ai config-as-code). I've also built native iOS and Android apps so you can connect to your cluster and create/manage agents remotely. The marketing page is at  https://optio.host  and the code is still open source at  https://github.com/jonwiggins/optio  Would love feedback or any thoughts you might have on how I could make it better!

source_text:
Show HN: Formstep, Request information from customers without the back-and-forth
I built Formstep:  https://formstep.io  The idea came from a problem I kept running into while working on loan applications. A workflow could automate a large part of the process, but eventually it would need something only the customer could provide: a document, a correction, a signature, an explanation, or confirmation of some information. At that point, workflow automation basically did not work. The forms themselves were also often the source of the problem. Applications came in with wrong documents, misunderstood questions, incomplete answers, or people simply forgetting to finish. Someone had to email the customer, explain what was missing, wait for a reply then follow up again. It was always back-and-forth. So I built Formstep to make requesting information from customers easier, not only for humans, but also for workflows and AI agents. The idea is: A person, workflow, or AI agent sends a customer a request through email or a link. Either re-use existing form  or create unique for each customer. You can prefill what you already know, lock fields, pass context, and only ask the customer what you need. For example, we might already know: * Address that you already have in the CRM * Company description from the internet * What a agreement document must contain * How a good answer should be Formstep can check inputs and uploaded files while the customer is filling out the form and tell them if something is missing or inconsistent before they submit.
For example “The PDF does not contain your signature” or “Invoice total does not match the order amount”. The goal is to catch problems while the customer is still there, rather than letting bad data continue through the workflow and discovering it later. On the automation side, requests can currently be created through n8n, Zapier, the REST API, or by an AI agent over MCP.
When the customer finishes, the structured answers can go back into the workflow so it can continue. Forms and invitation/reminder are multilingual, and submitted answers can be translated inside the dashboard with one click.  If you want, Formstep can be used as normal form builder and shared through public links, QR, embeds etc. It support custom themes for dark/light mode, with cover image, has Notion-style editor and much more. The list is too long to fit here. I want to make Formstep a plattform where it becomes more intelligent over time and ensures that we can get better answers from customers for any use case. My question to you:
Where do your automations currently stop because they need input from a customer or user, and how are you handling that today? If you are interested in trying out the n8n node:  https://www.npmjs.com/package/n8n-nodes-formstep  Zapier integration:  https://zapier.com/apps/formstep/integrations  Connecting your AI agent:  https://docs.formstep.io/developers/mcp-server/  Docs:  https://docs.formstep.io  I would love your feedback and please try a quick demo at  https://app.formstep.io/try

ASK: HN Help and Forward Advice, Ideas: New Lossless cmpr MRT/CT, Astro
Hey HN, at first, i'm not from that subject field so I dont know what to do. I'm an ordinary engeneer with basics and unorthodox thinking. I used Claude to help me implement. Its a process of several months and bazills of millions of tokens of work. I can't show or disclose, begging for your understanding. I can't beat WEBP lossless on kodak test suite, YET; But I'm like 5% worser on RGBa. CMYK's similar. Here, the advantage is me being 5-15x faster as WEBP / other lossless codecs. Not yet fully confirmed, but promissing results WEBP will be knocked too. My lossy compression is better than JPEG sometimes, but always ~10++ times faster. Very big building field right now. The figures are very promissing on lossless video. On cpu cycles beating every SOTA methods by being upto 15x faster or so. Possible path. My lossy shows better sharpness and details in (very) fast moving scenes (1080p, 2k, 4k incl. hdr), while being only ~5-10% bigger than heif and avc, and others with comperable compression params. May be is resolved in x-xx weeks. → noticed, my lossless works better as SOTA (JPEG LS, JPEG 2000 and JPEG XL, each lossless mode) on medical imaging / DICOM, voluminetric medical/scientific data, handles pixel bitdepths >32bit; >32000x32000px (jpeg didnt even consume). It seems to scale res/depth without issues. Runs on data from various MRT/CT Imagers and formats found for download show ~15%-50% percent better compression as SOTA/DICOM, at a fraction of cycles. Some results: CT volumes, ratio and (encode / decode seconds) - pancreas, 185 slices →  3.26 (0.7 / 0.6)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.69 (2.3 / 1.8) │ JPEG 2000: 2.71 (10.6 / 8.5) │ FFV1: 2.70 - COVID chest, 2464 slices →  4.48 (10.0 / 8.6)  │ JPEG-LS: 3.30 (24.6 / 18.9) │ JPEG 2000: 3.12 (129 / 101) │ FFV1: 3.21 - Colonography, 950 slices →  2.79, was 2.59  │ JPEG-LS: 2.73 (10.9 / 8.8) │ JPEG 2000: 2.61 (55.6 / 44.2) │ FFV1: 2.99 - LIDC lung, 764 slices, 12-bit →  2.67 (3.1 / 2.8)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.40 (9.9 / 7.7) │ JPEG 2000: 2.40 (46.1 / 37.9) │ FFV1: 2.37 - TCGA kidney, 820 slices →  3.31 (3.3 / 2.9)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.87 (9.2 / 7.1) │ JPEG 2000: 2.74 (48.1 / 37.3) │ FFV1: 2.80 MR and SAR data is also a possible play field with some prommissing results I've already seen. So, as everyone too, i want $$$. I decided to walk my own way after being fired in 2 mins two years ago and I dont have much financial reserves left, without getting income atm. Can't start employment; Need & Want to fight with Claude 23h/7d instead on other ideas I'm working on since years. Need MONEY!! So, if you would be me. Open Sourcing the algorithm is bread-less and doesn't pay my/your bills. I'm seeking Advice or Ideas on how would you approach it, if you were me - with max profit in the head (.. but still do good!). The actual and future storage/memory crisis opens up a lever. My approach puts together: storage AND compute can both be siginificantly reduced. - AWS health services, google health and some other smaller cloud service providers - Medical imaging device producers (mrt/ct) saving on cpu and memory - Physicians using SaaS for storage/viewing - Astro/Scientific imaging and processing - Possible space/SAR/satelite imaging/data, not giving up on it yet. But how to approach?? If you give it to x, then y will need it too for processing x's data. This gives a conflict in interest. Interest is profit max. What could end up as a strategy? How to find someone to pitch? Selling? Licensing? Other models? Patenting may not work / doesn't use patented methods. Appreciate any answer and 'thank you' to everyone reading. If I dont respond to your comment, think of me saying 'thank you' while bowing very deeply, weaving my hat. This post is not meant to let others do my work, its a scream for direction - kind of desperate & blind

Automations: ask the agent in plain words to schedule something for you
Check whether the agent can set up a schedule from a normal request in a thread.

## Try this

1. In a normal thread, ask: `Every weekday at 8:30 my time, check the top three posts on news.ycombinator.com and give me one line on each. Set that up.`
2. See what the agent does, and whether it asks for your timezone.
3. Open Automations and find what it made.
4. In the same thread, ask it to change the schedule to Mondays only, then to stop it.

## What to look for

- The agent sets up the automation, or tells you clearly how to.
- What shows on the Automations page matches what you asked: time, days, timezone and instructions.
- Changes and stopping from the thread show on the Automations page.
- Nothing runs more often than you asked.

## Your report

Post one comment here with:

- Links to your threads (`app.useagent.org/session/...`)
- What worked
- What broke or confused you, and what you expected instead
- Screenshots or a short screen recording

Open a separate bug issue for anything broken, with the steps to reproduce it, and link it in your comment.

No need to claim; post your report as a comment.

---

**General asks**
- Do the steps yourself in the hosted app. Sign up with your email at [app.useagent.org](https://app.useagent.org/login?ref=feedback); you don't need an API key or a card to start. The link in the sign-up email works for 24 hours, so check spam if it's missing.
- Run everything by hand. Reports from runs done or simulated by another AI tool get closed.
- Use made-up details, test accounts and data you own. Don't point the agent at other people's accounts, inboxes or private data, and don't send real forms or messages to strangers.
- More than one person can report on the same issue, and every report helps. If someone already found what you found, add only what's different.
- Stuck? Comment here with a screenshot and we'll help.

**Keep private details out of here**

This page is public. Don't post your real email, phone number, address, API keys, or screenshots that show any of them; blur them first. Send anything private to **hi@useagent.org** with a link to your comment here.

**Using AI tools, and what gets no reply**
- AI help is fine. Blind AI output is not. You must understand every line you submit, run it yourself, and show it working in the app with your own screenshots or recording.
- Pull requests that look generated and untested get closed without a reply and labeled `spam`, which also means they don't count for Hacktoberfest. Signs we look for: no proof from a real run, code that ignores this repo's patterns or reinvents helpers that already exist, unrelated files changed, a description that only restates the issue, and failing checks nobody looked at.
- One pull request per issue, by the person who claimed it. Opening pull requests on issues someone else has taken, or several near-identical pull requests for the same bounty, counts as farming and gets the same treatment.
- Bounties are paid only for the verified outcome the issue describes (for example, a workshop that actually happened, or an app that works on both systems), never for a write-up, a plan, or an unfinished attempt.
- When we ask a question in review, answer it in your own words. If you can't explain your change, we can't merge it.

If-node in sub-workflow causes properties of previous node to become not found when all items go the false path
### Bug Description

The properties of an earlier node can become not found. This Problem occurs when between the node that sets the property and the node that tries to access it there is a sub-workflow and inside that sub-workflow there is an if-node and all items inside the sub-workflow will go the false path of the if-node.

The error does not occur if all items of the sub-workflow will go the true path or if some items go true and others go false.

Also the property seems to be not found if the expression uses "item" to reference a previous node. When using "first()" or "all()[0]" it seems to work.

Maybe related: When debugging an execution where all items in an if-node use the false path and a merge node is behind it, the merge node is unable to execute.

### To Reproduce

[main-workflow.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33341808/main-workflow.json)
[sub-workflow.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33341809/sub-workflow.json)

These json files show a main-workflow and a sub-workflow to reproduce this issue. 
If the value properties of all items in the "Set Array Data" nodes myItems field  is true, the workflow works. But if all are set to false the code node at the end will throw an error and in the edit fiels node at the end you can see the difference between the expressions.

### Expected behavior

After the described sub-workflow, nodes should still be able to access earlier nodes via the " $('NameOfEarlyNode').item.json " expression, even if all items used the false path in the subworkflow.

source_text:
AI/semis evening brief, Oct 20: 65 updates, 23 high
# Anthropic's IPO filing shows $16bn in half-year revenue and up to $750bn in planned compute spending

**The bottom line:** Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus and SpaceX's results both show AI lab revenue and compute budgets growing very fast. That spending is feeding straight into chips, memory and power. The weak link is the neoclouds, the leveraged middlemen that rent out GPUs. Their IPOs are stalling and Nvidia appears to be stepping in to support them.

## Anthropic's prospectus puts numbers on the AI arms race

Anthropic, the maker of the Claude models, had first-half 2026 revenue of $16.3 billion, up from $1.1 billion a year earlier, according to its draft S-1 filing for an IPO ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmeu0824885.d.html)). Compute and infrastructure spending was nearly $9 billion, up from $2.3 billion. That already exceeds the $7.3 billion it spent on compute in all of 2025 ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510432?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

The headline $80.7 billion net loss looks alarming. About $72 billion of it, however, is a mark-to-market charge on convertible notes, an accounting cost rather than cash burned ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510432?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). The bigger number is forward-looking. Anthropic may spend an additional $750 billion on compute over the coming years, including deals still being negotiated ([Bloomberg video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6OnuO6Y5OQY)). One such deal: Bloomberg reports Nscale, a European AI cloud firm, is in talks to sell Anthropic about $45 billion of computing power ([Bloomberg video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3MlgPZREVCw)).

**Read-through:** A single lab committing that much to compute supports demand visibility for Nvidia (NVDA), cloud providers and the memory and networking chain. It also concentrates risk. Much of that $750 billion is contingent and depends on revenue continuing to grow at this pace.

## SpaceX becomes an AI compute company, and wants its own fab

SpaceX (SPCX) reported Q3 revenue of $14.58 billion, up 161% and well ahead of the $12.87 billion consensus. AI revenue was $7.56 billion, now larger than its space business ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmeu0844539.d.html)). Capex was $19.59 billion, of which $16.44 billion went to AI. Backlog stood at $63 billion. The CFO said the company is on pace for $100 billion in annual recurring revenue by year-end ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmfa8006816.d.html)).

The most telling remark was about returns. The CFO said newly deployed compute pays back in under a year at current pricing, and that pricing is slightly above the top of the $30–50 per watt range the company gave last quarter. Musk said payback could shrink to six months next year ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510662?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). That directly contradicts the "AI overbuild" narrative, at least for operators with their own demand. Musk also argued that power, cooling and infrastructure, not chips, are now the binding constraints ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmeu0873441.d.html)).

Terafab, the chipmaking joint venture of SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA), now has a timeline:

- A first SRAM test chip at its Austin R&D centre around May–June 2027.
- Mass production in Q3 2028.

Musk himself said the schedule has "very large error bars" ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxrpa4766903.d.html)). US advanced logic fabs typically take three-plus years to build. He said ASML (ASML), the Dutch monopoly supplier of lithography tools, and other suppliers have accelerated equipment deliveries ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmfa8010861.d.html)). Korean media report Terafab is in talks with about 10 South Korean materials, components and equipment suppliers, several under NDA ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902194273.html)).

**Read-through:** This is incremental demand for equipment makers. It is also a long-dated threat to foundry concentration at TSMC, but only if execution matches the ambition.

## Neocloud cracks contrast with booming server demand

Not every link in the chain is healthy. Bloomberg reports neoclouds are losing favour. Neoclouds are the startups that borrowed heavily to buy GPUs and rent them out. South Korean AI computing supplier Elice fell 32% on its Seoul debut ([Bloomberg video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4WE0jaDsEns)). Australia's Firmus pulled its IPO this month and now seeks $2 billion-plus privately. Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest hundreds of millions of dollars in it ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510465?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). The same report cites analysis that Nvidia has taken on over $170 billion of risk exposure to such customers through credit guarantees and debt help.

Singapore's DayOne Data Centers is reassessing a US IPO. It may delay the deal or halve it to $2.5–3 billion, from an original target of up to $5 billion at a $20 billion valuation ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510599?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Former PBOC governor Zhou Xiaochuan added a macro warning at the Bund Summit. Given the scale of AI capital flows, he said, some investments will fail and could trigger financial turmoil, so policymakers should stock up tools now ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610203901709630.html)).

Yet hardware demand shows no sign of cooling. Super Micro Computer (SMCI), which assembles AI server racks, raised fiscal Q1 revenue guidance to $18.5–19.5 billion from $14.5–15.5 billion. It also lifted gross margin guidance to 12.0–12.5% from 10.4–10.8% ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxmev7633676.d.html)). The news lifted Dell (DELL) and HPE (HPE) too ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902445297.html)).

**Read-through:** The tension is between strong end-demand and fragile financing for the middle layer. Nvidia's role as financier of last resort is a growing risk to watch.

## Chips and memory: the equipment cycle extends to 2028

The fab buildout keeps accelerating. Industry group SEMI now forecasts record 2026 chip-equipment sales of $165.9 billion, up 23.2%, rising to $229.5 billion by 2028, a fifth straight year of growth ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuy4668415.d.html)). The same report notes:

- **TSMC (TSM):** raised 2026 capex to $60–64 billion from $52–56 billion.
- **ASML:** Q3 sales of €9.326 billion beat guidance and consensus, and it raised full-year guidance a second time.

TSMC's Q3 revenue rose 50.9% and net profit 68.7%, at a 66.4% gross margin. High-performance computing was 68% of revenue, and full-year growth guidance is now about 44% ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902386734.html)). A grim note: four workers died in a fall at TSMC's F22 fab construction site in Kaohsiung ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuy4804601.d.html)).

The squeeze is spreading upstream:

- **Equipment components:** Chinese outlet 36Kr describes "historic" price increases across the component chain, with pricing power shifting toward smaller parts makers. It flags valves, ceramics, RF power supplies and gas boxes ([36Kr](https://36kr.com/newsflashes/4034867562255492)).
- **Argon:** liquid argon, a process gas, jumped 38–49% in China in under two weeks to ¥2,540–3,057 per ton. Low air-separation output collided with chip demand ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510516?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **Germanium:** Yunnan Germanium (002428.SZ), a producer of the critical mineral used in optics and infrared, posted Q3 net profit up 2,642% to ¥102 million on revenue up 135% ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610203901532426.html)).

In memory, TrendForce expects Q4 DRAM contract prices to rise about 20% quarter on quarter. That is a deceleration from about 80% in Q2 and about 40% in Q3, though prices remain at high levels ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510491?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Korea's early-October data shows the boom in trade numbers. Chip exports jumped 222.5% year on year, helping total exports rise 123% to $61.6 billion ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuw7945337.d.html)). That benefits SK Hynix (000660.KS) and Samsung (005930.KS).

**Read-through:** The slowing price gains are the first hint the memory cycle may be maturing. Micron (MU) is holding a technology webinar on DRAM, HBM and NAND roadmaps ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213901979132.html)). Separately, its President and CTO Scott DeBoer sold about 28,500 shares at roughly $900 under a pre-set 10b5-1 trading plan ([SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/723125/000156823826000003/0001568238-26-000003-index.htm)).

## Power and cooling: the real bottleneck shows up in the data

Musk's point about power shows up in the numbers:

- **China's grid:** data-centre electricity use rose 35.4% in September and 41.6% year to date, while total consumption grew just 1.2% ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510682?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **Gas turbines:** global orders hit about 38GW in Q2, up 71% from 22GW, according to McCoy Power Reports. Full-year 2026 orders are seen above 100GW. That supports GE Vernova (GEV), Siemens Energy (ENR.DE) and Chinese parts suppliers ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510595?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).
- **Fuel cells:** solid oxide fuel cells are gaining attention because they can be deployed in modules and delivered quickly. Order conversion is still unproven ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510464?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

Inside the rack, the story is similar:

- **Vicor (VICR):** the maker of high-density power modules that feed AI processors grew Q3 revenue 78.5% ([Motley Fool transcript](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/20/vicor-vicr-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)).
- **Liquid cooling:** megawatt-scale systems are entering standardised mass delivery. One Chinese vendor won a single overseas order above ¥2.7 billion with a 120-day delivery cycle ([Sina](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-21/detail-inivxvuw7904008.d.html)).
- **Capacitors:** Goldman Sachs research cited by CLS says MLCCs, the tiny ceramic capacitors on circuit boards, are now the third-largest cost in an AI server after GPUs and memory ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510590?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). That is supportive for Murata (6981.T) and Chinese peers.

## China: open-source inference, state data and humanoid robots

DeepSeek open-sourced its in-house inference framework, DeepInfer, along with a token codec. The release lets cloud providers run DeepSeek models at close to DeepSeek's own cost, and possibly below it ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610203901600750.html)). That further commoditises inference pricing.

Beijing registered China National Data Group, a central state-owned firm backed by the three telecom carriers and both state grids, to treat data as a factor of production for AI ([EastMoney](https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202610213902410455.html)).

On robotics, Chinese suppliers of actuators, harmonic reducers and sensors are reportedly preparing capacity for Tesla's third-generation Optimus, which Tesla says is ready for mass production ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510437?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)). Reliability, cost and algorithm generalisation remain open hurdles. Momenta's CEO separately pointed to 2028 as the inflection point for scaled L4 autonomous driving ([CLS](https://api3.cls.cn/share/article/2510579?os=web&sv=8.4.6&app=CailianpressWeb)).

## What to watch

- **Anthropic's IPO:** the final S-1 terms, and whether the Nscale deal and other compute contracts are confirmed.
- **Supermicro earnings on Nov 3:** whether the margin uplift is durable.
- **Neocloud funding:** whether Nvidia's Firmus investment closes, and whether DayOne proceeds or shrinks its offering.
- **Memory pricing:** Micron's roadmap commentary, and whether Q4 DRAM gains fade further toward a peak.
- **Terafab:** supplier announcements from Korea and ASML that test the 2027–2028 timeline.

---
